## B-292 — one component crash blanked the whole app and every control-bridge op timed out until a full reload

status: **fixed** (2026-10-28) · severity: **critical** (any render throw anywhere took down every tab, the owner's unsaved view state and the agent's control at once) · area: the React tree (no error boundary anywhere), the op registries' placement (`useEditorControl`, `useMotionControl`, `useChromaControl` / `useBrandControl` / `useDebugControl`)

- **found:** 2026-10-28 00:11:15, live, right after B-291's throw. The log shows React's own hint, "An error occurred in the `<i>` component. Consider adding an error boundary", then a blank white window; `editor_text_fonts`, `editor_get_state` and `motion_get_state` each timed out after 20 s ("op … timed out waiting for the frontend") until the webview was reloaded at 00:33.
- **cause:** there was no error boundary in the app (the only two, in Motion, are Remotion `<Player>` `errorFallback`s). An uncaught render error makes React unmount the whole root, and every op registry lives inside that root, so the control server's announced targets stopped answering.
- **fix (D-418):** `@apelles/ui` gains `PanelErrorBoundary` (React's canonical class boundary): a crash replaces just that panel with "The <panel> panel crashed", the error message and **Reload panel** (clears the error and remounts the children with a fresh key). It logs `[panel-crash] the <panel> panel crashed: <message>` with the error and component stack through `console.error` (forwarded to `app.log` as a `[frontend]` ERROR line) and records the crash in a small external store (`panel-crashes.ts`). Boundaries now wrap: the whole app (`main.tsx`), each tab and the Sources / library column (`Shell.tsx`), the Edit tab's Preview, Timeline and Inspector, the Motion tab's preview, keyframe timeline, Layers / Catalog, inspector and manifest editor, and the Colorist's left panels, viewer and right panels. Each registry is called by its tab's top-level component, ABOVE that tab's pane boundaries, so a crashed pane never takes the bridge down; only a crash in a tab's own top-level component reaches the tab boundary, and Reload re-announces the registry's claim (B-272), so ops answer again without a page reload. The debug-only `debug_get_ui_state` reports `crashedPanels` (panel, message, stack, component stack, time, count) — description updated in both MCP servers, parity corpus re-captured (244 tools).
- **verification:** `packages/editor/src/EditorTab.panelCrash.dom.test.tsx` (4, the real `EditorTab` + registry + boundaries, the timeline pane made to throw): the Timeline pane shows the fallback with the error while the Preview pane still renders; the crash is logged and recorded with its component stack; `editor_get_state` and an `editor_add_marker` write both answer while the pane is down; Reload panel brings the pane back and clears the record; a pane that throws again after Reload shows the fallback again. `packages/debug/src/debugOps.crashedPanels.test.ts` (1). Editor 2417/2417 (compiled), debug 54/54, motion 1036/1036, shell 26/26, app 46/46 green; `cargo test -p apelles-mcp --test parity` green; tsc editor 3, app 65, motion 0, motion-engine 0, debug 0, ui 0, shell 0 (baselines). **Not verified live** (the running app serves main's code): see the B-291 entry for the live check.

## B-291 — pinch-zooming the timeline locked the library's scroll state into an update loop ("Maximum update depth exceeded") and blanked the window

status: **fixed** (2026-10-28) · severity: **critical** (with B-292, a white window and a dead bridge mid-edit) · area: `packages/editor/src/TimelinePane.tsx` (the D-116/B-116 zoom-anchor restore), `@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor`'s scroll sync

- **found:** 2026-10-28 00:11:15, dev build, the owner's "Five Levels of Claude Code" timeline (64 linked V/A pairs over one 4K source, 6:25, rate 493480/20563), waveform/thumbnail fetches for 104-160 s in flight. React threw "Maximum update depth exceeded" from `ScrollSync._onScroll`'s `setState`, called by the edit-area `Grid`'s scroll memoizer from its `componentDidUpdate`, deep in a layout-effect commit. The coordinating session's transcript shows no bridge call between 00:09:51 and the crash, and the fetch log shows the visible range moving from ~213 s to 104-160 s, i.e. the owner was zooming the timeline by hand.
- **cause (reproduced):** the library keeps the horizontal scroll in two places that echo each other inside the commit phase: `ScrollSync` state and the edit-area `Grid`. The grid reports its position up from `componentDidUpdate`; the edit area pushes `ScrollSync`'s value down into the grid from a `useLayoutEffect`. Whenever one render changes the two to DIFFERENT values, every commit swaps them (the grid reports A while the push sends B; next commit the grid reports B while the push sends A) and nothing ever converges. `TimelinePane` wrote the library scroll for the zoom anchor from a PASSIVE effect (`editorRef.setScrollLeft`). In WebKit, with a heavy timeline, the next pinch event landed between that write and the render applying it, so `zoomBy` anchored on a `scrollLeft` state that had not caught up (logged: `px=192.9 sl=1524 → 160.75` right after a write of 1108.17), and that zoom's own passive write (1108.1692708333335 vs 1108.169270833333) was flushed by React after the edit area had pushed the first value down but before the grid reported it, which is exactly the two-values render. Evidence: a fake DevTools hook counting consecutive commits that leave sync work pending reached 53 in the failing runs (3 otherwise), and a trace of every `ScrollSync` / `Grid` `setState` shows the alternation from the second write on. Reproduced with Playwright WebKit against the D-142 harness (`app/harness.html`) seeded with the owner's real timeline, streaming ctrl+wheel zoom: **9 of 15 runs** hit it on the old code. Chromium never did (different frame scheduling), which is why the harness tier had not seen it. The scripts are kept in `scratch/b291-webkit-repro/` (gitignored; its README says how to run them).
- **fix:** the anchor restore is a `useLayoutEffect`. Written in the zoom's own commit, the write and the library's push/report round trip finish in one synchronous chain (commit-phase updates flush before control returns to the event loop), so no input or passive effect can interleave a second write; the layout already has the new zoom's widths (the library's own layout effects, children of the pane, run first), which keeps B-116's reason for using an effect at all. The library's echo is not patched: it only diverges when two writers race, and the pane was the only writer that could. Also new: `packages/editor/vitest.config.ts` compiles the package's `.tsx` with the app's React Compiler preset (the B-282 precedent from `packages/motion`), so every editor DOM test runs the component the app ships.
- **verification:** WebKit harness after the fix: **0 of 15 runs**. `packages/editor/src/TimelinePane.zoomScrollLoop.dom.test.tsx` (compiled, a real scheduler, the real `TimelinePane` with 64 linked pairs): a second zoom-in is issued where a real input can arrive relative to the pane's write (between a passive write and its render; at the next task after a commit-phase write); before the fix it fails with "Maximum update depth exceeded", after it passes. Editor suite green, compiled (2413 tests at this commit; TimelinePane's zoom tests included); tsc editor 3 (baseline). **Not verified live:** after the merge, pinch-zoom hard in and out on a long timeline while thumbnails load; the window must stay up and `app.log` must show no "Maximum update depth".

## B-290 — an audio-only timeline cannot be previewed or heard ("preview error: timeline has no video track")

status: **fixed** (2026-10-28) · severity: **major** (a voiceover- or podcast-first edit has no playback until a picture clip exists) · area: the Edit preview/playback path (compositor preview + audio monitor), and export (the same audio-only limit was hit earlier this week on Black October and worked around with a still)

- **found:** 2026-10-28 by the owner: timeline "Five Levels — Voiceover" holds only an audio track (the cut VO, 164 clips); the viewer shows "preview error: timeline has no video track" and pressing play gives no sound. Screenshot: `scratch/bug-refs/audio-only-timeline-no-playback.png`.
- **expected:** an audio-only timeline plays its audio in sync with the playhead over a black frame at the timeline's size, and exports (audio with a black picture, or an audio-only file on request).
- **cause:** two refusals in `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/edit.rs`, both `"timeline has no video track"`, both left from D-041's single-track MVP. (1) `render_timeline_frame` refused before resolving any layer, so `chroma_timeline_frame` errored at every position (the viewer's "preview error") and the compositor export (`renderer: "compositor"`) failed at frame 0. (2) `resolve_video_position`, the embedded-audio lookup, refused too, and `chroma::audio::resolve_sources_at` calls it before it resolves the audio tracks, so `chroma_audio_play` returned that error (the frontend only logs it) and no session started: silence. The frontend was not at fault: the play loop is wall-clock (D-049), not driven by decoded frames, so the playhead ran; and the default filter export already wrote audio-only timelines as black + mix (D-197). Two smaller defects on the same path: "nothing visible" was a 1×1 JPEG (an `object-contain` `<img>` shows one pixel, so there was no frame to play over), and a caption over a position with no video layer was never drawn by the preview or the compositor export.
- **fix (D-419):** both refusals removed: no video track is the same answer as a gap ("nothing visible", "no embedded audio here"), and the audio-track clips resolve and play as they always did. The preview's nothing-visible frame is opaque black at the composition's preview canvas (the timeline's own output size, D-411, else the project's; `black_frame_jpeg`, memoised on its size), the 1×1 frame kept only for a timeline with no size at all. A visible caption over no video layer is drawn over that black (`captions_over_black`), matching the filter export. `preview_canvas_size` is now the one definition of the preview canvas (shared with `composite_video_frame`). Gaps in ordinary timelines preview as black at frame size too. An audio-only FILE export was scoped and deferred (D-419, roadmap 0m): the export of such a timeline is a video, black picture + mix.
- **verification:** Rust, each failing before the fix (refusals temporarily restored: 4 failed) and passing after: `chroma::edit::audio_only_preview_tests::an_audio_only_timeline_renders_nothing_visible_rather_than_failing`, `…::a_caption_over_an_audio_only_timeline_is_drawn_over_black`, `chroma::audio::tests::resolve_sources_at_a_timeline_with_no_video_track_plays_its_audio`, and `chroma::edit_render::parity_tests::an_audio_only_timeline_exports_a_black_picture_and_its_sound` (a real compositor export: ffprobe finds one 160×90 video stream, one audio stream, 2.0 s, 48 frames, black pixels). New-behaviour tests `nothing_visible_previews_as_black_at_the_timelines_own_size` (a 9:16 output previews 540×960 black) and `the_black_frame_takes_the_project_size_and_degrades_without_one`; `track_resolution_opaque_top_wins_across_two_video_tracks` updated (past the end is now black at the composition, not 1×1). TS: `packages/editor/src/PreviewPane.audioOnly.dom.test.tsx` (the real `PreviewPane`: the frame is shown with no error; Play sends `chroma_audio_play` from the playhead, the playhead advances, Pause stops; passes before and after, it guards the frontend half) and a real-ffmpeg filter-export test in `timelineExport.ffmpeg.test.ts` (320×180 black video + audio, 4 s). `cargo test -p apelles --lib`: 470 passed, 5 ignored (one earlier full run had `audio_keeps_playing_across_ripple_cut_boundaries`, a real audio-device timing test whose fixture has a video track, silent for its first 4 s under load; it passes alone and in the rerun). `cargo test -p apelles-mcp --test parity --test http_transport` green on this branch. clippy clean on the changed code; tsc editor 3, app 65 (baselines). **Not verified live** (the running app serves main's code): see the CHANGELOG line for the check.

## B-289 — `editor_detect_silences` marks soft sentence endings and the first word as silence, so cutting its ranges clips real words

status: **open** · severity: **major** (a straight "cut the silences" pass silently removes speech) · area: `editor_detect_silences` (Silero VAD, D-319/D-342) and its consumers

- **found:** 2026-10-28 editing the "Five Levels" voiceover. A 350 ms sweep returned 134 silences; cutting them (each shortened by 3 frames a side) removed the first word ("Two weeks ago") and the trailing word of many sentences ("…where you are *at*", "that's *great*", "amnesia every *morning*", "your *signal*", "lives in a *file*"). The VAD's silence starts inside quiet, trailing-off words. Undone (one undo step).
- **workaround used:** each VAD silence was intersected with the word transcript so no cut overlaps a word (+3 frames); every word survived (1355/1355) but only 41.7 s was removed instead of 92.7 s.
- **expected:** the silence tool (or the roadmap 0l cut-words op) is word-aware when a transcript exists, so its ranges never overlap speech; a VAD-only answer says so.

## B-288 — `editor_ripple_delete_ranges` refused one valid range in a 30-range batch ("describes no real material")

status: **open** · severity: **minor** (it reports the skip honestly; the same range applied alone a moment later) · area: `editor_ripple_delete_ranges` / `applyRippleDeleteRanges`

- **found:** 2026-10-28. In a batch of 30 retake cuts on one audio track (two clips, 0..17219 frames), the range 11092..11462 (wholly inside clip 1) was skipped: "nothing on track 0 lies wholly inside frames 11092..11462"; the other 29 applied. Re-sent alone at its shifted position (9193..9563, wholly inside one clip) it applied fine. Suspect: back-to-front application with neighbouring ranges in the same clip (10950..11003 and 11715..11734) validates a range against clips already split by a later range.
- **expected:** every range wholly inside material is cut in one batch.

## B-287 — whole-file transcription silently dropped ~1.5 minutes of speech in 8 places

status: **open** · severity: **major** (the retake/cut tools then can't see that speech; a cut built on the transcript can remove it) · area: the Parakeet transcription job (`/transcribe`, D-381) that `editor_get_word_transcript(start=true)` runs

- **found:** 2026-10-28, two voiceover files (2:30 and 9:28 m4a, 48 kHz mono). The word view had 8 gaps of 6.5-37 s (e.g. 388.1→425.2 s) where the audio has continuous speech (ffmpeg silencedetect: no silence > 1.5 s there; a direct Parakeet run on the gap transcribed it fully). `editor_retranscribe_words` over each gap recovered every word (+203 words).
- **expected:** the full-file job never drops speech: windowing/segment merging must not lose a segment, and a stretch with audio energy but no words should be re-read or flagged.

## B-286 — a Motion VIDEO render is not bit-identical run to run (its PNG frames are)

status: **open** · severity: **low** (52 dB PSNR between runs: invisible, but CLAUDE.md's render-path invariant asks for identical pixels) · area: the Motion scene export (`scripts/render.mts video`, before D-417 `npx remotion render`)

- **found:** 2026-10-27, building D-417, comparing the old CLI export with the new renderer.
- **repro:** render `crates/apelles-motion/tests/fixtures/sample.json` frames 0-59 to `.mp4` twice (2x scale, 3840×2160, JPEG frames, H.264) and compare decoded frames (`ffmpeg -map 0:v -f framemd5`): 51 of 60 frames differ between two runs of the old `npx remotion render`, 47 of 60 between two runs of the D-417 renderer. Audio is identical. The same frames as a PNG sequence (`render.mts frames`, 0.25 scale) are identical across runs, as every still is (`preview_render.rs`).
- **cause:** not isolated. Pre-existing (the CLI path shows it too), so not the renderer change. Candidates: the JPEG frame encode at 4K in Chrome, or the encoder's threading.
- **fix:** none yet. First step: render the same frames as PNG at 2x scale twice, to split the browser from the encoder.

## B-284 — a new timeline ran at 24 fps whatever the project's rate was

status: **fixed** (2026-10-27) · severity: **medium** (a timeline created in a 30 fps project silently resolved every frame number at 24 fps until someone noticed the clip lengths) · area: `chroma::edit::chroma_timeline_create` (D-045), now `apelles_project::timeline::create_timeline`

- **found:** 2026-10-27, building D-411 Phase 0, reading the create path the Automatic Clipper's shorts will go through.
- **cause:** `chroma_timeline_create` built the new `Timeline` with `rate: None`, which every reader resolves as `DEFAULT_FPS` (24). B-097 fixed this exact gap at the two other creation sites (a new project, a timeline lazily built from shots) and did not reach this one.
- **fix:** `create_timeline` seeds the new timeline's rate from the ACTIVE timeline (what the person is working in, and for a short the long-form it is cut from).
- **verification:** `apelles-project` `create_seeds_the_active_rate_and_the_output_and_activates_on_request`.

## B-283 — undo after switching timelines wrote the other timeline's snapshot over the open one

status: **fixed** (2026-10-27) · severity: **high** (silent data loss: the open timeline's content, and its id, were replaced by another timeline's) · area: `packages/editor/src/timelineStore.ts` `restoreSnapshot` (D-051 undo, D-045 multi-timeline)

- **found:** 2026-10-27, building D-411 Phase 0 (timeline management for agents, which switch timelines constantly), by reading the undo path against `chroma_timeline_set`'s contract.
- **repro:** edit timeline A (any undoable op), switch to timeline B, press ⌘Z. **Expected:** A's edit is undone. **Actual:** the history entry's `undo` restored A's `before` snapshot into the store and `chroma_timeline_set` wrote it onto the ACTIVE timeline, B — B now held A's content and A's id, and A was unchanged.
- **cause:** the shared undo stack (D-051) is not per timeline, its entries close over whole-`Timeline` snapshots, and `chroma_timeline_set` writes to whichever timeline is active, never by id.
- **fix:** `restoreSnapshot` compares the snapshot's id with the open timeline's; when they differ it switches to the snapshot's timeline first (Premiere's behaviour: undo brings its sequence forward) and then restores, and refuses in words if that timeline was deleted.
- **verification:** `timelineOps.e2e.dom.test.tsx` "B-283: an undo made after a switch lands on its own timeline, not the open one".

## B-282 — the Motion player never shows a custom layer's proxy frames: it stays on "rendering preview…" after they exist

status: **fixed** (2026-10-27) · severity: **high** (every custom component layer in the live player was a placeholder box, so an agent or a human could not see what they had placed) · area: `packages/motion/src/customProxy.tsx` (D-409's live-player renderer), the React Compiler (D-091)

- **found:** 2026-10-27, live in the dev app, project "Fix check (scratch)": `ripple-rings@1` added with `motion_add_layer(use:"custom:ripple-rings")`, `motion_validate` clean, `motion_preview_frame` drew it, and the proxy was on disk (`<project>/motion/cache/proxy/0cb7ec65e376a06e/`: `done.json`, 90 PNGs), but the player kept drawing the placeholder, also after `motion_seek`. Reproduced again over the bridge: the layer's status line read `rendering preview…` (via `debug_dom_tree`) while `ed7c0863d4a0d99e/done.json` (90 frames, absolute paths) had been written at 14:36:21; nothing in the Tauri log.
- **cause:** the app compiles every component with the React Compiler, which memoizes what a render reads by its inputs. `useProxyFrames` returned `states.get(key)` straight off a module-level `Map`, and the compiler cached that read on `key` alone. When the render finished, the drain set the state to `ready` and bumped the component, but `key` had not changed, so the re-render returned the cached `pending`. Evidence: the module the running dev server serves (`/@fs/…/customProxy.tsx`) contains `if ($[8] !== key) { t2 = states.get(key) ?? { status: "pending" }; … } else { t2 = $[9]; }`; the same old code under the same Player passes a DOM test uncompiled and fails it compiled. The Rust side (`render_proxy`, the result shape, the asset-protocol scope) was correct. Found with it: the debounce timer belonged to the viewer that started it, so if that layer unmounted first, a second identical layer (same component, props and size) was left `pending` with nothing queued.
- **fix:** the request/queue/cache state moved to `customProxyStore.ts`, an external store with a subscribe/snapshot contract, read only through `useSyncExternalStore` (React calls `get` itself on every render and notification, which the compiler cannot skip). The timer belongs to the key. A failed render, a render with no frames, and a frame the webview cannot load (`<img onError>`, e.g. a scope problem) become `preview failed: …` on the layer and a `console.error`, which the app forwards to its log; the status line carries `data-custom-proxy-status` and is sized to stay readable in the scaled player. The debug-only `debug_get_ui_state` reports every proxy (`motion.customProxies`). D-409 amended.
- **verification:** `customProxy.dom.test.tsx` (4: the real `<Player>` + engine `Video` + `CustomProxyProvider`, compiled with the app's React Compiler preset through `packages/motion/vitest.config.ts`, Tauri `invoke` stubbed: waiting → rendering → the frame's `<img>`; a rejected render shows and reports its error; a render with no frames is an error; a frame load error is an error). Before the fix, the first test failed under the compiler and passed without it. `customProxyStore.test.ts` (10: debounce, dropped mid-edit keys, the stranded second viewer, StrictMode, a late render served from cache, one at a time, error report and retry, no frames, frame failure, the debug snapshot); `debugOps.motion.test.ts` (1). Motion suite 1000/1000 (986 + 14), debug 53/53, engine 218/218, `cargo test -p apelles-mcp --test parity` green (217 tools, corpus re-captured for the `debug_ui_state` description); tsc motion 0, motion-engine 0, debug 0, editor 3, app 65 (baselines). **Not yet verified live:** the running app serves main's code; after the merge, a custom layer should show its frames once `debug_ui_state` reports `status: "ready"`.

## B-281 — a Motion render of a document that does not set `grain`/`vignette` gets film grain and a vignette the live preview does not show

status: **fixed** (2026-10-27, owner: "yes both should be exact") · severity: medium · area: motion engine (render vs. preview)

- **Repro.** Render (`remotion render` / `still`, i.e. export or `motion_preview_frame`) any manifest with no top-level `grain` or `vignette` key; compare with the live player. Found 2026-10-27 (D-409) when a transparent proxy render came back with a dark radial edge (alpha up to 63) and noise.
- **Expected.** Absent means off, in both runtimes (the schema's own doc: `.optional()`, not `.default()`).
- **Actual.** The render has the engine sample's `grain: true` and `vignette: 0.35`.
- **Cause.** `Root.tsx` registers the `Animation` composition with `defaultProps={sample}`, and Remotion merges a render's input props OVER `defaultProps`, so every key a manifest leaves out is taken from the sample. The player is handed the manifest directly and does not merge.
- **Fix.** The reference is the live player (`Video.tsx` reads `manifest.grain ?? false`, `vignette ?? false`), so absent means off everywhere. `Animation`'s `defaultProps` is now `animationDefaultProps` (`engine/build.ts`): `title: ""`, the schema's own size/fps defaults and one placeholder scene (needed so the Studio's `calculateMetadata` parses), and no look setting. The engine sample moved to a separate `AnimationSample` composition for the Studio. Fields that could leak this way: `grain` and `vignette` were the only ones the sample set that a manifest may omit; `theme`, `themeDef`, `transparent` and `components` were not in the sample, `title` and `scenes` are required (always supplied), `width`/`height`/`fps` equal the schema's own defaults.
- **Verification.** `packages/motion-engine/src/Root.test.tsx` (5): the `Animation` composition's defaults are `animationDefaultProps` and not the sample; every optional manifest key is absent from them unless it equals what the schema itself supplies (so a future optional field that leaks from the defaults fails it); merging a bare and a fully-optioned manifest over the defaults gives exactly `parseManifest(input)`; the sample is still available as `AnimationSample`. Real renders: a brand-scene still before/after: corner pixels were `(14,15,20)` with noise, now the flat background `(11,13,18)`, card pixels unchanged to ±1. `preview_render.rs` and `component_render.rs --ignored` (10) pass, and a second run gives the same hashes. **Hashes superseded** (old → new, first 8): logo-reveal `a5f8643b`→`d74f47cf`, feature-callout `4f602990`→`3455d68f`, stat-counter `a6ed741f`→`70a85a1b`, testimonial `763a5de1`→`46f5b368`, pricing-card `181de97b`→`a0675f2b`, cta-end-card `a59c25f0`→`15255876`, stat-counter contact sheet `7b6dc200`→`e44837e4`, image `9038cbd4`→`1278c84e`, icon `7dcae9a5`→`642838c7`, shape `9e7a8345`→`d219f5e7`, counter `91819d80`→`1427cbc1`, group `f5c3492c`→`72d3a415`, brand-scene sheet `02a7e2c8`→`3b4858f5`, D-409 agent-built sheet `3793ddd7`→`89202915`. Unchanged: sample frame 60 `1142adab`, sample sheet `f47b03d1` (the sample sets both keys), D-409's per-component proof hashes (its proof documents set `grain: false, vignette: false`). The old hashes were of renders carrying grain and a vignette the player never showed, so they were not worth keeping. **Effect on users:** an existing project's export that never set `grain`/`vignette` stops having them; one that wants them sets the keys.

## B-280 — in dev, a hot update leaves the control bridge running the old op code

status: **fixed** (2026-10-27) · severity: **minor** (dev builds only; but a live check silently tests the old code, and once applied an edit the new code would refuse) · area: the bridge subscription in `packages/editor/src/useEditorControl.ts` and the other three registries (`useMotionControl`, `useDebugControl`, `app/src/hooks/useChromaControl.ts`), React Fast Refresh under `<React.StrictMode>`

- **found:** 2026-10-27, live-verifying D-408 / B-279. After merging D-408, Vite logged the HMR updates but the bridge answered `unknown editor op: editor_music_edit` until a full page reload. After the B-279 fix, the HMR'd page again ran the old pre-flight and cut the voice; after a full reload the same call was refused.
- **cause (confirmed by reproduction):** each registry builds its op table inside a `useEffect(…, [])` and the server targets the newest announced subscription (B-272). A hot update re-evaluates the registry module and the op modules it imports, and Fast Refresh re-renders the calling tab (it is a refresh boundary), but the effect never re-ran, so the OLD subscription, holding the old module's op table, stayed the one the server addressed. Why the effect did not re-run: React 19.2's dev Fast Refresh re-runs effects by ignoring their previous dependencies on the first render of a hot-swapped component (`ignorePreviousDependencies`), but StrictMode's second render (`renderWithHooksAgain` in `react-dom-client.development.js`) clears that flag and rebuilds the effect list, so `[]` compares equal and no effect is scheduled. Reproduced in a minimal Vite 8 + plugin-react 6 + React Compiler app shaped like the real one (`scratch/b280-repro/`, a headless Chrome driven over CDP): with `<StrictMode>`, editing the hook module or a pure op module re-rendered the tab (DOM updated, render counter up) but the registry kept the v1 subscription; without `<StrictMode>`, the same edit re-subscribed with v2. Today's `app.log` agrees: a `frontend bridge ready` handshake appears only on full reloads.
- **options:** (a) op modules decline HMR (`import.meta.hot.invalidate()`), turning every edit to `timeline.ts` and friends into a full reload, acceptable only with B-277's restore and still a slow dev loop; (b) drop StrictMode, which would hide the effect bugs it exists to catch (D-098); (c) make the subscription depend on the module evaluation. **Chosen: (c).** It keeps hot updates and fixes the real cause.
- **fix:** each registry declares a module-level `REGISTRY_EVALUATION = Symbol(…)` and lists it as the subscribing effect's one dependency. Within one module instance it never changes (one subscription, as before); a hot update to the registry or anything it imports mints a new one, so StrictMode's second render sees changed dependencies: the old subscription is released and a fresh claim (new `instance`, B-272) is announced with the new op table, which the server then targets. The rule is documented in `@apelles/bridge`'s `controlBridge.ts`.
- **verification:** `packages/editor/src/bridgeHotUpdate.dom.test.tsx` (2, StrictMode, the real `useEditorControl` and timeline store): `vi.resetModules()` + re-import is the hot update; re-rendering the same mounted component with the re-evaluated hook re-subscribes (new target instance), leaves exactly one live listener, and an `editor_add_marker` lands once, in the NEW evaluation's store (the old store untouched), across two successive updates; a plain re-render within one evaluation keeps the same subscription and announces nothing. With the dependency reverted to `[]` the first test fails (same target instance). In the repro app, the same pattern under StrictMode re-subscribed on a hook edit and on a pure op-module edit, one live subscription each time. Not yet observed in the running app (it runs main's code).

## B-279 — a D-408 music edit aimed at the voice track cut the voice

status: **fixed** (2026-10-27, live-verifying D-408) · severity: **major** (a mistyped `track` silently cut words out of the voiceover; undo recovered it) · area: `packages/editor/src/timeline.ts` (`checkMusicEdit`), `packages/editor/src/musicEditOps.ts` (`wordContext`)

- **found:** 2026-10-27, smoke-testing D-408 over the bridge in a scratch project. `editor_music_edit(track=2, start_frame=10, end_frame=20)` on the VO track was applied: the voice clip split and frames 10..20 were removed. The checks only refused non-audio, locked, A/V-linked and empty ranges, so any audio track counted as a bed.
- **fix:** the reducer's pre-flight (used by the GUI and both MCP servers) refuses a track that another track ducks under, naming it as the voice; a word-anchored edit refuses when `track` equals `word_track`, since the words come from the voice.
- **still possible, by design:** a voice track that nothing ducks under, addressed by frames, cannot be told from a bed (the timeline does not mark a track as voice). The `apelles-sound-design` skill always sets ducking on the bed, which arms the guard.
- **verification:** unit test (ducked voice refused, its bed allowed) and an op-layer test (`track == word_track` refused); editor suite 2362/2362; `tsc` editor 3 (baseline).

## B-278 — two `remotion` runs at once could collide: a shared default port, and bundle pruning that deleted a bundle still in use

status: **fixed** (2026-10-27, before D-403's merge) · severity: **major** (a preview could fail mid-run, or with two valid bundles on one port render another composition without any error) · area: `crates/apelles-motion/src/{lib,still}.rs`

- **found:** 2026-10-27, validating D-403/D-405. The real-render determinism tests (`preview_render`, `--ignored`) passed one at a time but 2 of 4 failed when run in parallel, with a 404 for the other bundle's `index.html` and then `EISDIR`.
- **cause 1:** `remotion render` / `still` serve the bundle over local HTTP and, without `--port`, search for a free port from 3000. That search is not atomic across processes, so two runs started together could share a port and load each other's bundle.
- **cause 2:** `ensure_bundle` deleted every other `bundle-*` directory after building a new one. A concurrent preview with a different fingerprint (another asset folder, or engine code changed in between) lost its bundle mid-run.
- **fix:** every `remotion` render and still gets its own OS-assigned port (`with_own_port`), with one retry on a fresh port if `remotion` still reports `EADDRINUSE` (`output_with_own_port`); a second clash is an error, never a render of something else. Bundles are marked on each use, and only those unused for 10 minutes are pruned (`BUNDLE_STALE_AFTER`).
- **verification:** `preview_render` 4/4 in parallel, three runs in a row (each render twice, matching SHA-256); unit tests for the port flag and the `EADDRINUSE` detection; `apelles-motion` lib 28/28; clippy clean.

## B-277 — after the web content process is killed, the reloaded app opens no project, so the recovered edits only appear once the user reopens it

status: **fixed** (2026-10-27, D-410) · severity: **major** (nothing is lost — D-402 replays the journal — but the user lands with no project open and can reasonably think the work is gone) · area: the page's start-up (`app/src/Root.tsx`, `app/src/utils/pageSessionRestore.ts`), `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/page_session.rs`

- **found:** 2026-10-26, live-verifying B-274. 3 `editor_set_clip_audio` edits, then `kill -9` of the WebKit content process. The app logged the termination at `warn`, reloaded and raised the notice, but came back with no project open (`editor_get_timeline`: "no timeline — open a project first"). The 3 edits replayed (volume 0.3, saved; the journal emptied) only after `open_project`.
- **also seen:** 2026-10-27, a plain dev page reload (Vite full reload after `main.tsx` changed) also lands with no project open; the journal again restored the unsaved bed clip once the project was reopened. Same start-up restore gap.
- **cause:** the page always started on the launcher (`useSessionStore` starts empty, and nothing at start-up asked the backend). The backend did know: `state::current_project()` survives a page reload (it is cleared only by "‹ Projects" or a new open), but no page start read it. The active tab was not kept anywhere outside the page.
- **fix (D-410):** `chroma::page_session` keeps the active tab in process memory (`chroma_page_session_set_tab`, reported by `Root.tsx` on every switch, only after this page's restore has read the previous one) and answers `chroma_page_session_get` → `{project, activeTab}` from it and `current_project()`. Once per page load, `restorePageSession` shows the remembered tab and reopens the project through `useSessionStore.openProject` (the launcher's action), so the existing identity bridge loads the Edit timeline and its first load replays the journal, raising "Restored N Edit timeline changes". A cold launch has nothing in memory and opens the launcher as before. A project moved or deleted meanwhile: the open fails, the backend binding is cleared (unless another open won the race) and a persistent error names the project and says to open it from the launcher. A page that already has a project open is never replaced. Not covered: an in-memory "Untitled" session, and Motion's unsaved manifest text (not journaled by D-402; roadmap follow-up).
- **verification:** `app/src/utils/pageSessionRestore.test.ts` (11: cold launch, closed project, reopen on the remembered tab, an unavailable tab, an already-open project, deleted project → reason + backend cleared + tab kept, a lost race does not close the winner, an unreachable backend, once per page load, tab reporting and its failure). `app/src/utils/pageSessionReload.test.ts` (3, through the real `useSessionStore` and the real Edit timeline store over a fake backend that outlives the page): a reload reopens the project on the Colorist tab and replays two journalled volume edits at once (`recoveredEdits` 2, volume 0.3); a cold launch opens nothing; a deleted project falls back to the launcher, is forgotten, and the next reload does not retry. Rust `chroma::page_session` (2). Not yet observed in the running app (it runs main's code).

## B-276 — a new project with no explicit frame size refuses `editor_export`: "no clip to derive a composition size from", even with a still on a video track

status: **fixed** (2026-10-26; not reproduced live) · severity: **major** (a fresh project cannot be exported until `set_project_settings` gives it a size, and the message points at the clips, not the missing setting) · area: `editor_export`'s composition-size resolution (`app/src-tauri/src/chroma/edit_render.rs` / the export request builder)

- **found:** 2026-10-26, live-verifying D-401. `new_project` → a 30 s VO clip, a music clip, a PNG still on a video track (its `boxWidth`/`boxHeight` were `null`) → `editor_export(renderer="compositor")` answered "no clip to derive a composition size from". It went away after `set_project_settings(width=1920, height=1080, fps=24)`.
- **expected:** a still's own pixel size (or the export's `width`/`height`) is enough to size the composition. A truly sizeless project gets a named error that says to set the project size, never a message that blames clips which are there.
- **cause (from the code):** two independent gaps, both on the compositor path. (1) `chroma::edit::composition_size` already counts a still's own pixel size (D-292, `composition_size_falls_back_to_a_still_when_no_real_video_exists`), but it reads the **persisted** `project.json`, and so does the compositor render (`chroma_render_timeline_export`). Edits persist ~400 ms after `applyOp` changes the store, and `runEditorExport` never settled that save, so an agent that placed the still and exported in the same breath had its export sized (and rendered) from the document as it was before the still: on a fresh project, an empty video track. The `boxWidth`/`boxHeight` nulls were a red herring (they are only a box override, `null` by default). (2) Even with nothing to size from, an export always has its own `width`/`height`, and the export compiler already reads a sizeless project's composition as exactly that (`compositionSizeSnapshot() ?? { width, height }`); the Rust render did not, and refused.
- **fix:** (1) `editorExport.ts`'s `flushTimelineForBackend` awaits `flushPendingSave()` at the start of `runEditorExport` and again in `runCompiledExport` before the compositor render (a queued job runs long after its enqueue); a failed save refuses the export with a named reason rather than exporting a document other than the one on screen. The Export dialog flushes before its enqueue-time `warmCompositionSize`. (2) `derived_composition_size` (new, `edit.rs`) answers `Ok(None)` for a sizeless project; `render_timeline` stands the requested output size in, the same reading the compiler takes, so both engines size every clip against the same composition. (3) `composition_size` turns `None` into `NO_COMPOSITION_SIZE`, which says the project has no frame size and to set one with `set_project_settings` (or put footage or a still on a video track), for the preview, clip geometry and `chroma_timeline_composition_size`.
- **verification:** Rust (`cargo test -p apelles --lib -- composition_size a_sizeless`, 5/5) `a_sizeless_project_is_refused_by_name` (named error, `derived_composition_size` is `None`), `a_sizeless_project_exports_at_the_requested_size` (a VO-only project with no settings renders 3 frames at the requested 64x36 through the real ffmpeg pipe), and the existing `composition_size_falls_back_to_a_still_when_no_real_video_exists` (a still's own size, unchanged) all pass. `editorExportFlush.test.ts` (3): a still placed and exported straight away is saved before the composition size and the render are read, and sizes the composition; a failed save refuses the export without rendering; nothing pending sends nothing. Editor vitest 2302/2302, `tsc` baseline only, clippy adds nothing in the touched files. Not reproduced or re-checked live against the running app.
- **left alone, found on the way:** a timeline with NO video track at all (not an empty one, which a new project has) still fails the compositor at its first frame with "timeline has no video track" (`resolve_video_position`'s own refusal). That is the frame resolver's rule, not composition sizing; an audio-only export through the compositor needs its own decision. **Taken by D-419 (B-290, 2026-10-28):** the refusal is gone and such a timeline exports as black + its sound.

## B-275 — `editor_search_audio` gave up on a slow Openverse after 30 s and reported it as "could not reach"

status: **fixed** (2026-10-26) · severity: **major** (the D-400 tools failed outright whenever Openverse was slow; the message pointed at the network) · area: `crates/apelles-audio-library/src/client.rs`

- **found:** 2026-10-26, live-checking D-400 after the merge. `curl` measured Openverse's audio search at 34 s for one query, against a 30 s total-request timeout. The error read "could not reach Openverse: error sending request". The same total timeout also capped downloads, so a large music bed on a slow link would have failed partway.
- **fix:** a 15 s connect timeout plus a 90 s idle timeout (no bytes arriving), with no cap on total time, for search and download alike. `send_error` names a timeout as a slow server ("sent nothing for 90 s … try again") or a failed connect, rather than "could not reach".
- **verification:** crate tests 18/18, clippy clean; live `editor_search_audio` after the dev rebuild (see the CHANGELOG line).

## B-274 — the Edit webview's memory grows to ~18 GB under a burst of edits, macOS kills it, and the reload silently drops unsaved edits

status: **fixed in code (2026-10-26): the main allocation, the silent reload, edit durability (D-402) and native termination handling; live confirmation remains** · severity: **critical** (performance and data loss: edits made since the last save vanish with no message) · area: the Edit tab's frontend memory (audio decode/waveform caches, image/still caches, undo history snapshots), `WKWebView` reload handling, project autosave

- **found:** 2026-10-26, Black October project (~490 clips, 14 tracks, 7 audio lanes including 803 s and 580 s music beds). The owner saw Apelles at ~18 GB in Activity Monitor. The dev log shows the frontend re-handshaking at 13:44, 13:50 and 13:59 with no app restart (the Rust process stayed up from 13:30). Each time a new `WebKit.WebContent` process appeared, i.e. the web content process was replaced. Each reload landed during a burst of a few hundred `editor_*` ops (SFX placement, per-clip volume changes).
- **data loss seen:** 62 `editor_set_clip_audio` volume changes all read back correctly. Minutes later 39 had reverted with no undo on the stack: the reload restored `project.json` from before them. Likely also behind the doubled-op handshakes in B-272.
- **expected:** memory stays bounded and is released (decoded audio and stills cached once per source with an LRU cap, not per clip or per edit; undo snapshots structurally shared or capped). A web content process termination is detected (`webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate`) and surfaced, never a silent reload. Unsaved edits are flushed or journaled so a reload loses nothing.
- **to measure first:** Safari Web Inspector memory timeline / heap snapshots before and after a burst of 200 `editor_set_clip_audio` calls; which allocations grow (AudioBuffers, ImageBitmaps, history entries).
- **investigated (2026-10-26, from the code; no running app, so no heap snapshot):**
  - **Undo history is NOT the 18 GB.** 200 `set_clip_audio` ops through the real store on a 482-clip timeline (7 audio lanes, 803 s and 580 s beds) cost 0.25 ms/op and leave the shared history at its cap of 100 (`editBurst.test.ts`). A snapshot per op is still a snapshot per op (100 retained timelines); structural sharing would shrink it but is not the cause here.
  - **The waveform peak cache is bounded** (200 entries, then cleared; ~6 MB at most).
  - **The unbounded allocation was the waveform `<canvas>`.** `Waveform` sized its canvas to the WHOLE clip: `width x devicePixelRatio`. An 803 s bed at the default 100 px/s is 80,300 css px, 160,600 device px, about 67 MB for one clip, growing with zoom (an SFX pass zooms in), with seven audio lanes and a redraw on every edit (assigning `canvas.width` reallocates the backing store). The timeline library mounts every clip of a row regardless of horizontal scroll and the D-334 gate only avoids the peaks FETCH, not the canvas for a clip that is partly visible.
- **fixed:** (1) `waveformWindow.ts` / `Waveform.tsx`: the canvas backs only the visible span plus a 256 px margin, quantised to 256 px, and never wider than 4096 css px (`MAX_WAVEFORM_CANVAS_PX`); only the peak buckets inside that span are drawn. `waveformWindow.test.ts` (6) checks an 803 s clip at 500 px/s gets a viewport-sized canvas and the visible slice stays covered at every scroll position. (2) A web content process termination is no longer silent: `@apelles/bridge`'s `pageLifecycle` marks the page `running` in `sessionStorage` and flips it to `unloading` on `pagehide`; a page that starts and finds `running` was preceded by one that never said goodbye, so `Root.tsx` logs `webview_restarted_unexpectedly` and shows a persistent warning toast. A deliberate reload (dev full reload) fires `pagehide` and is not reported. (3) The 39-of-62 revert had a second, independent cause, fixed under B-272: `load()` overwrote unsaved edits with the older backend copy.
- **fixed, second pass (D-402):** (4) **no edit is lost to a reload any more.** A write-ahead journal: every `applyOp` (and every undo/redo, as the snapshot it restores) is appended to `<project>/edit-journal.jsonl` through `chroma_edit_journal_append` the moment it is made; the debounced save records the last included entry as `ProjectManifest.edit_journal_seq` in the same atomic write as the timeline, then compacts. A page's first load replays the entries after that number through the same pure reducer, saves, and toasts "Restored N Edit timeline changes". Options and why this one: D-402. (5) **the termination is handled natively.** The earlier note here was wrong: no patch was needed. Tauri 2.11.5 exposes WebKit's `webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate` as `Builder::on_web_content_process_terminate` (wry 0.55.1's `with_on_web_content_process_terminate_handler` underneath); without a hook of ours `tauri-runtime-wry` installs one that logs at `debug` and reloads. `chroma::webview_lifecycle` now logs it at `warn`, records it and reloads deliberately; the reloaded page reads it once through `chroma_webview_take_termination` and `Root.tsx` says so (the `pagehide` marker stays as the fallback). (c), a debug-only memory reading tool, was not built: optional, and the journal makes the loss itself impossible regardless of what the memory does.
- **verification (second pass):** `editJournal.test.ts` (10): `replayJournal` (sequence order, saved-sequence cut, other timelines ignored, snapshots, refused ops counted, malformed lines rejected), and the incident simulated through the real store against a fake backend that keeps `project.json` + the journal the way Rust does: three edits made, the page "killed" inside the debounce (module state discarded, timer never fired, nothing saved) and a fresh page loads the identical timeline with `recoveredEdits` 3, then saves it and empties the journal; a reload after a save replays nothing; numbering continues across two crashes; an undo replays as its snapshot. Rust: `apelles_project::journal` (4: round trip, seq required, torn last line dropped, compaction), `chroma::edit_journal` (3: sequence recorded and never backwards, an unjournalled save supersedes, no journal records nothing), `chroma::webview_lifecycle` (1), and the existing `chroma::project` command tests through the changed `chroma_timeline_set` (19/19 in that filter); `apelles-project` 75/75. `@apelles/bridge` 30/30 (`webviewTermination.test.ts` new); editor vitest all green; `tsc`: no errors in any touched file.
- **not verified:** no real web content process has been killed under this build, so the WebKit hook, the reload it performs and the toast are unexercised live (`kill -9` on the `WebKit.WebContent` process of a dev build is the check: expect a `warn` line in `app.log`, the toast, and the timeline intact). `sessionStorage` surviving a web process replacement is still unconfirmed (it is now only the fallback). Whether the canvas fix alone brings the Black October session's memory under control still needs the original heap measurement (Web Inspector memory timeline across 200 ops) on the running app.

## B-273 — `editor_add_clip` without a `track` fails with "no track NaN" (its own error text says to do exactly that)

status: **fixed** (2026-10-26) · severity: **major** (an agent cannot get a fresh track for a clip in one call; an `editor_add_track` made first can be pruned as empty before the clip lands, B-259's shape) · area: `editor_add_clip` handler in `packages/editor/src/useEditorControl.ts` (the B-259 fix, D-398 branch)

- **found:** 2026-10-26, placing SFX on the Black October timeline. `editor_add_clip(sourcePath, sourceStart, duration, startFrame)` with no `track` answered `no track NaN — … or add the clip without a track to get a new one`.
- **expected:** with `track` omitted, a new track of the kind the source needs is appended and the clip lands on it, as the error text and the docstring promise; `track` validated only when given.
- **cause:** the handler coerced `track` with `Math.round(Number(a.track))` unconditionally, so an omitted track became `NaN` and `checkAddClip` refused it with the message that told the caller to omit it. Neither MCP server let a caller omit it anyway: `track` was a required parameter in `mcp/server.py` and `crates/apelles-mcp`, and neither docstring mentioned the new-track behaviour (only the error text did).
- **fix:** the `add_clip` op's `onNewVideoTrack: boolean` became `onNewTrack?: 'video' | 'audio'` (`timeline.ts`). `'video'` is unchanged (a new video track at index 0, the top, as titles and adjustment clips already use, D-262); `'audio'` appends a new audio track at the bottom, where `add_track` and `ensureAudioTrackWithRoom` put audio, and refuses picture as a no-op. Either way it is one op, so one Undo removes the clip and the track. On an empty timeline it now makes exactly one track (the old video path made the B-259 first track and then a second, empty one). `editor_add_clip` validates `track` only when given (a non-index is refused by name, never as `NaN`); omitted or null, it picks `'audio'` for an audio-only source (probed 0x0, the B-259 test) and `'video'` for footage or a still, and reports where the clip really landed (`track`), `createdTrack` and `trackCount`, the shape `editor_add_text_clip` already returns. Both MCP servers make `track` optional and document the behaviour; the parity corpus was re-captured.
- **verification:** `addClipNewTrack.dom.test.tsx` (7, through the real `chroma://request` path into the real store: omitted track with an audio source lands on a new bottom audio track with one undo entry that removes both; footage and a still land on a new top video track; `track: null` is omitted; a non-existent track is still refused with nothing changed; a non-numeric track is refused without `NaN`; a given track reports `createdTrack: false`). `timelineAddClipTrack.test.ts` +4 reducer cases. Editor vitest 2298/2298; `tsc` only the 3 baseline errors; `cargo test -p apelles-mcp --test parity` 5/5, clippy and fmt clean. Not verified live against the running app.

## B-272 — every control-bridge op is applied twice after dev reloads

status: **fixed** (2026-10-26) · severity: **critical** (an agent's edits silently double: one `editor_split_clip` makes two splits, one `editor_ripple_delete_ranges` of 44 frames removes 88, one `editor_add_marker` adds two markers) · area: the frontend control-bridge subscription (`chroma://op` listener / bridge registration in `@apelles/editor` / `app/src`), `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/control.rs`

- **found:** 2026-10-26, cutting a retake on the Black October timeline (a session with several full webview reloads, `touch app/index.html`). The dev log showed 7 `frontend bridge ready: prefix "editor_"` handshakes. A single `editor_add_marker` call then produced two markers with consecutive ids.
- **cause:** `chroma://request` is a Tauri broadcast and each op registry (`useEditorControl`, `useMotionControl`, `useDebugControl`, `useChromaControl`) subscribed with a plain `listen()`. A subscription whose `unlisten` did not run (`safeUnlisten` deliberately swallows the dev-mode HMR teardown race, so a failed release is invisible) stayed live next to its replacement, and both executed every op for the prefix. The server had no way to say which listener should run a request, and the handshake registry (keyed by prefix) only ever knew the latest one.
- **fixed:** one op, one executor, enforced on both sides. `@apelles/bridge`'s `newBridgeClaim(prefix, defers)` gives every subscription a fresh `instance` id, announced on `chroma://bridge-ready`. `control.rs` keeps the latest announcer per prefix and stamps every request with a `target` (the instance of the most specific claim serving the op). Each registry's handler returns immediately unless `isForMe(payload)`, so a leaked listener is inert however many are alive. The four copies of the claim constant became this one helper (Motion and Debug now depend on `@apelles/bridge`).
- **second mechanism, found from the coordinator's evidence (stale store snapshot):** after 62 separate `editor_set_clip_audio(volume=0.15)` calls all read back at 0.15, 39 were later back at 0.35 with an empty undo stack. Cause in `timelineStore.load()`: it replaced the in-memory timeline with the backend's copy unconditionally, while `applyOp` persists ~400 ms AFTER changing the store. A refetch landing in that window (window `focus`, the composition-root bridge, a retry) took the older copy, and the pending debounced save then persisted it, so recent edits were lost in memory and on disk. The same shape explains an index from `get_timeline` reported as "no clip N" by the next op. **Fix:** `load()` discards a fetched copy when the store owed the backend a write at any point between the request and its answer (a save pending on its timer or in flight at the start, a local edit/undo during the fetch, or a timer pending at the end); a first load with no timeline in the store always lands, and an undo's own reconcile refetch still lands (it exempts the save it just finished). Tests: `timelineStore.test.ts` "a refetch never replaces a newer local edit with an older backend copy (B-272)" (4; the first two fail with the guard removed, checked). Not reproduced live; B-274 (the web process being killed and reloaded from `project.json`) is the other route to the same loss.
- **verification:** `controlBridge.test.ts` (two live registrations, an op addressed to the second executes exactly once; distinct instances; untargeted requests from direct handler tests accepted); Rust `a_second_registration_of_a_prefix_becomes_the_only_target` and `a_claim_without_an_instance_names_no_target` (`chroma::control` 12/12); vitest bridge/editor/motion 3279 pass and debug 52/52 from its package dir; tsc unchanged (editor's 3 baseline errors; bridge's one `import.meta.hot` error is pre-existing in `@apelles/store`). Not verified live in the running app: a real reload cycle with a leaked listener.

## B-271 — clip highlights make the compositor ~2.5× slower: every frame clones the whole source still

status: **fixed** (2026-10-26) · severity: **high** (performance is this project's first priority: a 15-minute 960×540 compositor export went from ~4 to ~10+ minutes once 38 clips carried highlights) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/edit.rs` (`apply_highlights_to_rgba`)

- **found:** 2026-10-26, exporting the Black October draft after applying D-396 highlights.
- **cause:** `Arc::make_mut` on the decoded still. The still is shared through the decode cache, so every frame clones the full source image (2880×1620×4 ≈ 18 MB) before drawing a few small boxes. That includes every frame after the last sweep has finished, when the highlighted picture never changes again.
- **fixed:** the strokes moved to their own module, `chroma/highlight_draw.rs`. `highlighted_picture` keeps ONE working copy per clip (4 clips at most, keyed by clip id + the decode cache's picture identity + the highlight list) instead of cloning the still per frame. Each frame it restores only the rows the previous frame's strokes touched from the untouched original and redraws only the band of rows the strokes reach (`draw_sweeps` no longer walks the whole image). Once every sweep has finished the finished picture is constant, so later frames return the same `Arc` with no work. A video clip's frame is private (refcount 1) and is still drawn on in place, as before. The decode cache's picture is never written.
- **verification:** `highlight_draw` tests (memoised output equals the plain operator on every frame of a two-stroke clip played forward, scrubbed backwards and jumped; the cache picture stays byte-identical; a finished clip reuses one `Arc`; an unstarted one is returned untouched; a private frame is drawn in place). The D-396 cross-engine table `highlight_matches_real_ffmpegs_own_measured_pixels` and the other 5 compositor highlight tests are unchanged and pass. Measured with the `#[ignore]` harness `bench_shared_still_two_highlights_240_frames` (release, 240 frames of a 2880×1620 still, 2 highlights, sweeps in frames 10–70, finished after): pre-fix operator **500.6 ms (2.09 ms/frame)**, now **137.6 ms (0.57 ms/frame)**, 3.6× less. The frames after the last sweep (170 of 240) now cost nothing; the remaining time is the two sweeps' own drawing.

status: **fixed** (2026-10-26) · severity: **minor** (an agent can write highlights with `editor_set_clip_highlights` but cannot read them back from the timeline read every other clip property comes from) · area: `packages/editor/src/useEditorControl.ts` (`editor_get_timeline`'s clip summary), both MCP servers' docs

## B-269 — `editor_suggest_clip_highlights`' headline fallback picked logos, sidebar strips and photo text

status: **fixed** (2026-10-26) · severity: **major** (46 of 59 real article captures fell back to the headline rule; most boxes were not the headline) · area: `packages/editor/src/highlightSuggest.ts`

- **found:** 2026-10-26, validating D-397 on the Black October captures. "The largest line" won with a site logo in the nav bar (TNW, W3Techs, php.net, Sansec), a vertical sidebar strip (PPC Land), the "OpenAI" text inside an AP photo, and a BleepingComputer sidebar ad.
- **fix:** `pickHeadline`. A headline line has at least 3 words, is at least 3× wider than tall and spans at least 18% of the page width, and sits below the top 7% site-chrome band. The largest-type such line is taken with the same-size lines stacked directly above and below it (its wrap, up to 3), swept in reading order.

## B-268 — a Motion theme can only be added by changing engine code; themes are not data

status: **fixed (D-399, 2026-10-26)** · severity: **major** (a look that is not already compiled in needs an engine change, a commit and a rebuild; neither a user nor an agent can add one at runtime) · area: `packages/motion-engine/src/design.ts` (`THEMES`), `engine/schema.ts` (`theme` is a `z.enum` of the compiled names), `themeFonts.ts`, `motion_set_project_theme`

- **found:** 2026-10-26, owner: "why we needed to do code change to convert to light theme — themes should be dynamic". Making the Black October edit light required adding `apelles-studio-light` to the code (D-394).
- **actual:** switching among EXISTING themes is a setting, but a theme itself is a compiled TypeScript object, the manifest schema only accepts compiled names, and each theme's fonts are a code loader.
- **expected:** a theme is a validated DATA document (the existing `Theme` shape plus its font list) that can live in the manifest (`manifest.themeDef`), in the user library (shared across projects, like components) or be derived from a token file. It is creatable and editable in the GUI (a theme editor next to the Theme picker) and over MCP (`motion_define_theme`, `motion_list_themes`), and resolved at render time with the compiled presets as built-in defaults. Fonts load from the same Google Fonts mechanism by family name.
- **fixed (D-399):** a theme is a validated `ThemeDef` (colours as opaque `#rrggbb`, stroke feel, font stacks, Google Fonts families). It can be embedded in the manifest (`themeDef`, which `manifestSchema` REQUIRES for any non-built-in `theme` name), kept in a user library, or derived from a `--apelles-theme-*` token file. MCP `motion_define_theme` / `motion_list_themes` / `motion_delete_theme`, a theme editor beside the picker, compiled presets kept as built-ins. Verified by tests and a real offline Remotion render of a custom theme; the custom-font download and the GUI editor in the running app are not verified (see D-399).
- **note:** keep D-339's determinism rule. A manifest naming a user theme must embed or pin its definition, so the same document renders the same pixels on any machine.

## B-267 — after an app restart the Edit timeline panel draws no clips, though the timeline holds all of them

status: **mitigated, not confirmed live (2026-10-26): a defensive re-measure is in, the cause is a candidate** · severity: **high** (the timeline looks empty; a user reasonably concludes the edit is gone) · area: `packages/editor/src/TimelinePane.tsx` (clip rendering)

- **found:** 2026-10-26, owner: "see the timeline shows nothing?". After restarting the dev app (B-265) and reopening "Black October", every track row is empty at 1% zoom; markers still draw.
- **the data is intact:** `editor_get_timeline` and `project.json` both hold 59 + 1 + 1 + 63 + 56 + 1 video clips and 56 + 1 audio clips, and the preview plays them. Before the restart the same project drew its clips at the same zoom.
- **investigated (2026-10-26, no running app available to the investigator):** `TimelinePane.zoomedOut.dom.test.tsx` mounts the owner's shape (240 clips, 21,992 frames, 1200 px viewport), zooms to the 1 px/s floor with the real ctrl-wheel handler and checks the library's output: all 240 clip hosts are mounted, each 3.03 px wide, left to right with no overlap, each carrying its coloured body (`CLIP_BODY_BACKGROUND`). So the model, the zoom arithmetic and the action geometry are not the cause, and the pane does no horizontal clip culling (only `Filmstrip`/`Waveform` self-cull, and they paint nothing when culled, leaving the body colour). That leaves something jsdom cannot show: real layout/paint (the row/viewport height, a zero-height virtualised row list on the first layout after a restart) or, given that the report coincides with B-265's stale-module webview, a stale `TimelinePane`/library module in the reloaded dev page.
- **next:** on a freshly restarted app showing the empty timeline, take `debug_dom_tree` of one track row: are the `.timeline-editor-action` hosts present, and with what size and height? Present with size = a paint/CSS cause; absent = a render cause (check the console for a thrown error in `getActionRender`). Compare against the same project after a hard reload. The regression test stays as the floor; do not close this entry without a live reproduction.
- **candidate cause found by reading the layout path (2026-10-26, second pass; still no running app):** the Edit tab is MOUNTED while hidden. `Shell.tsx` keeps every inactive tab panel in the tree under `display: none`, so after a restart the timeline lays out with every box at 0 px. The timeline library sizes its rows with react-virtualized's `AutoSizer` + `Grid` (`edit_area.tsx`), which measured 0 x 0 at mount; if it is not told when the element later gets a real size, the grid renders zero rows: the clip hosts do not exist, while the ruler and the markers (our own overlays, outside the grid) draw, the data and the preview are intact, and it never happens when the Edit tab was visible from the start (the pre-restart session). That matches every symptom in the report and explains why the jsdom test (no layout, no AutoSizer) could not show it. What is NOT established: react-virtualized's `detectElementResize` has a CSS-animation path meant to catch a hidden element being displayed, so it may handle this in some cases; whether it fails in this WKWebView needs the DOM check below.
- **mitigation landed:** `useViewportWidth(editArea)` (`useViewportWidth.ts`) replaces the pane's hand-rolled observer and returns an `epoch` that bumps exactly once, the first time an element first measured at 0 px gets a width; `TimelinePane` uses it as the library's `key`, so the grid remounts and measures a visible element. An element visible at first measure never bumps (no remount in the normal case), and a later hide/show of an already-sized grid is left alone. `useViewportWidth.dom.test.tsx` (2) pins both. Editor suite 2277/2277, no new tsc errors.
- **still needed:** the `debug_dom_tree` check in **next** above on a freshly restarted app, with the Edit tab not active at launch: if the track rows have no `.timeline-editor-action` hosts and the AutoSizer wrapper has a 0 height before the fix and a real one after, this entry can be closed. If hosts exist and are sized, this was not the cause.

## B-266 — a fully pinned Motion `graph` still ran the force layout and re-fit, so pinned nodes moved

status: **fixed** (2026-10-26) · severity: **major** (authored layouts drifted; a pinned PHP node at x = 960 landed near 1440, on top of a neighbouring layer) · area: `packages/motion-engine/src/primitives/Graph.tsx`

- **found:** 2026-10-25, owner review of the attack scene ("this one is overlapping").
- **cause:** pinned nodes went through the d3-force pass and then the fit-to-margin rescale that exists for unpinned layouts, which moved them by a uniform scale and re-centred them.
- **fix:** `pinnedPositions(nodes)`, a pure function. When every node carries x/y, those are the drawn positions verbatim, with no simulation and no fit. A partly pinned graph is unchanged.
- **verification:** `pinnedPositions (B-266)` tests; `vitest run packages/motion-engine packages/motion` 946/946; the attack scene re-rendered with the server clear of the memory grid.

## B-265 — a Motion render dies silently when the webview reloads, and the reloaded page can run STALE engine code

status: **fixed except the dev stale-module root cause (D-398, 2026-10-26)** · severity: **high** (a ~40-minute render stopped at scene 19 of 55 with no error, no log line and no notice; the app then reported the render as never having started) · area: `packages/motion/src/renderLoop.ts` + `useMotionManifest.ts` (the loop lives in the webview), the dev webview's module loading

- **found:** 2026-10-25, Black October edit. A source edit to `Graph.tsx` at 21:45 caused the dev webview to reload mid-render.
- **what happened, in order:**
  1. The render loop is a JavaScript loop inside the page (D-359). The reload destroyed it between scenes: `s18` landed at 21:45:15, and nothing after it.
  2. `motion_get_state` then answered `state: idle, scenesTotal: null`, which means "never started this session". Nothing recorded that a render had been interrupted, and nothing in the app log said so either. The only way to find out was to notice no new files for 7 minutes.
  3. The page that came back ran an OLD `design.ts` (its theme registry lacked `apelles-studio-light`, added ~15 min earlier). Vite served the current file to `curl` at the same moment, and touching the file produced no HMR update at all. So the manifest failed to parse (`theme: Invalid option`) until the whole dev app was restarted.
- **why it matters beyond dev:** (1)-(2) are not dev-only. Any webview reload (a crash recovery, a future auto-update) kills an in-flight render the same way, and the app forgets the job.
- **expected — prevent, detect, recover:**
  - **Prevent:** run the render JOB in the backend, which owns the process and survives a webview reload, instead of a loop in the page. The page only starts it and watches it. This also solves B-264's snapshot problem: the job holds the exact manifest it was started with.
  - **Detect:** persist the job (manifest hash, scene list, done/failed per scene) under the project (`motion/render-job.json`). Log start, every scene and stop. `motion_get_state.render` reports `interrupted` with what is left, never a blank `idle`.
  - **Recover:** on project open, an interrupted job is offered as **Resume** in the GUI and resumable through MCP (`motion_render(resume=true)`), rendering only the scenes not yet written. Together with B-263's per-scene render.
  - **Dev staleness:** reproduce and root-cause the stale module (watcher missed the edit? webview HTTP cache?) before deciding the fix. A dev-only "engine version" stamp compared at load would at least make it visible.
- **fixed (D-398):** the render job moved from the page into the backend (`apelles_motion::job`, `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/motion_job.rs`). It runs on a worker thread of the app process, so a webview reload does not touch it; it renders from a snapshot of the manifest taken at the start; every transition is persisted to `<project>/motion/render-job/job.json` and emitted as `chroma://motion-render`. `motion_get_state.render` reads the live job, or the persisted one after a restart, and reports `interrupted` with `remainingSceneIds` instead of a blank `idle`. The GUI shows **Resume render** (or **Retry from failed scene**) and MCP has `motion_render(resume=true)`: only the scenes not yet written render, and a finished scene whose file has gone is re-rendered. A scene that finishes while no page is listening is delivered to Sources when one returns (`unreconciled` / `chroma_motion_job_ack`). Tests: 8 state-machine tests in `apelles_motion::job` (interrupted vs running, resume, delivery, persistence round trip), a persisted-job-after-restart test in `motion_job`, and the page-side helpers in `renderLoop.test.ts`.
- **stale dev module (NOT root-caused):** the second symptom, the reloaded page running an old `design.ts`, was investigated against a Vite dev server started on the same layout (workspace package outside the Vite root, served through `/@fs/`): an edit to `design.ts` is picked up within 2 s, the response carries `Cache-Control: no-cache` and a changed ETag. So the server side behaves; the stale copy was in the webview's own module cache or a missed watcher event on the owner's checkout, neither of which can be observed without the running app. **Next:** when it recurs, before restarting, `curl` the module through the dev server and compare with what the page evaluated (`debug_dom_tree` / devtools Sources), and check whether the file was written by a rename-over (a new inode). If the server answers current and the page is stale, the fix is a cache-busting query on the Tauri dev URL.
- **stale dev module, second pass (2026-10-26, from the config and the dep cache; still no running app, no new root cause, no change made):**
  - **Not pre-bundling.** The usual way a dev page runs a stale workspace module is Vite's dependency optimiser serving a cached bundle under an immutable `?v=` URL. The live dev cache (`app/node_modules/.vite/deps/_metadata.json`) holds no `@apelles/*` entry at all: the workspace packages are symlinks to source (`main: ./src/index.ts`) and are served as ordinary source modules, which carry `Cache-Control: no-cache` plus an ETag (revalidated on every request, including after `location.reload()`).
  - **Not a Vite setting.** `app/vite.config.mjs` has no `optimizeDeps`, `server.fs`, `server.headers` or `cacheDir` override; `watch.ignored` is only `src-tauri`. Nothing there changes module caching.
  - **What is left.** The server answered `curl` with the current file at the same moment, so the staleness was in the page. Two candidates remain and both need the running app to separate: (1) the WKWebView process came back with an old in-memory module (B-274 shows the web content process is replaced under memory pressure on this checkout; a page reloaded into such a process is not evidence about HTTP caching), (2) the page imported the module under a `?t=` timestamp Vite had issued for an earlier HMR update. The check when it recurs is unchanged: compare the module's served text with what the page evaluated, and read `app.log` for a `webview_restarted_unexpectedly` event (B-274) next to it. If that event is present, this is the same incident as B-274, not a cache bug.
- **workaround used:** checked the timeline was saved, restarted the dev app, and re-rendered only the missing scenes from a temporary manifest (see B-263).

## B-264 — `motion_render` renders each scene's CONTENT from the manifest file on disk but its FRAME WINDOW from the in-memory copy, so a manifest change during a render misaligns every later scene

status: **fixed (D-398, 2026-10-26)** · severity: **major** (a render can silently write the wrong seconds of the wrong scene into a scene's file, with no error) · area: `packages/motion/src/renderLoop.ts`, `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/motion.rs` (the old `chroma_motion_render`, now `motion_job.rs`)

- **found:** 2026-10-25, during a 55-scene render for the "Black October" edit. A new manifest that lengthened one scene by 7 s was written to the project's sidecar mid-render.
- **cause:** the frontend loop computes each scene's absolute `frameRange` once, from the manifest it held when the render started (`sceneStartFrame`/`sceneDurationFrames`), and passes it per scene to `chroma_motion_render`. That command renders `manifest_path(&dir)`, the file on disk, read fresh for every scene. If the file changes mid-loop, every scene after the change gets a window computed against one document and content from another.
- **expected:** a render is a snapshot. Either the loop hands the backend the exact manifest it computed the windows from (a temp file per render, or the JSON inline), or the backend refuses when the file's content hash differs from the one the render started with.
- **fixed (D-398):** the render is a snapshot. `chroma_motion_job_start` takes the EXACT manifest the page computed the windows from, writes it to `render-job/manifest.json`, and every scene renders from that file, never from `manifest.json`; the snapshot's blake3 hash is stored on the job and reported. A manifest changed on disk (or by an edit in the app) mid-render therefore cannot reach a scene's content. `chroma_motion_render` was deleted.
- **workaround used:** the original manifest was restored from the app's in-memory copy (`motion_get_manifest`) within a minute; the scenes rendered in that window were queued for re-render.

## B-263 — a Motion render cannot target one scene: adding or changing a single scene means re-rendering the whole manifest

status: **fixed (D-398, 2026-10-26)** · severity: **major** (on a 55-scene, ~9-minute manifest, one changed card costs a ~40-minute full render) · area: `motion_render` (both MCP servers), `packages/motion/src/renderLoop.ts`, the Motion tab's Render button

- **found:** 2026-10-25. Owner feedback changed four cards, then one more scene, in a manifest whose full render takes ~40 minutes; each round re-rendered all 55 scenes.
- **expected:** "render this scene" / "render these scenes" (and "render what changed since its last render"), in BOTH the GUI (per-scene Render in the layer panel) and MCP (`motion_render(scene_ids=[…])`), per the human-and-AI rule. The per-scene files and D-260's refresh-in-place already make a partial render safe: each scene is its own file.
- **fixed (D-398):** `motion_render(scene_ids=[...])` (both MCP servers) and a **Render this scene** button on each scene row of the layer panel. A chosen scene keeps its place in the whole manifest, so it writes the same frames a full render would; ids are validated (an unknown id is an error naming it) and rendered in manifest order. "Render what changed since its last render" is not built: it needs a per-scene content hash, which the job's snapshot hash could grow into.
- **workaround used:** temporarily installing a manifest that holds only the scenes to re-render, rendering, then restoring the full one. It works because files are named by scene id, but it is a workaround, not a feature.

## B-262 — a Motion manifest changed outside the app is not picked up until the project is switched away and back

status: **fixed (D-398, 2026-10-26)** · severity: **minor** · area: `packages/motion/src/motionProjectStore.ts` (`setOpenProject` / `load`)

- **found:** 2026-10-25, authoring a 55-scene manifest as a file (the documented, hand-authorable sidecar) for an agent-built edit.
- **actual:** the store reads the sidecar only on a project SWITCH (`setOpenProject` is a no-op for the same path, so `open_project` on the open project does nothing), a window-focus recheck, or the Retry button. Picking up the new file meant opening a different project and then this one again: every time, for every iteration.
- **expected:** a real reload path. Either watch the sidecar (with a "the file changed on disk — reload?" prompt when the in-app document is dirty), or a `motion_reload_manifest` tool plus a GUI "Reload from disk" action. Better still for agents, a `motion_set_manifest(manifest)` op that validates and commits a whole document as one undoable edit.
- **fixed (D-398):** `motion_reload_manifest(force?)` (both MCP servers) and a **Reload from disk** button in the Motion toolbar, both through `useMotionManifest.reloadFromDisk`. It refuses while the in-app document has unsaved edits unless `force` (the button arms first: "Discard edits and reload?"). A file watcher was not built: the prompt it would need is exactly this explicit action, and a silent reload mid-edit is the worse failure. Not built: `motion_set_manifest` (commit a whole document as one undoable edit); a reload is not undoable and earlier undo history refers to the previous document.

## B-261 — a Motion `graph` node's label sat almost on its ring

status: **fixed** (2026-10-25) · severity: **minor** (labels crowded their node; with a highlight glow the gap disappeared) · area: `packages/motion-engine/src/primitives/Graph.tsx`

- **found:** 2026-10-25, owner review of the discovery timeline ("have some space between Aug 1 and the circle").
- **cause:** the label's BASELINE was at `nodeR + 34`, so at the 30 px base label size the glyph tops sat ~10 px under the ring.
- **fix:** the label is anchored by its top (`dominantBaseline="hanging"`) at `nodeR + GRAPH_LABEL_GAP` (24 px), a named constant, so the clearance no longer depends on the label's font size.
- **verification:** `vitest run packages/motion-engine packages/motion`: 942/942; checked on the re-rendered timeline scene.

## B-260 — the lit card in a Motion `layers` stack snapped forward, shifted 40 px right and grew over the card above it

status: **fixed** (2026-10-25) · severity: **minor** (visibly broken "3D hover" on every stack with an `active` schedule) · area: `packages/motion-engine/src/primitives/Layers.tsx`, `engine/registry.ts`

- **found:** 2026-10-25, owner review of the hotel-analogy stack: "the 3D hover on this component is not right".
