- **cause:** the active card got a fixed `translateZ(90px) translateX(40px)`. Under the stack's 1400 px perspective that is a 1.07× scale, so a 104 px card grew ~7 px at each edge across a 22 px gap and overlapped its neighbour. The sideways shift threw it off-centre, and it jumped on the changeover frame with no easing.
- **fix:** `activeLift(framesSinceLit, cardH, gap)`, a pure function: the lift is capped so the grown card stays inside 90% of the gap (and at most 90 px), with no sideways shift, eased out-cubic over 8 frames from the frame the card became active. The registry passes that frame (`activeSince`, from the same `resolveActiveStep` `claudechat` uses).
- **verification:** new `activeLift (B-260)` tests (never past the gap for four card/gap shapes; eases from 0). `vitest run packages/motion-engine packages/motion`: 942/942. Checked live in the Motion preview.

## B-259 — `editor_add_clip` on a track index that no longer exists silently places the clip on track 0, then reports that it did not place it

status: **fixed (2026-10-26)** · severity: **minor** (the clip lands somewhere unexpected and the tool's own answer is wrong) · area: `packages/editor/src/timeline.ts` (`add_clip` reducer), `packages/editor/src/useEditorControl.ts` (`editor_add_clip`)

- **found:** 2026-10-25. `editor_remove_clip` removed a clip and its linked half, and the tracks they left empty were pruned. A follow-up `editor_add_clip(track=1, …)` then targeted a track that was gone.
- **actual:** `checkAddClip` did not refuse the out-of-range index. The reducer fell back to `trackIdx = 0` (`requested < next.tracks.length ? requested : 0`) and placed the clip there. The handler then looked for it on track 1 and answered `add_clip did not place the clip`. On a timeline with no tracks at all, the same path creates a **video** track for an audio-only source (`if (next.tracks.length === 0) push video`).
- **expected:** an out-of-range track is refused with a reason before anything is placed, and an empty timeline gets a track of the kind the source needs.
- **fixed:** `checkAddClip` refuses a track that does not exist once the timeline has tracks, with the valid range and the hint to re-read `get_timeline` (pruned tracks), so the reducer returns the same timeline and `editor_add_clip` reports the reason instead of "did not place the clip". The reducer's `requested < length ? requested : 0` fallback is gone. An empty timeline is the one exception: the first track is created and the clip goes on it (index 0 whatever was named), of the kind the source needs: a new `newTrackKind` on the op, which `editor_add_clip` sets to `audio` for an audio-only source (probed 0x0) and which a title, adjustment clip or still overrides to `video` (picture is always video). Nothing in the suite or the GUI relied on the fallback. Tests: `timelineAddClipTrack.test.ts` (7).

## B-258 — a Motion `text` layer anchored at `x` wrapped at the space right of `x`, not at its `maxWidth`, so every centred headline wrapped at half the canvas

status: **fixed** (2026-10-25) · severity: **major** (any centred title wider than ~960 px broke onto two lines and overlapped whatever sat below it, in the preview and the render) · area: `packages/motion-engine/src/primitives/Text.tsx`

- **found:** 2026-10-25, building title cards in the `apelles-studio` theme. `BLACK OCTOBER` at 190 px, centred at `x: 960` with `maxWidth: 1760`, rendered as two lines, and its subtitle overlapped the second one.
- **cause:** a positioned `text` layer is an absolutely positioned box at `left: x`, shifted by `translateX(-50%)` (centre) or `-100%` (right). An absolutely positioned box with no width shrinks to fit the space between `left` and the containing block's right edge. At `x = 960` that is 960 px, so `maxWidth` never applied. Right-aligned text near the right edge wrapped sooner still.
- **fix:** the positioned wrapper sets `width: max-content`, so the box is as wide as its text up to `maxWidth`, wherever the anchor sits. Unpositioned text is unchanged. A layer that used to wrap only because of this bug now wraps at its own `maxWidth`, which is what its author asked for.
- **verification:** `vitest run packages/motion-engine packages/motion`: 935/935 pass. Live in the Motion preview, the same title now holds one line with its subtitle below.

## B-257 — placing an audio-only source on an audio track added a second, linked copy of it on another audio track, so it played twice

status: **fixed** (2026-10-25) · severity: **major** (any VO or music bed placed this way played at roughly +6 dB, doubled, in the preview and the export) · area: `packages/editor/src/timeline.ts` (`add_clip` / `edit_in` reducers)

- **found:** 2026-10-25, building a voiceover-led edit over MCP. `editor_add_clip(track=0, …)` with an `.m4a` on audio track 0 answered `linkedAudio: {track: 1}`: a new audio track 1 held a second clip of the same source window, linked to the first.
- **cause:** D-129's linked-audio rule builds the half from the source alone (`hasAudio` and not a still), in both `editor_add_clip` and the Sources-panel drag (`linkedClipsFromDraggedMedia`). The reducers then placed it unconditionally. They never asked whether the primary clip had itself landed on an audio track, where it already is the source's audio.
- **fix:** one helper in the reducer, `resolveLinkedHalf`, used by both `add_clip` and `edit_in`. When the destination track is an audio track, it drops the linked half and clears the clip's `link_group` (a partner-less group would mean nothing). A video-track placement is unchanged. It lives in the reducer rather than in a caller so the drag and the MCP tool cannot disagree. `labelForOp` asks the same helper, so the history entry no longer says `Add "…" + audio` for a placement that added no audio.
- **verification:** new test `B-257: a clip placed on an AUDIO track is its own audio — no second linked copy` in `timeline.test.ts` (also checks the history label). `timeline.test.ts` + `editTypes.test.ts`: 329/329 pass. `tsc -p packages/editor` shows only the 3 errors already there before (in `RecutPanel.dom.test.tsx` and `recutSweep.test.ts`). Re-placing the VO live in the running dev app gave one clip and no second track.

## B-256 — the v0.2.0 release build failed on a fresh runner: `ort-sys` downloaded a prebuilt ONNX Runtime from cdn.pyke.io that the app never uses

status: **fixed** (2026-10-21) · severity: **major** (the release pipeline could not build; any machine without the cached download could fail the same way) · area: `app/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`, `crates/apelles-speech/Cargo.toml`

- **found:** 2026-10-21, the first run of the release workflow (D-392): `failed to run custom build command for ort-sys v2.0.0-rc.10` … `Failed to GET https://cdn.pyke.io/0/pyke:ort-rs/ms@1.22.0/aarch64-apple-darwin.tgz: failed to lookup address information`. The CDN answered fine from a developer Mac minutes later, so the trigger was a transient DNS failure on the runner. The developer Mac had never hit it because the download was cached there.
- **cause:** both crates enabled `ort` with `features = ["ndarray", "load-dynamic"]` but left its **default** features on, and those include `download-binaries` (plus `copy-dylibs`). With `load-dynamic` nothing links that download: the app loads the `libonnxruntime.dylib` its own `build.rs` fetches, verifies and bundles. So every build made an extra network fetch for a binary nobody used.
- **fix:** `default-features = false, features = ["std", "ndarray", "tracing", "load-dynamic"]` in both crates. `cargo tree -i ort -e features` no longer shows `download-binaries` or `copy-dylibs`.
- **verification:** `cargo build -p apelles -p apelles-speech` clean; `cargo test -p apelles-speech` all green (including the ONNX-backed VAD tests); `cargo test -p apelles --lib` 427/427 (one run hit B-255, the reruns were clean). The re-tagged release run is the end-to-end check.

## B-255 — `audio_keeps_playing_across_ripple_cut_boundaries` failed once in a full `cargo test -p apelles --lib` run and passed on every rerun

status: **open** (intermittent, not reproduced) · severity: **minor** (a test that can fail without a code change; the behaviour it guards was verified live by B-235's checks) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/audio.rs` (the B-190/D-323 end-to-end test)

- **found:** 2026-10-21, the pre-tag run for v0.2.0 (`docs/releases/README.md`). `cargo test --workspace`: 426 passed, 1 failed, at the assertion that every peak sampled from 1.8 s on is above 0.001. The panic's peak readings were not captured (the workspace run's output was filtered to result lines).
- **since:** passed alone (once), and in two further full `-p apelles --lib` runs (427/427 each) and the full `--workspace --no-fail-fast` run. Failed again later the same day in a full `-p apelles --lib` run, then passed three in a row: **2 failures in 8 full runs** so far, never alone. That rate is a real problem, not noise; the next run that fails must keep its `peaks by ms` stderr line.
- **not known:** whether this is test fragility (it plays through the real `cpal` output device and reads D-050's level meter, which refreshes about once per second of written audio, B-106, while the rest of the suite loads the machine) or a real dropout under load. Next step: rerun it in a loop under load with its `peaks by ms` line kept, and see whether a failing run is silent at a boundary (B-190's shape) or merely misses a meter refresh.
- **not blocking v0.2.0:** the release does not run Rust tests on CI (D-392), and playback across cuts was verified live (B-235).

## B-254 — the installed release build started every sidecar from the build machine's checkout: `ai-media/` sources, the developer's `ai/.venv`, and `target/debug/apelles-mcp`

status: **fixed** (D-390, 2026-10-15) · severity: **blocker** (release: on any other Mac transcription, every AI tool and MCP cannot start) · area: `crates/apelles-ai` (`sidecar.rs`, `ai_env.rs`), `app/src-tauri` (`build.rs`, `chroma/sidecar.rs`, `lib.rs`, `tauri.macos.release.conf.json`), root `package.json`, `ai/server.py`

- **found:** 2026-10-15, testing the installed release `/Applications/Apelles.app` opened from Finder. The log showed `[sidecar/ai-media] starting: cd "/Users/…/chroma/ai-media" && "<app support>/ai-env/.venv/bin/python" -m uvicorn …`, `[sidecar/ai] using this sidecar's own /Users/…/chroma/ai/.venv/bin/python and NOT the shared …/ai-env/.venv`, and `[sidecar/mcp] starting: "/Users/…/chroma/target/debug/apelles-mcp" --http --port 19790`.
- **cause:** nothing shipped them. The bundle had no `ai/`/`ai-media/` sources and no `apelles-mcp`, and `apelles_ai::sidecar`'s `resolve_dir`, `resolve_shared_python` and `resolve_bin` (plus `ai_env::paths`) all fell back to `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`-relative paths — compiled in, naming the build machine's checkout, which exists on the build machine and so "worked" exactly where the release was tested. `ai` then picked the checkout's per-sidecar `.venv` (the more specific rung of D-314's ladder). The same `ai/server.py` would also have `makedirs`'d `models/` and CPython its `__pycache__/` inside the signed bundle. Documented as an open gap (`docs/notes/sidecar-lifecycle.md` "STILL OPEN"), never closed before the first DMG.
- **fix (D-390):** an explicit `Layout` (`Dev` / `Packaged{resources,data}` / `PackagedUnresolved`) set by the app from `tauri::is_dev()` before any supervisor starts; every manifest-dir sweep is dev-only. `build.rs` stages the runnable sources into `resources/sidecars/{ai,ai-media}` (release builds) and the release `apelles-mcp` into `binaries/` for an `externalBin` declared in `tauri.macos.release.conf.json`, which `npm run tauri:build` passes. Packaged Python sidecars run only on the shared app-data venv, with `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX` and `APELLES_SIDECAR_DATA_DIR` under app data.
- **verification:** `cargo test -p apelles-ai` (new: packaged resolves the bundled sources; packaged never falls back to the checkout although it exists; overrides win in both layouts; packaged Python = shared venv or "not yet", never the per-sidecar venv or `PATH`; bins beside the exe, no `target/` sweep when packaged; packaged writes go to app data). `cargo test -p apelles` for the externalBin/overlay/staging guards. **Verified live (2026-10-21):** the installed `.app` (DMG with D-391, quarantined, opened via Open Anyway from Finder, so App Translocation applied) logged `[sidecar] packaged layout: sources …/Apelles.app/Contents/Resources/resources/sidecars`, both Python sidecars on `shared ai-env venv (app data)` with their `cwd` inside the bundle (`lsof`), and `[sidecar/mcp] starting: "…/Apelles.app/Contents/MacOS/apelles-mcp"`. Afterwards `codesign --verify --deep --strict` still passed and the bundle held no `__pycache__`.

## B-253 — the installed release build could not decode, probe or thumbnail anything: ffmpeg was run by bare name and not bundled, and a Finder launch has no Homebrew on its PATH

status: **fixed** (D-389, 2026-10-15) · severity: **blocker** (release: the core decode/playback/export path is dead in the installed app) · area: `crates/apelles-media` (`video.rs`, `decode_pipe.rs`), `app/src-tauri/src/chroma` (`export.rs`, `ffmpeg_run.rs`, `edit_render.rs`), `app/src-tauri/build.rs`, `tauri.macos.conf.json`, `ai-media/`

- **found:** 2026-10-15, testing the installed release build `/Applications/Apelles.app` (D-388's first DMG). The live log showed `decode pipe fell back to single-frame decode: spawning decode pipe` and `thumb regen failed: running ffmpeg thumb`; nothing decoded.
- **cause:** two layers. (1) **Nothing was bundled**: `Contents/MacOS` held only `apelles` and `uv`. D-015 (2026-09-01) took ffmpeg to be "a hard dep … on every target" and only anticipated `CHROMA_FFMPEG`/`CHROMA_FFPROBE` "for a pinned/bundled binary". (2) **Every spawn was by bare name** (~32 sites across `apelles-media` and `chroma/`, three copy-pasted `ffmpeg_bin()` helpers, most sites ignoring even the override), so resolution was left to `execvp` against the process `PATH`. An app opened from Finder inherits launchd's minimal `PATH` (`/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`), with no `/opt/homebrew/bin`, so even a machine with Homebrew ffmpeg failed. Dev runs never showed it because `npm run tauri:dev` inherits the shell's `PATH`. The `ai-media/` sidecar's audio extract and scene-detect had the same bug one process further out.
- **fix (D-389):** a static GPL-3.0 ffmpeg 9.0.2 + ffprobe (Martin Riedl's arm64 build, pinned URL + archive and binary sha256s) is fetched by `build.rs` and bundled as Tauri `externalBin`s beside `uv`; a single resolver, `apelles_media::ffmpeg_locate` (env override → beside the executable → `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin` → `PATH`; resolved once, cached, logged at startup, a clear `ToolMissing` error otherwise) replaces every bare-name spawn and all the duplicate helpers; the sidecar supervisor passes the resolved paths to its children as `CHROMA_FFMPEG`/`CHROMA_FFPROBE`, which `ai-media/ffmpeg_bin.py` reads. Licence text + source pointers ship in `resources/licenses/`.
- **verification:** `git grep 'Command::new("ff'` → no matches; `ffmpeg_locate`'s 8 unit tests drive the ladder with temp dirs (each rung wins over the ones below it, a stale override and a non-executable file fall through, bare-name override, the not-found message); `ai_env.rs`'s externalBin test asserts `uv`, `ffmpeg`, `ffprobe`. `cargo check -p apelles` downloads, verifies and stages both binaries (`Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64`, `-hwaccels` lists `videotoolbox`). `cargo test` green on `apelles-media`, `apelles-project`, `apelles-ai`, `apelles`, and `apelles-media`'s suite also green with `CHROMA_FFMPEG`/`CHROMA_FFPROBE` pointed at the staged bundled binaries. **Verified live (2026-10-15):** the installed `.app` (DMG, quarantined, opened via Open Anyway from Finder) logged `[ffmpeg] using ffmpeg at /Applications/Apelles.app/Contents/MacOS/ffmpeg (bundled with the app)`, and the owner confirmed import, thumbnails and playback work.

## B-252 — dark-region recovery deleted correct whole-file words next to a short stretch

status: **fixed** (2026-10-15, D-387) · severity: medium (silently removes real words from the transcript retake grouping and captions read) · area: `packages/editor/src/darkRegions.ts`

- **found:** 2026-10-15, investigating D-381's four imperfect recoveries. On C038 the whole-file word "everything." (501.20-501.92 s) was missing from the spliced transcript — "Word one, reread Word two…" — and on C019 "for" (325.96 s) next to a timestamp-collapse stretch.
- **cause:** `recoveryWindows` grew a stretch shorter than 4 s symmetrically to 4 s without regard to word boundaries, so the window began or ended inside a neighbouring word. `spliceTranscript` replaced every word whose midpoint the window held, with whatever the isolated read heard there — and a read of half a word at a window edge is usually nothing.
- **fix (D-387):** a window reads context but changes only its `holes` (the stretch); words outside a hole are never replaced. Measured on all 19 stretches: 2 deleted words → 0. Pinned by `darkRegions.test.ts` "keeps the whole-file words in the context it read, even when the read lost them".

## B-251 — Recut panel labelled some AI-confirmed reasons by bare index (`"#203"`) instead of the word

The reason lines looked each offending word up in the row's own take text. The offending words belong to the whole group, so one in a sibling take (or outside the shown window) was not found and fell back to `#index`, while the first, which was in the take, showed its text. Fixed: the rows carry the group's offending words and every reason reads `“word” (#index)`. Test: `RecutPanel.dom.test.tsx` "every AI-confirmed reason is labelled word-then-index".

## B-250 — `editor_get_word_transcript` told the agent to start a transcription that was already running

status: **fixed** (2026-10-14) · severity: low (a wrong instruction, not a wrong result: following it only re-asks for a job already in flight) · area: `packages/editor/src/retakeProposalOps.ts`

- **found:** 2026-10-14, live MCP test: a source on the track had no transcript yet and a transcription for it was already running, started by another caller. `editor_get_word_transcript` (without `start`) still answered "Call editor_get_word_transcript with start: true to transcribe them."
- **cause:** the pending note chose its wording from the call's own `start` argument ("did *this* call start it?") instead of from the store ("is a transcription running for these files?"). Only a call that started the job itself was told it was running.
- **fix:** the note reads `mediaUnderstandingStore.transcribing` for the pending files. If all are running it says transcription is running and to call again shortly; if none are, it says to call with `start: true`; for a mix it says how many are running and how many still need `start: true`. No tool description changed.
- **verification:** new case in `retakeProposalOps.dom.test.tsx`: a transcription started outside the op makes the note say "Transcription is running; call this again" with no `start: true`. With the old code it fails on exactly that assertion. Whole `@apelles/editor` suite green (2160 tests); `tsc` in `app/` at the 65-error baseline.

## B-249 — retake dark-region recovery stalled forever when the agent polled, as the start call told it to

status: **fixed** (2026-10-14) · severity: medium (a retake sweep never answered unless the agent ignored its own instructions and called the start tool again) · area: `packages/editor/src/useEditorControl.ts`, `packages/editor/src/mediaUnderstandingStore.ts`

- **found:** 2026-10-14, live MCP test: `editor_detect_retakes` (sweep) started the D-349 dark-region scan and answered `state: transcribing`, with a note saying to poll `editor_detect_retakes_status`. Polling then reported the run as still transcribing (recovering) forever; only another start call got it moving.
- **cause:** the job is a chain (transcript, scan, one re-read per dark window, grouping), and each step can only start once the previous one lands. The sweep's status path called `runTranscriptView` with `start: false`, so after the scan finished nothing ever called `startRecovery`. The single-clip status path had the same gap one step later: it advanced the re-reads but never started the grouping. Nothing recorded that a start call had asked for the job, so a status read could not tell "continue what was asked for" from "read only".
- **fix:** a start call records a retake request in the store (`retakeRequests`, keyed by `retakeRequestKey`: run, `recoverDarkRegions`, tuning). A status call for a recorded request continues the chain through the re-reads and into the grouping. It starts the grouping only from `idle`, and the request is settled once the grouping has a terminal answer, so a poll never retries a failure. A status call with no recorded request is a pure read that starts nothing and answers `idle` naming the start tool. That last part is a change for the single-clip status, which used to start the scan for any clip. D-349's rules are unchanged: language pinned, errors degrade and only `force` retries them, same cache keys. The Recut panel always runs as a start, so it is unaffected. The start/status notes and the `editor_detect_retakes_status` description (Python + Rust, parity corpus re-captured) now describe this. Write-up: `docs/notes/retake-detection.md` §13.
- **verification:** new B-249 block in `recutSweep.dom.test.tsx` (sweep and single clip: start, scan lands, poll starts the re-read pinned to `en`, re-read lands, poll groups the spliced words and answers `done`; plus an unasked status read starting nothing). With the old op code all three fail. Whole `@apelles/editor` suite green (2159 tests); `tsc` in `app/` at the 65-error baseline; `cargo test -p apelles-mcp` green.

## B-248 — `undo` / `redo` answered every call with the whole Colorist grade and histogram

status: **fixed** (2026-10-14) · severity: low (correct behaviour, ~30 KB of irrelevant payload on every undo — an agent's context, not the app, paid for it) · area: `app/src/hooks/useChromaControl.ts`

- **found:** 2026-10-14, the first live run of D-383: undoing an Edit-tab ripple delete returned `{result: {undone: …}}` plus the full Colorist `adjustments` object and a four-channel 256-bin `histogram`.
- **cause:** D-383 placed `undo` / `redo` in the Colorist dispatcher's `READ_ONLY` set to skip the frame capture and the activity feed, but that set's response path still spreads `adjustments` + `histogram` into every answer — right for a Colorist read, meaningless for a cross-tab history step. Not caught by the parity corpus, which records the MCP layer against a canned bridge envelope and never runs this dispatcher.
- **fix:** a `CROSS_TAB` op class in the same dispatcher (`undo`, `redo`): no settle-and-capture, no activity-feed entry, and the answer is only `{ok, error, result}`. D-383's "where the ops live" paragraph updated.
- **verification:** live, after the change hot-reloaded: `undo` / `redo` answer with only their result (see CHANGELOG 2026-10-14).

## B-247 — every dark-region re-read and every `editor_retranscribe_words` call was refused on Parakeet: the seam rejected the `language` it had itself reported

status: **fixed** (2026-10-14) · severity: high (dark-region recovery — the only net under Parakeet's measured drops — silently did nothing, and D-380's re-transcribe step of the refusal loop always errored) · area: `ai-media/asr/base.py`, `ai-media/asr/parakeet_mlx.py`

- **found:** 2026-10-14, the first live smoke of D-380 on C040 in the running app. `editor_detect_retakes` found the four dark regions and re-read all four, yet reported `recoveredUtterances: 0`; `editor_retranscribe_words` over the first region then answered with the reason: *"the speech model (parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3) cannot transcribe 'unknown'…"*.
- **cause:** with no language named, the Parakeet backend reports `language: "unknown"` — the honest value, since Parakeet surfaces no detection (D-381). The app pins every re-read to the whole-file pass's own `language` (D-349: auto-detection on short windows was unreliable on Whisper), so every window was sent back with `language: "unknown"`, and `check_language` refused it as an unsupported language. Recovery degrades by design (a failed window never blocks the rest), so it failed silently. Not caught by D-381's measurement because that ran windowed recovery through the Python entry point, which never pins a language; not caught by tests because nothing round-tripped a contract's own `language` back through the seam.
- **fix:** at the seam, as an invariant rather than in one caller: `asr.base.UNDETECTED_LANGUAGE` names the sentinel, and `BackendDescriptor.supports_language` accepts it back as "not specified" — **every `language` the seam emits must be accepted back unchanged**. The app's pinning rule is untouched (still right for any backend that does detect a language).
- **verification:** `test_asr_seam.py` now round-trips a Parakeet contract's own `language` through `check_language` and through a pinned `transcribe(...)`; with the old `base.py` it fails with the exact live message, with the fix it passes. All model-free ai-media suites green. Re-run live on C040 after the merge (see the D-380 live smoke).

## B-246 — the retake detector still proposes cutting speech that repeats nothing: D-366's guard exempts single-utterance takes, and `similarity`'s containment arm admits a long utterance on a matching tail

status: **fixed** (D-386, 2026-10-15; mitigated by D-382 the day before) · severity: high (over-cutting — the one direction D-318 rules out: a proposal a human accepts silently deletes speech absent from the result) · area: `crates/apelles-speech/src/retake.rs`

- **fixed (D-386):** `retake.rs` now keeps a non-kept take in its group only when the keeper holds every content word of it — `proposal::text_is_covered`, the coverage gate's own content rule (`content_shortfall`), not a second bar — and drops a group left with fewer than two takes. It covers all three shapes below, single-utterance takes included. Measured on `eval/retake/`: **over-cut 0.00 s on all eleven corpus tasks** (Parakeet 24.40 / 12.64 / 3.20 s → 0.00 s; Whisper 10.36-24.16 s → 0.00 s), protected 0.00 s, precision 1.000; ungated retake recall 0.265 / 0.523 / 0.606 → 0.232 / 0.189 / 0.296 on Parakeet, but what the app shows (the gated tasks) went 0.161 / 0.189 / 0.232 → **0.232 / 0.189 / 0.296**, and the gate now refuses none of the detector's groups (was 13 of 27). `proposed_cuts.rs`: "repeats nothing" 5.42 s / 56.92 s → **0.00 / 0.00 s**, and "absent from the keeper" 89.40 / 56.92 s → 0.00 / 0.00 s. The applying-`MIN_UTTERANCE_OVERLAP`-to-single-utterance-takes fix proposed below was measured and rejected: it leaves C019 Parakeet 1.44 s and every Whisper task 9.68-24.16 s. **What remains:** recall — a take whose words the ASR mis-heard (`bag`/`back`, `behind`/`being`) is not proposed, the gate's known cost (§11.4). Detail: D-386, `docs/notes/retake-detection.md` §14.
- **mitigated (D-382):** every detector group now goes through D-380's coverage gate before it reaches the Recut panel or `editor_detect_retakes`'s answer; a group whose cut would lose words is marked `refused` with those words, untickable until a person who listened unlocks it, and never bulk-ticked. Measured on `eval/retake/` (`C0xx/parakeet-gated`): over-cut **24.40 / 12.64 / 3.20 s → 0.00 s** on C019 / C038 / C040, cut precision 1.000 on all three, at a recall cost (retake recall 0.265 → 0.161, 0.523 → 0.189, 0.606 → 0.232); 13 of the detector's 27 groups refused. **Not fixed:** `retake.rs` still forms the over-cutting groups, so the refusals cost the detector recall it would keep if it grouped correctly, and the measurement covers Parakeet transcripts only (the gate runs on any word-timed transcript). The primary path is now the MCP client's judgement (D-380); this detector is the fallback.

- **found:** 2026-10-10, doing **D-374 step 4** (→ **D-377**) — widening the B-238 cut audit from the two corpus transcripts to every raw source the owner has, on both ASR backends. Pinned by `crates/apelles-speech/tests/proposed_cuts.rs::b246_the_cuts_that_repeat_nothing_are_exactly_these`, which itemises all six cases.
- **repro:** `cargo test -p apelles-speech --test proposed_cuts -- --nocapture`. The test is green: it pins the defect as a measurement, the way `real_transcripts.rs` pins D-365's one known false positive. A fix makes it fail with the list it emptied.
- **expected:** no utterance a group proposes for deletion shares less than `MIN_UTTERANCE_OVERLAP` of its own vocabulary with the take the group recommends keeping. That is exactly the invariant **D-366** stated and tested — `retake::tests::nothing_proposed_for_deletion_is_unique_content`.
- **actual:** six violations across three speech sources (2,192.6 s). mlx-whisper 1 (5.42 s), parakeet 5 (56.92 s):

  | source | backend | # | secs | overlap vs keeper | only this repeats |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | C019 | whisper | 50 | 5.42 | 0.417 | "there's actually a name for this" — the monthly-invoice line is said once |
  | C019 | parakeet | 14 | **14.96** | 0.156 | the trailing "Writing the notes into the" |
  | C019 | parakeet | 23 | 12.24 | 0.381 | "One more thing to know the notes never" |
  | C038 | parakeet | 17 | 11.36 | 0.280 | "and the trick behind use to bring that cost" |
  | C038 | parakeet | 40 | 14.52 | 0.240 | "But the real reason it's this expensive" |
  | C040 | parakeet | 36 | 3.84 | 0.375 | "read than write" |

- **cause:** two layers, both of which made the earlier green look right.
  1. **`anchor_is_justified` (D-366) only guards *glued* spans.** `MIN_UTTERANCE_OVERLAP`'s own doc says so explicitly — "single-utterance takes are judged by `similarity` alone, as they always were". Every one of the six is a **single-utterance take**, so the guard never ran. `similarity` maximises over `containment`, so an utterance whose *tail* matches the next delivery scores above 0.82 however much unrelated speech precedes it, and the take is cut whole (§2's "a take is a range of whole utterances" limit, pointed the over-cutting way instead of the under-cutting way §6.6 claims).
  2. **D-366's invariant test only ever ran on two hand-picked excerpt fixtures** (`REAL_GLUED_ANCHORS`, `REAL_GLUED_ANCHOR_INTRO`), never on a whole transcript. That is the same shape of miss B-238 itself was: the pairwise predicates were swept exhaustively and the resulting *cut* was not. **A green number that measured nothing** — third time on this detector, which is why D-377 added a whole-transcript tier rather than another excerpt.
- **a second, distinct class found alongside, not counted above:** 13 more cut utterances (83.98 s of Whisper's 89.40 s "absent from the keeper") repeat *another discarded take* but not the keeper, because the ASR's segment boundary fell mid-repetition. Accepting the group still loses that speech. It is less severe (the content is genuinely redundant, just not with what survives) and needs a different fix — choosing `keep` by coverage rather than by recency — so it is recorded here and not merged into the count.
- **the phrase arm is the whole source of it, measured:** `phrase_min_words: 0` (the D-365 escape hatch) takes both backends to **0 cases / 0.00 s**, at 13 and 16 groups instead of 25 and 27. `phrase_min_words: 6` leaves 1 case each (5.48 s / 12.24 s). So this is D-365's arm admitting pairs whose redundancy is a sub-utterance phrase, which the whole-utterance take model then cannot express. Full grid in `docs/notes/retake-detection.md` §8.3.
- **fix:** not attempted here, deliberately. The obvious one — apply `MIN_UTTERANCE_OVERLAP` to single-utterance takes too — moves the group counts the **five existing corpus tests pin against Whisper**, and D-377's brief forbade touching them (`CLAUDE.md`: do not edit a failing assertion until it passes). It needs its own pass, with the recall cost measured rather than assumed: the sweep above shows the naive levers trade real catches for it. Tracked in `docs/04-roadmap.md`.
- **measured again by D-378 (2026-10-13), against hand-labelled ground truth — and the six-case count understates it.** `eval/retake/` scores the cut itself (content lost, in source seconds) rather than `word_overlap` per utterance, and **all eight corpus tasks fail its over-cut gate, on both backends**: per backend, one transcript per source, **mlx-whisper loses 60.40 s, parakeet 46.48 s** (protected content 6.18 s vs 35.54 s). Every charged range was checked against the detector's own groups and is real. Three shapes, of which the table above is only the first: (1) the six utterances that repeat nothing, all present; (2) the "straddled" class above, which in its worst form is a **kept take that is a fragment** — C040's recap keeps `"by matching each word's query against every other word's key"` and cuts both deliveries of `"So, quick recap. Attention is the model deciding how much to focus on each part of what you said"`; C038's outro keeps the fourth `"not just what it can do"` and cuts both `"and subscribe if you want more of this"`; (3) **unique speech `word_overlap` ≥ 0.5 waves through**, because shared function words or a shared tail lift a mixed utterance over the bar — C019 Whisper #37 (`"about an 80% cut from one structural change"`, riding on `"one more thing to know the notes"`), C019 Parakeet's `"This is the mistake."`, C038's welded `"corner"` and `"it so expensive"`. So applying `MIN_UTTERANCE_OVERLAP` to single-utterance takes, the fix proposed above, would clear shape 1 and leave 2 and 3: **the fix pass should be judged on `retake_eval.rs`, not on `proposed_cuts.rs`**, whose "repeats nothing" column is the proxy this eval replaces. Pinned as `expect: "fail"` tasks with a committed `baseline.json`; the `b246_tail_repeat` control is this bug's shape isolated. Detail: **D-378**, `docs/notes/retake-detection.md` §9.

## B-245 — `test_transcribe_subprocess.py`'s server-wiring stub went stale and the check it exists for stopped being made at all

status: **fixed** (2026-10-09, while landing D-374 steps 1-2) · severity: low (a test, not shipped behaviour — but it was the only guard on the B-189 regression) · area: `ai-media/test_transcribe_subprocess.py`

- **found:** 2026-10-09, running `ai-media/`'s three test files before touching `transcribe.py` for D-374. The file failed on `main`, unmodified, with `AssertionError: {... 'state': 'error', 'error': "TypeError: check_server_wiring.<locals>._stub() got an unexpected keyword argument 'start_secs'"}`. Confirmed pre-existing by running a clean `git archive HEAD` copy.
- **cause:** `check_server_wiring`'s stub for `transcribe_subprocess` named a fixed signature — `(path, model, language, word_timestamps)`. D-349 then added `start_secs` / `duration_secs` to `server.py`'s call. The stub could no longer be called, so the job recorded a `TypeError` and the assertion tripped on `state == "error"` — and the question the check exists to ask (**is `/transcribe` wired to the subprocess and not to the in-process function?**, which is B-189 itself) stopped being asked.
- **why it mattered:** B-189 was 11 GB of unreleasable `IOAccelerator (graphics)` in the uvicorn parent. This was its only automated guard, and it had been dark since D-349.
- **fix:** the stub takes `(path, **kwargs)` and records every keyword; the assertion pins the whole kwarg set. Drift still fails the test — but as a readable diff of what `server.py` now passes, rather than as a stub that cannot be invoked.
- **the lesson:** a test stub that mirrors a signature is a second copy of that signature, and it rots exactly like any other duplicate. Record what the caller passed and assert on that instead.

## B-244 — B-240's fix shipped a worse regression: a correct layout rendered as a one-glyph-wide vertical column, because `maxWidth` is a cap and cannot give a shrink-to-fit box room

status: **fixed** (same day, before reaching a render) · severity: high (total loss of the callout, and visibly broken rather than merely absent — strictly worse than the bug it replaced) · area: `packages/motion-engine/src/primitives/Layers.tsx`

- **found:** 2026-10-07, by eye, immediately after merging B-240's fix — the first live render of `c038-tricks` showed the callout "none of it is free" set as `n / o / n / e / o / f / …` running vertically off the bottom of the frame.
- **cause:** B-240 restructured the text box to be a sibling of the arm, absolutely positioned inside the stack's **zero-width** origin container, and set `width` only for the `below` placement — the two side placements kept `maxWidth` alone plus `overflowWrap: "anywhere"`. `maxWidth` is a CAP: it can shrink a box, it cannot give one room. With no explicit `width`, shrink-to-fit resolved against ~0 available space and `overflowWrap: "anywhere"` then did exactly what it was told, breaking at every character.
- **why the tests did not catch it:** B-240 extracted `layoutCallout` as a pure function and tested it hard — 49 cases, verified failing against the pre-fix geometry. The layout was never wrong. The bug lived entirely in the *consumer*, the inline style object, which had no test at all. **A pure core with a well-tested contract does not protect you if the one caller misuses it**, and an inline style in a render body is exactly the place that escapes a unit test.
- **fix:** `calloutBoxGeometry(layout)` — the style's geometry extracted as a pure function, setting a real `width` on every placement, with the cap retained alongside it. `every_placement_gets_a_real_width` pins it and was verified failing against the old conditional.
- **verified live**, not just by test: `c038-tricks` ("none of it is free") and `c038-chaiwala` ("10 cups vs 10 million") both render on one line beside their arm again.
- **the process lesson:** the subagent that wrote B-240's fix reported "a RIGHT placement is byte-identical… cap above the text's own width so it never wraps" and listed what it could not verify without a render. That claim was wrong, and it was in the half it believed it had verified — not in the half it flagged. The honest reading is that the flagged list was not the risky part; the confident claim was. Render-path work does not count as verified until something renders.

## B-243 — a big timeline's `-filter_complex` graph exceeds `ARG_MAX` and `editor_export` cannot spawn ffmpeg at all

status: **fixed** (the spawn; see the second half for what the fix then exposed) · severity: high (total failure of export, with an OS-level error that names nothing about the timeline) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/ffmpeg_run.rs`

- **found:** 2026-10-05, exporting c038's finished split-screen (D-368) — 98 clips: 77 footage + 21 graphics.
- **actual:** `failed to spawn ffmpeg: Argument list too long (os error 7)`. Nothing rendered; the error comes from the OS, not ffmpeg, so it says nothing about which part of the timeline is responsible.
- **cause:** `timelineExport.ts` passes the whole filtergraph as one argv element after `-filter_complex`. **Measured on this project: 1,476,115 bytes.** macOS's `ARG_MAX` is 1,048,576 for argv AND envp combined, so the graph alone was ~1.4× the entire limit. Each eased keyframe segment is expanded into 20 linear steps (ffmpeg has no bezier solver), so a timeline's graph grows with clips × keyframes × eased properties — 14 camera ramps × 7 properties here.
- **fix:** `run_ffmpeg` rewrites `-filter_complex <graph>` to `-filter_complex_script <file>` past 100 KB, which is what that ffmpeg flag exists for. Done at the **spawn** layer, not in `timelineExport.ts`: the limit is a property of process spawning rather than of the timeline model, the TS builder is deliberately pure and unit-testable with no filesystem, and this fixes it once for every ffmpeg caller. A `Drop` guard owns the temp file and is held across the spawn — `-filter_complex_script` makes ffmpeg read the path at startup, so deleting it earlier would be a race visible only on busy machines. The 100 KB bar is deliberately well below the OS limit (which cannot be computed reliably, since envp counts against it) so an ordinary export's argv is untouched and still reads as one copy-pasteable command line in a log.
- **verified:** 3 unit tests (small graph untouched, oversized graph spills verbatim and is cleaned up on drop, no-filtergraph argv is a no-op), plus a real 98-clip export that now spawns and runs where it previously died instantly.

### What fixing it exposed — read before using `renderer: "filter"` on a big timeline

Spawning was only the first wall. With the graph spilled, that same export ran **31 minutes at 61 % CPU and wrote zero bytes** (confirmed by reading the output file descriptor's offset, still 0). `-filter_complex_threads` is capped at 2 by **B-229** to stop a thread explosion, and one graph of this size through two threads is not a viable export.

**The answer is not to raise that cap — it is `renderer: "compositor"` (D-350),** which renders frames with the preview's own Rust compositor and hands one raw RGBA stream to ffmpeg, so no large graph exists. On the same project it immediately ran 6 parallel segment lanes (D-360) and began producing output. It also supersedes the parity bugs (B-201/B-208/B-218/B-223) that bear on `scale` and `crop_*` — exactly the fields a split-screen camera ramp animates — so for this class of timeline it is the more correct path as well as the only practical one.

**Still open, deliberately:** `editor_export` still defaults to `renderer: "filter"` and gives no warning when a timeline is far past what that path can serve. A caller finds out by waiting. Candidate fixes: pick the compositor automatically above some clip/graph-size threshold, or refuse the filter path with a named reason pointing at the alternative. Not done here because the right threshold wants measurement rather than a guess.

## B-242 — a scene's `id` is its display name, but nothing can properly set it: no Inspector row, and the one MCP tool that writes it warns that it shouldn't

status: **fixed** (2026-10-07, **D-371**) · severity: low (there was a working path, it just told you it was wrong — but see "what fixing it found", which is not low) · area: `packages/motion/src/propCatalog.ts` (`SCENE_FIELDS`), `packages/motion/src/editLinks.ts` (the new `checkSceneRename`), `packages/motion/src/motionOps.ts`, `packages/motion/src/InspectorPanel.tsx`, `motion_add_scene`/`motion_set_scene_field` in both MCP servers

- **found:** 2026-09-27, by a builder agent adding scenes to `2026-09-12-c038-mgfx`. It passed `scene_id: "c038-training"` to `motion_add_scene` and got `id: "scene-kl4e06"`.
- **actual:** `motion_add_scene` has no id parameter at all (an unknown argument is silently dropped by the MCP layer, so the caller gets no signal). The working path is `motion_set_scene_field key="id"`, which writes correctly but returns `"id" is not one of the known scene fields (dur, bg, grain, vignette, transition) — set anyway`. So the tool that ought to set the id can't, and the one that does believes it shouldn't.
- **why it matters beyond cosmetics:** the scene id IS the scene's name everywhere a person sees it — the layer panel's section headers, the scene selector, and `motion_render`'s per-scene output filenames. It is not an internal handle. Under this repo's "every feature is built for a human AND an AI" invariant it currently has neither a real GUI affordance (no Inspector row, because `SCENE_FIELDS` omits it) nor an honest MCP one.
- **deliberately not fixed on the spot:** a builder agent was driving the live app at the time, and editing `packages/motion` would have HMR-remounted its preview mid-verification.

### The fix (D-371)

`id` is in `SCENE_FIELDS` (`kind: 'string'`, label "Name (scene id)", content group), so the Inspector renders a row for it and the spurious warning cannot fire. `motion_add_scene` takes an `id`, so naming a scene is one call. Both halves of the invariant are now real: a GUI affordance and an MCP parameter, over the same `setSceneField`/`checkSceneRename` underneath.

**What the rename-safety check of this entry actually found — the part that was NOT cosmetic.** A rename was unsafe, in two ways, and the checking had to be done by reading the code rather than reasoning about it:

1. **`motion_get_edit_links` does NOT reference scenes by anything stable.** `computeEditLinks` (`packages/motion/src/editLinks.ts`) builds its whole map from the **`motionSceneId` stamp copied onto each media-pool item at render time** (D-260). That stamp is a copy of the id, not a reference to the scene, so a rename leaves it pointing at the old name: the renamed scene reads as "never rendered", and the stale stamp survives as a link to a scene that no longer exists. `renderStaleness` (`motionOps.ts`) reads the same `links[s.id]`, so a rename also silently takes a scene out of the "your renders went stale" report.
2. **`motion_render` names the output file by scene id** — `default_output_path` (`app/src-tauri/src/chroma/motion.rs`) writes `<project>.chroma/motion/renders/<id>.mp4`, D-180. So after a rename the next render writes a **different file**, while every placed Edit clip keeps reading the old one. That is exactly the failure B-219 described for a filesystem-copied project, reached by an ordinary rename instead.

**So a rename CAN orphan a placed clip, and it is refused rather than followed.** Following the references would mean renaming a file on disk, rewriting the pool item's `sourcePath` and stamp, and rewriting every placed clip's `source_path` — three layers `@apelles/motion` structurally cannot reach (D-039 forbids a tab package importing `@apelles/bridge` or `@apelles/editor`; the pool arrives as a read-only injected accessor). The refusal is `checkSceneRename`, the repo's established shape for this (`checkRemoveGap`/B-227, `checkSplit`/B-197): **one pre-flight predicate shared by the Inspector row and the MCP tool**, returning a reason that names the clips it would orphan and the two ways out. `force: true` (MCP) / a "Rename anyway" confirm button (GUI) accepts the broken link deliberately — a rule that made a rendered scene's name permanent forever would be a worse bug than this one.

**The test for "would this orphan something" is `renderStaleness`' test, not a second one:** `links[id] !== undefined && links[id].refreshedByRender !== false`. A link into a DIFFERENT project (B-219) is not a render this project owns, so renaming past it orphans nothing of ours. One rule, not two.

**Three further refusals the same read turned up**, none of which `force` lifts, because each produces a document that is simply wrong rather than a tradeoff:
- **Deleting the id.** `motion_set_scene_field key="id" value=null` deleted the key, and `schema.ts` declares `scene.id` as a required `z.string()` — the manifest would stop parsing.
- **A collision.** Two scenes sharing an id render to the same `<id>.mp4` (the second overwrites the first) and cannot be told apart by the link map, which is keyed by id.
- **An id that is not a usable filename.** `default_output_path` joins the id onto the renders directory with **no escaping at all**, so `motion_set_scene_field key="id" value="../../x"` would have written the render outside the project. Empty, whitespace-padded, `/`, `\`, `.`, `..` and control characters are all rejected.

- **verified:** 15 new `checkSceneRename` cases in `editLinks.test.ts`, 7 new op cases in `motionOps.test.ts`, 3 in `propCatalog.test.ts`; **9 of them confirmed failing against the pre-fix code** (reverted in place and re-run, not assumed). `packages/motion` 811/811, `apelles-mcp` 25 + 5 parity + 3 transport (corpus re-captured for the two reworded tools), `cargo fmt`/`clippy` clean, `tsc` 65 errors — all 65 pre-existing and in `app/src/`, none in any file this touched.
- **not verified, and could not be:** nothing was driven in the live app (another session held it). The Inspector's new `id` row, its refusal text and the "Rename anyway" button are verified by reading and by the shared predicate's unit tests, not by a screenshot of the running Inspector.

## B-241 — one bad frame latched the Motion preview forever: `@remotion/player`'s error boundary has no reset path

status: **fixed** (D-367, 2026-09-26) · severity: high (the whole Motion tab's preview, not one layer — and the only recovery was restarting the app) · area: `packages/motion/src/MotionPreview.tsx`

- **found:** 2026-09-26, live, building `c038-tpusplit`. A `graph` layer was authored with `enter` as an array instead of `{at, stagger}`, so `Graph.tsx:352` called Remotion's `interpolate` with `[NaN, NaN]` and threw: `inputRange must contain only finite numbers`.
- **expected:** fix the manifest → the preview renders again.
- **actual:** the preview stayed a black frame with an error triangle **permanently**. Correcting the layer, saving, switching scenes, switching to the Edit tab and back, and an HMR update to `Graph.tsx` itself all left it wedged; three consecutive screenshots came back byte-identical while `motion_get_state` reported `playerMounted: true`, `parseError: null`, `loadState: "ready"` — i.e. the app was healthy and only the preview was dead. The dev log confirmed no NEW error after the fix; the ORIGINAL one was simply still being displayed.
- **cause:** read `@remotion/player`'s own `error-boundary.tsx` — `hasError` is set by `getDerivedStateFromError` and cleared by **nothing**. No prop, no `key`, no imperative reset. Once caught, that boundary renders its fallback for the rest of its mounted life, and `MotionPreview` never remounted `<Player>`.
- **why B-211 did not already cover this:** B-211 hardened `Graph` against ONE known cause (dangling edge ids). It could not address the latch, which any throw from any primitive re-triggers — and this was a different cause in the same primitive.
- **fix (D-367):** `MotionPreview` now owns a `playerEpoch` key on `<Player>`, plus an `errorFallback` that reports the crash by MOUNTING (a `frameupdate`/`error` listener would miss a first-frame throw, since `getDerivedStateFromError` runs before the parent's passive effects). The next manifest edit or scene change bumps the epoch and remounts, and `initialFrame` restores the playhead. Deliberately not an immediate retry: that would re-render the same bad frame in a loop and hide the message from whoever needs to read it.
- **verified:** the wedged session recovered in place — the `graph` fork rendered at 4.4 s and the full scene at 7.2 s, no restart.

## B-240 — a `layers` callout is side-anchored and `nowrap`, and when it does not fit on the right it flips LEFT to a negative x and renders fully off-canvas, silently

status: **fixed** (2026-10-07, **D-370**) · severity: medium (silent, total loss of an authored element — no error, no clipping artefact, the callout is simply not in the frame; and it is reachable by ordinary authoring, not an edge case) · area: `packages/motion-engine/src/primitives/Layers.tsx` (the callout side-picker and its `nowrap` text)

- **found:** 2026-09-26, live, while reshaping c038's motion canvas 1920×1080 → 1252×1016 for the D-348 side-by-side. `c038-tricks` was in exactly this state after D-347's reflow: its callout had flipped left and was rendering at a negative x, entirely outside the canvas. A static audit of the same manifest had rated that scene "clean, polish only" — only the live render showed it.
- **mechanism:** the callout picks a side, then draws `nowrap`. It needs `cardW/2 + 314 + textWidth` of clear space; the picker flips to `"left"` when `cx + cardW/2 + 314 + 17·len > width − 60`. On the left it is then laid out at a negative x rather than being re-fitted, re-anchored or wrapped.
- **why a narrow canvas makes it routine:** the budget is roughly `cardW + 17 × len(callout) ≤ ~794` on a 1124-px content box. Three of this project's four `layers` scenes needed both a narrower `cardW` and a shortened callout to stay on canvas — e.g. "none of it makes inference free" had to become "none of it is free".
- **a second, smaller trap in the same primitive:** `tilt: 24` makes the near card ~7% wider than `cardW`, so a stack's practical left edge is ≈84 px, not the content box's 64.
- **note the internal width estimate is itself conservative:** the picker assumes 17 px/char at fontSize 34 (0.5em), but Kalam's real average advance is ≈0.42em, so it can flip a callout to the unusable left side even when the text would have fitted on the right.
- **fix (D-370): the third option — fall back to centring under the stack — with the other two kept as the bound rather than the fix.** The placement is now a pure, exported `layoutCallout` in `Layers.tsx` instead of an inline expression, because a geometry decision that can silently put content outside the frame deserves a test. It picks right, then left, then `below`; it clamps the anchor into the safe area; and it caps the text box's width at the measured distance from that anchor to the far margin, so the box's whole extent is provably inside the canvas **for any text length**. *Why the third and not the others:* on this very repro there is genuinely no room beside the stack (566 px of clear space, 624 px wanted by the text's near edge alone), so a clamp would have pinned the text to the frame edge on top of the stack and a wrap would have squeezed it into a zero-width column; under the stack it gets the full 1132-px content box and sets on one line. A clamp alone also cannot deliver the guarantee at all — a `nowrap` line can be wider than the canvas, so no x puts it fully on screen.
- **the width estimate is corrected too:** `CALLOUT_CHAR_WIDTH_RATIO` is now the 0.42 `Graph.tsx`'s own label fitter measures with, not the 0.5em the picker assumed.
- **a third defect found while fixing it, and fixed:** the LEFT side was not a mirror of the right at all. The text was a child of the arm's own shrink-to-fit container, so `right: len + 34` put its right edge **14 px inside the arm's start** — on top of the arm, not clear of its tip. Correcting the mirror costs the left side the 240 px of room it had been borrowing from the arm, so a callout that used to flip left and sit on its own arm now goes `below` instead. A RIGHT placement is byte-identical to pre-fix.
- **verified:** `packages/motion-engine/src/primitives/Layers.test.ts`, 49 cases, including this entry's own numbers (the pre-fix picker's flip, the pre-fix negative x, and `below` with the full content box), the 0.42-vs-0.5em case, and a sweep of 7 text lengths × 5 canvas/stack shapes all asserting the box lies inside the margins. Confirmed non-vacuous: **34 of the 49 fail** against a transcription of the pre-fix geometry put back in place. `@apelles/motion-engine` 84/84, `@apelles/motion` 787/787, `tsc -p app/tsconfig.json` unchanged at the same 65 pre-existing errors (identical error set, diffed, not counted), package `tsc` unchanged at B-232's same 12, eslint clean.
- **not verified:** nothing was rendered. The live app was in use by another session, so what a wrapped or below-the-stack callout actually looks like on the c038 canvas is still unseen.
- **deliberately left:** the `tilt: 24` trap above (the near card ~7% wider than `cardW`). It widens the stack's own footprint, not the callout's, so it can make the arm overlap a card but cannot push the text off-canvas.

## B-239 — motion primitives bake their own type size in px, and D-347's reflow scales AUTHORED text by the WIDTH factor, so a canvas that changes aspect silently inverts the type hierarchy

status: **fixed** (2026-10-09 — piece (2) done for `Plot` 2026-10-07 and for `Layers` 2026-10-09, `Matrix` audited and found to draw no type at all; piece (1) closed by **D-372**, which keeps `su` and rejects this entry's own `sy` proposal — see the two bullets at the end) · severity: low-medium (nothing crashes and nothing is lost, but a reflowed manifest comes out with captions smaller than the charts' own axis labels, which is a real quality regression that looks like "the reflow worked") · area: `packages/motion/src/manifestReflow.ts` (`EXTRA_FIELDS.text = [{key:'size', axis:'u'}]`) plus hardcoded type in `packages/motion-engine/src/primitives/` — `Plot.tsx` (28 at :265, 24 at :285/:300/:317, 26 at :349/:404), `Layers.tsx` (card label 40 / sublabel 24 / callout 34)

**This entry was filed earlier the same day with a wrong premise and is corrected here.** The original said reflow does not scale type at all and framed the problem as `Plot`-only. Both halves were wrong, and the coordinating session's own spot-check repeated the error because it verified the arithmetic without checking the text anchor. Recording that rather than quietly rewriting it: a static read of a primitive's source predicted the failure mode, and the live render showed a *different* one.

- **what is actually true.** Reflow DOES scale an authored `text.size`, by the **uniform** factor `su` (= `sx`). So authored captions shrink with canvas WIDTH. But every primitive's *internal* type — a `layers` card label, a `plot` axis tick — is a literal with no prop, no theme hook and no canvas-relative derivation, so it does not move at all.
- **the failure that produces.** c038's canvas lost 35% of its width but only 6% of its height (1920→1252, 1080→1016). Authored captions reflowed by 0.652 landed at **22–23 px** while the primitives' own fixed 24–40 px type stayed put — so supporting captions rendered *smaller than the chart's own axis labels* and the intended hierarchy inverted. Nothing overflowed; it just looked wrong in a way no static check flagged.
- **what the wrong premise predicted instead:** that `maxWidth` would scale while `size` did not, causing rewrapping and collisions. Since `maxWidth` scales by `sx` and `size` by `su`, and `su === sx`, **wrapping is identical before and after** — the predicted collisions never existed.
- **the workaround that was actually applied**, and the shape of a real fix: rescale authored `size` by **`sy`** (canvas height, 0.9407) rather than `su`. Type tracks height, not the axis that happens to have changed most. Every caption then landed 32–68 and the house scale (headline 54–72 / supporting 34–40) was preserved.
- **two separable pieces:** (1) reflow should scale `text.size` on a height-ish axis, or at minimum let the caller choose; (2) primitive-internal type needs to be canvas-relative or prop-driven so it participates at all. `Matrix` and `Graph` were not audited for the same pattern.
- **piece (2), fixed for `Plot` (2026-10-07).** The six literals are now five named constants (`PLOT_TITLE_FONT_SIZE` 28, `PLOT_ANNOTATION_FONT_SIZE` / `PLOT_BASELINE_LABEL_FONT_SIZE` 26, `PLOT_AXIS_TITLE_FONT_SIZE` / `PLOT_TICK_FONT_SIZE` 24) multiplied by one `plotTypeScale(width, height)`. *Derived from the plot's own box, not the canvas:* a plot hand-authored small on a full-size canvas has exactly the same problem as a reflowed one, and the box solves both with nothing to keep in sync — the same call `Graph.tsx` made for `graphLabelFontSize` under **B-225**, and for the same reason it is a rendering-time derivation rather than a new manifest field (so no `propCatalog.ts` entry and no MCP parameter is owed: there is no new authored value). *`min` of the two ratios,* because type cannot be stretched per axis and has to fit a box that moved on both — the tick row is width-bound, the title is bound by the top margin's height. Note that is a different question from piece (1), where a caption floating free on the canvas tracks height. Floored at `PLOT_TYPE_MIN_FONT_SIZE` 14 for the smallest role, matching `GRAPH_LABEL_MIN_FONT_SIZE`; the floor does not bind until the box is under ~58% of default, so it is nowhere near the c038 reflow's 0.652. **Exactly 1 at the primitive's own default 820×520 box**, so a plot at the default renders byte-for-byte as before; a plot whose box was *already* non-default now gets type proportional to it, which is the fix rather than a regression. `MARGIN`, `MARKER_R` and `LABEL_LIFT`/`TROUGH_LABEL_LIFT` are deliberately NOT scaled — layout geometry, not type; leaving them is conservative (more air around a shrunk label, never less) and keeps `plotLabelY`'s contract and its existing `plotLabel.test.ts` untouched.
- **verified:** `packages/motion-engine/src/primitives/Plot.test.ts`, 20 cases — the six pre-fix literals pinned, scale exactly 1 at the base box, this entry's own c038 factors (`sx` 0.6521 / `sy` 0.9407 → ticks 24 → 15.65 px, back under the 22–23 px captions), `min`-not-average, the floor, no upper cap, and a non-numeric/degenerate box falling back to 1 rather than `NaN`. Confirmed non-vacuous: **8 assertions fail** against a `plotTypeScale` stubbed back to the pre-fix constant 1. `@apelles/motion-engine` 84/84, `@apelles/motion` 787/787 (`plotLabel.test.ts` included, untouched), `tsc` introduces zero new errors in either the app project or this package.
- **not verified:** nothing was rendered — the live app was in use by another session, so a reflowed plot's new label sizes have not been seen on screen.
- **~~still open:~~ both pieces closed 2026-10-09.** The two bullets below replace this one. (`Graph` is deliberately left: its label size is already derived, by B-225, from node clearance rather than its box, so it DOES participate in a reflow — a shrunk box moves nodes closer and the fitter shrinks the labels. Its one asymmetry is that `GRAPH_LABEL_BASE_FONT_SIZE` is also a cap, so a graph given a bigger box gets no bigger labels. Noted, not filed: nothing is wrong on screen, and the fitter's input is clearance rather than a box, which is the right input for a collision.)

- **piece (1) closed by D-372 — and this entry's own proposed fix is REJECTED.** `text.size` keeps `su`. The entry's `sy` proposal was overfitted to the one reshape it was measured on: (a) the hierarchy inversion it was reacting to was piece (2), and with piece (2) landed the authored caption and a primitive's internal type scale by the same factor, so the authored ratio is preserved exactly (a c038 card label lands at 26.1 px against a 22.2 px caption — 40/34, what the author set, where pre-fix it was 1.80×); and (b) `sy` exceeds `sx` precisely when the canvas lost relatively more width, so it scales glyphs up against a `maxWidth` that scaled by `sx`. On a 16:9 → 9:16 reflow — a vertical reel, which this project does routinely — `sy` is 1.778, and a `size: 46` caption comes out at **82 px against 26 px under `su`**, i.e. certain overflow, which is B-240's failure class (content off-frame, silently) rather than this one's. The statement that replaces "type tracks height" is **`su` is the largest factor that cannot worsen any text block's wrapping** — and because `su = min(sx, sy)` it already *is* the height ratio whenever height is the binding axis. Also checked before touching the axis table, as the brief asked: `su` additionally drives `matrix.cell`, `deviceframe.scale`, `matrix.gap`, `layers.gap`, `graph.nodeR` and `claudechat.radius`, all of which genuinely want `min` — the table is per-field, so splitting type out would have been mechanically safe; it is not split because the answer for type is the same one.
  - **the rewrapping consequence, since this entry asked for it explicitly:** the entry's claim that wrapping is identical before and after **keeps holding** under `su`, exactly where it held before — every reshape with `su === sx`, c038 included. Where `su === sy < sx`, a block gets MORE characters per line, so it can only un-wrap. `maxWidth` therefore does **not** move axes: it is a width, and scaling it by anything but `sx` lets a block grow past the frame. The one residual is `px()`'s whole-pixel rounding, which can give back up to half a pixel on each side — under a percent at ordinary factors, ~4% of a line's character budget at a 4× shrink. The guarantee is exact in the factors, half-a-pixel loose in the written values, and the tests pin both bounds separately.
- **piece (2) fixed for `Layers` (2026-10-09).** The card label (40) and sublabel (24) were JSX literals and the callout (34) a bare constant; all three are now named constants (`LAYERS_LABEL_FONT_SIZE`, `LAYERS_SUBLABEL_FONT_SIZE`, `CALLOUT_FONT_SIZE`) times one `layersTypeScale(cardW, cardH)` — the same shape `plotTypeScale` has, for the same reasons: derived from the primitive's own box (a stack authored small on a full-size canvas has the identical problem), `min` of the two ratios (the label is width-bound, the label+sublabel pair height-bound), floored at `LAYERS_TYPE_MIN_FONT_SIZE` 14 for the smallest role, **exactly 1 at the default 620×110 card** so existing scenes render byte-for-byte unchanged, and no new manifest field or MCP parameter owed (there is no new authored value). The box is the CARD, not the stack: the stack's height is `n · cardH + (n−1) · gap`, so deriving type from it would shrink every label the moment an author added a fifth card. `gap`, `tilt`, the arm geometry (`CALLOUT_TEXT_OFFSET` and its three parts), the canvas margin and `borderRadius` are deliberately NOT scaled — layout, not type, the same line `plotTypeScale` draws at `MARGIN`/`MARKER_R`.
  - **the B-240/B-244 interaction, checked as the brief required.** `layoutCallout` already took `fontSize` and its whole budget is in px (the `text.length · fontSize · 0.42` line estimate and the `lines · fontSize · 1.5` block height), so `Layers` now passes the SCALED size and `Callout` renders at the same number — the size the box was laid out for and the size it is drawn at cannot drift. At the default card that product IS `CALLOUT_FONT_SIZE`, so every placement B-240/B-244 signed off is byte-identical (asserted). For a non-default card the placement can legally differ, and that is correct rather than a regression: a smaller callout needs less room, so one that would have fallen `below` can now sit beside the stack (pinned with a squat 620×66 card, where a 25-char callout goes `right` at 0.6× and `below` at 1×), and a shorter predicted block is clamped less hard by the bottom margin.
- **`Matrix` audited (2026-10-09): there is nothing to fix.** It draws no text of any kind — cells are fills plus hand-drawn borders, no labels, no ticks, no legend — so it has no baked-in type and deliberately gets no `matrixTypeScale`. Its only two lengths, `cell` and `gap`, are authored manifest fields the reflow already scales. Recorded in the primitive's own header so this is not re-audited; if labelled cells are ever added, that is when it owes a type scale. This entry's earlier "the same hardcoded-type pattern in … `Matrix`" was an assumption, never a measurement.
- **verified (this pass):** `Layers.test.ts` 77 cases (28 new), confirmed non-vacuous — **10 fail** against `layersTypeScale` stubbed back to a constant 1. `manifestReflow.test.ts` 24 cases (12 new for D-372) over eight reshapes including the two extremes, confirmed non-vacuous the only way a no-code-change decision can be: flipping the axis table to `'y'` **fails 6 of 24**, the pre-existing "scales a font size … UNIFORMLY, never per axis" among them. `@apelles/motion-engine` 112/112, `@apelles/motion` 823/823, `tsc` unchanged at 65 pre-existing `app/src` errors.
- **not verified (this pass):** nothing was rendered — the owner was using the app — so a reflowed `layers` stack's new label sizes, and the callout placements that a non-default card now chooses, have not been seen on screen.
- **related, same pass, NOT a bug:** `Matrix`'s `fill-in` preset ignores `values` entirely — only `heatmap` reads them (`cellFill`, `Matrix.tsx:95-112`). Documented behaviour working as designed, but a live trap: "tidying" a `heatmap` into a `fill-in` deletes its data with no error.
- **related, same pass, NOT a bug:** `emphasis` `preset:"ring"` is an expanding *ping* at radius `1.65 × max(w,h)`, not an enclosing ring. On a 1.23-aspect canvas any box large enough to enclose a line of text yields a circle wider than the frame. `preset:"scribble"` is the one that draws a held ellipse fitted to the box.

## B-238 — `editor_detect_retakes` silently proposed DELETING unique, never-repeated speech: a take glued from several utterances matched on one of them and offered all of them for the cut — 259.8 s across two real transcripts, including one video's own opening hook

status: **fixed** (2026-09-25, **D-366**) · severity: **blocker** — this is the worst failure mode this feature has. Every other retake bug so far (B-198, B-237) was a *missed* detection, which leaves a stumble in the video and wastes the owner's time. This one proposed destroying content the speaker only said once, silently, inside a range the Recut panel's Cut button and `editor_ripple_delete_ranges` would have removed on one click — and it did so while every test was green and the feature had just been reported correct twice · area: `crates/apelles-speech/src/retake.rs` (the anchor's missing half of the `MIN_UTTERANCE_OVERLAP` guard) — NOT the sweep layer (B-237's area) and NOT the predicates (`similarity` / `is_phrase_repeat` are untouched and correct)

- **found:** 2026-09-25, by the owner asking, after two sessions of celebrated retake fixes, whether the tool had actually cut anything it shouldn't — then diffing a resulting cut against the original transcript. Two cases were confirmed by hand; a sweep over both real fixture transcripts then showed they were the rule, not the exception. Full measurement: `docs/notes/retake-detection.md` §6.
- **repro:** `detect_retakes` on `crates/apelles-speech/tests/fixtures/A001_09122319_C038.json` with default params.
  - **expected:** group 2 proposes cutting only `#30` (210.26–222.74 s), the utterance that genuinely repeats the keeper's line.
  - **actual:** it proposed 190.52–222.74 s — `#28` ("place."), `#29` ("Today I actually want to show you why that's true, what's happening technically that makes") and `#30`. `#29` is a 6-second setup line sharing 0.133 of its vocabulary with the keeper and repeating nothing. **This is D-364's own "decisive proof" case, shipped and celebrated as correct.**
  - **and via the phrase arm, worse:** group 0 proposed 2.04–32.74 s — the Nvidia sentence and the \$20-billion sentence, i.e. the video's entire cold open — because `#2` ("and here's the actually interesting part") genuinely repeats in `#4` and the other two were glued in front of it.
- **cause, measured:** a group discards each non-kept take **whole**, and both D-327's span gluing and D-365's phrase arm match a span on *part* of itself — `containment` scores a span by its best matching window and ignores the rest (bounded only by the 3× length ratio), and `is_phrase_repeat` needs one shared run anywhere in it. D-327 had already built the guard for exactly this failure mode, `MIN_UTTERANCE_OVERLAP`, but applied it only to the **candidate** side, deliberately exempting the anchor on the reasoning that *"a junk anchor is self-limiting […] because nothing later will match it."* **That reasoning is false**, and it is the whole bug. Over both transcripts: 17 of 22 groups had a glued anchor and 16 of those 17 were carrying unique content. The matched takes were never wrong — they already pass the guard.
- **fix (D-366):** `anchor_is_justified` applies the same bar to the anchor, referenced to the **union** of the deliveries that matched it (per-take referencing would reject genuine glue — C040 `#9` scores 0.125 against delivery two and 0.875 against the union, its repeat having landed in delivery three), and an unjustified chain is **rejected rather than trimmed**, letting the anchor loop reach the justified utterance and explore it properly. A member must also carry `min_words` distinct words before its overlap fraction is believed, since over two words that fraction can only be 0, 0.5 or 1.
- **effect:** proposed cut seconds across both fixtures **441.4 s → 181.6 s**; all 259.8 s of the difference repeated nothing. C038 still finds all 11 groups. C040 goes 11 → 7 — mostly chains *merging* now the junk prefixes are gone, plus **one group dropped that was itself a false positive**: gluing a 20-second "the middle." fragment onto the anchor had stretched the time window far enough to match `#47`–`#49` against `#51`'s unrelated advice, proposing 38 s of real explanation for deletion. So the glued anchor was manufacturing matches as well as over-claiming cuts. No output-shape change, so no MCP parity re-capture.
- **the trustworthiness question, answered plainly:** any cut range `editor_detect_retakes` proposed **before 2026-09-25** should be treated as possibly over-claiming — this was not two unlucky instances but the default behaviour for any multi-utterance take, which is most of them. The *groupings* it reported were sound; the *ranges* were not. Anything already applied to a real timeline in those sessions is worth re-checking against the transcript.
- **the process lesson:** "the group is found" and "the range it offers to delete is right" are two separate claims, and only the first had ever been measured — twice, in two consecutive passes that both reported success. Recorded at the top of `docs/notes/retake-detection.md` as its fourth trap.

## B-237 — `editor_detect_retakes`'s whole-track sweep is scoped PER CLIP, so most real retakes that span a clip boundary are structurally invisible to it — measured at 6 of 7 real cases on a real project

status: **fixed** (2026-09-24, **D-364**) · severity: high (this was the owner's own diagnosis — "the algorithm is broken cant take retakes at all" — and it was confirmed: a real human re-edit found 30 spans, 96.5s, that the tool never flagged) · area: `packages/editor/src/useEditorControl.ts` (`resolveRetakeArgs`, scopes the transcript view to `clipSourceRangeSecs(c, fps)` — one clip's own trimmed range, not the track); `packages/editor/src/recutSweep.ts` (the whole-track sweep that calls it once per clip); NOT `crates/apelles-speech/src/retake.rs` (the grouping algorithm itself checks out against the numbers, see below)

- **found:** 2026-09-24, by comparing the owner's manual re-edit of `2026-09-12-c038-mgfx` (77 clips, ~7:19) against the same timeline after `editor_detect_silences`/`editor_detect_retakes` had already run (94 clips, ~8:41). Diffed in source-frame space, cross-referenced against the RAW whole-file transcript (`editor_get_transcript`, not the per-clip-mapped `editor_get_timeline_transcript`, which double-counts a segment once per clip it overlaps and looked like a Whisper bug before the raw transcript ruled that out). Full methodology, the real similarity numbers, and the per-case clip-count table: `docs/notes/retake-detection.md` §4.
- **root cause, measured, not inferred:** the whole-track sweep runs retake detection **once per clip**, each call's transcript view restricted to that one clip's own source range (`clipSourceRangeSecs`). When a clip is shorter than the utterance it's part of — routine after an earlier fine-grained silence cut; this project has clips as short as 0.25s and 0.58s — the two halves of a real restart land in *different* clips' views, and no single call ever sees both halves to compare them. Checked directly: **6 of 7 real retakes the owner cut by hand span 2-5 original clips each; the one retake the sweep DID catch is also the one whose two takes happened to sit inside a single, less-fragmented clip.** Not a coincidence — flipping that one variable flipped the outcome every time it was checked.
- **the grouping algorithm itself is not the (main) problem.** `crates/apelles-speech/src/retake.rs`'s span/containment logic, run directly on real numbers from this footage, correctly scores a same-clip restart at 0.844 (above the 0.82 bar). One separate, genuinely hard case was found where the algorithm DOES see both takes (single clip) and still misses at 0.495 similarity — a stumble on a two-word technical term inside two otherwise-different sentences, not a repeated line — recorded in the note as a real, harder, *different* limitation of "same line again" as the detection model, not this bug.
- **~~not fixed here~~ — fixed 2026-09-24 by D-364**, along exactly the lines this entry proposed. Detection's unit is now a **run**: consecutive analysable clips sharing a `source_path`, moving forward through it, separated by at most `window_secs` of removed material — the reconstruction of one continuous recording that a silence cut chopped up. `detect_retakes` is called once per run over the merged utterance list, and a found group's takes (absolute source seconds) are mapped back onto the clips and frames they land in. New pure module `packages/editor/src/recutRuns.ts`; the stateful merge is `runTranscriptView` in `darkRecovery.ts`, next to the per-clip view it wraps, so the Recut panel and the MCP tool share it the way they already shared `clipTranscriptView`.
  - **What did NOT widen:** the merged list is the union of the clips' own filtered, D-349-spliced views, so material an earlier cut removed still contributes nothing, and the D-349 scan/recovery is unchanged (still per clip, same keys, same cost). Overlapping segments are deduped — one segment across two clips of a run is one utterance, not two.
  - **The single-clip call widens too, deliberately** (D-364 states why): `editor_detect_retakes(track, clip)` reads the clip's whole run and reports the groups that touch that clip, carrying `readAcrossClips` when it did. One cache key per run means a single-clip answer and a sweep cannot disagree about the same material.
  - **A take that spans clips comes back as one range per clip** (`clips` + `segments`); the flat `startFrame`/`endFrame` is kept for a single-clip take and deliberately omitted for a straddling one, so nothing can pass a clamped range to `editor_ripple_delete_ranges` and quietly under-cut. The Recut panel's Cut button passes every segment of a ticked row.
  - **Regression test built from this entry's own first table row** — the 210-230 s restart across clips including the real 0.25 s and 0.58 s lengths, second take straddling a boundary. Against the pre-fix per-clip scoping the sweep answers "no retake groups anywhere on this track"; with the fix it returns the group with both of the straddling take's ranges. `recutRuns.test.ts` (14) + 4 new op-layer cases in `recutSweep.dom.test.tsx`.
  - **~~Still not solved, and still a different problem~~ — the eighth case (0.495 similarity on a fumbled two-word technical term) is fixed too, by D-365 (2026-09-24), in a separate pass.** It was never a scoping bug and D-364 did not touch it. What reaches it is a **second, independent detection signal** beside the edit-distance one: a repeated, content-bearing word n-gram — the "rough copy" property of a reparandum/repair, the established non-ML signal for exactly this disfluency. A pair matched by *either* arm is a group; `similarity`'s 0.82 still means what it always meant, and `phrase_min_words: 0` turns the new arm off. Measured on two whole real transcripts (187 segments, 1,671 s, 698 utterance pairs): **22 pairs newly admitted, 21 of them real retakes the tool had been missing, 1 a false positive** — a deliberate parallel construction, disclosed and pinned rather than tuned away, because no threshold separated it from a genuine repair without losing several. Four more rows of this entry's own table are among the 21. Full measurement: `docs/notes/retake-detection.md` §5; the tradeoff and what must NOT be claimed about negation: **D-365**.

## B-236 — a gap left by a manual split on the Edit timeline can't be selected/deleted through the normal gap-click UI
