- **expected:** `scale` ramps 1→2 linearly across the whole 0..100 span, unaffected by an unrelated `opacity` key in the middle of it — the contract `timelineExport.ts` has always had (it filters every key by `hasOwnProperty(param)` before interpolating, so each param sees only its own keys) and the one an exported file really produces.
- **actual:** `scale` holds flat at 1.0 up to frame 50, then jumps and holds flat at 2.0 — a step function. The preview shows no zoom at all; the export of the identical project shows the correct smooth zoom.
- **cause:** `resolve_clip_transform_unfaded` resolved every field out of ONE call to `chroma::keyframes::interpolate`, which brackets by frame across ALL keys and then applies this module's documented rule "a field present in only one of the two bracketing keys is held from that key." For frame 25 the bracket is 0→50; only the low key names `scale`, so `scale` is *held* at 1.0. For frame 75 the bracket is 50→100; only the high key names it, so it is held at 2.0. That rule is correct for mask/relight geometry (D-034), where every key is written by one gesture and carries the same field set — it is simply not a per-property resolver, and nothing had ever fed it per-property data before.
- **fix (D-208):** a second entry point, `chroma::keyframes::interpolate_param(keyframes, frame, name)` — filter to the keys that actually define `name`, THEN bracket and lerp, holding outside that param's own range; same `lerp_value`, so `rotation`'s shortest-arc rule still applies. `resolve_clip_transform_unfaded` resolves each of its eleven fields through it. `interpolate` is deliberately left untouched and remains the mask/relight resolver: its union-and-hold rule is that path's documented, tested contract, not a bug there. Byte-identical results for any clip whose keys all carry the same params — i.e. every keyframe the pre-D-208 whole-clip button ever wrote.
- **verification:** the failing test above now passes, plus `an_unkeyed_param_keeps_its_static_value_on_a_keyframed_clip`, five new `chroma::keyframes` per-param tests (one of which pins that `interpolate` really does still differ, so the two resolvers cannot be "simplified" back into one by accident, and one proving they agree for complete keys), and — the strongest — `the_preview_really_animates_one_keyed_property_and_holds_the_rest`, a real resolve-then-composite **pixel** test through the same pair `composite_video_frame` runs per frame, sampled at frame 25 *inside the diverging bracket* (endpoints alone would have passed either way — the first draft of that test made exactly that mistake and was rewritten). Both new `chroma::edit` tests were re-confirmed to FAIL against the pre-fix resolver by temporarily restoring it. `cargo test -p apelles --lib chroma::` 150 passed / 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (`chroma::project::tests::track_resolution_opaque_top_wins_across_two_video_tracks`, confirmed failing on the clean baseline too).

## B-095 — `editor_export`'s ffmpeg compiler ignores `opacity` and `rotation` completely — not just their keyframes, their STATIC values too — and animates only `position_x`/`position_y`/`scale`, so a half-transparent or rotated clip exports fully opaque and upright

status: fixed (2026-09-08, D-215) · severity: high (silent wrong output in the one tool that produces a real file: `opacity` and `rotation` are first-class `Clip` fields, real Inspector controls, real `editor_set_clip_transform` params and — as of D-208 — properties the GUI now shows a keyframe stopwatch for, and none of that reached an exported file) · area: `packages/editor/src/timelineExport.ts` (`buildClipFilterChain`)
- **found:** 2026-09-08, while auditing the export compiler's per-param keyframe coverage for D-208 (to confirm which properties the new per-property diamonds could honestly claim to animate). `grep` for `opacity`/`rotation` in `timelineExport.ts` returned **nothing at all** — they were not in the filter chain in any form, static or animated. Only `position_x`/`position_y` (`positionExpr`) and `scale` (`scaleExpr`, added by B-090) built keyframe expressions; the four crop insets were read but only as static values.
- **repro (pre-fix):** set a clip's `opacity` to 0.5 (or `rotation` to 45) in the Inspector — the live preview honours it, `chroma_timeline_get` reports it — then `editor_export`. The output file showed the clip fully opaque and unrotated. Keyframing either property (one diamond click, D-208) made no difference: the animation was absent from the export for the same reason the static value was.
- **expected:** every transform property the live preview composites and the Inspector exposes reaches the export, statically at minimum, and animates when keyframed — the standing "same doc ⇒ same picture" expectation, and the same bar B-090 was fixed to.
- **cause:** the two fields were simply never implemented in this compiler. D-196's own FCPXML interchange table had already noted it in passing for rotation ("MORE complete than `timelineExport.ts`'s own ffmpeg compiler, which never implemented rotation at all") without a bug entry of its own.
- **fix (D-215):** `buildClipFilterChain` now emits, only when a clip actually needs them (identity-preserving — a clip untouched by either field compiles byte-identically to before):
  - `format=rgba` (both effects below need a real alpha plane a plain decoded frame doesn't have),
  - `rotate=angle='(<deg-expr>)*PI/180':fillcolor=black@0.0` for `rotation` (static or keyframed; verified empirically against the Rust compositor's own `imageproc::rotate_about_center` that the two agree on both sign/direction and on keeping the original frame's own dimensions — no negation, no `ow`/`oh` needed),
  - `geq=r='r(X,Y)':g='g(X,Y)':b='b(X,Y)':a='alpha(X,Y)*(<alpha-expr>)'` for `opacity` — **not** `colorchannelmixer=aa=<expr>`, the shape this bug originally suggested: verified empirically that `colorchannelmixer`'s options flatly reject a `t`-based expression ("Undefined constant... in 't,...'"), unlike `scale`/`crop`/`rotate`. `geq` is the filter that actually supports a time-varying per-pixel expression, and its time variable is spelled `T` (uppercase) — also a real trap, since every other filter here uses lowercase `t`.
  - The alpha expression is `opacity × fade`, mirroring `resolve_clip_transform`'s own composition (D-147) and `buildTextDrawtextStep`'s existing `alphaExpr` exactly — this **also** fixes a previously-unfixed adjacent gap: a VIDEO clip's own fade handle (D-207, real in the GUI on every clip, video or audio) only ever reached the exported EMBEDDED AUDIO, never the picture, since there was no picture-opacity filter step of any kind to fold it into.
  - `eval=frame`/no-eval-needed established empirically per filter, not assumed: `rotate`'s `angle` and `geq`'s `alpha_expr` both re-evaluate every frame with no extra flag (unlike `scale`/`crop`, whose default `eval=init` is the B-090 trap).
- **verification:** three new real-ffmpeg pixel tests in `timelineExport.ffmpeg.test.ts` (mirroring B-090's own methodology — a decoded pixel, not a string match): a keyframed opacity ramp sampled near-full and near-zero; a static 90° rotation moving an asymmetric top-left marker to top-right (the exact direction confirmed empirically first, not assumed); a video clip's fade-in handle sampled dark-then-lit. `npm test --workspace @apelles/editor`: 694/694 (was 691 pre-fix, +3; every pre-existing test, including the pure string-match `timelineExport.test.ts` suite, is unchanged — confirming the identity-preserving claim above for every clip that doesn't touch either field). `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/editor` clean.
- **still open, deliberately not folded in here:** crop's four insets remain STATIC-only in export — `hasKeyframesFor(clip, 'crop_left')` etc. is never checked, so a keyframed crop animates in the live preview (`resolve_clip_transform` resolves it) but exports frozen at whichever value the clip's base fields hold. Filed separately as B-098 rather than absorbed, matching this bug's own original discipline (it was filed apart from D-208 for the identical reason) — same `eval=frame`-on-a-time-varying-`crop=` shape `scaleExpr` and this fix's own `rotate=` already established, next in line to reuse it.

## B-068 — The solo-scene transport bar (D-181) let a click "see through" it to select/drag the canvas underneath
status: fixed (2026-09-06, D-182) · severity: medium (silent wrong-target mutation — a click meant for the transport moved/selected canvas content instead, with no visible error) · area: `packages/motion/src/MotionCanvasOverlay.tsx`, `packages/motion/src/MotionPreview.tsx`
- **found:** 2026-09-06, live, while testing D-182's own per-card drag — clicking the D-181 transport's scrubber unexpectedly selected and moved the whole `layers` stack rendered behind it.
- **repro:** solo a scene (D-181), click anywhere on the custom transport bar at the bottom of the preview.
- **expected:** the transport's own control (scrubber/play button) responds; nothing on the canvas is touched.
- **actual:** the click "saw through" the transport bar to the canvas layer rendered at that exact pixel, selecting AND dragging it (a zero-delta drag, since the pointer never moved, but still committed via the existing "always commit on pointerup" convention).
- **cause:** `MotionCanvasOverlay.tsx`'s hit-tests (`findLayer`/`findLayerItem`) deliberately walk the WHOLE `elementsFromPoint` stack at a point (needed to see through `data-motion-layer`'s own `display:contents` wrapper) — a side effect nothing exercised before D-181 put an OPAQUE sibling on top of the canvas for the first time.
- **fix:** a `data-motion-transport` marker on the transport bar (`MotionPreview.tsx`) and one check at the top of `onPointerDown` — `e.target.closest('[data-motion-transport]')` bails before any hit-testing. `e.target` (real stacking-aware pointer target), not `elementsFromPoint`, is the right tool for "was this actually our own chrome."
- **verification:** live, in `app/motion-harness.html` — reproduced the bug pre-fix (clicking the scrubber selected the layer, manifest went dirty), confirmed fixed post-fix (clicking the scrubber only moves the scrubber, no selection, no dirty flag).

## B-077 — The Edit-tab GUI (transport bar, filmstrip/waveform width, gap detection, ripple/insert math) mis-converts a clip's `duration`/`source_start` at the WRONG frame rate — the same B-075 bug, everywhere else it appears
status: fixed (2026-09-07, D-194) · severity: high (every displayed clip/timeline duration, gap boundary, insertion snap, and ripple-shift amount was silently wrong for any clip whose native rate differs from the project's `timelineFps` — B-075 only fixed the export compiler, not the live GUI these numbers actually come from) · area: `packages/editor/src/timeline.ts` (`endFrame` and everything that calls it), `packages/editor/src/TimelinePane.tsx`, `packages/editor/src/marquee.ts`
- **found:** 2026-09-07, live, a real project with `timelineFps()` defaulting to 24 (unset `rate`) and one clip at 2113 native frames @ 44.128089105464674fps (real duration 47.86s) — the GUI's transport bar displayed **00:01:28:00** (88s), exactly `2113 / 24`, nothing to do with the clip's real length.
- **repro:** put a clip whose `source_fps` differs from the timeline's own `timelineFps()` on the timeline; read its displayed duration, or the timeline's own total duration, or drop/drag a clip near it.
- **expected:** every displayed/derived duration reflects the clip's REAL length (`duration` source frames ÷ its own `source_fps`, converted to the project's timeline-frame grid), matching what `timelineExport.ts` already got right after B-075.
- **actual:** `endFrame(c) { return c.start_frame + c.duration; }` added `start_frame` (timeline frames) and `duration` (source frames, per `apelles-timeline::Clip`'s own doc) directly, with no fps conversion — correct only when a clip's native rate happens to equal the project's, which is exactly why ordinary same-fps footage never caught this. Nearly every position-deriving function in `timeline.ts` routes through `endFrame` (gap detection, insertion snapping, ripple-shift amounts, sync-lock straddle checks, the trim clamps) and inherited the same wrongness; `TimelinePane.tsx` additionally divided `clip.duration`/`clip.source_start` by the single project-wide `fps` directly (not the clip's own `source_fps`) for filmstrip/waveform fetch ranges and drag-preview widths.
- **cause:** B-075 (D-187, same session) added `Clip.source_fps` and used it correctly, but scoped the fix to `timelineExport.ts` alone (the only place a real ffmpeg failure had surfaced it) — its own bug entry explicitly flagged "everywhere else it appears" as still open. Nothing else in the codebase had been re-audited against the field once it existed.
- **fix:** `endFrame(c, fps)` now converts `c.duration` through `c.source_fps ?? fps` before adding it to `start_frame`; `fps` (the project's own `timelineFps(tl)`) threads into every function that combines a `start_frame`-space position with a `duration`/`source_start`-space quantity — `trackDuration`, `timelineDuration`, `computeInsertion`/`resolveClipLanding` (now take the real clip, not a bare duration number), `nextAppendFrame`, `gapAt`, `clipAt`, `findStraddlingSyncLockedTrack`, `collectSyncLinkedClips`, `syncLinkedClipIds[AtPosition]`, the two trim clamps, and `applyOp`'s `add_clip`/`move`/`trim_start`/`trim_end`/`split`/`remove_gap` cases. `trim_start`/`split` needed a real split (not just an fps parameter): the UI's own drag delta/offset is timeline-native, applied to `start_frame` unconverted but to `source_start`/`duration` via its source-frame equivalent — the pre-fix code applied the SAME raw delta to all three. `TimelinePane.tsx`'s filmstrip/waveform/drag-overlay props switched from `/ fps` to `/ (clip.source_fps ?? fps)`. See D-194 for the full design writeup (why "convert at every consumption site," matching B-075, was chosen over "normalize duration to timeline frames at clip-creation time") and the real persistence gap this pass also closed (`Clip.source_fps` didn't exist on the Rust struct, so it silently vanished on every `chroma_timeline_set`/`_get` round trip — B-075's fix would have stopped working after the first save of any session).
- **verification:** `npm test --workspace @apelles/editor` — 335/335 (was 324; 11 new tests in a `B-077 — mixed native-fps clips` block, pinning the exact live repro numbers and a clean 48fps-on-24fps ratio for `add_clip`/`move` ripple, `computeInsertion`/`gapAt`/`clipAt`, and `trim_start`/`trim_end`/`split`). `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/editor` clean. `cargo test -p apelles-timeline` 129/129 (128 pre-existing + 1 new, pinning `source_fps`'s serde round trip).

## B-079 — The live Rust playback/preview engine (`Track::clip_at`, `clip_spans_from`, `Track::duration`, and `chroma::audio.rs`'s inline position math) has the SAME `duration`/`start_frame` unit conflation as B-075/B-077 — found during that audit, not fixed
status: fixed (2026-09-07, D-200) · severity: medium-high (a mixed-native-fps clip's actual video scrub/preview frame, audio decode length, duck-envelope timing, and the timeline-switcher's displayed duration were all wrong, independently of B-077's GUI-edit-model fix — a real, reachable defect on the live playback path, not a hypothetical — plausibly the root cause, or a contributing cause, of the SAME session's separately-reported "live preview shows the AFTER clip full-bleed instead of stacked with BEFORE" — see D-199/`docs/notes/preview-canvas-boundary.md`) · area: `crates/apelles-timeline/src/lib.rs` (`Track::clip_at`, `Track::clip_spans_from`, `Track::duration`, `Clip::end_frame`), `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/edit.rs` (`chroma_timeline_frame`/`timeline_frame`, `resolve_track_duck`, `resolve_audio_track_positions`), `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/audio.rs` (`chroma_audio_play`)
- **found:** 2026-09-07, live, during the B-077 audit — checking "does the live Rust preview/scrubbing path need the same fix" (as instructed) surfaced that it does, and that the defect is broader than just the preview: `Track::clip_at(&self, timeline_frame: i64) -> Option<(&Clip, i64)>` computes `(c, c.source_start + (timeline_frame - c.start_frame))` — the identical B-075/B-077 conflation, with no `source_fps` conversion — and is used by BOTH `chroma_timeline_frame`'s video-preview decode path (`resolve_visible_video_layers_at`/`resolve_video_clip_at`) AND `chroma::audio.rs`'s own audio-clip-at-playhead lookup (`chroma_audio_play`, line ~288). `Track::clip_spans_from` (the duck-envelope trigger boundaries) and `Track::duration` (the `chroma_timeline_list`/`TimelineSummary` display the timeline switcher shows) both call `Clip::end_frame()` — same plain `start_frame + duration` addition. `chroma::audio.rs` additionally REIMPLEMENTS the same math inline twice more (`chroma_audio_play`'s embedded-audio and audio-track branches: `source_frame = clip.source_start + elapsed_frames`, `remaining_frames = clip.end_frame() - start_frame`) rather than going through `Track::clip_at`.
- **repro:** play/scrub a timeline with a clip whose `source_fps` differs from the project's; the decoded video frame, the audio actually heard, its fade/duck timing, and the switcher's displayed duration for that timeline are all computed from the unconverted, wrong `source_frame`/`remaining_frames`.
- **expected:** the same fps-aware conversion B-077 gave the GUI/MCP edit model (`source_fps ?? timeline_fps`) applied to every one of these Rust-side position lookups.
- **cause:** this Rust crate's own frame-resolution methods predate `source_fps` entirely (it didn't exist until B-075) and were never revisited once it did — B-077's audit found them but they are OUT OF SCOPE for that pass: unlike the Rust crate's `trim_start`/`trim_end`/`split`/`move_clip` (confirmed dead code — every real edit, GUI or MCP, goes through `@apelles/editor`'s `applyOp` + `chroma_timeline_set`, never these Rust ops directly), `clip_at`/`clip_spans_from`/`Track::duration` ARE on the live path, so this is a real bug, not a documentation nit — it is being filed rather than fixed in the same pass because fixing it correctly means threading a new `timeline_fps: f64` parameter through methods with ~30 existing Rust unit-test call sites, touches the real-time audio mixer's actual sound output (a much higher-stakes surface to change under the same pass as an unrelated GUI fix), and deserves its own focused verification (a real audio/video output diff, not just unit assertions) rather than a rushed addition here.
- **fix (D-200):** added `Timeline::fps(&self) -> f64` (mirrors `timeline.ts`'s
  `timelineFps` — `rate.num/rate.den` when both positive, else a new
  `DEFAULT_FPS: f64 = 24.0`) and `source_frames_to_timeline`/
  `timeline_frames_to_source` (mirror `sourceFramesToTimeline`/
  `timelineFramesToSource` exactly — same formula, same rounding). Added
  `Clip::end_frame_at(&self, fps: f64) -> i64` alongside the existing plain
  `end_frame()` (kept, unchanged, re-documented as "for this crate's own
  confirmed-dead editing ops only"). `Track::duration`/`clip_at`/`clip_spans_from`
  all gained an `fps: f64` parameter and route through the new fps-aware
  arithmetic; `Timeline::duration`/`resolve_video_clip_at`/
  `resolve_visible_video_layers_at` compute `self.fps()` once and thread it
  through, with unchanged PUBLIC signatures. `Track::gap_at` (the dead
  `remove_gap` op's own lookup) is deliberately left fps-naive, paired with the
  unchanged `end_frame()`. `resolve_audio_track_positions` now returns the
  SOURCE FRAME `Track::clip_at` already resolves correctly instead of discarding
  it — its caller, `chroma_audio_play`, used to silently RE-DERIVE it with a
  second, fps-naive `clip.source_start + elapsed_frames` formula, which is
  deleted in favor of the resolver's own (now correct) value. Both
  `remaining_frames` computations in `chroma_audio_play` (embedded-video-audio
  and audio-track) now use `end_frame_at(fps)`, `fps` from a new
  `chroma::edit::timeline_fps()` helper. `resolve_track_duck`'s
  `clip_spans_from` call is fps-corrected too. One incidental call-site fix:
  `crates/apelles-project/src/manifest.rs`'s `append_media_clip` (Colorist's "add
  to grading" convenience) needed `Track::duration`'s new `fps` argument.
- **a TS mirror, fixed in the SAME change as instructed by this entry's own prior
  note:** `packages/editor/src/clipKeyframes.ts::clipSourceFrame` now takes a
  `fps: number` parameter and converts via `timelineFramesToSource` (B-077),
  exactly mirroring `Track::clip_at`'s now-fixed formula — fixed together with
  the Rust half specifically to avoid the authoring/playback desync this entry
  warned a TS-only fix would cause. `EditorInspectorPanel.tsx` (the only caller)
  passes `timelineFps(timeline)`.
- **verification:** `cargo test -p apelles-timeline` 137/137 (129 pre-existing + 8
  new, a `b079_mixed_native_fps` test module — `end_frame_at` conversion/
  identity/fallback, `Track::clip_at`/`duration`/`clip_spans_from` at a clean
  48fps-on-24fps ratio, `Timeline::fps`'s rate-field/malformed/default cases,
  `resolve_visible_video_layers_at` resolving a mixed-fps layer end to end).
  `cargo test -p apelles --lib` 146/146, `cargo test -p apelles-project` 52/52 —
  every existing fixture in both suites is same-native-fps, where the fix is a
  strict identity, so no existing expected number changed. `cargo clippy -p
  apelles-timeline -p apelles --all-targets -D warnings` clean; `apelles-project`
  has 15 PRE-EXISTING clippy errors (confirmed via `git stash` present in
  identical count/location on `main`, none touching the one line this pass's
  `append_media_clip` fix changed) — left alone, not folded into this fix's
  diff. `cargo fmt --check` confirmed clean on every line this pass added or
  changed (pre-existing, unrelated drift elsewhere in the same files, confirmed
  present on `main` before this branch, deliberately
  left alone — same discipline D-193's own verification note used).
  `packages/editor`: `clipKeyframes.test.ts`'s new "B-079 — mixed native-fps
  clips" block (3 tests) + the whole suite at 360/360, `tsc` clean. See D-200
  for the complete design writeup.
- **roadmap:** `docs/04-roadmap.md` item 19, closed.

## B-080 — Switching or creating a timeline while an edit's debounced save is still pending silently drops that edit — never reaches disk, never reachable again in memory either

status: **fixed (2026-09-10, D-308)** · severity: high (silent data loss on the Edit tab's own multi-timeline feature — no error, no warning, the app looked completely normal both before and after) · area: `packages/editor/src/timelineStore.ts` (`flushPendingSave`/`trackSave`/`_flushSave`, `createTimeline`, `setActiveTimeline`, `restoreSnapshot`), `packages/editor/src/TimelineSwitcher.tsx`, `app/src/store/useSessionStore.ts` (the project axis)
- **found:** 2026-09-07, live, during D-195 Task 3's own multiple-timelines verification (`docs/notes/timeline-editing-feature-gap-analysis.md`'s "needs live verification" item) — extended the D-142 browser harness (`app/harness.html`+`app/src/harness-main.tsx`) to mount `TimelineSwitcher` alongside `TimelinePane` with a real in-memory multi-timeline fake backend (mirroring `chroma::edit`'s `chroma_timeline_list`/`_create`/`_set_active`/`_get`/`_set` exactly, including `_set`'s real "always writes onto whichever timeline is ACTIVE, never by matching the posted timeline's own id" behavior) and drove it with real Chromium `PointerEvent`s via chrome-devtools MCP.
- **repro (exact, reproduced live in the harness):** on timeline A (active), call `applyOp` with any edit (e.g. `add_track`) — this schedules `_flushSave` `SAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS` (400ms) later via the module-level `saveTimer`. Before that timer fires, switch the active timeline to B (`setActiveTimeline`, e.g. clicking another tab) or create a new one (`createTimeline`, e.g. the "+" tab). Wait past 400ms. Timeline A's edit is gone — not on disk (the fake backend, mirroring the real `chroma_timeline_set`, never received it), and not recoverable from memory either (the store's `timeline` field has already been overwritten by B's own content via `setActiveTimeline`'s `load()`). Confirmed both ways: A's track count reverts to its pre-edit count, and B is untouched (not corrupted with A's stale edit either) — the edit is simply discarded, nowhere.
- **expected:** an edit made just before switching timelines either (a) is flushed to disk before the switch proceeds, or (b) if that's not chosen, at minimum the app warns / the switch waits — never a silent, un-flagged loss. The **happy path** (switch timelines with >400ms since the last edit) is unaffected and verified correct: `TimelineSwitcher`'s "+" tab, tab-click switching, and both timelines' own independent content (persistence AND non-bleed) all work exactly as designed once the debounce window has already elapsed — this bug is specifically about the RACE, not the feature's basic correctness.
- **cause:** `applyOp` (`timelineStore.ts`) debounces its own `_flushSave()` (`invoke('chroma_timeline_set', {timeline: get().timeline})`) by `SAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS` = 400ms via a single module-level `saveTimer`, deliberately (a documented perf fix, see the surrounding comment: "a full `chroma_timeline_get` refetch after every single debounced save... was pure redundant latency"). `restoreSnapshot` (undo/redo) is careful to `clearTimeout(saveTimer)` before restoring a snapshot, precisely because it knows a stale pending save could otherwise fire against the wrong state — but `createTimeline`/`setActiveTimeline` have NO such handling at all: they call `chroma_timeline_create`/`chroma_timeline_set_active` then `load()` (which overwrites `get().timeline` with the NEWLY active timeline's own fetched content) with the OLD timeline's debounce timer left running untouched. When that stale timer eventually fires, `_flushSave` reads `get().timeline` AT FIRE TIME (not at schedule time) — by then it's already B's content — and posts `chroma_timeline_set({timeline: B's own already-current content})`, which the real Rust command (and this bug's own fake-backend mirror) writes onto whichever timeline is CURRENTLY ACTIVE (B, by definition, since nothing switched again) — a harmless no-op FOR B, but A's real edit was never sent anywhere and no longer exists in memory to retry.
- **the same race exists on the PROJECT axis, and B-083/D-203 only made it deterministic, not fixed** (2026-09-07): switching *projects* has the identical pending-save hazard, with a worse worst case — by the time `setOpenProject` hears about the switch, the Rust side already points at the INCOMING project, so a surviving `saveTimer` would have written the outgoing project's timeline into the incoming one. `setOpenProject` therefore cancels the timer outright, which is the safe half of the trade: an edit made in the last `SAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS` before a project switch is still silently dropped, exactly as described above. Closing it properly (flush before the switch proceeds) is still this entry's own scoped fix, and should cover both axes when it lands. *(2026-09-10: it did — see the fix below. The cancel in `setOpenProject` deliberately stays as the second line of defence.)*
- ~~**fix:** not attempted here…~~ — **fixed 2026-09-10 (D-308)**, taking the entry's own proposed shape (the stronger half of it: a real `await`ed flush, not a bare `clearTimeout`), plus two hazards the proposal did not name:
  - **`flushPendingSave()`** is the new store action and the rule. It clears `saveTimer`, runs its save immediately, and resolves only once `chroma_timeline_set` has actually **returned**. `createTimeline`/`setActiveTimeline` `await` it before issuing their own command — the ordering matters, not merely that both were sent, because `chroma_timeline_set` carries no timeline id and lands on whichever is active when it arrives.
  - **the in-flight window.** A cleared timer is not the same fact as "the backend holds this edit": between the timer firing and the invoke resolving, the save is neither pending-as-a-timer nor done, and a timer-only cancel races straight through it. `trackSave`/`inFlightSave` register every `chroma_timeline_set` round trip so the flush waits that out too.
  - **`restoreSnapshot` had the identical hazard.** Undo/redo bypasses the debounce and posts straight away — also addressed to "whichever timeline is active" — so its save is tracked the same way and a switch waits for it as well. (It was previously careful to cancel the *timer*, which is what made this look like a `createTimeline`/`setActiveTimeline`-only gap.)
  - **the project axis, closed at the layer that can close it.** `setOpenProject` still cancels rather than flushes, deliberately and correctly: by the time it is called the backend already points at the incoming project, so a flush from there would misfile A's timeline into B. The real flush is one layer up, in `app/src/store/useSessionStore.ts`'s `openProject`/`newProject`/`saveUntitledAs`/`closeProject` — the last point that still runs while the OUTGOING project is active. Both interfaces already funnel through those actions (GUI launcher directly, MCP via `useChromaControl.ts`), so one flush covers both.
  - **the UX judgment call this entry flagged, decided:** a failed flush **refuses** the switch rather than proceeding. The edit exists only in `timeline` at that moment and `load()` is about to overwrite it, so proceeding would be this very bug with a broken backend instead of a pending timer as the cause. `TimelineSwitcher` holds the tab strip inert (`aria-busy`, `pointer-events-none`) for the flush and renders the refusal in words; no spinner, because the normal case is one already-scheduled IPC round trip. `closeProject` is the deliberate exception — best-effort, never refusing, because "‹ Projects" is also the human's escape hatch from a wedged session (B-132/D-268).
- **verification:** six new regression tests in `packages/editor/src/timelineStore.test.ts`, against a fake backend that mirrors the real `chroma_timeline_set`'s one load-bearing property (writes into whichever timeline is ACTIVE, never by matching the posted document's id) and records `[activeAtArrival, trackCount]` per write. They cover the exact live repro (edit → immediate switch → the edit is on A, not B, and not lost), the command *ordering* (`_set` strictly before `_set_active`), `createTimeline`, the happy path issuing no extra write, a failed flush refusing the switch with the edit still in memory, the already-in-flight window, and an undo's immediate save. **All six were confirmed to FAIL against the pre-fix code** and pass after. Full suite green (96 files / 1744 tests), `tsc` unchanged at its 65-error baseline. Still **not live-verified against the real Rust backend** in a running app — the original entry asked for that and it remains the one open gap; the fake backend mirrors `chroma_timeline_set`'s behaviour but is not it.
- **harness note:** while extending `app/src/harness-main.tsx`/`app/harness.html` for this verification, also fixed a real usability defect in the harness itself (not a product bug): `#harness-status`'s fixed, `z-index: 9999` debug overlay was pinned `top: 0; left: 0`, directly on top of `TimelineSwitcher`'s own left-anchored tab strip (also mounted at the very top) — a real CDP pointer click at those screen coordinates silently landed on the (click-inert) status badge instead of the tab underneath it, even though the accessibility tree still reported the tab as a normal, clickable element. Moved the badge to `top: 0; right: 0` (nothing else docks there). Worth remembering for the next feature that adds UI to the very top of this harness's `#root`.

## B-096 — The Edit tab's own preview/timeline split was a fixed `h-[46%]` flex row, not a real resizable panel — a direct violation of this repo's own standing rule

status: fixed (2026-09-08) · severity: low (display/UX only — the timeline area worked correctly, it just could not be resized) · area: `packages/editor/src/EditorTab.tsx`
- **found:** 2026-09-08, owner live, reporting the Inspector panel's content cut off against the window edge and, separately with a screenshot, "the timeline panel is also not resizable" — while auditing the first report, found the SECOND is real too: `EditorTab.tsx`'s preview/timeline split was `<div className="h-[46%] min-h-[180px] shrink-0">`, a fixed CSS percentage, not a `ResizablePanel` at all — while the SAME file's Inspector column (to its right) already correctly uses one. CLAUDE.md's own standing rule ("every resizable-by-nature panel/pane/sidebar must actually be resizable," 2026-09-03) names exactly this class of pane and says a fixed one found later is "a real, worthwhile fix ... not something to leave as-is out of inertia."
- **repro:** open the Edit tab with a project loaded — there is no drag handle between the preview and the timeline; the split is permanently 46%/54% of the remaining height regardless of window size or user preference.
- **expected:** a real, user-draggable vertical split, matching the Inspector column's own horizontal one, and matching `packages/motion/src/MotionTab.tsx`'s own preview/timeline split, which already uses exactly this pattern correctly.
- **fix:** wrapped the preview and timeline blocks in a nested `<ResizablePanelGroup orientation="vertical">` (same `@apelles/ui` component, same pixel-based `defaultSize`/`minSize` convention this file already uses for the Inspector column and `MotionTab.tsx` already uses for its own vertical split) — `PREVIEW_MIN_HEIGHT = 200`, `TIMELINE_DEFAULT_HEIGHT = 320`, `TIMELINE_MIN_HEIGHT = 180` (matching the old fixed min-height so nothing gets more cramped than before). No new component, no new pattern — the exact one already proven elsewhere in this same codebase.
- **verification:** `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/editor` clean; `npm test --workspace @apelles/editor` 610/610 (no regressions — this is a pure layout change, no test targets the exact pixel split). Not live-verified against the real running app (no visual-inspection tool available yet at fix time — see `docs/notes/debug-tooling.md`, in progress); high confidence from the pattern being a verbatim, already-shipped-and-working match to `MotionTab.tsx`'s own equivalent split, but flagging the gap honestly rather than claiming a look that didn't happen.

## B-097 — a project's timeline ran at `DEFAULT_FPS` (24) while its own recorded timebase said otherwise, so frame arithmetic past a clip boundary read one frame off (`Track::clip_at` itself was never wrong)

status: **fixed (2026-09-09)** · severity: low as filed (a one-frame source-frame drift at a boundary), but the real root cause below is wider than the symptom: every project seeded from non-24fps media had its whole edit resolving against a timebase nothing had chosen · area: `crates/apelles-project/src/manifest.rs` (`infer_timeline_rate`, `new_project_in`), `crates/apelles-project/src/timeline.rs` (`build_from_shots`). **Not** `crates/apelles-timeline/src/lib.rs` — `Track::clip_at`, this entry's original suspect, is arithmetically correct and is unchanged.
- **found:** independently reconfirmed 3 times across this session's merge-verification `cargo test` runs (each time as a pre-existing, unrelated failure alongside real work being verified), traced but never filed with its own entry until now.
- **repro:** `cargo test -p apelles --lib chroma::project::tests::track_resolution_opaque_top_wins_across_two_video_tracks` — deterministically fails today:
  ```
  thread '...' panicked at app/src-tauri/src/chroma/project.rs:1577:9:
  assertion `left == right` failed: B's own source frame at this timeline position (it starts at 0)
    left: 26
   right: 25
  ```
  The test: track 0 has clip A (~25 frames) then nothing; track 1 has clip B (~75 frames) starting at timeline frame 0. Querying `resolve_video_position(dur_a)` — the first timeline frame where track 0's gap begins and track 1 (starting at frame 0) should show through — correctly picks clip B (the track-priority/fallthrough logic itself is right), but reports B's own **source frame** as `dur_a + 1` instead of `dur_a`.
- **expected:** since clip B starts at timeline frame 0 with no trim (`source_start = 0`) and (per the test's own guard assertion at line 1547) probes at the same fps as the project timeline, `Track::clip_at`'s source-frame formula (`c.source_start + timeline_frames_to_source(c.source_fps, timeline_frame - c.start_frame, fps)`, `crates/apelles-timeline/src/lib.rs:2258`) should reduce to plain identity — the source frame at timeline position `dur_a` should just be `dur_a`.
- **cause:** not fully re-derived this session (the mechanism was traced once already and not written down anywhere durable — this entry exists to close that gap). `timeline_frames_to_source`'s own formula (`crates/apelles-timeline/src/lib.rs:141-144`, `round(timeline_frames * src_fps / fps)`) is an exact identity when `src_fps == fps` and `timeline_frames` is an integer — no floating-point rounding can produce a whole-number-off-by-one here. That points at one of the two inputs to the subtraction (`timeline_frame - c.start_frame`) being off by one instead: either clip B's `start_frame` lands at `-1` rather than `0` after `chroma_timeline_move_clip(0, 1, 1, 0, false)` (the move that puts it on track 1), or `Timeline::resolve_video_clip_at`/the test itself passes `dur_a` when the fallthrough boundary is actually meant to be evaluated one frame later (an inclusive/exclusive fencepost in `end_frame_at`). Previously traced to predate every change from this session, in the original `Multi-track NLE Phase B1` commit that introduced `resolve_video_clip_at` (`ffb23d2`, 2026-09-03, D-056) — i.e. this is not a regression from anything shipped tonight, it has been latent since two-video-track resolution first existed, just never exercised by a GUI user landing exactly on that boundary frame at a moment they'd notice a one-frame source drift.
- **2026-09-09 — the real cause, and this entry's own diagnosis corrected rather than quietly dropped.** Both of the mechanisms guessed above are wrong, and so is the "expected" paragraph's premise. `Track::clip_at` computes **26 correctly**, and there is no off-by-one anywhere in it:
  - The test's fixture clips are synthesised at **25fps** (`make_test_clip(…, "25", 1)`), and B-082 seeds each placed clip's `source_fps` from its real probe, so `source_fps = 25.0`. There is no fps guard at line 1547 in this test — that reference belonged to a different test, and checking it was skipped when this entry was filed.
  - The project's `Timeline.rate` was left `None` at creation, so `Timeline::fps()` returned `DEFAULT_FPS` = **24**. The mapping is therefore *not* the identity the "expected" paragraph assumed.
  - So A's 25 source frames occupy only 24 timeline frames (`round(25 × 24/25)`): the gap really begins at timeline frame **24**, not 25. The test then probes `dur_a` — 25, which is A's **source**-frame count being used as a **timeline** frame, a unit confusion that is only invisible when the two rates agree. At timeline frame 25 (= 1.0417 s at 24fps), clip B, running at 25fps from timeline 0, is genuinely showing its source frame `round(25 × 25/24)` = **26**. Correct answer; wrong question.
  - Confirmed by construction, not by reading: `b097_source_frame_at_the_frame_a_top_track_gap_begins_mixed_timebase` reproduces the literal `left: 26` from a pure `apelles-timeline` fixture with no ffmpeg and no app crate at all.
- **the real defect this exposed.** `infer_settings_from_clip` (D-038) already probes the first media and records its real rate in `ProjectSettings::fps` — and every timeline-creation site then left `Timeline::rate` at `None`, which is what `Timeline::fps()` actually reads. Two sources of truth for one project's timebase, only one of them ever filled in: a project seeded from 25fps footage said 25 in its settings and resolved its entire edit at 24. That is not a boundary condition, it is every frame of that project; the boundary is just where a caller reasoning in the media's own frames could finally *see* it. Same shape as B-082 — a creation site that never read the probe sitting right above it.
- **fix (2026-09-09):** `apelles_project::infer_timeline_rate(clip)` returns the probe's own **exact rational** (`fps_num`/`fps_den`, so 30000/1001 stays 30000/1001, never a float re-rationalised by guesswork), and both creation sites use it — `new_project_in`, and `build_from_shots`'s lazy build for a pre-D-046 manifest. `None` for no path / an offline or unprobeable source / a nonsensical rate, which leaves the timeline on `DEFAULT_FPS` exactly as before. **Applied only to a timeline being created**: a timeline already persisted with `rate: None` keeps it, deliberately — its edits were made against the timebase it has, and silently re-timing an existing project would be a far worse bug than the one being fixed. `Track::clip_at`, `timeline_frames_to_source` and `end_frame_at` are untouched.
- **verification:** `chroma::project::tests::track_resolution_opaque_top_wins_across_two_video_tracks` — the deterministic failure quoted above — now passes **as written**, because the condition its assertion always assumed is finally true, not because the assertion was relaxed. Three new tests pin the behaviour directly: `apelles-timeline`'s `b097_source_frame_at_the_frame_a_top_track_gap_begins_same_timebase` (a top-track gap beginning at a named frame; the fallthrough clip's source frame at that frame, and at the frames either side of it, asserted exactly — so an off-by-one in *either* direction fails) and `…_mixed_timebase` (the same boundary when the rates genuinely differ, pinning that the fps-converted answer is right and reproducing this entry's own `26`), plus `apelles-project`'s `new_project_seeds_the_timeline_rate_from_the_real_probe_b097` (the rate is the exact rational, `Timeline::fps()` and `settings.fps` now agree, a clip's timeline footprint equals its own source frame count, and it survives the save/reload round trip). `cargo test`: `-p apelles-timeline` 250/250, `-p apelles-project` 59/59, `-p apelles` 264/264.

## B-098 — `editor_export`'s ffmpeg compiler still crops with STATIC insets only — a keyframed crop animates in the live preview but exports frozen

status: fixed (2026-09-08) · severity: medium (a real, narrower instance of B-095's own shape — the live preview and the export disagreed, just for one field instead of two) · area: `packages/editor/src/timelineExport.ts` (`buildClipFilterChain`)
- **found:** 2026-09-08, while fixing B-095 (opacity/rotation). `buildClipFilterChain`'s crop step read `clip.crop_left`/`crop_top`/`crop_right`/`crop_bottom` as four plain static numbers (`const cl = clip.crop_left ?? 0`, etc.) and never called `hasKeyframesFor(clip, 'crop_left')` or built a `keyframeExprAt` expression for any of them — unlike `position_x`/`position_y`/`scale`/`opacity`/`rotation`, which all check for and honour keyframes. The Rust preview side (`resolve_clip_transform_unfaded`, `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/edit.rs`) already resolves all four crop insets through the same per-property keyframe engine (D-132/D-208) as everything else — so this was purely an export-compiler gap, not a missing model capability.
- **repro (pre-fix):** keyframe any of the four crop insets on a clip (`editor_set_clip_keyframes`) to animate a reveal/hide over time — the live preview animated it correctly; `editor_export` produced a file cropped at whichever value the clip's own static `crop_*` fields held, for the clip's entire duration.
- **expected:** same bar as B-095 — a keyframed crop inset exports animated, matching the live preview frame for frame.
- **fix:** each of the four insets now gets the same `hasKeyframesFor` + `rebaseKeyframesToClipInput` + `keyframeExprAt` treatment `scale`/`opacity`/`rotation` already have, wired into `crop`'s `w`/`h`/`x`/`y` as quoted expressions (same B-075 single-quoting requirement). **This entry's own original fix guidance was wrong, corrected here rather than silently**: it assumed `crop` needed an `eval=frame` flag the way `scale` does (B-090's own trap) — checked empirically instead of assumed, and `crop` has **no `eval` option at all** (`ffmpeg -h filter=crop` lists none): a real two-colour test (an `hstack` source, an animated `x` expression) confirmed `crop`'s `w`/`h`/`x`/`y` are simply always evaluated per frame, with nothing to add.
- **verification:** a new real-ffmpeg pixel test in `timelineExport.ffmpeg.test.ts` — a `crop_left` keyframe animating 0 → 0.3 across a clip with a marker in its leftmost quarter, sampled visible-then-gone. The pre-existing static-crop string-match test in `timelineExport.test.ts` was updated to the new quoted/named-param shape (same "not weakened, just corrected to the new-but-equivalent syntax" discipline B-090's own verification note used) rather than left asserting the old, now-superseded unquoted form. `npm test --workspace @apelles/editor`: 718/718 (was 717 pre-fix, +1 new pixel test — the string-match update doesn't add a test, it corrects an existing one). `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/editor` clean.

## B-100 — the debug screenshot tool shipped ungated: `chroma_debug_screenshot` / `chroma_debug_sample_pixel` were compiled into a RELEASE build

status: fixed (2026-09-08, D-219) · severity: medium (no user-facing symptom and no exploitable surface — the commands only write a PNG of the app's own window under `$TMPDIR` — but a direct violation of the project's own stated invariant, and the pattern was about to be copied by four more tools) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/{mod.rs,control.rs}`, `app/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, `app/src/hooks/useDebugScreenshot.ts`
- **found:** 2026-09-08, while reading D-210's implementation as the reference pattern for D-219's own tools. The brief was to "match whatever gate the already-shipped commands use." They used none.
- **repro:** `grep -rn "debug_assertions" app/src-tauri/src/` on the pre-fix tree returns two hits, neither of them debug tooling (`main.rs`'s `windows_subsystem`, and a *comment* in `lib.rs` about the `e2e-testing` Cargo feature). `chroma::debug_capture` was an unconditional `pub mod`; both commands were unconditional entries in `tauri::generate_handler!`; both `native_op` arms in `control.rs` were unconditional; and the human-facing Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+D hook invoked the command unconditionally too.
- **expected:** per CLAUDE.md's standing rule (owner, 2026-09-08) — "every one of them must be compiled out of a production build via a real compile-time gate (`#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`, a Cargo feature, or equivalent) — never a runtime flag, never 'just don't call it in prod.' For us, never shipped." — a `tauri build` release binary contains no webview-screenshot code path.
- **actual:** it contained all of it. A shipped Apelles could be asked over IPC to photograph its own window and write the PNG to disk.
- **cause:** D-210's own decision entry never states a gate, and neither does `docs/notes/debug-screenshot-tool.md`. The rule and the tool landed on the same day; the rule was written in CLAUDE.md, the tool was written without it. Nothing in the build would ever have complained — an ungated debug command compiles and works perfectly, which is exactly why this class of miss survives review.
- **fix (D-219):** `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` on `chroma::debug_capture` (the whole module), on both commands *inside* `tauri::generate_handler!` (the macro re-emits an outer attribute onto that command's match arm — verified in `tauri-macros` 2.6.3's `command/handler.rs`, so the IPC name genuinely does not exist in a release build), and on `control.rs`'s `native_op`, which gains a `None`-returning `#[cfg(not(debug_assertions))]` twin so its single call site reads identically either way. The frontend half (the Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+D hook) is gated on `import.meta.env.DEV`, which Vite folds to a literal `false` at build time — otherwise the shortcut would survive into a release build and only ever toast "command not found". D-219's own five new tools use the same two gates from the start, and the frontend one is verified by grepping a real production `vite build` output rather than assumed.

## B-099 — D-217 broke the real-Chromium browser harness outright: `atob` on a string that still carried its `data:` prefix, so `harness.html` mounted nothing at all

status: fixed (2026-09-08) · severity: medium (no shipped-app impact whatsoever — this is debug tooling; but it silently removed a whole VERIFICATION TIER, which is exactly the class of failure this repo keeps paying for) · area: `app/src/harness-main.tsx`
- **found:** 2026-09-08, on the first attempt to use the harness since D-217 — opening `harness.html?mode=preview` to verify D-218's preview zoom in a real browser. The page rendered its status strip and nothing else; `window.__chromaHarness` was `undefined`.
- **repro:** serve `app/` (`npm run dev`) and open `/harness.html?mode=preview`. Console: `Uncaught InvalidCharacterError: Failed to execute 'atob' on 'Window': The string to be decoded is not correctly encoded.` Nothing mounts, so every check the harness exists to perform is silently unavailable.
- **cause:** D-217 changed `chroma_timeline_frame`'s payload from a `data:image/jpeg;base64,…` string to raw bytes, and correctly updated the harness's stub to hand back bytes — `Uint8Array.from(atob(STUB_FRAME_BASE64), …)`. But `STUB_FRAME_BASE64` was (and had always been) the whole **data URL**, prefix included; it was previously handed to an `<img src>` verbatim, where the prefix belongs. `atob` on `"data:image/jpeg;base64,/9j/…"` throws, at module scope, before `render()` is ever reached — so the failure is total rather than a broken picture, which is why it read as "the harness is dead" rather than "the stub frame is wrong."
- **expected:** the harness page mounts, exactly as D-142 built it to, and its stub frame arrives as the bytes the real command now returns.
- **fix:** the constant is now the bare base64 payload its own name always claimed (prefix removed), with a comment at the declaration saying why it must stay that way. One line of real change.
- **verification:** the page mounts and `window.__chromaHarness` is live again — and it was then used for real, as D-218's whole real-browser verification tier (real layout, real `document.elementFromPoint` hit-testing, real `PointerEvent` drag, two screenshots). Only remaining console entry on the page is a `favicon.ico` 404, pre-existing and unrelated.
- **worth noting for next time:** the harness has no automated coverage of its own (it deliberately does not run in CI — `harness-main.tsx`'s own header says so), so nothing could have caught this except opening it. The cheap habit that would have: when a change alters a stub's own contract, open the harness once in the same pass rather than trusting the edit.

## B-101 — A panned MONO clip exports 3 dB quieter than it plays: the two paths adapt mono→stereo by different laws

status: **fixed (2026-09-09, D-269)** · severity: low (mono sources only, and only once a pan is set — stereo sources, the normal case, are bit-for-bit unaffected, before and after) · area: `packages/editor/src/timelineExportAudio.ts` (`buildAudioSourceChain`), with the probed channel count newly threaded through `crates/apelles-project/src/manifest.rs` (`MediaVideoInfo::audio_channels`, `backfill_audio_facts`) → `packages/bridge/src/media.ts` → `packages/editor/src/{editorExport,timelineExport}.ts`. `crates/apelles-media/src/audio.rs`'s `adapt_channels` is **unchanged** — see below for why it is the one that was right.
- **found:** 2026-09-08, while building D-223's export half. Not a guess — measured directly with `ffmpeg -af volumedetect` on real files before the code was written, precisely because the mono case is where a channel-adaptation difference would hide.
- **repro:** `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "sine=frequency=440:duration=2" -ac 1 mono.wav` measures `mean_volume: -21.1 dB`. Push it through the exporter's own upmix — `-filter_complex "[0:a]aformat=channel_layouts=stereo"` — and each channel measures `-24.1 dB`. The live mixer's `adapt_channels` instead does `out.extend(repeat_n(frame[0], dst_channels))`, i.e. each output channel carries the mono sample unchanged, `-21.1 dB`.
- **expected:** the same clip at the same pan sounds the same in the preview and in the exported file — the "same doc ⇒ same output" bar this repo holds every render/audio path to (the standard B-053/B-095 were fixed against).
- **actual:** an exported panned mono clip is 3.01 dB below what the preview played. Only reachable with `pan != 0`: with no pan the exporter never inserts the `aformat` node at all, so a mono clip stays mono end to end and nothing rematrixes.
- **cause:** two different, individually defensible mono→stereo laws. `adapt_channels` **duplicates at unity** (each speaker gets the full sample, so total power doubles — +3 dB). libswresample's default mono→stereo matrix **preserves power** (each channel at 1/√2). Neither is wrong on its own; they simply disagree, and D-223's pan is the first feature that makes both run over the same clip.
- **which one is right — this entry's own answer was wrong, corrected here rather than silently:** the **live mixer's**. The original reasoning (a hard-panned mono clip lands at exactly the source's own level under the exporter's law) is sound in isolation and misses the two facts that decide it:
  1. **The exporter's law does not actually make the two agree — it moves the disagreement.** The `aformat` node is only inserted when a pan is set; with no pan a mono clip stays mono end to end and nothing rematrixes. So adopting the power-preserving law in the mixer (fix 1 below) would leave a **centred** mono clip playing 3 dB below what it exports — the same bug with the sign flipped, and now affecting every mono clip in live playback rather than only panned ones.
  2. **This codebase already chose a 0 dB-centre pan law, and it only means what it says on top of a unity duplicate.** `apelles_types::pan_gains(0.0)` is exactly `(1.0, 1.0)` and `gl² + gr² == 2` (see that module's own doc, which states the +3 dB at the extremes as a known, accepted cost). On a power-preserving upmix, `pan = 0` would quietly be −3 dB, so a mono clip's level would jump the instant it was nudged off centre — a discontinuity in a control that is meant to be continuous.
- **the two real fixes** as originally scoped: (1) make `adapt_channels`' mono→stereo case power-preserving (`* FRAC_1_SQRT_2`) — **rejected**, per the two points above: it does not fix the divergence, and it contradicts the pan law this codebase already ships; or (2) plumb the probed `audio_channels` through `MediaVideoInfo` → the media pool DTO → `TimelineExportOptions` and emit `pan=stereo|c0=c0|c1=c0` (a unity duplicate) for a known-mono source instead of `aformat` — **taken**.
- **fix (2026-09-09, D-269):** exactly option 2. `apelles_media::video::VideoInfo::audio_channels` was already probed and simply never surfaced; it now rides `MediaVideoInfo::audio_channels` → `MediaItemDto` → `@apelles/bridge` → `editorExport.ts`'s `resolveAudioChannelsOverrides` → `TimelineExportOptions.audioChannelsOverrides`, the same "the compiler stays pure, the caller supplies what only it can know" split `hasAudioOverrides` (D-197) established. `buildAudioSourceChain` swaps `aformat=channel_layouts=stereo` for `pan=stereo|c0=c0|c1=c0` **only for a source positively known to be mono** — that expression on a real stereo source would copy its left channel over its right, which is far worse than a 3 dB error, so an unknown or non-mono channel count keeps the old node byte-identically. `Option<u16>` with the same "absent means never probed, not zero" migration sentinel as `has_audio` (D-129), resolved once by `backfill_audio_facts` (the renamed `backfill_has_audio` — both facts come off one probe, so two passes would be waste) on the next `chroma_media_list`.
- **verification:** `apelles_media`'s `b101_export_mono_upmix_matches_the_live_mixer` **measures both sides** rather than comparing formulae — the live level is the real `adapt_channels` output with the real `pan_gains` applied as `SourceEnvelopes::apply` applies them, the export level is a real `ffmpeg` run of the chain the TS compiler emits (raw f32le in and out, no codec between the filter and the measurement) — and asserts the two agree within **0.05 dB**. The same test measures the **pre-fix** chain in the same run and asserts it sits 3.01 dB low, so it demonstrably can see the bug it fixes. On the TS side, `timelineExport.ffmpeg.test.ts` exports a real hard-panned mono clip and measures its channels against the **source file's own measured level** (+3.01 dB in the destination channel, silence in the other), exports the same clip with and without the channel count to measure the 3 dB gap directly, and asserts a panned STEREO clip's argv is unchanged; `timelineExportAudio.test.ts` pins the emitted chain string (mono → unity duplicate, stereo/unknown/multichannel → `aformat`, unpanned mono → no channel plumbing at all) so the Rust test's copy of that string cannot drift from the compiler.
- **documented at the point of use:** `editor_get_capabilities`' `export.per_clip_level` entry is updated to say it is fixed, and to name the one remaining case an agent can hit — a mono pool item that predates the probed channel count and has not been backfilled yet, where the old upmix is kept rather than guessed at (run `editor_list_media` once, or `editor_reprobe_media` that item, and re-export).

## B-102 — Total silence during live preview playback: `symphonia` was never built with MP3 decode support, so every `.mp3` clip fails to open and is swallowed silently

status: fixed (2026-09-08) · severity: blocker (the owner's own real project has 4 audio tracks — SFX clicks/whooshes/chimes plus a full music bed — every one of them an `.mp3`; ALL of it was silent, on every playback) · area: `app/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`, `crates/apelles-media/Cargo.toml` (symphonia feature flags)
- **found:** 2026-09-08, reported live by the owner ("BTW IN PREVIEW CANT HERE ANY AUDIO AT ALL") against their real `perf-comparison-reel-v3` project — 2 video tracks, 4 audio tracks (`click.mp3`, `whoosh.flac`, `chime.mp3`, `music.mp3`).
- **repro:** `CHROMA_TEST_AUDIO_VIDEO=<any .mp3 with real audio> cargo test -p apelles --lib chroma::audio::tests::chroma_audio_play_produces_non_silent_pcm_end_to_end -- --exact --nocapture` — this integration test is gated on that env var and had evidently never actually been run with it set before tonight (a prior session summary's "28/28 passing, proves the mixer is correct" claim covered only the unconditional unit tests; every test that exercises a real file through the real `cpal` device — the one that would have caught this — was silently skipped for lack of the env var). Run for real: `peak=0`, and the swallowed error (temporarily surfaced via `eprintln!` in `apelles_media::audio::start`'s session thread, since `run_session` errors only ever reach a `log::warn!` with no logger backend installed) was `probe: unsupported feature: core (probe): no suitable format reader found`.
- **expected:** any audio-track clip with a real audio stream (mp3, flac, wav, aac, …) plays audibly during live timeline playback, matching the mixing math's own 28-test suite.
- **actual:** every `.mp3` source — clicks, whooshes, chimes, and the entire music bed, i.e. everything on the user's 4 audio tracks — failed to open in `apelles_media::open_source` (a `symphonia::default::get_probe().probe(...)` call), and that failure was swallowed on a background thread with no UI surface at all: `chroma_audio_play` itself still returns `Ok(())` (the spawn succeeded; the decode failure happens later, async, inside the spawned thread), so nothing in the frontend ever saw an error either.
- **cause:** `symphonia = { version = "0.6.1", features = [...] }` in both `app/src-tauri/Cargo.toml` and `crates/apelles-media/Cargo.toml` listed `["isomp4", "aac", "alac", "aiff"]` — covering exactly video-embedded audio (mp4/mov containers, AAC/ALAC codecs) — with **no `mp3` feature**. `symphonia`'s own `default` features (`flac`, `wav`, `vorbis`, `pcm`, `mkv`, `ogg`, `adpcm`, `all-meta`) are additive on top of an explicit `features = [...]` list (Cargo only drops defaults with `default-features = false`, which this dependency never set) — which is why `whoosh.flac` was NOT affected, and why this bug was invisible to anyone testing with FLAC/WAV/embedded-video-audio and not specifically MP3. `mp3` (like `mp1`/`mp2`) is the one common format symphonia deliberately keeps OUT of `default` (it ships behind its own `symphonia-bundle-mp3` dependency), so it needs the same explicit opt-in `isomp4`/`aac`/etc. already got — it was simply never added.
- **fix:** added `"mp3"` to symphonia's feature list in both Cargo.toml files (kept in sync, as they already were). Verified via the real end-to-end test above: `peak=1.0267, rms=0.1889` against the project's own real `music.mp3` post-fix. Re-ran the FLAC case too (`whoosh.flac`, `peak=0.0790`) to confirm it was never actually broken, just already covered by `default`. Full `chroma::audio::` module (28 tests) still green.
- **worth noting for next time:** the real-device integration tests in this file (`CHROMA_TEST_AUDIO_VIDEO`/`CHROMA_TEST_SILENT_VIDEO`-gated) are the ONLY tests that would ever catch a codec-support gap like this — the unconditional unit tests all operate on synthetic in-memory buffers, never through `symphonia::probe` at all. They should be run with a real fixture set (one file per format actually used in this project — mp3, flac, wav, mp4/aac) at least once per session that touches the audio stack, not left to whichever file a past session happened to have on hand.
## B-103 — the ffmpeg export compiler never placed a clip in TIME: any clip at `start_frame > 0` rendered its last frame, frozen, for its whole window

**Status: fixed, 2026-09-08 (found while building D-226's transitions).**

**What was wrong.** `timelineExport.ts` gives every clip its own `-i` (with
`-ss`/`-t`) and composites it with
`overlay … enable='between(t, startSec, endSec)'` onto a shared `[base]`. Each
input decodes to a stream whose own timestamps start at ~0, and `overlay` pairs
its two inputs **by timestamp** (ffmpeg's `framesync`) — nothing ever shifted a
clip's stream to where that clip actually sits on the timeline. So a clip at
`start_frame > 0` had its real frames consumed against the base stream's opening
seconds, where its own `enable` gate was still shut, and then — once the gate
opened — showed nothing but its **last frame, repeated** for the rest of its
window (`overlay`'s default `eof_action=repeat`).

The second half of the same mistake: `overlay`'s `x`/`y` expressions run on the
main stream's clock (timeline seconds), but a clip's position keyframes were
emitted in **clip-relative** seconds, so a position animation on a clip at
`start_frame > 0` ran `start_frame / fps` seconds early.

**Why it survived this long.** The audio half of the same compiler always did
place its sources (`timelineExportAudio.ts`'s `adelay`, D-197) — only video
never grew the equivalent. And every existing real-ffmpeg test placed its clips
at frame 0, or used a flat colour, or a single clip: with either, a frozen frame
and the right frame are the same pixels. The pure argv tests string-match a
filtergraph and cannot see it at all. Confirmed live before fixing, not reasoned
about: a two-colour source (red for its first second, lime for its second)
placed at t=2 rendered **lime, frozen, for its whole window**.

**Fix.** `setpts=PTS[/speed]+<inputStart>/TB` at the **head** of every clip's
filter chain — timestamps only, no frames generated, no decode cost, the video
equivalent of `adelay`. Putting it first gives the whole chain one time base
(timeline seconds), which is what the two-time-bases confusion caused in the
first place; every expression authored against the clip's own in-point (its
keyframes, its D-147 fade, `overlay`'s `x`/`y`) is now explicitly re-based
through `(t − clipStartSec)` / `(T − clipStartSec)`, the exact re-basing
`buildTextDrawtextStep` already did for a title.

**Regression test.** `timelineExport.ffmpeg.test.ts` — "B-103: a clip at
start_frame > 0 renders its OWN REAL FRAMES at its own position". It builds the
two-colour source deliberately, because that is the only fixture shape that can
see this: it asserts red in the clip's own first second, lime in its second, and
black in the gap before it. The whole rest of the suite (856 TS tests) passes
unchanged, and the compiled argv is byte-identical for a clip at frame 0.

**Severity.** Real and silent for any sequential edit — which is the ordinary
use of an NLE. Masked in practice because the exporter's heaviest real use so
far has been stacked comparison reels, where both clips start at frame 0.

## B-104 — The on-canvas transform box detaches from the picture and drifts further the longer playback runs: three decoders each meant something different by "source frame N", and VFR footage made them disagree by up to 4 seconds

status: fixed (2026-09-08, D-228) · severity: high (the Edit tab's whole direct-manipulation surface — the transform box, and every position/scale keyframe authored through it — is wrong on any variable-frame-rate source, which means every macOS screen recording and most phone footage; the same fault silently mis-rendered exports and Colorist thumbnails) · area: `crates/apelles-media/src/{decode_pipe.rs,video.rs}`, `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/export.rs`
- **found:** 2026-09-08, reported live by the owner with a screenshot — "THE CANVAS BOX AND THE VIDEO CLIP IS DETACHED AND LAGGING :/" — against their real `perf-comparison-reel-v3` project (`b093-verify.chroma`), clip `e2192723-b56a-4bdc-8f1a-12a2b4f396c4` on track 1, source `scratch/reel-src/before-1.09.51pm.mov`, a heavily keyframed macOS screen recording.
- **repro:** put any **variable-frame-rate** source on the timeline (a macOS screen recording is the easy one — it only encodes a frame when the screen changes), give the clip position/scale keyframes, and play. Confirmed with the file's own numbers: `ffprobe` reports `avg_frame_rate` 126780/2873 ≈ 44.128, `r_frame_rate` 60/1, `nb_frames` 2112, `duration` 47.86 s — i.e. a real 1/60 s tick base with 47 holds of up to 0.567 s, not 60 fps CFR (which would have ~2872 frames).
- **expected:** the box tracks the picture. Frame `N` of a source means one thing to every part of the app.
- **actual:** the box and the picture separate by a growing amount for as long as playback continues, then snap back together on a scrub. Measured from the file's own PTS list: coded frame `k` and nominal frame `k` are up to **4.07 s apart** (≈180 frames, worst at k=866; +1.36 s the other way at k=1228).
- **cause:** not the probe, and not a single wrong line — three decode paths had each independently picked a different meaning for a frame index, and CFR footage had hidden the disagreement since D-015.
  - The **model** — `apelles_timeline::timeline_frames_to_source`, `Clip::source_start`/`duration`, `resolve_clip_transform`, the audio clock — says source frame `N` is *the picture at `N / source_fps` seconds*. That is the only meaning consistent with a CFR timeline, and it is what the keyframes the owner authored are indexed by.
  - `decode_pipe::FramePipe` and `export::spawn_decoder` instead seeked by time **once** and then counted **coded** frames — `-fps_mode passthrough` emits one output frame per coded frame — so after a respawn the pipe's index and the model's index walked apart at whatever rate the source's real frame timing differed from its average. This is why the drift *accumulated during playback* and *reset on a scrub*: a scrub forces a respawn, which re-synchronises the two at that instant.
  - `video::decode_frame` (the pipe's own error fallback) and the filmstrip chunk path seeked by time **per call**, so they were nearly right — but "nearly": checked against the file's PTS oracle at 49 grid indices, the bare `-ss N/fps` law returned a different frame from the true hold at **36** of them.
  - `video::extract_thumb_strip` selected on the filter graph's coded-frame counter (`select=not(mod(n,step))`) and returned those `n`s as frame indices, so every Colorist thumbnail was labelled with an index pointing somewhere else.
  - **`probe` preferring `avg_frame_rate` over `r_frame_rate` is NOT the bug**, though it looks like a suspect. The average is the only scalar that keeps `nb_frames`, `duration` and `Clip::duration` mutually consistent, and no scalar at all can describe unevenly-spaced frames. It was left alone deliberately — changing it would alter `source_fps` for every source and hence the meaning of every stored `source_start`/`duration`, i.e. a project migration, in exchange for nothing.
- **fix (D-228):** a new `crates/apelles-media/src/conform.rs` states the invariant once — *source frame `N` is the picture on screen at `N / source_fps` seconds, i.e. the last coded frame with PTS `<= N / source_fps`* — and builds the ffmpeg arguments that deliver it: `fps=<num>/<den>:start_time=0:round=up` under `-copyts`, with `-noaccurate_seek` and a half-frame-early `select=gte(t,…)`. All four decode paths above now build their commands through it, so they cannot disagree again. No transcode, no proxy, no cached artefact, no schema change, no migration — the conform is computed per decode, so `project.json` + the original file stay the only inputs to a render. `round=up` is the load-bearing part: measured against the real file's PTS oracle over 49 indices, `up` had 0 mismatches, ffmpeg's default `near` had 20, `down` had 29. Applied to CFR sources too, because it is free there (2.51 → 2.50 ms/frame measured) and one code path beats two.
- **regression tests:** `crates/apelles-media/src/decode_pipe.rs`, six new tests over an ffmpeg-synthesized VFR fixture with a known 2 s hold (`testsrc` at 30 fps, coded frames 30–89 dropped, timestamps preserved ⇒ `avg_frame_rate` exactly 15), plus `conform.rs`'s own 8 argument-construction tests. Three encode this exact fault and were **confirmed to fail against the pre-fix behaviour** (the old `-ss` + `passthrough` law temporarily restored inside `conform::from_frame`): `a_held_frame_is_held_for_every_grid_slot_it_covers` (mean|Δ| 0.47 where 0.0 is required), `a_frame_is_the_same_picture_wherever_the_pipe_was_opened` (1.69), `pipe_and_single_frame_decode_agree_on_a_vfr_source` (2.45). `a_cfr_source_is_unaffected_by_the_conform` passes both before and after, which is the point of having it.
- **verified against the real file:** `the_real_vfr_source_resolves_every_index_to_the_picture_on_screen` (env-gated on `CHROMA_TEST_VFR_VIDEO`) runs the actual `FramePipe` over the owner's own clip and checks each nominal index against `ffprobe`'s PTS list — an oracle that shares no code with the thing under test — asserting the argmin over a ±3 neighbourhood rather than a bare residual, since decoding forward from a seek and decoding from frame 0 legitimately differ in the last bit on non-IDR recovery points. All 8 probes correct, including the early frame 20 (→ coded 26) and the late frame 1600 (→ coded 1633) the report called for, and the worst-drift region (frame 866 → coded 969, 1020 → 1011).
- **verification gap (honest):** proven by test, by measurement against the real source, and by tracing — **not** by driving the real Tauri window and looking at the box. This pass ran in an isolated worktree while the owner's own `npm run tauri:dev` held the main checkout, and the transform box is drawn by the frontend overlay, so no backend-side capture can show box-vs-picture directly. What is proven is the half this bug actually lives in: the decoder now returns, for every index, the picture the box's own keyframe math was evaluated at. Same constraint D-125/D-130/B-058 recorded for their own fixes.
- **same family as B-075 / B-077 / B-079 / B-097, from the other side.** Those four are all "a frame number was interpreted in the wrong *unit*" — a SOURCE-frame count added to a TIMELINE-frame position without converting through `source_fps` (B-075 in the exporter, B-077 in the GUI, B-079 in the live engine), or off by one at a boundary (B-097 in `Track::clip_at`). Each was fixed by making a *consumer* of the model convert correctly. B-104 is the first one where the model and every consumer of it were already right and the **decoder** was the odd one out: the index was in the correct unit, and the picture fetched for it was not. Worth keeping the distinction, because the reflex those four trained — "check the `source_fps` conversion" — finds nothing here. The lesson B-104 adds is that a frame index is only meaningful if the thing that turns it back into pixels agrees about what it names, which is why `conform` exists as one module rather than a corrected line in each decoder.
- **adjacent finding, deliberately NOT fixed here:** `video::probe` records only a single scalar rate, so nothing in the app can currently *say* that a source is variable-rate — there is no `is_vfr` to show in the Inspector, warn on import, or expose over MCP. D-228 does not need it (the conform is unconditional and correct for both), so adding a field nothing reads would be dead code. Worth revisiting if a "this footage is VFR" affordance is ever wanted for the human/AI pair.

## B-105 — two `chroma::*` test modules raced over the process-global `current_video()`, so a relight test passed or failed purely on scheduling order

status: fixed (2026-09-08) · severity: low (a test-suite isolation defect — no shipped behaviour is wrong; the cost is a `cargo test --workspace` that fails for a reason unrelated to whatever is being verified, which is exactly how a real regression gets waved through) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/state.rs` (`active_shot_change_busts_the_thumb_cache`) and `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/relight.rs` (`keyframed_light_without_a_loaded_video_falls_back_to_raw_fields`)

- **found:** 2026-09-08, during D-230's (adjustment clips) final verification. `cargo test --workspace` reported **two** failures where only the documented pre-existing B-097 was expected. The second was
  `chroma::relight::tests::keyframed_light_without_a_loaded_video_falls_back_to_raw_fields`, in a module D-230 never touched. Isolated before being explained rather than assumed pre-existing:
  - the relight test **passes alone** (`cargo test -p apelles --lib <that test>` → ok);
  - the full suite **with D-230's new tests skipped** (`-- --skip preview_adjustment`) → only B-097 fails;
  - the full suite **with them** → B-097 *and* the relight test fail, reproducibly.
  That pattern says "order-dependent", not "broken by the new code".

- **root cause:** `current_video()` is process-global state (`chroma::state`), and it is read far outside the module that owns it — `chroma::keyframes::interpolated_parameters` consults it to decide whether to resolve a keyframed parameter against the current frame, and returns `None` (fall back to the raw fields) when no video is loaded. `chroma::relight`'s test asserts exactly that fallback, so its entire premise is `current_video() == None`. Meanwhile `chroma::state::tests::active_shot_change_busts_the_thumb_cache` called `set_current_video(Some(…))` **twice, took no lock, and never restored it** — leaving a video set for the remainder of the process. Whichever test won the race decided the outcome.

  **D-230 did not cause this; it exposed it.** Its new `preview_adjustment_tests` spawn real `ffmpeg` and decode real frames, which widened the scheduling window enough to turn a latent coin-flip into a deterministic failure. The defect had been present for as long as both tests have existed.

- **expected:** a test that depends on process-global state establishes that state; a test that mutates it restores it. Neither should be able to decide the other's result.

- **fix:** both halves, deliberately — fixing only the leaking side would leave the relight test passing by luck rather than by construction, and there are other `set_current_video` callers in the suite (`chroma::export`'s own tests, as `state.rs`'s existing comment already noted).
  - `active_shot_change_busts_the_thumb_cache` now takes `PROJECT_STATE_LOCK` (the shared cross-module test mutex that exists for precisely this, `chroma/mod.rs`) and calls `set_current_video(None)` on the way out.
  - `keyframed_light_without_a_loaded_video_falls_back_to_raw_fields` now takes the same lock and sets `set_current_video(None)` itself, so its documented precondition is asserted rather than inherited.

- **verification:** `cargo test -p apelles --lib --no-fail-fast` run **three times**: 189 passed, 1 failed every time — and that one is B-097, the documented pre-existing failure, alone. Before the fix the same command gave 188 passed / 2 failed.

- **not fixed here, deliberately:** the underlying design smell — a process-global `current_video()` that a pure-parsing helper three modules away reads — is untouched. `PROJECT_STATE_LOCK` is the existing, documented mitigation for exactly this class across `chroma::*` tests, and widening its use is the fix that matches the codebase as it is. Making `interpolated_parameters` take the frame as an argument instead of reaching for a global is the real repair and is a much wider change than a test-isolation bug warrants; noted here so it is on the record.

## B-109 — the app's logger has never written a single byte: a plugin takes `log::set_logger` before `setup_logging` runs, so every `log::*` in the whole app goes nowhere

status: fixed (2026-09-08) · severity: high (not a wrong pixel — a blind spot. Every diagnostic the audio subsystem has, including the D-049 rms/peak verification hook and every one of its silent failure paths, was unreachable in the running app; three separate investigations of B-111 in one night were slowed by reading a log that could not contain anything) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/lib.rs` (`setup_logging`, `run`)

- **found:** 2026-09-08, while root-causing B-111. Looking for the once-per-second `chroma audio: rms=… peak=…` line that `apelles_media::audio`'s output callback emits, and finding no trace of it, led to `app_log_dir()`: **every `app.log` on this machine was 0 bytes** — `io.github.CyberTimon.RapidRAW`, `…RapidRAWWt`, `…dev-d214`, `…dev-motion-mcp-*`, `io.chroma.debugtools.worktree`, `io.github.chroma.perfagent` — across a week of builds and every worktree. `setup_logging` opens the file with `truncate(true)`, so each one had been created and emptied at that build's last launch and never written to again.

  B-102 had already brushed against this ("`run_session` errors only ever reach a `log::warn!` with no logger backend installed") but read it as a property of the *test* binary. It is true of the shipped app.

- **repro:** launch the app and look at `~/Library/Logs/<bundle identifier>/app.log`, or at `tauri dev`'s own stderr. Nothing — not even `setup_logging`'s own closing `log::info!("Logger initialized successfully…")`.

- **expected:** `fern` writes to stderr and to `app.log`, filtered by `RUST_LOG` (default `info`), as `setup_logging` plainly intends.

- **actual:** nothing, ever. Confirmed by instrumenting the failing branch directly and running the real app:

  ```
  DBG Failed to apply logger configuration: attempted to set a logger after the
  logging system was already initialized
  ```
