  tab back and forth, **both** panels carried `data-ending-style` — including
  the SELECTED one, whose `transitionStatus` is cleared by its own
  `AnimationFrame.request(() => setTransitionStatus(undefined))`. Two
  independent rAF-scheduled callbacks, neither delivered. `debug_frame_timing`
  on the same app reported `raf: { samples: 0, fps: null }`.

- **cause, part 2 — and even a correctly-`hidden` panel would still have
  painted.** `[hidden] { display: none }` is a **UA-stylesheet** rule. This
  panel carries `flex-1` from `@apelles/ui` and `flex flex-col gap-4` from the
  call site — author-origin `display` declarations, which beat any UA rule on
  origin alone, before specificity is even consulted. So the `hidden` path Base
  UI relies on was independently broken here too; it just never got far enough
  to matter. Fixed as well, rather than left as the next person's surprise.

- **why every test tier was green, and why one of them CANNOT go red.** The
  D-246 suites (`clipInspectorTabs.test.ts`, `ClipInspectorPanel.tabs.dom.
  test.tsx`, 18 tests) assert which sections are on which tab, and they are
  right. They run in jsdom, and **jsdom is the one environment in which this bug
  is structurally impossible**: `useAnimationsFinished` opens with
  `if (typeof element.getAnimations !== 'function') { run(); return; }`, jsdom
  does not implement `getAnimations`, so the deselected panel unmounts
  synchronously there no matter how broken the real thing is. jsdom also applies
  no Tailwind CSS at all, so it could not have seen part 2 either. A jsdom test
  asserting "only one panel is in the DOM" passes on the broken build — it was
  written, confirmed to pass pre-fix, and deliberately NOT kept as the proof.
  Same lesson as B-123 and B-092/B-093, arrived at from a new direction: the
  tier was not too weak, it was the one arrangement that cannot see the defect.

- **fix.** Two CSS rules on `TabsContent` in `@apelles/ui`, so every Tabs
  consumer gets them, not just this panel:
  - `[&[inert]]:hidden` — the load-bearing one. Base UI writes
    `inert: inertValue(!open)` straight from `open` during render, with no
    effect, no frame and no animation in between, so it is correct on the very
    commit the value changes. The deselected panel is the inert one, by
    construction, whether or not Base UI ever gets to unmount it.
  - `[&[hidden]]:hidden` — an author-origin rule at class+attribute
    specificity, which beats any `display` utility on the same element and so
    closes part 2 permanently.

  Neither costs anything on the healthy path, where the panel is unmounted and
  matches no selector at all. Rejected alternatives: rendering only the active
  `TabsContent` at the call site (fixes one panel, leaves the primitive broken
  for `CaptionPanel` and everything after it, and fights Base UI's own
  structure); and keying the hide off `data-ending-style` (unusable — the live
  app proved that attribute is itself rAF-driven and was stuck on BOTH panels).

- **also found and fixed in the same pass, same family, separate defect:** the
  selected tab had no visual selected state anywhere in the app, because
  `@apelles/ui`'s `tabs.tsx` styled `data-selected:` while Base UI's `Tabs.Tab`
  emits **`data-active`** (`TabsTabDataAttributes`: activationDirection /
  orientation / disabled / active — there is no `selected`). Dead since D-042.
  Measured on the real app: the selected Audio trigger and the unselected Video
  trigger had byte-identical computed style — `background-color: rgba(0,0,0,0)`,
  `color: oklab(… / 0.6)`, `box-shadow: none`. `TimelineSwitcher.tsx` carried
  the same one-word defect in its own `data-selected:border-b-accent`, so the
  active timeline's accent underline had never once drawn either. Both fixed;
  the retheming that follows is D-254.

- **verification — real Chromium with `requestAnimationFrame` stubbed dead**,
  which is the only honest way to reproduce a bug whose trigger is "rAF does not
  tick", and which jsdom passing is what shipped in the first place. Driven over
  CDP against D-142's own harness (`app/harness.html`), extended with a
  `?mode=inspector` mode that mounts the real `EditorInspectorPanel` inside the
  same bounded-height flex column `EditorTab.tsx` gives it. The tab is flipped
  through the SAME `setInspectorTab` store action `debug_set_inspector_tab`
  calls — never a synthesised click.

  - **rAF dead, before the fix** (reproduces the live app exactly): 2 panels,
    both `display: flex` — Video at y=89 h=1082, Audio at y=1171 h=921; the
    deselected one carrying `inert` and `data-ending-style` and NO `hidden`.
  - **rAF dead, after the fix:** deselected panel `display: none`, rect 0×0;
    selected panel `display: flex`, y=88, h=938. Mirrored exactly on switching
    back.
  - **rAF healthy, after the fix:** exactly one panel with a box in each state,
    first heading `Transform` on Video and `Audio` on Audio; a real trusted
    CDP `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` click on the Video trigger behaves
    identically to the store-driven path.
  - **the live app** is where the bug was reproduced in the first place, with
    the measurements in the table above and a native `debug_screenshot` showing
    the Video tab's fields under a tab bar with no selected state. The fix
    itself could not be re-verified there, because that instance runs from the
    main checkout and this work is on its own branch.

- **regression test:** `ClipInspectorPanel.tabChrome.dom.test.tsx`, 5 tests.
  Its header states plainly that jsdom cannot see B-124 itself, so what it pins
  is the CONTRACT the fix stands on — that Base UI marks the selected tab
  `data-active` and the deselected panel `inert`, both checked against the real
  primitive — alongside the class strings that consume those attributes, so an
  attribute rename can never again silently leave the styling matching nothing.
  3 of the 5 were confirmed to fail on the pre-fix source (`expected … to
  contain 'data-active:border-b-accent'` / `'[&[inert]]:hidden'` /
  `'[&>*+*]:border-t'`); the other 2 are contract tests that pass either way, by
  design and as documented in the file.

  `@apelles/editor` 1513/1513 green (78 files), `@apelles/debug` 32/32,
  `npx tsc --noEmit` clean on `packages/editor` and `packages/ui`.

- **worth noting for next time.** Any Base UI primitive that hides a child by
  unmounting it — `Tabs.Panel`, and by inspection the same
  `useOpenChangeComplete` path in the popover/dialog/collapsible family — is
  relying on `requestAnimationFrame` to finish the job, and in a non-frontmost
  window it will not finish. That is not an exotic condition here: it is the
  normal condition for every agent-driven session this repo's debug tooling was
  built for. When a `debug_*` op reports the right state and the screenshot
  disagrees, suspect a frame that was never scheduled before suspecting the
  store.

---

## B-125 — `motion_select` had silently drifted away from the GUI gesture it exists to mirror: it always re-seeked, throwing away the playhead

**Found:** 2026-09-09, by the new `motionOps.test.ts` (D-257) — the first tests
this op surface has ever had. Not reported by a user; nothing outside the webview
could observe Motion's selection or playhead before D-257, which is part of why
it went unnoticed.

**Symptom.** An agent calling `motion_select` to look at a layer lost the
playhead every time: the preview jumped to the start of that layer's SCENE, even
when the playhead was already parked inside the exact layer being selected. The
equivalent human gesture — clicking the same row in the layer list — correctly
stayed put.

**Root cause: drift, not a coding error.** `motion_select` (D-170) was written to
mirror `MotionTab.tsx`'s `onSelect`, and at the time it did, exactly:
`setSelections([s]); playerRef.current?.seekTo(sceneStartFrame(...))`. `onSelect`
then gained two refinements that the op never received:

- **D-173** — only seek when the target is in a DIFFERENT scene than the playhead,
  fixing "scrub to a moment, then edit what's there," which is the tab's core
  workflow.
- **D-176** — a layer target seeks to where that LAYER actually starts
  (`layerVisibleFrameRange`), not merely to its scene's start, so selecting a
  layer that hasn't begun yet actually shows it.

Both edited the GUI callback. Neither edited the op, and nothing connected them —
the op was an untested copy of a two-line gesture, so the copy rotted in place
while the original improved. The generalisable lesson, and the reason this is a
`B-` and not just a diff: **an MCP op that re-implements a GUI handler's logic
instead of calling it will drift, and only a test comparing the two catches it.**

**Fix (D-257).** `motion_select` now runs the same conditional logic `onSelect`
does — `layerVisibleFrameRange` first, the scene-boundary check as the fallback
for scene/camera targets — and reports `seekedTo` (the frame it moved to, or
`null` when it deliberately stayed put) so the behaviour is observable rather
than merely correct. Three tests pin it: seeks when outside the target's window,
does NOT seek when already inside it, and applies the scene-boundary rule to a
scene target from another scene.

**Not fully fixed, and honestly so.** The op still holds its own copy of that
logic rather than calling a single shared function — `onSelect` closes over
`MotionTab.tsx`'s own `setWholeVideo` (D-181 solo-scene state) and its player ref,
so extracting it is a real refactor of the tab, not a rename. The test that
compares the two behaviours is what keeps them honest until then; extracting the
shared seek decision is the proper follow-up.

## B-126 — the marketing site publishes an MCP tool count that is 37 tools stale, and its own anti-fabrication test cannot currently fail loudly enough to stop it

status: fixed (2026-09-09/2026-09-10, D-264 + D-266 + D-270, reconciled through the D-293 merge) · severity: medium · area: website / docs-accuracy

**Original repro (2026-09-07).** `grep -c '^@mcp.tool()' mcp/server.py` returned
**152**. `website/src/data/mcp.ts` declared `TOOL_TOTALS = { all: 115, shipped:
106, debugOnly: 9 }`, and `website/tests/mcp-data.test.ts` asserted
`TOOL_TOTALS.all === TOOLS.length` against that same file — those could not
both be true, so the test failed as things stood.

**Verified fixed, 2026-09-10.** `grep -c '^@mcp.tool()' mcp/server.py` now
returns **161** (9 `debug_*`, 37 `motion_*`). `website/src/data/mcp.ts`'s
`TOOL_TOTALS` is `{ all: 161, shipped: 152, debugOnly: 9 }` and its `TOOL_GROUPS`
breaks down as Edit 69 + Colorist 42 + Motion 37 + Media understanding 4 = 152
— matching exactly. The stale "Motion tab's 0 MCP tools" framing is gone
(`TOOL_GROUPS` now has a real `Motion` entry, and `GAPS` no longer mentions it).
Ran `website/tests/mcp-data.test.ts` directly (`npm install && npm test` in
`website/`, since it's still deliberately outside the npm workspace): **77/77
pass**, including `total tool count matches the server`, `Motion matches the
real motion_* tools`, and `does not claim a gap that has actually been closed`.
`npm run check` (astro + tsc): 0 errors. This entry itself was left at
`status: open` after the fix landed — corrected in this pass rather than
re-fixing an already-fixed bug.

**Cause (historical).** Ordering, not a coding error. D-255 (the website)
landed on 2026-09-09 with numbers correct as of that moment; D-257 added 32
`motion_*` tools later the same day and did not update `website/`, and a
follow-up pass added 4 more. `website/` being outside the npm workspace meant
`npm test` at the repo root never ran its suite, so the guard test's failure
was invisible from the normal test command.

**What actually fixed it.** D-264 (2026-09-09) rebuilt `website/src/data/mcp.ts`
and rewrote `website/tests/mcp-data.test.ts` as a real anti-fabrication guard:
it now parses `TOOLS` directly out of `mcp/server.py` at test time (a regex
over `@mcp.tool()` decorators) and asserts every published total/group
count/sample name against that live list, rather than a hardcoded number — the
"must be 0" `motion_` assertion the original bug called out no longer exists in
this form. D-266 (2026-09-09) and D-270 (2026-09-10) each re-counted and
updated `TOOL_TOTALS`/`TOOL_GROUPS` as real tools were added
(`editor_reprobe_media`, the media-pool read/organise tools, the two
audio-monitoring ones), and the 2026-09-10 merge (D-293 branch) reconciled two
concurrent count bumps (160→161) during conflict resolution rather than
silently picking one side.

**Still open, deliberately not folded into this fix (a real decision, not an
oversight):** `website/` remaining outside the root npm workspace means its
suite still is not reachable from a bare `npm test` at the repo root — the
"deeper fix" this entry originally flagged. `mcp-data.test.ts` is now robust
enough that a future tool addition fails LOUDLY the next time anyone runs
`npm test` inside `website/` (which `npm run verify` there also does), but
nothing forces that run automatically from the root. Worth its own `D-NNN` if
it's ever prioritized; not re-scoped into this bug fix.

## B-127 — the filmstrip's keyframe-interval MEMORY cache was keyed on the path alone, in front of a disk cache keyed on (path, mtime, len): a replaced source served the old file's interval forever

status: fixed (2026-09-09, D-260) · severity: medium (silent, and it decides how filmstrip tiles are extracted; invisible within a session, and an app restart cleared it) · area: `crates/apelles-media/src/filmstrip.rs`

- **found:** 2026-09-09, while auditing which caches over a source file a D-260 Motion re-render would and would not invalidate. Not user-reported — by construction it cannot produce an error message, only slightly wrong tiles.
- **repro:** open a project, scroll a clip's filmstrip (this measures and memoises the source's keyframe interval), replace that source file in place — a re-export over the same name, `ffmpeg -i … same.mov`, or D-260's Motion re-render — then scroll the filmstrip again in the same session.
- **expected:** the new file's own keyframe interval is measured, as `media_cache`'s whole (path ‖ mtime ‖ len) identity exists to guarantee.
- **actual:** the previous file's interval is served for the rest of the process's life.
- **cause:** `KEYFRAME_MEM` was `HashMap<PathBuf, f64>` — path-keyed and insert-only — sitting directly in front of a disk layer (`media_cache::read_json(NS_KEYFRAME, source_key)`) keyed on `blake3(path ‖ mtime ‖ len)`. Two different keys for one question, with the weaker one in front, so the memory layer answered before the correct key was ever consulted. **This is byte-for-byte B-056**, which `crates/apelles-media/src/probe.rs`'s module doc already records and which D-146 fixed — in `PROBE_CACHE`. That sweep did not reach this map, which is the one cache in `filmstrip.rs` that had no staleness check at all (`CHUNK_MEM`/the chunk disk cache are both `source_key`-keyed; `CHUNK_LOCKS` is bounded by B-057's guard).
- **why it matters, concretely:** the interval decides `keyframe_only` in `extract` — whether a chunk's tiles are decoded at their real frames or snapped to the nearest keyframe. A stale interval from a differently-encoded file makes that call wrong in either direction: visibly wrong tiles, or a much slower extraction.
- **fix (D-260):** the map is `HashMap<PathBuf, (Option<String>, f64)>` — the interval paired with the `source_key` it was measured under — and a hit is accepted only when that key still matches. `source_key: None` (an unstattable, offline source) serves the remembered value unvalidated rather than re-probing a file that cannot be read, which is exactly `probe_cached`'s own documented call for the same situation. The key is already computed by the caller, so this costs one `HashMap` value comparison and no extra `stat`. Pinned by `keyframe_interval_rejects_a_memory_hit_from_a_replaced_file`, which needs no media and so runs everywhere, unlike this module's env-gated siblings.

## B-128 — a media pool item whose source file was replaced in place kept the old file's probed duration and old thumbnail forever, and `Root.tsx` claimed in a comment that it did not

status: fixed (2026-09-09, D-260) · severity: medium (the pool's `video` block is what `editor_add_clip` reads for a clip's `source_len`/`source_fps`, so a stale one bounds trims against a length the file no longer has) · area: `crates/apelles-project/src/manifest.rs`, `app/src/Root.tsx`

- **found:** 2026-09-09, reading `Root.tsx`'s `onMotionRendered` while scoping D-260. The comment there asserted the opposite of the truth, which is why this counts as a defect rather than an unimplemented feature.
- **repro:** render a Motion scene (its output path is fixed per scene, so it always writes the same file), change the manifest, render again. Watch the item in Sources.
- **expected:** the Sources item reflects the new render — its poster thumbnail and its probed frame count/duration/fps.
- **actual:** both stay as they were at the FIRST render, for the life of the project, not just the session — they are persisted in `project.json` and in `<video_dir>/.chroma/thumbs/<media id>.jpg`.
- **cause:** two independent halves, both structural.
  1. **`add_media` skips a path already in the pool** — correct for its own job (re-importing one file twice must not duplicate it) and exactly wrong for a file replaced in place. So the only path that ever writes `MediaItem::video` never ran again.
  2. **The thumbnail cache has no staleness check at all.** It is keyed on the *item's* id (`thumbs/<media id>.jpg`, D-059), which by design never changes — unlike every `media_cache`-backed artefact in this workspace, which is keyed on `blake3(path ‖ mtime ‖ len)` (D-128).
- **the wrong comment, which is the part worth recording.** `Root.tsx`'s D-062 fallback branch read: "already in the pool from an earlier render at the same path … refresh so its thumbnail/video info reflect the new render, not silently leave a stale entry." `refresh()` calls `chroma_media_list`, which re-reads `project.json` — and `project.json` is precisely where the stale probe was stored. The code did the opposite of what its own comment promised, and a reader checking whether this case was handled would have concluded it was.
- **fix (D-260):** a new `refresh_media` model function (and `chroma_media_refresh` command) that *reconciles* rather than imports: it adds a path that is not pooled, re-probes one that is, and regenerates the thumbnail only when `thumb_is_stale` — the thumbnail file's mtime against the source's — says so. `Root.tsx` calls that instead, and its comment now describes what actually happens. Everything expensive stays conditional: `probe_cached` is `(mtime, len)`-memoised, so an unchanged file costs a couple of `stat`s and writes nothing (asserted: "reconciling an unchanged file must not dirty the manifest").

## B-129 — "Add Title" never chose a track: it dropped the title on whatever track was already selected, video OR audio

status: fixed (2026-09-09, D-262) · severity: high (a title that lands in a gap in the footage track renders over BLACK instead of over the picture, and one on an audio track renders nowhere at all — both silently, with a correct-looking clip in the timeline) · area: `packages/editor/src/timeline.ts`, `packages/editor/src/EditLibraryRail.tsx`, `packages/editor/src/useEditorControl.ts`, `mcp/server.py`

- **found:** 2026-09-09, reported live by the owner with a screenshot, and then confirmed by reading their real project (`~/Movies/Chroma/perf-comparison-reel-v3.chroma`) through `get_timeline` before any code was touched. Two real instances in one project:
  - `text-mttqgc8c-ia26` (startFrame 30, duration 72) sitting on **track 0, a video track**, in the gap between `after-1.08.16pm.mov` and `before-1.09.51pm.mov` — i.e. inside an existing footage track's clip list rather than on a layer of its own.
  - `text-mtsxdpkb-gr8e` (startFrame 1263) sitting on **track 1, an AUDIO track** — a text clip on an audio track composites into nothing and can never be seen.
- **repro:** open a project that already has footage on track 0. Open the library rail's Titles popover, press "Add at playhead". The title is spliced into track 0 alongside the footage. Separately: call `editor_add_text_clip(track=N)` for any `N` that happens to be an audio track — the clip is placed, with no complaint.
- **expected (the owner's own words):** "it should be added on a new timeline meaning a new track instead of adding on top of other." A title is an overlay; it belongs on its own video layer above the picture, which is also what this repo's own Resolve reference already said ("drag it into the timeline **above your video tracks**", `scratch/resolve-reference/resolve-edit-features.json`, quoted verbatim in `EditLibraryRail.tsx`'s own module doc since D-248).
- **actual:** the title went onto whichever track the caller named, unvalidated, and the GUI's own "caller" was hardcoded to the first EXISTING video track.
- **cause — three layers, one real defect.** The defect is that **the track-kind rule existed in exactly one caller instead of in the op**:
  1. **`applyOp`'s `add_clip` reducer (`timeline.ts`) had no track-kind gate at all.** It splices whatever clip it is handed into whatever track index it is handed. The ONLY guard anywhere in the app was in `TimelinePane.tsx`'s `onDrop` (D-248, `A ${label} is picture — drop it on a video track…`), which is a UI handler — so every non-drop caller walked straight past it. That is the audio-track title, exactly.
  2. **The library rail's click-to-add targeted `videoTrackIndex(timeline)`** — documented in its own comment as "the topmost video track", which is true and is not the same thing as "a track a title should go on". On any real project that track is full of footage, so the title either landed in a gap (the frame-30 instance) or was refused for want of room. The D-248 comment reasoned correctly about *z-order* ("a lower index is on top") and then silently equated "on top" with "the first existing video track".
  3. **`editor_add_text_clip`/`editor_add_adjustment_clip` required an explicit `track` and validated nothing about it.** Worse, the failure message they printed when the clip did not land — "check the track index (and that it is a video track)" — asserted a check that did not exist anywhere, so a reader would conclude the reducer enforced it. And the MCP docstring taught agents a three-call `editor_add_track` → `editor_move_track` → `editor_add_text_clip` dance to get a title above existing footage; an agent that skipped it landed the title on whatever that index happened to be.
- **fix (D-262):** the rule moved into the op, and the default moved to a new track. `checkAddClip(tl, track, clip)` is the one answer — shaped like the existing `checkTransition`/`checkEditIn`, refused by `applyOp` as a no-op and asked by the MCP tools for the real sentence. `add_clip` gained `onNewVideoTrack`, which inserts an empty video track at index 0 and places there **in one op** (one history entry, so one Undo removes both the clip and the track — the drop path's `add_track` + `move_track` + `add_clip` sequence takes three). Both the GUI button and the MCP tools now default to it; `track` on `editor_add_text_clip`/`editor_add_adjustment_clip` became optional, and passing a non-video one is refused with a real message rather than accepted. The GUI can no longer fail to place a title at all, since a fresh track always has room.
- **pinned by:** `TimelinePane.drop.dom.test.tsx` tests 10-14 — click-to-add makes a new video track and leaves the existing edit untouched; it still works with the playhead over an occupied clip (the old silent refusal); the add is one history entry labelled "on a new video track"; the reducer refuses a title on an audio track whatever the caller, while still allowing one on a video track; and an adjustment clip is gated and re-homed by the same rules.

## B-130 — a title's on-canvas selection box was the whole 1080x1920 frame, around text 12% of the frame tall

status: fixed (2026-09-09, D-262) · severity: medium (nothing renders wrong, but the box is the only on-canvas affordance a title has, and it also made a selected title swallow every canvas click meant for the footage beneath it) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/edit.rs`, `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/text.rs`

- **found:** 2026-09-09, reported live by the owner from a screenshot of a real title (`{content: 'Title', font: 'sans-bold', size: 0.12, color: '#FFFFFF'}`) whose selection box spanned essentially the entire composition while the rendered text sat small and centred. Their words: "why it has such a big frame."
- **repro:** select any title clip in the Edit tab. The `TransformOverlay` box is the full composition, at every font size and every content length.
- **expected:** a selection box around the thing that is selected.
- **actual:** a box around the whole frame.
- **cause — and this is the part worth recording, because it looked deliberate and was not.** `clip_geometry`'s `is_text()` branch returned `natural_width/height = 1.0`, on the reasoning D-211 wrote there: "a text clip's layer is generated at exactly the composition's size, so its natural footprint IS the whole frame." That statement is *true about the buffer* and irrelevant to the question being asked: `render_text_layer` allocates a composition-sized RGBA canvas and then draws a small, centred ink box into it — the rest is transparent. Nothing ever decided that the whole buffer was the right thing to report as a footprint; D-211's actual decision about the on-canvas box was to hide the corner HANDLES (a text clip's `scale` is pinned server-side), and `docs/notes/text-title-clips.md` listed on-canvas title drag as deferred work that "should be close to free" — so the box size was inherited from a Rust implementation detail, never weighed. The stale test name `renders a full-frame box (its natural footprint is the whole composition)` documented the side-effect as if it were the intent.
- **second, quieter half:** `useCanvasClipPick` hit-tests the same footprint, so a title claimed the ENTIRE canvas for click-to-select. With a title selected, no click anywhere on the picture could select the footage under it.
- **fix (D-262):** `clip_geometry` reports a title's real rendered INK box as a fraction of the composition, measured by a new `chroma::text::text_layer_ink_fraction` built on `lay_out_text` — the same advance-and-kern glyph walk `rasterise` draws with, extracted so there is one measurement rather than an estimate beside it. An adjustment clip keeps `1.0 x 1.0` (its correction genuinely is full-frame), so the two cases are no longer grouped under one comment that was only right about one of them. A title with no ink — empty content, its ordinary state the moment it is added — falls back to the whole frame rather than a zero-size, ungrabbable box. **No frontend change was needed:** `TransformOverlay` was already asking the right question and being given a wrong answer.
- **pinned by:** four Rust tests in `text.rs` — the measured ink is a small box, not the frame, for the owner's own title on a 1080x1920 frame; it scales with font size and grows with content; empty text measures as no ink; and `the_measured_ink_box_is_where_the_glyphs_actually_land` scans the actual rasterised alpha and asserts the measurement matches the drawn glyphs to within a pixel and is centred. Plus `TransformOverlay.textClip.dom.test.tsx`, whose stale full-frame assertion was replaced by one that the box tracks the reported ink and is well under half the canvas.

## B-131 — `add_clip` still has no occupancy check: an explicit `track` + `startFrame` from the MCP layer can splice a clip into a span another clip already covers

status: **fixed** (D-272, 2026-09-10) · severity: low-medium (unreachable from the GUI; an agent naming a track and a frame could still produce a same-track overlap the drag path refuses to create) · area: `packages/editor/src/timeline.ts` (`checkAddClip`, `applyOp`'s `add_clip` case), `packages/editor/src/useEditorControl.ts` (`editor_add_clip`/`editor_add_text_clip`/`editor_add_adjustment_clip`)

- **found:** 2026-09-09, writing D-263's DOM coverage for the docked library panel. A test that expected the documented refusal ("There is already a clip at the playhead on the top video track…") found no refusal at all — the clip had been placed, overlapping.
- **what changed the same night.** D-262/B-129 rewrote the GUI's click-to-add to place on a **brand-new video track** (`onNewVideoTrack`), so the gesture this was found through cannot overlap anything any more, and the drag path never could (`computeInsertion`/`resolveClipLanding`, D-095/D-104: "landing mid-overlap is never a reachable outcome of a plain drag, full stop"). What remains is the op itself.
- **repro (MCP):** `editor_add_text_clip` (or `editor_add_clip`) naming an explicit `track` AND a `startFrame` inside a clip that track already holds.
- **expected:** the same answer the drag path gives — place it in the gap, or refuse in words.
- **actual:** spliced in regardless; two clips on one track now cover the same frames.
- **cause:** `applyOpPure`'s `add_clip` case branches only on `op.ripple`; with `ripple: false` it clamps `startFrame` to `>= 0` and splices, never asking whether the span is free. `checkAddClip` — the precondition the MCP tools *do* call — validates the track's KIND only (is this picture going onto an audio track), not its occupancy.
- **fix (D-272):** `checkAddClip` gained three optional trailing params (`fps`, `startFrame`, `ripple`) and now also answers the occupancy question — the same "explicit position, overlap rejected unless `ripple`" contract `move`'s own `overlaps` check already enforces, not a new pattern. It refuses naming the conflicting clip and its span (e.g. `frames 150-179 on track 0 are already covered by "B-roll 1" (frames 100-199) — pass ripple: true …`). `applyOp`'s `add_clip` case calls the widened check against the pre-clone tracks and no-ops on refusal, same convention `move` uses. All three MCP placement tools (`editor_add_clip`, `editor_add_text_clip`, `editor_add_adjustment_clip`) now run this pre-flight and surface `check.reason` as a real tool error — `editor_add_clip` had never called `checkAddClip` at all before this. No Rust change: `apelles-timeline` has no `add_clip` op of its own to mirror (its own module doc says so explicitly).
- **tests:** `packages/editor/src/timeline.test.ts`, `add_clip occupancy check (B-131)` — the naive overlap is refused (both `checkAddClip` and `applyOp`, which leaves the timeline unchanged), a legitimate non-overlapping add still works, and `ripple: true` remains the escape hatch. Full `packages/editor` suite (1641 tests, 85 files) green.

## B-132 — `useSessionStore.busy` was a latching flag with no owner, no recovery and no visibility: one `await` that never settled left a running app permanently unable to create or open ANY project

status: **fixed** (D-268, 2026-09-09) · severity: **blocker** (a wedged app cannot create or open a project at all, by GUI or by MCP, until it is quit and relaunched) · area: `app/src/store/useSessionStore.ts`, now `app/src/store/sessionLock.ts`

- **found:** 2026-09-09, live. On a running app with nothing visibly in flight, `new_project` (MCP) returned `{"ok": false, "error": "session busy"}` for call after call. `debug_ui_state` reported `projectOpen: false, timelineStatus: idle` — which read as "the app is idle but refuses to work".
- **repro:** hold the session lock and never release it — any `await` inside a `busy: true` block that never settles will do (a lost Tauri IPC transport, B-081; a Rust command that blocks the async runtime; or simply an op still running after `control.rs`'s 20s `BRIDGE_TIMEOUT` has already answered the HTTP caller). Then call any session action.
- **expected:** the session recovers, or at minimum says what is holding it.
- **actual:** `busy` stayed `true` for the rest of the process's life. All seven session actions (`newProject`, `openProject`, `addShots`, `removeShot`, `switchToShot`, `relinkShot`, `saveUntitledAs`) are gated on it, so every one of them returned the same opaque `session busy` forever. The only user-facing recovery was quitting the app.
- **cause — three defects in one bare boolean, not one:**
  1. **No recovery.** `busy` was set `true`, cleared in a `finally`, and had no timeout, no owner and no reset path. `finally` never runs if an `await` never settles, so a single hung call latched the flag permanently. This is what made a transient hang into a dead app.
  2. **Not re-entrant — the guard was partly fictional.** `_hydrateOpenDto` is called both directly (`SourcesPanel`'s "add to grading") and from inside five actions that had *already* set `busy: true`. It unconditionally set the flag on entry and cleared it in its own `finally`, so on all five in-store paths it released its **caller's** lock while the caller was still running: the tail of `newProject`/`openProject`/`addShots`/`removeShot`/`relinkShot` ran with no mutual exclusion at all. Introduced by D-063, which set the flag there for a real reason (the direct caller needed it) without noticing the nested case.
  3. **Invisible and unactionable.** The refusal named nothing — not the holder, not its age. No surface reported the flag either: `debug_ui_state` reports the **Edit tab's** `openProjectKey`, not this store, so the `projectOpen: false` that made the app look idle was answering a different question entirely. Nothing anywhere exposed `useSessionStore.busy`.
- **what was RULED OUT.** The first hypothesis was zustand `persist` rehydrating `busy: true` from a snapshot written by a process killed mid-action. Refuted outright: `useSessionStore` is a plain `create(...)` with **no `persist` middleware**, `busy: false` is the literal initial value, and nothing outside the store's own actions ever writes it. So no on-disk state was ever corrupted and **no recovery path for existing installs is needed** — a relaunch always started clean, which is exactly why the wedge looked like it appeared from nowhere.
- **live evidence** (`~/Library/Logs/studio.apelles.app/app.log`, the session this was found in): launch at 17:39:06, then four minutes with no telemetry at all, then `project_open` (`shotCount: 0`) at 17:43:12, `project_close` at 17:43:13, `project_new` (`mediaCount: 0`) at 17:43:17. The flag was therefore **held and later released**, not restored-as-true at boot — consistent with a long-running or failed in-flight holder, and inconsistent with the persistence theory.
- **honest limit.** The specific `await` that first took the lock and did not come back was NOT identified: the app was no longer running by the time this was investigated, and a sibling agent's `cargo test` made starting a concurrent build unsafe (this repo's own `e2e/run.sh` refuses for the same reason). What is fixed is the defect that turns any such hang into a permanently dead session — and the stale-lock break now logs the holder's op name, which is the evidence a recurrence needs and which did not exist before.
- **fix (D-268):** `busy` becomes a real lock (`app/src/store/sessionLock.ts`) that names its holder in the refusal, is re-entrant by explicit hand-off (a caller passes its handle to `_hydrateOpenDto`; `release()` is identity-checked so a nested callee can never drop a lock it did not take), and breaks a lock abandoned for longer than `STALE_SESSION_LOCK_MS` with a loud `console.error`. `closeProject` drops it too, so "‹ Projects" is a real human recovery. `get_state` now reports `session.busy` / `heldBy` / `heldForMs` so an agent can see the wedge instead of guessing.
- **why it reached a live session:** `app/` had **no test runner at all**, so the store gating every project operation in the product had zero tests. D-268 adds vitest to the `app` workspace; the two new suites fail against each of the behaviours above (verified by reintroducing them).

## B-133 — selecting a trim tool (Slip/Slide) or arming the smart-trim heuristic never visibly changed the cursor

status: **fixed** (2026-09-09) · severity: **minor** (the underlying edit still worked — D-235/D-250/D-261's toolbar readout and badge told you the mode — the cursor itself, the fastest of the three signals, just never moved) · area: `packages/editor/src/TimelinePane.tsx`

- **found:** 2026-09-09, live — the owner selected the Slide tool (D-261's trim palette) and reported "when i change the [tool] the mouse does not change".
- **expected:** hovering a clip with an edit tool selected (or Alt armed under Select) shows the cursor `trimModeCursor` resolves for that hover — `grabbing` for Slip/Slide, `ew-resize` for Ripple/Roll/a plain trim.
- **actual:** the cursor never changed, regardless of tool.
- **cause:** `trimModeCursor(hoverTrimMode)` was already being computed correctly and written to the edit area's own `style.cursor` (D-250) — but only `ClipBody`, the element the pointer is actually over, carries a hardcoded `cursor-grab active:cursor-grabbing` Tailwind class on every clip regardless of tool. An element's own declared `cursor` always wins over an ancestor's, no matter the ancestor's specificity, so that class silently masked the container's inline style on every clip — the one place the feature actually needed to be seen. Ripple/Roll's edge-zone cursor happened to still show correctly, because their `ew-resize` is resolved on the library's own stretch-handle elements, which (checked in the vendored CSS) set no cursor of their own.
- **fix:** `onTrimHoverMove` now also writes the resolved mode's cursor straight onto the specific hovered clip's own element (a direct DOM write, not React state — the same per-pointer-move performance discipline `placeTrimBadge` already uses), clearing the previous element's override first; `onTrimHoverLeave` clears it. No `ClipBody` prop changes needed, since the fix targets exactly the element already masking the ancestor.

## B-134 — dragging a clip does not visually move its A/V-linked partner on the other track during the gesture

status: **fixed** (2026-09-10) · severity: **minor** (the op that commits on drop was always correct — the linked partner really did end up in the right place, see D-098/D-100's own linked-move handling — this was a live-feedback gap during the drag itself, not a wrong result) · area: `packages/editor/src/TimelinePane.tsx` (`linkDragGhosts`), `packages/editor/src/timeline.ts` (`linkedDragGhosts`)

- **found:** 2026-09-09, live — the owner dragged a clip on Video 1 and its linked audio clip on Audio 1 sat still on screen for the whole gesture, only snapping to its real new position once the drag was released. Screenshot: the dragged video clip shows dnd-kit's live drag styling; the audio clip directly below it shows none.
- **expected:** an A/V-linked clip's other half tracks the drag in real time, the way a real NLE (and this app's own same-track ripple-shift ghosts, `dragSyncGhosts`) shows a live preview of everything a drag is about to move, not just the one thing under the pointer.
- **actual:** only the directly-grabbed clip moves with the pointer; its linked partner was visually inert until drop.
- **root cause, confirmed:** `ClipBody`'s live drag transform comes from dnd-kit's own `useDraggable`, which only ever animates the element whose `id` (`clip:${track}:${clipId}`) matches `event.active.id` — i.e. the exact node the pointer pressed. The linked partner is a separate `ClipBody` instance, with a different `clipId`, on a different track's row; nothing hands it a matching live transform.
- **fix:** the same shape of fix `clipDragPreview`/`dragSyncGhosts` (D-098/B-077) already used for ripple-shifted clips on OTHER tracks — a synthesized ghost overlay — applied to a dragged clip's `link_group` instead. `TimelinePane.tsx`'s new `linkDragGhosts` renders one dashed, accent-toned box (distinct from `dragSyncGhosts`'s neutral `text-secondary` styling, matching `avLinkedIds`'s own convention that an A/V link is a stronger, more specific relationship than a sync-lock ripple — D-128) per OTHER member of the dragged clip's link group, for the whole gesture, gone the instant it ends. Unlike `dragSyncGhosts`, it is NOT gated on `clipDragPreview.ripple` — an A/V link moves with its primary on every move, ripple or not (`timeline.ts`'s `move` op unconditionally computes and applies the link delta before it even asks whether a ripple fired).
- **the two "not investigated yet" questions, both resolved:**
  - **Does a cross-track drag need the ghost to jump tracks?** No. `timeline.ts`'s `move` op (D-129) moves every other link-group member by the same frame DELTA while leaving it on its OWN track — "a linked pair keeps sync, it does not follow the video half onto the video half's new track" (that op's own comment, mirroring Resolve's documented behaviour). The new `linkedDragGhosts` function is not even given the primary's destination track as an input, by construction — there is no `toTrack` for it to (wrongly) follow.
  - **Does `onDndDragEnd`'s commit path already have the position math this ghost needs?** Yes, exactly: `onDndDragMove`/`onDndDragEnd` both resolve the primary's landing via the same `resolveClipLanding` call and pass the resulting `startFrame` to `applyOp({kind:'move', ...})`; `timeline.ts`'s `move` case then derives `delta = op.startFrame - c.start_frame` and applies it to every linked sibling. The new ghost reuses that exact delta (computed from `clipDragPreview.startFrame`, itself already `resolveClipLanding`'s output) so the preview can never disagree with what actually commits.
- **implementation note — pulled out to a pure function, unlike `dragSyncGhosts`:** the position math lives in `timeline.ts`'s new `linkedDragGhosts(tl, fromTrack, clipId, landingStartFrame, fps)`, with `TimelinePane.tsx`'s `linkDragGhosts` as a one-line `useMemo` wrapper over it. This was not a style choice — it is why the fix has a real test at all. Attempting a real-DOM proof first (mounting `TimelinePane`, driving a real pointer drag via `testUtils/pointerHarness.ts`, same pattern as `TimelinePane.marquee.dom.test.tsx`/`TimelinePane.trim.dom.test.tsx`) confirmed, empirically, a limitation those two files' own headers already disclosed from a different angle: jsdom has no layout engine, so `<DndContext>`'s collision detection resolves NO `event.over` at all without real droppable geometry. Going one step further than either prior file — stubbing `TrackDropZone`'s own rect too, which neither had done — still failed: dnd-kit's `DragOverlay` preview node (not the original clip) is what collision detection actually measures as the dragged rect once a `DragOverlay` is in use, and that node's on-screen position comes entirely from a CSS `transform` dnd-kit itself manages, invisible to jsdom's (real, necessary) inline-style-based rect stubbing — confirmed directly by instrumenting `onDndDragMove` and observing `event.active.rect.current.initial` come back `{left:0, top:0}` regardless of any droppable stub, no matter how permissive. A DOM test therefore cannot observe this fix's real output; the pure function is what makes it provable at all, with **8 real unit tests** in `timeline.test.ts`'s new `linkedDragGhosts (B-134)` suite — including one that asserts the previewed shift equals EXACTLY what `applyOp`'s real `move` case commits for the same siblings, so the preview and the commit cannot drift apart.
- **verification:** `npm test --workspace @apelles/editor` — 85 files, 1645 tests, all passing (the 8 new ones among them); `tsc --noEmit` on the package clean.

## B-135 — an external write to a focused Inspector numeric field (undo, most visibly) does not show up until the field loses focus

status: **fixed** (2026-09-09) · severity: **minor** (the underlying value was always correct — this is a display staleness, not data loss) · area: `packages/ui/src/hooks/use-number-scrub.ts` (`useNumberField`)

- **found:** 2026-09-09, live — the owner typed into the Opacity field, then pressed Cmd+Z. Screenshot: the field still reads the typed value; the owner's own words, "it applies the changes but value does not change at all until we defocus :/ not connected to real state."
- **expected:** undo pops the history stack and applies the previous value (confirmed working correctly and immediately at the store level — this bug is purely about what the FOCUSED FIELD shows), and a focused field showing that same property should reflect it right away.
- **actual:** the field kept showing what was typed, unrelated to the real value, until blur.
- **cause:** `useNumberField` keeps a `draft` string while focused so a trailing `.` or `0` mid-typing survives re-renders (documented, correct, necessary). It was cleared in exactly one place: `onBlur`. Any OTHER reason the `value` prop changed — an undo, a redo, a different clip becoming selected while this same row stayed focused, a keyframe/playhead move — left the stale draft in place, because nothing ever told the field the prop's new value did not originate from its own typing.
- **fix:** a `lastPushedRef` records the exact number this field itself last sent via `onValueChange`. Adjusted during render (React's own documented pattern for resetting derived state on an external change, chosen over an effect specifically so the correction lands in the same frame — an effect would commit one stale frame first and visibly flash the old draft): whenever `draft !== null` and the incoming `value` does not match what this field itself last pushed, the draft is cleared immediately, letting the real value show while still focused.
- **verification:** `PropertyRow.numericField.dom.test.tsx`'s new `B-135` suite types into a field, then writes the store directly (exactly what undo does — no idea the field or its draft exist) and asserts the field shows the new value without ever blurring. Confirmed to fail without the fix (reverted the hook, re-ran: `expected '0.35' to be '1'`) before confirming it passes with it.

## B-136 — the numeric field's drag-to-scrub gesture never visibly changed the mouse cursor

status: **fixed** (2026-09-10, D-271) · severity: **minor** (the scrub itself worked — the value changed correctly under the pointer — only the cursor affordance was missing) · area: `packages/ui/src/components/ui/scrubbable-number-input.tsx` (the fix); `packages/ui/src/hooks/use-number-scrub.ts` (cleaned of the abandoned CSS attempt)

- **found:** 2026-09-09, live — the owner dragged an Inspector numeric field to scrub its value and reported the cursor never changed, with a screenshot of the plain OS arrow sitting over the field mid-drag.
- **expected:** the pointer shows an `ew-resize`-style cursor for the whole drag, the way Resolve's own "virtual slider" and Blender's number buttons do.
- **actual:** the plain arrow, unchanged, for the entire gesture.
- **first attempt, wrong (not this codebase's bug — a WebKit platform limit):** assumed this was the same shape as B-133 (a same-element class masking an ancestor's `style.cursor`) and applied the identical fix — writing `document.body.style.cursor = 'ew-resize'` directly during the drag. The owner's own follow-up screenshot showed this made no difference. Investigated further rather than assumed fixed: WebKit freezes the VISIBLE system cursor for the ENTIRE duration of an actively-held mouse button and does not re-query CSS `cursor` again until release, no matter how many times the DOM property is written mid-drag — a documented WebKit limitation, not a masking bug any CSS write can route around. (A `releasePointerCapture`-on-active-drag change was tried alongside this on the theory that WebKit's freeze was tied to pointer capture specifically; also confirmed to make no difference, since the freeze turns out to be an AppKit-level mousedown tracking behaviour independent of the DOM capture API. Left in as harmless — it is still correct hygiene, since capture was never the drag's actual delivery mechanism here.)
- **real fix (D-271):** Tauri's native `getCurrentWindow().setCursorIcon(...)` sets the OS cursor directly, bypassing WebKit's CSS-during-mousedown freeze entirely because it never asks WebKit to repaint at all. Lives in `ScrubbableNumberInput` (not the shared `useNumberScrub`/`useNumberField` hooks, which stay framework-agnostic for `@apelles/motion`'s sake) since every real consumer of that component already runs inside the Tauri window. `@apelles/ui` gained a real `@tauri-apps/api` dependency for this.
- **second bug, same session — the fix was wired correctly and still did nothing:** rebuilt and retested, the owner reported "the cursor does not works at all" with no change at all. Cause: Tauri v2 gates `setCursorIcon` behind `core:window:allow-set-cursor-icon` (confirmed against this app's own generated `gen/schemas/desktop-schema.json`), and `app/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json` never granted it — an ungranted Tauri v2 command is refused with a rejected promise, not a thrown exception, and the original `setNativeCursor` helper's own `.catch(() => {})` swallowed that rejection identically to "no Tauri runtime present" (the one case that legitimately should stay silent). Fixed two ways: the permission is now granted, and `setNativeCursor` checks `'__TAURI_INTERNALS__' in window` first (the only silent case) and `console.error`s anything that fails past that, naming the capability grant as the first thing to check — so a recurrence of this exact shape is loud, not a second multi-round-trip mystery.
- **third bug, same session — the grant was necessary but not sufficient:** rebuilt with the capability granted, confirmed (via the new logging staying silent) that the call was genuinely succeeding, and the owner STILL reported no visible change. Cause: WKWebView owns real AppKit cursor-rect tracking over its own bounds and re-asserts its OWN cursor — frozen per the WebKit bug above, whatever it was before the mouse went down — on every native mouse-moved event the drag generates. A single `setCursorIcon` call at the moment scrubbing starts wins for exactly one frame before the next native move overwrites it back. Fixed by fighting on the same terms: a `window` `pointermove` listener, live only while scrubbing, re-asserts `ewResize` on every move instead of trying to win with one call up front.
- **fourth bug, same session — conclusive proof the native API cannot win this fight at all:** rebuilt with unconditional (not error-gated) diagnostic logging, and the owner tested again. The log showed `setCursorIcon` resolving successfully on every single call, both `ewResize` and `default`, at the same cadence as the drag — and the owner still saw no visible change whatsoever. This rules out failure, misconfiguration, and timing all at once: WKWebView's own cursor-rect tracking wins this fight at a level no JS-visible `setCursorIcon` IPC round-trip can react fast enough to preempt.
- **real fix, finally (D-271):** abandoned the cursor-API approach entirely. `ScrubCursorGhost` (`scrubbable-number-input.tsx`) renders a small icon that tracks the pointer as an ordinary portaled DOM element — `style.transform` written directly on every `pointermove`, the same per-frame-direct-write discipline `TimelinePane.tsx`'s `placeTrimBadge` (D-250) already uses. This is not a cursor property in any sense WebKit's tracking has a stake in, so there is nothing left for it to override. `@apelles/ui` drops the now-unused `@tauri-apps/api` dependency and gains `react-dom` for the portal; `app/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json` drops the now-unused `core:window:allow-set-cursor-icon` grant in the same commit (an unused capability is attack surface with no offsetting benefit); `useNumberScrub`'s confirmed-non-functional `document.body.style.cursor` write is deleted rather than left as dead code.
- **confirmed live:** the owner tested and the ghost icon genuinely renders and tracks the pointer — the first of five rounds on this bug to actually show something. Remaining cosmetic gap: the real OS arrow was still also visible alongside it, since nothing had hidden it.
- **fifth bug, same session — a regression from trying to hide the real arrow, reverted:** tried `document.body.style.cursor = 'none'` set unconditionally inside `onPointerDown` itself (before a drag is even confirmed), on the theory that setting it at the exact moment of the native `pointerdown` might land before WebKit's freeze latches in. The owner reported the cursor disappearing in unrelated places — the timeline, other fields entirely outside this gesture. Global, shared, mutable state (`document.body.style.cursor`) set unconditionally with cleanup only in one path is exactly the "no guaranteed release" shape this same session's `sessionLock` work (D-268) already named as a defect class, and a missed/raced cleanup here doesn't fail quietly — it leaves the WHOLE app's cursor invisible, a strictly worse failure than the cosmetic redundancy it was trying to fix. Reverted outright; `useNumberScrub` touches no `cursor` property anywhere now.
- **owner pushed back, asked for real research rather than accepting the redundant-arrow state:** two things came of it. First, real research caught a genuine, unrelated latent regression from this bug's own second attempt: an early `releasePointerCapture()` call (added on an abandoned cursor theory, never cleaned up) would have silently broken tracking for any scrub that exits the actual app window's bounds, independent of the cursor saga entirely — reverted, capture now correctly holds for the whole gesture. Second, a real published precedent (`camwebby/shadcn-react-number-scrubber`, a community shadcn registry component, fetched and read directly) uses `active:cursor-none` — Tailwind's `:active` PSEUDO-CLASS, resolved natively by the browser at mousedown, not a scripted toggle — where all five prior attempts here were scripted toggles reacting to a state update on a later tick.
- **sixth attempt, the one that finally sticks:** WebKit bug 53341 is titled "Changing CSS cursor style doesn't have any effect while the mouse is down" — CHANGING, taken literally for the first time. `ScrubbableNumberInput`'s cursor class is now `cursor-none` UNCONDITIONALLY, from the very first render, never toggled by focus/hover/scrubbing state — there is no press-time transition for the freeze to catch, because nothing transitions. A stricter version of the shadcn scrubber's own proven pattern (permanently absent rather than conditionally-on-`:active`). `ScrubCursorGhost` now activates on hover as well as mid-scrub (previously scrubbing-only) so the field is never left with an invisible cursor and no affordance at all.
- **honest limit:** the ghost icon's own tracking was confirmed live by the owner before this final round; the STATIC `cursor-none` specifically (as opposed to the moving ghost, already proven) still needs the owner's own trackpad to confirm the real arrow is finally gone too. No amount of unit testing would have caught any of this bug's five live-only failure modes (a WebKit CSS freeze, a missing capability grant, a native cursor-API fight that cannot be won, a global-cursor-state regression, a latent pointer-capture regression from an abandoned theory) — all five were found only by shipping, watching it fail or break something else, and investigating further each time.

## B-137 — a clip drag's cursor-follow ghost sits at the clip's original position instead of under the pointer

status: **fixed** (D-279, 2026-09-10) · severity: **minor** (visual feedback only — the edit a drag commits was never wrong) · area: `packages/editor/src/TimelinePane.tsx`, `packages/editor/src/dragGhost.ts`

- **found:** 2026-09-10, live — the owner dragged a clip with the Trim tool active and reported the preview box staying at an "arbitrary start position" instead of tracking the cursor. Screenshot: `scratch/b137-trim-drag-preview-static.png` — a clip-sized highlight box sitting near `00:00:00`–`00:00:02` while the cursor is around `00:00:05`, with no visual connection between the two.
- **expected:** whatever preview represents the in-progress drag stays with the pointer for the whole gesture.
- **root cause (D-279):** the "preview box" is the `@dnd-kit/core` `DragOverlay` clip ghost, and two individually-correct things collide in it. `DragOverlay` anchors itself at the dragged node's own measured rect (`PositionedOverlay` writes `left: rect.left; top: rect.top`, then applies the drag transform — read in its bundled source), while D-119 caps that ghost's WIDTH at 320px so an hour-long clip does not become an off-screen-sized DOM node. For any clip wider than the cap the ghost is therefore a 320px stub pinned to the clip's LEFT EDGE, while the pointer is wherever in the body it actually pressed. At the default 90px/s zoom the cap is reached by every clip longer than ~3.5s, so this fires on essentially every real drag, and the further right you grab, the further behind the ghost sits. A single frame of that reads exactly as "pinned at the original position."
- **what the three candidates in the original entry turned out to be, since none of them was right:**
  - *"a regression in the vendored library's edge resize"* — **ruled out.** The gesture in the screenshot is not an edge resize at all: the box is identifiable as the dnd-kit ghost by the two things only it has (a floating, accent-ringed, clip-named box that overhangs the track-header column, i.e. outside the edit area entirely) and by its width being exactly D-119's 320px cap, measured against the 52px row height in the same image. A library edge-resize writes inline `left`/`width` on the action element in place and cannot leave the edit area.
  - *"something specific to the Trim TOOL"* — **ruled out, and it is worth saying why the tool looked implicated.** With Ripple or Roll chosen, a body drag is still the plain move it has always been (D-261, its own test 8), so it reaches the identical ghost — as does the Select tool. Covered by `TimelinePane.dragGhost.dom.test.tsx` test 4, which runs the same drag under Select and under Roll and asserts the two ghosts are identical, precisely so the wrong reading cannot be re-derived later. The likely reason the owner was on an edge when it happened: the library's stretch handles are only ~10px wide, so a press aimed at the edge that lands just inside it is a dnd-kit body drag, not a resize.
  - *"a one-off"* — **ruled out.** Reproduced deterministically in a real jsdom pointer drag (`TimelinePane.dragGhost.dom.test.tsx`), and it reproduces for every clip longer than the cap.
- **fix:** D-279 — the ghost is now a WINDOW onto the clip centred on the grab point, shifted right by that window's own offset (via a dnd-kit `Modifier` on `<DragOverlay>`, that library's own extension point) so the pixel under the cursor is the pixel being held. A strict no-op for clips that fit inside the cap.
- **tier note, for whoever is next in this area:** the vendored library's interact.js EDGE resize still cannot be driven under jsdom — re-verified by probe during this pass (a full, correctly-targeted `PointerEvent` sequence on `.timeline-editor-action-right-stretch` leaves the action's inline `left`/`width` untouched and the store unchanged), unchanged since D-235 established it. That is a limit on what the jsdom tier can cover, not on this diagnosis, which rests on the screenshot identifying a dnd-kit ghost.

## B-138 — Colorist's keyboard shortcuts fire in the Edit and Motion tabs

status: **fixed** (D-273, 2026-09-10) · severity: **major** (silent state changes in a tab the user isn't looking at) · area: `app/src/hooks/useKeyboardShortcuts.ts`, `packages/shell/src/Shell.tsx`

- **found:** 2026-09-10, by the D-273 shortcut audit (not a live report — the owner's request was for the audit itself).
- **cause:** `useKeyboardShortcuts` is mounted by `App.tsx`, which stays mounted underneath every tab (B-007, all tabs mount from boot), and it installed a bare `window` `keydown` listener. A `window` listener has no idea which tab is on screen, and every Colorist action whose `shouldFire` was `() => true` — the panel toggles (`M`, `D`, `R`, `K`, `P`, `I`, `E`, `A`), the rating keys, the colour-label keys, copy/paste adjustments, `open_settings` — therefore fired while the user was in the Edit or Motion tab.
- **actual:** pressing `M` in the Edit tab dropped a marker **and** toggled Colorist's Masks panel behind it (React's root handler and the `window` handler both ran — `preventDefault` does not stop propagation). ⌘1 both switched to the Edit tab and zoomed Colorist to 100%. `E` opened Colorist's Export panel from anywhere. None of it visible until the user switched back.
- **expected:** a tab's shortcuts apply only while that tab is frontmost.
- **fix:** D-273. Every action carries a `scope`; `Shell` — the one component that knows which tab is active — reports it to `@apelles/keymap`, and the single shared dispatcher will not consider an out-of-scope action. Where a `global` action and a tab action genuinely collide (⌘1), precedence is deterministic (global wins) and the shadowed one is flagged ⚠ in the Keyboard Shortcuts window instead of silently losing. Covered by `useShortcut.dom.test.tsx` ("does not fire a tab-scoped action while another tab is frontmost") and `TimelinePane.markers.dom.test.tsx` test 9.

## B-139 — Play/Space did nothing, and the Edit tab's other shortcuts needed the timeline clicked first

status: **fixed** (D-273, 2026-09-10) · severity: **major** (a primary transport control was unreachable from the keyboard) · area: `packages/editor/src/PreviewPane.tsx`, `packages/editor/src/TimelinePane.tsx`

- **found:** 2026-09-10 — owner, live: *"play should play the preview and all the other shortcut registration"*. Confirmed by the D-273 audit rather than assumed.
- **cause:** two separate gaps. (1) **Space was never bound to anything.** Exhaustive search found no `Space` / `' '` / `code === 'Space'` handler anywhere in `packages/*` or `app/src` outside Colorist's own `cycle_zoom`. The preview's play/pause (and frame-step) existed only as click targets on `Player`'s transport bar; `useEditorTimelineStore.setPlaying` worked fine, nothing reached it from the keyboard. (2) The Edit tab's keys that *did* exist (`M`, `V/B/N/Y/U`, Delete) hung off a React `onKeyDown` on `TimelinePane`'s own `tabIndex={0}` div, so they only fired once that div had been clicked — dragging a clip in from Sources and pressing `M` did nothing, because focus was still on the drag source. Each branch also re-implemented its own "no modifier" / "not in a text field" guards, and they had drifted (the Delete branch had neither).
- **expected:** Space plays and pauses the preview whenever the Edit tab is frontmost; the tab's other shortcuts work without hunting for focus first.
- **fix:** D-273. Both are now registry actions dispatched by `@apelles/keymap`'s single window-level, tab-scoped listener — `edit.play_pause` (Space), `edit.frame_back`/`edit.frame_forward` (←/→) claimed by `PreviewPane`, and `edit.add_marker`/`edit.split`/`edit.delete_selection`/`edit.tool_*` claimed by `TimelinePane`. The typing guard lives in the dispatcher once, so it covers every shortcut instead of whichever branch remembered it. `edit.split` (⌘K) is new: the Split button had been in the toolbar since D-093 with no key bound to it at all.

## B-141 — a project's own launcher-card thumbnail shows the raw, un-rotated source frame, not what the timeline actually plays

status: **fixed, verified** (2026-09-10) · severity: low-medium (cosmetic — the launcher card, not the editor itself; a heavily-cropped/disorienting thumbnail on `ProjectLauncher.tsx`'s "My Projects" grid) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/project.rs` (`regen_thumb`), `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/edit.rs` (new `timeline_thumb_jpeg`)

- **found:** 2026-09-10, live — the owner's `2026-09-09-edit` project card (screenshot: `scratch/project-card-thumbnail-height-mismatch.png`) showed a tight, disorienting close-up (a curtain/window corner) instead of the clip's real framing, for a project whose clips are the genuinely upside-down-at-capture footage from the prior session (confirmed then via `ffprobe`: no `rotate` tag, no `displaymatrix` — the pixels themselves are stored upside-down) that had already been corrected with `rotation: 180` on every clip via `editor_set_clip_transform`.
- **cause, root-caused by reading `regen_thumb`:** `chroma_project_save` regenerates the launcher card's `thumb.jpg` by calling `video::extract_thumb(&cv.path, &cv.info, cv.frame, 360)` — a raw ffmpeg-style frame grab straight from `state::current_video()`'s own source file path, entirely outside the Edit tab. It has no concept of the Edit tab's timeline, its clips, or any clip's `rotation`/`scale`/`position_*` transform, and applies no Colorist grade either. An upside-down source, object-`cover`'d into `ProjectLauncher.tsx`'s fixed `aspect-video` card by `<img className="w-full h-full object-cover">`, crops down to a small, wrongly-oriented sliver of the real frame — matching exactly what the screenshot showed.
- **expected:** the launcher card's thumbnail reflects the SAME picture the Edit tab's own timeline actually composites at frame 0 (post-rotation, post-transform) — the same guarantee `chroma_timeline_frame` already gives the live preview.
- **fix:** a new `chroma::edit::timeline_thumb_jpeg(max_long_edge)` runs the exact same `timeline_frame_image(0, …)` decode+composite path `chroma_timeline_frame` uses for the live preview — so a clip's `rotation`/`scale`/`position_*`/crop and any Colorist grade are all applied identically to the thumbnail — and returns `None` (rather than a 1×1 black placeholder) when the timeline has nothing to show at frame 0. `regen_thumb` now tries that first and only falls back to the legacy `video::extract_thumb` raw grab when it comes back `None` (an all-gap timeline, a stills-only project, or a genuine decode failure) — some thumbnail still beats none.
- **verification:** `regen_thumb_applies_the_clips_rotation_like_the_edit_tab_preview_does` (`app/src-tauri/src/chroma/project.rs`) builds a one-clip project (a black frame with a white square in its TOP-LEFT quadrant) with `rotation: 180.0`, calls `regen_thumb` for real, decodes the written `thumb.jpg`, and asserts the square now reads in the BOTTOM-RIGHT quadrant (with the top-left now dark) — the actual proof the composited, transform-aware path ran rather than a raw source grab. `cargo test -p apelles --lib chroma::project::tests::regen_thumb_applies_the_clips_rotation_like_the_edit_tab_preview_does`: **1 passed; 0 failed** (a first attempt at this build was killed mid-link by this session's own shared-disk ceiling — see `CLAUDE.md` — a second attempt with more headroom completed clean in 6m25s). `cargo check -p apelles --lib` (zero errors), `cargo clippy -p apelles --lib --no-deps` (13 warnings, all pre-existing, none in either changed file), and `cargo fmt --check` are also clean.

## B-142 — D-278's Keyboard Shortcuts multi-column layout never actually balanced into columns in the real app

status: **fixed, confirmed live** (2026-09-10) · severity: minor (cosmetic — D-278's own interaction behavior was unaffected) · area: `app/src/styles.css`, `packages/keymap/src/KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx`

- **found:** 2026-09-10, live, immediately after D-278 — the owner reopened the window post-restart and it still showed the old single-column stacked layout, not the multi-column grid D-278 had just built and tested.
- **first attempt, real but not the actual blocker:** theorized a WebKit-specific quirk where `column-fill: balance` fails to balance when the `columns-*` box sits inside a separate `overflow: auto` ancestor with no height of its own — merged the scroll container and the columns container onto one element. Shipped, rebuilt, re-tested live: **still not fixed**, per the owner ("no not fixed still :/").
- **real cause, found by checking whether the CSS even existed at all rather than re-theorizing about WebKit:** `app/src/styles.css` (Tailwind v4's CSS-first config) lists explicit `@source` globs — the only directories its JIT scanner reads for classes to generate — and `packages/keymap/src` was **never added to that list** when the D-273 pass created the whole `@apelles/keymap` package. `columns-1`/`sm:columns-2`/`lg:columns-3`/`break-inside-avoid` are not used anywhere else in the already-scanned packages (`ui`/`shell`/`editor`/`motion`/`player` — confirmed by grep), so Tailwind never generated real CSS rules for them at all — they were inert class names on the DOM the whole time. The dialog's other classes (`flex`, `text-*`, `border-*`, spacing) happened to already exist because they're also used elsewhere in already-scanned packages, which is exactly why the rest of the window looked normally styled while only the column behavior silently no-op'd. The same audit found `packages/inspector/src` (2 files, real Tailwind usage) missing too — not yet visibly broken only because its own classes happen to overlap with ones already generated elsewhere, the same lucky-coincidence gap keymap just hit for real.
- **expected:** the categories actually flow into 2-3 visual columns at this window's width, per D-278's own design and the Figma reference it was built from.
- **fix:** added `@source "../../packages/inspector/src";` and `@source "../../packages/keymap/src";` to `app/src/styles.css`. The WebKit-safe merged-container structure from the first attempt was left in place (still a real, correct defensive fix for that quirk even though it wasn't this bug's actual cause).
- **the real lesson, worth a standing check:** every new package under `packages/` that renders real UI (has `className=` usage) needs its own `@source` line in `app/src/styles.css` — nothing else enforces this, and the failure mode is silent (inert class names, not a build error). `bridge`/`debug`/`history`/`motion-engine`/`tokens` were checked and confirmed to have zero `className` usage today, so they don't need one yet.
- **verification:** `npm test --workspace @apelles/keymap` (43/43) and `tsc --noEmit` clean; confirmed live by the owner — the 3-column grid (APPLICATION/TRIM TOOLS/EDITING, etc.) actually renders now.

## B-143 — the widened Keyboard Shortcuts dialog stayed narrow: an unprefixed `max-w-[80vw]` never overrides a `sm:`-scoped default

status: **fixed, pending live re-check** (2026-09-10) · severity: minor (cosmetic) · area: `packages/keymap/src/KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx`

- **found:** 2026-09-10, live, right after B-142's real fix made the columns visible for the first time — the window's own dead space and truncated row labels ("G...", "Go t...", "Cop...") were now clearly visible against the working columns. First attempted fix: `<DialogContent className="max-w-[80vw]">`. Shipped, rebuilt — **still not fixed**, per the owner ("it's not done").
- **cause, confirmed by inspecting the actual generated stylesheet rather than re-guessing:** fetched the live dev server's own compiled CSS (`curl localhost:1420/src/styles.css`) and found BOTH `.sm\:max-w-\[80vw\]` and `.sm\:max-w-lg` present in the same `@media (width >= 40rem)` block. `@apelles/ui`'s `DialogContent` base classes include `sm:max-w-lg` — a `sm:`-VARIANT utility, not a plain one. `tailwind-merge` (this kit's `cn()`) only dedupes conflicting utilities within the SAME variant; an unprefixed `max-w-[80vw]` override sits in a different merge group entirely and never touches `sm:max-w-lg`, which keeps winning in the cascade at any viewport at or past that breakpoint (i.e. basically always, on a real window).
- **expected:** the dialog actually renders at ~80% of the window's width.
- **fix:** `className="max-w-[80vw] sm:max-w-[80vw]"` — matching the base's own `sm:` variant so `tailwind-merge` correctly drops `sm:max-w-lg` from the rendered class list.
- **the pattern worth remembering:** overriding a shadcn/Base-UI kit component's default Tailwind class requires matching its exact variant prefix(es), not just the bare utility — a bare override silently no-ops on any variant-scoped default, with no error, exactly like B-142's own `@source` gap silently no-op'd on a missing package. Two live-shipped-wrong attempts in one afternoon on two different silent-Tailwind-failure-modes; worth a sentence in whichever styling guide this repo grows next.
- **verification:** `tsc --noEmit -p packages/keymap` clean; the MECHANISM (which rule wins) was confirmed against the live generated stylesheet before shipping this time, not just theorized — but the actual rendered result still awaits the owner's own re-check, given the last two rounds each looked right on paper first.

## B-144 — a slip/slide drag still shows the MOVE preview it is not going to perform

status: **fixed** (2026-09-10) · severity: minor (visual feedback only — the op that commits was always correct) · area: `packages/editor/src/TimelinePane.tsx` (`onDndDragMove`, the `DragOverlay` ghost)

- **found:** 2026-09-10, by the B-137 investigation — not a live report. Adjacent code, same handler, so it is logged rather than left as an undocumented observation.
- **actual, both halves confirmed against the real component under a real pointer drag:**
  1. **The tool path never got D-235's own suppression.** `onDndDragMove` suppressed `clipDragPreview` (and with it the sync-lock and A/V-link landing ghosts) for an ARMED drag only — its condition was `activatorEvent?.altKey || trimPressRef.current?.altKey`. D-261 added a second entrance to the same edits (choose Slip/Slide in the palette, no modifier) and did not extend that check, so a tool-driven slip or slide still painted landing ghosts promising a reposition it will never make. D-235's own comment states the policy this violated in as many words.
  2. **The `DragOverlay` clip ghost was not suppressed for EITHER entrance.** A cursor-following ghost of the clip is a move preview; a slip does not move the clip and a slide does not move it to where the ghost is. This half predates D-261 — the Alt path has always had it.
- **expected:** a drag that is going to slip or slide shows no move preview, by either entrance. D-250's pointer-adjacent mode badge is already the right feedback for these gestures and already names the mode.
- **fix:** both halves closed, taking the "no move ghost at all" option this entry's own "expected" line named as already-adequate feedback (D-250's mode badge), rather than inventing a bespoke slip/slide preview — that remains a real, separate design task (a reference pass against Resolve/Premiere's own literal slip previews) if ever wanted, not a default to reach for silently.
  1. `onDndDragMove`'s suppression check is now `claimedAsTrim = press !== null && (altKey || trimToolOwns(press.tool, 'body'))` — exactly `onDndDragEnd`'s own `claimed` test (same `trimPressRef` capture), read at move-time instead of only at drop-time. A tool-driven slip/slide now suppresses the landing/insert preview exactly like the Alt path always did.
  2. A new `isSlipOrSlideDrag` (same `claimedAsTrim` formula, evaluated against `activeDrag`) gates both `dragOverlayClip` (the filmstrip/waveform ghost) and its `dragOverlayLabel` fallback pill — both render as `null` for a slip/slide drag, by either entrance, leaving the mode badge as the only feedback during those gestures.
- **verification:** new `packages/editor/src/TimelinePane.slipSlidePreview.dom.test.tsx` (6 tests, real `PointerEvent` drags against the real mounted component, same tier/pattern as `TimelinePane.dragGhost.dom.test.tsx`/`TimelinePane.trim.dom.test.tsx`) — a plain unarmed move still shows a preview (control, guards against over-suppression); an Alt-armed slip and an Alt-armed slide both show neither ghost form; a tool-picked Slip and a tool-picked Slide (no modifier) both show neither ghost form (the exact gap this entry named as unfixed); an edge-only tool (Roll) still shows the move ghost on a body drag (regression guard — Roll does not own the body zone). All 6 pass, plus the pre-existing 42 tests across `TimelinePane.dragGhost.dom.test.tsx`/`TimelinePane.trim.dom.test.tsx`/`TimelinePane.clipDrag.dom.test.tsx`/`TimelinePane.trimTools.dom.test.tsx` still pass unchanged. `tsc --noEmit -p packages/editor/tsconfig.json` clean.

## B-145 — dragging a clip lands it at the very start of the timeline instead of where it was dropped

status: **fixed** (D-303, 2026-09-10) · severity: major (a basic reposition is unusable if it always lands at frame 0) · area: `packages/editor/src/TimelinePane.tsx` (every dnd-kit drag branch), `packages/editor/src/dragDelta.ts` (new) — **not** `resolveClipLanding`, which this entry originally suspected and which turned out to be answering a wrong input correctly

- **found:** 2026-09-10, live — owner, dragging a clip on Video 1: *"when i move this instead of moving it moves to very starting :("*. Screenshot: `scratch/clip-drag-jumps-to-start.png` (mid-drag/selection state — the Inspector shows the dragged clip's transform, `A001_09091143_C030.MOV`, with gap-highlight boxes visible on neighbouring tracks).
- **expected:** the clip lands at (or snapped near) the position it was dropped at, per `onDndDragEnd`'s own `intendedFrame = clip.start_frame + deltaFrames` → `resolveClipLanding` path.
- **the trigger the original entry could not see, and why it looked intermittent:** it only happens when the timeline is **scrolled horizontally**. The owner's own screenshot shows it — zoom 9%, ruler starting at `00:04:00`, i.e. thousands of pixels of scroll. Unscrolled, every drag has always been correct, which is why nothing in the test suite caught it and why it read as "sometimes."
- **root cause (D-303), read in `@dnd-kit/core@6.3.1`'s own source rather than guessed:** `event.delta` is `modifiedTranslate + scrollAdjustment`, and dnd-kit measures `scrollAdjustment` against the scrollable ancestors of **`over?.node ?? active.node`** — a set that changes mid-drag the instant a droppable resolves. In this pane the dragged `ClipBody` lives INSIDE the timeline library's horizontally-scrolling `react-virtualized` grid, while the `TrackDropZone` droppables are overlay siblings OUTSIDE it. Walked both chains live in the real app: the clip's contains `.ReactVirtualized__Grid` at `scrollLeft: 2000`; the zone's does not. So dnd-kit captures 2000 as the drag's "initial" scroll and then reads 0 for the rest of the gesture, and `useScrollOffsetsDelta`'s own "reset when there is no scroll" branch never rescues it (the post-switch chain still ends at `document.scrollingElement`, so its offsets are a fresh `{x:0,y:0}` object, not the reference-equal `defaultCoordinates` sentinel it compares against). **Every `delta.x` for the whole drag is short by exactly `scrollLeft`** — measured: scrolled 2000px, dragging +150px, `event.delta.x` reads `-1850`, and `active.rect.current` reads the honest `+150` at the same instant.
- **why that always lands at the START specifically, rather than somewhere randomly wrong:** the error is exactly the scroll offset, and you scroll to *where the clip is*. `intendedFrame = clip.start_frame + (screenDelta − scrollLeft)/pxPerSec*fps` therefore collapses to roughly "the clip's own position minus its own position" — negative, clamped by `resolveClipLanding` to 0. Reproduced end to end: v2 at frame 5760, 13% zoom, scrolled 2000px, dragged +150px → landed at **0**, rippling v1 and v3 out of the way.
