- **what was ruled out, since the original entry named all three as suspects:** B-137's `dragGhost.ts` change (it only shifts the OVERLAY's rendered position through a `DragOverlay` modifier — `DragOverlay` modifiers are applied in the overlay, never to `DndContext`'s own `modifiedTranslate`, so it cannot reach `delta`), D-280 (touches no file in this package), and `resolveClipLanding`/`computeInsertion` (correct throughout — they were handed a wrong `intendedFrame` and clamped it exactly as designed).
- **fix (D-303):** `dragDelta.ts` derives the drag's displacement from `active.rect.current` (`translated.left − initial.left` is dnd-kit's pre-scroll-adjustment translate, both corners written from the same `draggingNodeRect` in the same layout effect) and adds back the pane's OWN scroll change since the drag began. One helper, `dragPx`, used by all five consumers — the live landing preview, the committed move, the create-a-track branch, the slip/slide body drag and the transition drop — none of which can drift apart again. Two of those five were silently broken by the same offset and nobody had reported them yet: `dndBoundary`'s "is the pointer still over the pane" test (a scrolled drag could cancel or offer the wrong insertion boundary) and the transitions-palette drop (a scrolled drop could not find the cut it was aimed at).
- **verified, three ways.** Live in a real browser against the real component (`app/harness.html` + CDP): same-track right/left, cross-track, and create-a-track above/between/below, at 88%/43%/14% zoom with scroll offsets from 0 to 18779px — every one landed on exactly the expected frame, and a transition dropped at 43% zoom scrolled 9668px landed exactly on the cut (`at_frame: 6240`). In CI: `TimelinePane.clipDrag.dom.test.tsx`, a real `PointerEvent` drag against a really-scrolled grid, whose test 4 lands the clip at `startFrame: 0` on the pre-fix code and at the right frame after. And `dragDelta.test.ts` for the arithmetic.
- **the map this produced:** `docs/notes/timeline-drag-interactions.md` — every drag gesture on this surface, pointer-down to `applyOp`, including which of the two displacements each consumer must use and why they are not interchangeable.

## B-146 — preview playback lags in general, and 4x rate visibly jumps frames rather than playing smoothly — the frame-rate ceiling is the WEBVIEW, not the decoder

status: **root-caused and partly fixed** (D-290, 2026-09-10) · severity: high (raised from the "medium" this was first logged at: playback smoothness is the thing an editor judges the whole tab by, and CLAUDE.md's own priority order puts performance first) · area: `packages/editor/src/PreviewPane.tsx` (the rAF play loop), `packages/editor/src/useCanvasClipPick.ts`, and the Edit tab's per-frame React render cost generally — **not** `crates/apelles-media/src/decode_pipe.rs` or `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/audio.rs`, both of which this entry originally suspected and both of which measured out

- **found:** 2026-09-10, live, immediately after using the new D-280 playback-rate control — owner: *"playback lags btw :)"* (screenshot: `scratch/playback-rate-lag-report.png`) and, separately, *"4x speed jumps the frames at playback :D"*; then, clarifying that it is not rate-specific: *"related to clip and all in the whole thing :/"*.
- **expected:** ordinary 1× playback feels smooth (no perceptible lag), and 4× playback — even though D-280's own decision doc already documents frame-dropping at high rates as expected/by-design — feels like a fast but coherent shuttle rather than a visibly janky jump.
- **actual (measured, `debug_frame_timing` against the running app and the owner's own `2026-09-09-edit.chroma`):** the play loop runs one pass every **25.0 ms — ~38.5 fps — with zero hitches**. That is over the 41.7 ms budget 24 fps allows, so 1× fits and everything above ~1.6× does not; at 4× the timeline demands 96 fps and gets 38.
- **cause:** **not the decoder.** Playing over a timeline GAP — where `timeline_frame` returns `blank_frame_jpeg()`, a 1×1 black JPEG, with no probe, no ffmpeg and no composite — still costs **21.5 ms a frame**. So decode + composite + JPEG is ≈3.5 ms and ≈21.5 ms is on the webview side, paid whatever is on the timeline, which is exactly why the owner's report is "the whole thing" rather than a rate-control bug. Closing the Inspector alone moved it 25.0 → 23.0 ms: eight components subscribe to `playhead` and every one re-renders on every displayed frame. The loop is work-bound, not vsync-bound (3.5 ms of added decode moved the median by exactly 3.5 ms), so there is no dead animation-frame wait to reclaim.
- **not a D-280 regression:** that decision's video half is one multiplication and its audio half runs on the `cpal` thread; the loop costs the same 21.5 ms over a gap where neither is doing anything. The rate control made a pre-existing ceiling visible.
- **the audio-seek lead this entry was filed with, ruled out with a number rather than by reading:** the `could not seek to …s — skipping forward by packet timestamps instead` warnings observed firing repeatedly in the live dev log are B-052's fallback. It really does fire on the reported file (`A001_09091123_C024.MOV`, 568 MB, 124.6 s — confirmed at 40 s and 74 s by capturing that very `log::warn!` in the test below), and reaching a late start costs **5.4-5.6 ms warm / 65.7-67.4 ms cold** (0:00 costs 5.6 ms warm, 9.3 ms cold), **once per source per session, not per frame**. Bounded, correct, and not the lag either way — three to four orders of magnitude short of explaining a per-frame 21.5 ms. Now guarded by a permanent ceiling test in `crates/apelles-media/src/audio.rs` that also asserts which of the two paths it measured, so it cannot start passing vacuously.
- **fix (D-290), the part that is done:** (1) a displayed frame no longer costs a React render at all — the `<img>`'s `src` is written imperatively rather than through `setFrameSrc`, which removed the *second* full commit of `PreviewPane`'s subtree every frame (**38 commits → 22 for the same 20 painted frames**, in the test that guards it); (2) pausing no longer re-decodes the frame already on screen, which also stops asking the decode pipe for a frame it had already streamed past (D-125's ffmpeg-respawn case) on every pause; (3) `useCanvasClipPick` no longer tears down and re-adds a capture-phase `pointerdown` listener on the preview surface once per displayed frame.
- **still open, deliberately, as scoped work rather than a TODO** (`docs/04-roadmap.md` item 25): the picture path is still `Blob` → object URL → `<img src>` → main-thread JPEG decode per frame (wants `createImageBitmap` → `<canvas>`), and `playhead` still lives in the store slice eight panels subscribe to (wants a transient subscription / its own slice). Those two are where the remaining ~19 ms lives.
- **how to re-measure:** `debug_frame_timing` gained `fetch` and `tick` duration channels in the same pass for exactly this — `fetch` is Rust+IPC, `tick − fetch` is the loop's own JavaScript, `raf − tick` is React's commit plus the animation-frame wait. Two traps that both look like "it stalled": a playhead already parked on the last frame, and a stretch of timeline with a gap under it.
- **provenance of this record:** filed `investigating`, dispatched to an Opus agent (worktree `agent-ac1ef7a51336493e7`) to profile rather than guess, per this repo's own "root-cause before fixing" standard — and updated in place with the finding above, as that original entry asked for. The agent's first pass was interrupted before it committed; the work was picked up and finished 2026-09-10 (see D-290's closing note for the three things that correction pass had to change, including its own decision number).
- **status update, 2026-09-15 (D-325) — status stays "partly fixed", NOT closed:** a follow-up live `debug_frame_timing` pass (after D-323/D-324 fixed the per-cut audio/stall bugs) found the *overall* preview still far below 24fps: a clean 1-clip project painted at 94ms/frame (10.5fps) and a heavily recut 96-clip project at 218ms/frame (4.3fps), both far worse than this entry's own documented ~21.5-25ms/frame ceiling. Root-caused further, not just re-confirmed: `TimelinePane.tsx` was one of this entry's own "eight components [that] subscribe to `playhead`" (the actual count is now known to be **eleven**, this pass counted them directly) — but unlike the other ten, it is a ~4500-line component that ALSO fails its own React Compiler coverage test (B-184, filed 2026-09-13, still open) and walks every clip on every track to render, so its playhead-driven re-render cost **scales with clip count**, a dimension this entry's own original measurement (a project with a handful of clips) never exercised. Measured before the fix: 2 React commits per playhead tick (a redundant reactive re-render on top of the same effect's own imperative `editorRef.setTime()` call), 3.75-27.1ms/commit depending on clip count (2 vs. 200). **Fixed:** the reactive `playhead` selector removed in favour of `useEditorTimelineStore.getState()` reads at the three places that actually need the value — now exactly one commit per tick, at every clip count (`TimelinePane.playheadCost.dom.test.tsx`). **Why this is not "fixed" for the bug as a whole:** the remaining per-commit cost still scales with clip count (now entirely inside `@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor`'s own internal re-render, not eliminated), the other ten reactive-`playhead` subscribers are untouched, and this pass could not retake live `debug_frame_timing` numbers against the real running app (a worktree-isolated agent does not touch the shared dev server) — so the real-app 94ms/218ms numbers are not yet re-measured post-fix. See D-325 for the full investigation, the ruled-out leads, and the honest limits.
- **status update, 2026-09-15 (D-328) — still "partly fixed", one more subscriber down:** D-328 (ranged markers + the Edit tab's Index panel) had to fix **`EditLibraryPanel`**, one of the ten reactive-`playhead` subscribers D-325 named and left, because the new Index panel is its CHILD — a parent that re-renders on every displayed frame re-renders its children too, so the new panel would have paid a playback cost for a value it does not use. Same shape as D-325's own find and the same fix: the reactive selector was read by nothing but a single click handler (`addAtPlayhead`), so it became a `useEditorTimelineStore.getState().playhead` read at the point of use. **Nine reactive subscribers remain** (`CaptionLibrary`, `ClipCurveEditor`, `CaptionsFromTranscriptButton`, `CaptionTransformOverlay`, `EditorInspectorPanel`, `PreviewPane`, `ScrubWaveform`, `TransformOverlay`, `useCanvasClipPick`). D-328 also establishes the pattern for a component that genuinely DOES need to react to the playhead rather than merely read it: subscribe to the store and `setState` only when the derived value the UI actually shows changes (there, which transcript row is highlighted), not on every tick — 30 ticks inside one segment cost 0 React commits, versus 30 for the naive selector, both measured. Nothing else about this entry changes; the live-app 94ms/218ms numbers are still un-remeasured.
- **status update, 2026-09-15 (D-334) — still "partly fixed"; three more subscribers down, and the median is now attributed with a measurement rather than a suspicion:** D-334 went looking for the decoder cause of the owner's "still doesn't feel smooth" on `2026-09-12-c040` and found the decoder is **not** where the baseline cost lives — it measured sequential mid-clip decode at **6.8 ms/frame (146 fps, six times real time)** at the preview's real 960 px scale, and showed that the measured 10 s window (median 200 ms/frame, p95 620 ms) contained only **3 cuts and no short clips**, so a *median* of 200 ms cannot be a per-cut decoder cost at all. That median is this entry, confirming D-325's attribution by elimination rather than by assumption. D-334 fixed the decoder's own separate defect (the hitches — see B-199) and, on this entry's side, took three more of the nine subscribers off the per-frame path: **`CaptionLibrary`** and **`CaptionsFromTranscriptButton`** (both read the value only inside a click handler → D-325's `getState()` pattern), and **`useCanvasClipPick`**, the highest-leverage of the nine because it is called from `PreviewPane` and so its re-render IS the preview's — it now subscribes to the visible clip/caption SET at boundaries (D-328's `useActiveTranscriptRow` shape) rather than to `playhead`. Its per-frame half became *more* correct in the process: the `pointerdown` hit test now recomputes candidates at the live playhead instead of reading a ref filled during the last render, which matters for a keyframed clip whose box really does move every frame. Measured both ways in `packages/editor/src/playheadCost.dom.test.tsx`: **30 commits → 0** over 30 ticks for each of the three, and exactly 1 commit on a genuine cut. **A fourth, `CaptionTransformOverlay`, moved in the same pass** to a boolean on/off-screen subscription — its own comment had called the per-frame re-render unavoidable "because what the canvas shows is a function of the playhead", and only that one boolean is, flipping twice per cue. **Five reactive subscribers remain** (`TransformOverlay`, `EditorInspectorPanel`, `ScrubWaveform`, `ClipCurveEditor`, and `PreviewPane`'s own — that last one legitimately draws a moving position bar and is the one D-290 already accepted). **Two findings from D-334's live pass that change how this entry should be read, both measured:** (1) **Removing those React commits did not move the live median at all.** Reverting just D-334's four frontend files against the same Rust binary on a settled machine measured **40 ms**, against **41.5 ms** with them — so in that scenario the preview was not commit-bound, and the remaining subscribers should not be assumed to be worth their fix until a measurement says so. (2) **Machine load dominates this number.** The same build measured **40 ms at load ~10, 62 ms at load ~80 and 86 ms at load ~133** (the machine was concurrently running another agent's worktree at 128% CPU, macOS MediaAnalysis at 114%, and a second instance of the app decoding the same 4K file). This entry's own 94 ms/218 ms figures, and the owner's 4.11 fps report, were all taken under that kind of contention — so an unknown but large share of them is contention, not a ceiling. **Any future measurement here must record `getloadavg` beside the number.** (3) **The bottleneck has moved since D-290.** At low load `fetch` (Tauri IPC + all of Rust) is **26-33 ms of the 41 ms frame**, leaving the webview ~12 ms — the opposite of D-290's ~3.5 ms Rust / ~21.5 ms webview split on a simpler project. Sequential decode is only 6.8 ms of that, so the ~20 ms remainder is composite + JPEG encode. That, not `createImageBitmap`, is the next real target, which **reverses the priority this entry and roadmap item 25 currently state**. B-184 was explicitly out of scope for that pass.

## B-147 — the Colorist tab's main preview shows the RAW source frame, ignoring the Edit timeline's own clip transform and trim entirely

status: **fixed** 2026-09-10 (**D-294**) · severity: **critical** (Colorist grades the wrong picture: a rotated, differently-trimmed frame than what the Edit tab and the final export actually show) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/commands.rs` (`seek_and_install`, Colorist's real frame-fetch path — *not* `ImageCanvas.tsx`, which only displays what that installs), the same underlying gap as B-141

- **found:** 2026-09-10, live — owner, pointing at Colorist's own preview showing the clip upside-down despite the Edit tab's timeline having `rotation: 180` set on every clip in this project (applied deliberately last session to correct genuinely upside-down-at-capture footage): *"see in colorist even though we have transformed the clip its taking from source with 0 :D we need to get it from the timeline :) right the length etc.."* (screenshot: `scratch/colorist-ignores-timeline-transform-and-trim.png`).
- **expected:** Colorist's own preview shows the SAME picture the Edit tab and the final export show for that clip — its real transform (rotation, scale, position) applied, and its real trim (`source_start`/`duration` from the Edit timeline's `Clip`, not the raw source file's own frame 0 and full length).
- **cause, and why this is the same root gap as B-141:** Colorist's shot list and its own `ImageCanvas.tsx` preview pipeline operate on the RAW SOURCE FILE PATH directly (`state::current_video()` and whatever Rust command backs it), with no concept of the Edit tab's `Timeline`/`Clip` model at all — no `rotation`, no `source_start`, no `duration`. B-141 found the exact same disconnect for the project-launcher thumbnail (`regen_thumb`'s raw `extract_thumb` call); this is the identical architectural gap surfacing in Colorist's OWN main preview, live, while grading — a much higher-severity instance of it, since it means every color decision made in Colorist right now is being judged against the wrong picture.
- **fixed (D-294):** a new one-way bridge, `chroma::colorist_view`, resolves the decode session's active shot **path** to the `apelles_timeline::Clip` the open project's active timeline holds for it. `seek_and_install` (which both the scrub path `chroma_seek` and the playback path `chroma_play_frame` share) now takes a **clip-local** frame, maps it to the source frame through the clip's own trim via `Clip::clamped_source_frame_at` — the same function the Edit preview and the exporter use — and runs the decoded frame through `edit::composite_layer_onto`, the real compositor, with the clip's crop/scale/rotation/position. `chroma_video_info` reports the clip's length and the project's composition size rather than the source file's. Deliberately **not** carried across: the clip's saved grade (the Colorist is what produces it — baking it in would double-apply, see D-256), its opacity/fade (nothing beneath this canvas to blend against), and every other layer. An untransformed clip that already fills the composition takes an identity fast path and is byte-identical to before.
- **the diagnosis above named the wrong file, and that is worth recording:** `ImageCanvas.tsx` was never the problem — it displays `AppState.original_image`, and the raw-source frame was already installed there by the time it ran. The fix is entirely in Rust, and no part of it is in the 3,259-line canvas component. That matters for the "one common player" ask this entry pointed at: unifying the two preview *components* would not have fixed this bug, and fixing this bug did not need them unified (see D-299).
- **residual, closed separately:** Colorist's own `chroma_export_video` still decoded the raw source with its own ffmpeg pipeline, so between D-294 and D-297 it exported a different picture than its own preview. **D-297** closed it — by making that exporter clip-aware through this same `colorist_view` bridge (clip-local frame range, `apply_geometry` before the grade), *not* by retiring it: it turned out to be the only path that renders the spatial half of a grade (masks/local layers, relight, the Colorist crop), which the Edit exporter drops when it bakes a grade to a LUT (D-256). A speed-ramped clip is refused there rather than silently exported from the wrong frames.
- **one migration consequence, stated plainly:** tracked mattes (D-019), mask keyframes (D-034) and depth tracks (D-036) are all indexed by `current_video().frame`, which is clip-local now. Artefacts authored before D-294 are indexed in source-frame space and will land on the wrong frames for a trimmed clip; re-tracking is the fix. There is no migration because those indices carry no record of which clip they were authored against.

## B-153 — `add_subject_mask` reports a tool error even when the mask is actually created successfully

status: **fixed** (2026-09-10, D-307) · severity: medium (misleading failure signal — an agent following the error would retry or give up on a call that already worked) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/control.rs` (the frontend bridge timeout), `mcp/server.py` (`_op`'s 504 handling)

- **found:** 2026-09-10, live — `mcp__chroma__add_subject_mask(bbox=[850, 0, 1920, 1085])` returned a bare `Error executing tool add_subject_mask` with no detail. A follow-up `list_masks` call showed the mask had actually been created correctly (real `ai-subject` sub-mask, bbox matching what was requested, id `a15f8e35-ff0e-45c0-be0f-483e83b9c743`), and a subsequent `set_mask_adjust` against that id worked and was independently verified (via `sample_region` before/after) to actually change the masked pixels.
- **expected:** a tool call that succeeds server-side returns its normal success payload (mask id, rendered frame), not an error.
- ~~**not yet root-caused:** … Likely candidates to check first: the response payload for a freshly-generated AI-subject mask may be large/shaped differently than other mask-adjust responses (e.g. carrying the matte data) in a way that trips whatever the MCP layer uses to detect a tool error.~~ **That guess was wrong** — nothing about the payload is involved. Kept as a record of what the trail looked like before it was walked.
- **root cause, 2026-09-10 — a TIMEOUT, and the caller was never told that's what it was.** `control.rs` waited a flat `BRIDGE_TIMEOUT` of **20 seconds** for the frontend to answer *any* op. `add_subject_mask` on a video routes through `useAiMasking.handleGenerateAiMask` → `chroma_subject_mask` → the AI sidecar, i.e. SAM 2 + ViTMatte over a full 4K frame, which routinely runs longer than that. At 20s the control server stopped waiting and replied 504 — **but the frontend kept running and finished the job**, which is exactly why the mask existed and was correct when `list_masks` was called afterwards. `mcp/server.py`'s `_op` turned the 504 into a bare `RuntimeError`; FastMCP masks a non-`ToolError` exception, so all that reached the agent was `Error executing tool add_subject_mask` with no detail — the "no detail" in the report is a direct consequence of the raise, not a separate mystery.
- **fixed (D-307), in two halves.** (1) `POST /op` now accepts an optional `timeout_ms`, clamped to 1s..=300s, default unchanged at 20s; the MCP layer — which owns the tool list, unlike the control server, which deliberately does not — passes a 180s budget for the four model-driven tools (`add_subject_mask`, `add_component`, `track_subject`, `apply_haze`). (2) A 504 is no longer raised: `_op` returns the control server's own `{ok, error}` envelope, which is the contract `control.rs` already documented for its native ops and the one place that was breaking it. The message names the op and the real budget and says the work may have completed anyway, with the check to run (`get_state` / `list_masks`) before retrying.
- **still open, and deliberately not half-solved here:** `track_subject` blocks until a whole-clip SAM 2 propagation finishes — minutes on a long clip, past even the 300s ceiling. The longer budget stops it failing falsely on short clips, but the real fix is to return a job id and be polled, the way `depth_track` already does. That's a separate piece of work, not a timeout tweak.
- **verified:** `bridge_timeout`'s clamp is unit-tested in `chroma::control` (default when absent or non-numeric; a caller's value honoured in range; 0 and one hour both clamped). **Not** re-tested live against the sidecar — see the CHANGELOG line.
- **workaround used this session:** called `list_masks` after the apparent failure to confirm the real state, then proceeded normally. (Still the right move for any timed-out op, and the new error message now says so.)

## B-154 — Colorist's transport bar shows the raw source's full duration/frame count, not the trimmed clip's duration on the Edit timeline

status: **fixed** (2026-09-10) · severity: low (cosmetic/misleading, not a data-loss or playback-correctness bug) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/session.rs` (`ShotDto::from`), `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/colorist_view.rs` (new `display_info`/`display_info_for`), `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/commands.rs` (`chroma_video_info`)

- **found:** 2026-09-10, live, screenshot — owner: *"this playhead shows full 2:04 minute but our clip on timeline is little bit shorter so now it's not playing after that which is fine and right but this playhead show[s] to be moving."* Screenshot shows the transport bar reading `0:16.5 / 2:04.6 · f396 / 2990` for `A001_09091123_C024.MOV` (the active Colorist shot).
- **expected:** the transport bar's total (both the `2:04.6` time and the `2990` frame count) should reflect this clip's actual trimmed duration as placed on the Edit timeline — `1380` frames (`source_start: 131`, `duration: 1380`) — matching what D-294's `colorist_view` bridge already makes the main preview/decode respect.
- **actual (root cause):** `ColoristTransport.tsx` (`app/src/components/panel/editor/ColoristTransport.tsx`) itself was never the bug — it just renders whatever `videoInfo` the Zustand store holds, and `chroma_video_info` (D-294/B-147, `commands.rs`) already ran every value through `colorist_view::resolve` correctly. The gap was a **second, unfixed call site**: `chroma::session::ShotDto::from` (`session.rs`) — what `chroma_session_list`/`_add`/`_set_active`/`_remove` actually return, and what the ShotStrip and `useSessionStore.ts`'s `applyLoaded` build the transport's `videoInfo` from on every shot switch — still read `frame_count`/`duration_secs`/`resolution` straight off `Shot.info`, the raw ffprobe of the whole source file, never consulting `colorist_view::resolve` at all. D-294 had fixed the main preview's *decode* (`chroma_seek`/`seek_and_install`) and *one* of its two duration-readout call sites, leaving this one still reporting the source's 2990/2:04.6. That is also exactly why playback correctly stopped at the real trim boundary while the bar kept advertising the source's full length: the decode path and this display path were simply two different pieces of code, only one of which had been fixed.
- **fix:** extracted the correction D-294 gave `chroma_video_info` into a shared `colorist_view::display_info(path, info) -> (resolution, frame_count, duration_secs)` (clip-local via `resolve` when a clip is found, else the raw source — split into a pure `display_info_for(Option<&ClipView>, &VideoInfo)` for unit testing without a live project on disk), and routed both `chroma_video_info` and `ShotDto::from` through it. One correction, two callers, instead of a second hand-rolled copy of the same arithmetic. As a side effect this also fixes `ShotDto`'s `width`/`height` to report the project's composition size instead of the raw source's when a clip resolves — the same D-294 correctness `chroma_video_info` already had — so a shot switch via the ShotStrip no longer briefly sets `originalSize` to the wrong resolution either.
- **found but NOT fixed this session, logged separately:** `session.rs`'s `decode_and_install` (the pixel half of `chroma_session_set_active`/`_remove`) treats `Shot.frame` — which is clip-local once a clip resolves (see `seek_and_install`'s own comment) — as a raw source frame index, with no `colorist_view::source_frame`/`apply_geometry` mapping at all. That looks like a real decode-correctness bug on shot-switch (distinct from this ticket's readout-only scope, and the owner's own report was specifically about the scrub bar staying correct on playback) — see **B-158**.
- **verified:** new unit tests in `colorist_view.rs` (`display_info_reports_the_clips_length_not_the_sources_b154`, using this bug's own 2990-source/1380-clip numbers; `display_info_falls_back_to_the_raw_source_with_no_resolved_clip`) — `cargo test -p apelles --lib chroma::colorist_view`. `tsc` unaffected (no frontend change was needed — both `ColoristTransport.tsx` and `useSessionStore.ts` were already correctly reading whatever the backend reported). Not live-tested against a running app with a real trimmed clip this session — see the session's own final report for what live verification was/wasn't done.

## B-150 — a second Edit-timeline clip of an already-open source file doesn't appear in Colorist's shot list at all

status: **fixed** (2026-09-10, D-306) · severity: high (silently drops a clip from Colorist entirely — not a wrong-picture bug like B-147, an *invisible* one) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/state.rs` (`Session::upsert`), `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/colorist_view.rs` (D-294)

- **found:** 2026-09-10, live — owner added a second Edit-timeline clip pointing at the same source file as an already-open one (`A001_09091123_C024.MOV`, both on the Edit tab as separate `Clip`s at different `start_frame`s — one already graded via `match_to_reference`, the second added fresh for a "cinematic" grade experiment): *"one more bug i added two dublicate clips right :/ in colorist that dublicate clip is not there at all."*
- **repro (confirmed this session):** open a project with two Edit-timeline clips sharing one source path; call `open_project`/`list_shots` — the returned `shots` array has exactly ONE entry for that path, not two. Reproduced directly: `2026-09-09-edit`'s timeline has two separate clips of `A001_09091123_C024.MOV`, `list_shots` returns 7 shots total with only one `A001_09091123_C024.MOV` entry.
- **expected:** each Edit-timeline clip is independently selectable/gradable in Colorist, even when two clips share a source file — matching how the Edit tab itself treats them (two distinct `Clip`s with independent trims, transforms, and now independent grades since D-294's `colorist_view` bridge resolves a shot to *the specific clip*, not just the source path).
- **cause:** `Session::upsert` (`state.rs`) keys a shot by its **source path** — adding a second shot for a path already in the session updates/reselects the *existing* entry (see `state::tests::upsert_of_existing_path_switches_active_and_reports_change`) rather than appending a second, independently-addressable one. D-294 fixed *which picture* a shot renders (resolving path → the timeline's `Clip` for that path), but a session with two `Clip`s sharing one path still has only one path to resolve, so `colorist_view` has no way to know which of the two clips a given shot entry means — the ambiguity D-294 left unresolved, not a regression it introduced.
- ~~**not yet fixed:** needs a real per-clip shot identity (keyed by `(timeline_id, clip_id)` or similar, not bare path) threaded through `Session`, `colorist_view`, and every saved-grade/mask/keyframe path that currently assumes one shot per source file (see B-147's own "one migration consequence" note — those are indexed in source-frame space today and would need the same identity fix). Logged rather than fixed inline; needs its own design pass given how many subsystems key off path today.~~
- **confirmed detail, 2026-09-10 (via a correct `get_timeline` call):** the second C024 clip this bug is about is on Video 2, named `"C024-cinematic-experiment"`, `startFrame: 9275`, same `sourcePath`/`sourceStart: 131` as the Video 1 C024 clip — but `rotation: 0`, where the Video 1 copy is `rotation: 180`. Whether that rotation difference is intentional (the two were meant to look different) or a leftover from however the second clip was created is unconfirmed; worth checking now that D-306 has landed and this clip IS independently addressable in Colorist — each clip resolves to its own geometry, so the two now genuinely render differently and the owner can say which is wanted.
- **fixed, 2026-09-10 — D-306: a shot's identity is its Edit-timeline clip, not its source file.** `chroma::state::ShotId` is the new key: the `apelles_timeline::Clip` id when the session came from a real project, the source path when it did not (an Untitled loose-clip session, where a path is already unique — that case is unchanged). `Session::{upsert, prune_except}` and `resolve_session_index` key off it, `load::register_video_shot` takes the clip id, `load::install_frame` takes the whole `CurrentVideo` (so a re-install cannot lose the identity and append a phantom path-keyed shot beside the real one), `colorist_view::resolve_for` resolves by id, `ShotDto.clipId` puts the identity on the wire, and `useSessionStore`'s `reattachIds` reads it there instead of inferring one from a `source path → clip id` map that could only ever answer with ONE id for two clips of a file. Full rationale, the options weighed, and the deliberate identity-is-per-clip / decode-pipe-is-per-file asymmetry: **D-306**.
- **nothing to migrate:** grade files, mask mattes and `.cube` bakes were already clip-id-keyed (D-070) — the guess above that "every saved-grade/mask/keyframe path assumes one shot per source file" was wrong on re-reading the code. Only the *decode* session assumed it; this fix makes it agree with the persistence layer, not the other way round. Frame-keyed artefacts (tracked mattes D-019, mask keyframes D-034, the depth track D-036) are indexed per shot in the transport's own clip-local space (D-294) and were unaffected.
- **verified:** new unit tests in `chroma::state` (two clips of one file are two independently addressable shots; a re-upsert of the same clip updates in place; switching between two clips of one file is *not* a decode-pipe invalidation; a clip-id shot and a path shot of one file don't collide; `prune_except` drops exactly one of a doubled pair) and in `app/src/store/useSessionStore.test.ts` (the wire's `clipId` is the shot's id; two shots of one path keep two separate grades; an Untitled session still falls back to the path). `cargo fmt`/`clippy` clean, `cargo test -p apelles --lib` green. **Not** re-tested against the owner's live project — see this fix's CHANGELOG line for what that still leaves open.

## B-151 — `debug_screenshot` on the Colorist tab returns a stale, byte-identical snapshot across repeated calls

status: **fixed** (2026-09-10) · severity: low (debug-only tooling, D-210, compiled out of release builds — blocked *inspecting* the Colorist tab via this tool, not the tab itself) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/debug_capture.rs`, `app/src-tauri/src/gpu_processing.rs`

- **found:** 2026-09-10, live, while showing the user a freshly-applied cinematic grade — `debug_set_active_tab(tab="colorist")` correctly reported `activeTab: "colorist"` (confirmed independently via `debug_ui_state`'s `shell.activeTab`), but the resulting `debug_screenshot` showed a blank white canvas, an empty right panel, and the top nav still visually highlighting "Edit" as active.
- **repro (confirmed this session):** with a project open and any grade adjustment just applied on the active Colorist shot, switch to Colorist and call `debug_screenshot` repeatedly (including round-tripping through `edit`→`colorist` and `motion`→`colorist` in between calls to rule out a one-off transition frame). Three separate screenshots taken minutes apart, across intervening tab switches, were **byte-identical** (`md5` match, `537683` bytes each) — not merely similar, the literal same file. A screenshot of the Motion tab taken in between produced a different, correctly-sized file (`1200075` bytes), ruling out the tool being globally stuck.
- **expected:** each `debug_screenshot` call reflects the tab/state that is actually current at call time — this tool's own contract ("SEE the UI instead of inferring it") is violated if it silently hands back a stale frame.
- **root cause, confirmed by reading the real render path (the working theory was right):** Colorist's picture is not webview content at all. `gpu_processing::get_or_init_gpu_context` creates a wgpu `Surface` directly from the main `WebviewWindow` itself (`instance.create_surface(window)`) and `WgpuDisplay::render` presents straight to it every time a grade re-renders — a native layer painted onto the window **behind** the webview, entirely outside WebKit's own compositing tree. `packages/shell/src/store.ts`'s `wgpuSurfaceActive` doc already named this precisely: the shell goes `bg-transparent` over that spot so the wgpu layer shows through a deliberate "hole" in the DOM. `debug_capture.rs`'s only mechanism, `-[WKWebView takeSnapshotWithConfiguration:]`, snapshots exclusively WebKit's own render tree — it cannot see a sibling native layer at all, so it always returned whatever static (transparent → rendered opaque-white by the snapshot API's own default backdrop) content sat in that hole. That explains both symptoms in one mechanism: blank/white (nothing at the webview layer to show) and byte-identical across calls (the webview's own content there never changes; only the invisible-to-this-API wgpu layer does).
- **fix:** `debug_screenshot` now composites the real picture in, rather than trying to make the snapshot see a layer it structurally cannot. `gpu_processing::read_display_frame` (new) does a one-off, on-demand GPU→CPU readback of `GpuProcessor::output_texture` — the exact texture `WgpuDisplay::render`'s bind group points at, already kept warm on every Colorist render and already `COPY_SRC` — gated on the same off-screen "hidden" sentinel (`rect` at `-999999`) the shell itself uses to mean "nothing to show here right now," so Edit/Motion screenshots take the old, cheap, webview-only path completely unchanged. `debug_capture::composite_wgpu_overlay` then pastes that frame onto the webview PNG at the exact on-screen `rect`/`clip` `shaders/display.wgsl` itself draws into (same device-pixel grid `Editor.tsx`'s `syncWgpu` posts and the webview snapshot is already in — no unit conversion needed, just a defensive scale correction if the window resized between the last layout sync and the screenshot). Deliberately **not** a permanent per-frame readback: it only runs when a screenshot is actually requested, so the interactive render path (CLAUDE.md: performance first) is untouched — confirmed by grep, `read_display_frame` has exactly one caller.
- **verified:** `cargo fmt`/`cargo clippy -p apelles` clean on the changed files; `cargo test -p apelles chroma::debug_capture` passes, including 5 new unit tests on the pure placement geometry (`compute_overlay_placement`) covering the 1:1 case, a clip smaller than its rect, the shell's off-screen sentinel, a resized-window scale correction, and a rect entirely outside its clip. The GPU readback itself has no unit test — it needs a live wgpu device/surface and a running app window, which is exactly the "eyeball + document" testing tier this file's own testing rules carve out for anything that needs the real render pipeline, not the "has a correct answer" tier; the placement math (the part that has one) is what's actually tested.
- **not independently re-verified against a live running app this session** (no interactive `npm run tauri:dev` session was available to drive): the fix is code-complete, root-caused against the real render code (not the working theory alone), and unit-tested at the geometry layer, but the end-to-end "screenshot Colorist twice with a grade change in between and diff the bytes" repro from this bug's own report was not re-run live. Flagging this explicitly rather than claiming full live verification.
- **B-157's open side question, checked while in this code:** B-157 (below, retracted) asked whether the inline image each mutating Colorist tool call returns (`set_primary`, `set_color_grade`, `inspect_color`, etc.) could ALSO be stale, "in the spirit of B-151." It cannot be a case of *this* bug's mechanism: that inline image is produced by the CPU JPEG-encode branch in `lib.rs` (`process_and_get_dynamic_image_with_analytics` → JPEG bytes returned directly over Tauri IPC), which only runs when `use_wgpu_renderer` is `false` for that call — it is a completely different code path from the `WGPU_RENDER` sentinel branch this bug lives in, with no shared caching or staleness mechanism between them. Whether it can be stale for some OTHER reason is still open and unrelated to B-151's root cause; not chased further here per the scoping this session was given.
- **workaround used before this fix:** the inline image each mutating Colorist tool call already returns (`set_primary`, `set_color_grade`, `inspect_color`, etc.) is a separate, working render path — unaffected by this bug — and was used instead to actually verify grading work landed correctly. Still a fine fallback, no longer required.

## B-148 — website's Hero mobile ask: the inline email form overlapped the headline, then the fallback button rendered full-width (not subtle)

status: **fixed** (2026-09-10) · severity: low (visual/layout only, mobile width) · area: `website/src/components/Hero.astro`

- **found:** 2026-09-10, live — owner, with screenshots (`scratch/website-hero-mobile-overlap.png`, `scratch/website-beta-section-target.png`): *"can you fix this overlapping on website at some media port, in mobile view let's do one thing keep the button only not the form on click of button it will drop us to the [beta section]"*. The hero's inline beta-signup form (email input + `Signature` button + err/status text) visually overlapped the headline at `max-width: 640px`.
- **fix, pass 1:** at `max-width: 640px`, hide the email input, error, and status elements in `.ask`, leaving only the `Signature` button; intercept the form's `submit` event in the capture phase on `.hero` (an ancestor, so it always runs before Beta.astro's shared `[data-beta-form]` handler regardless of script execution order) and, on mobile, `preventDefault()` + `stopPropagation()` + navigate to `/#beta` — the full standalone Beta section — instead of submitting inline. Constraint: `tests/build-output.test.ts` asserts at most one `.signature`-classed element per built page, so the fix reuses the existing button rather than adding a second one.
- **found, pass 2** (same day, live, screenshot): *"[Image #158] 100% width does not makt sen"* — the fallback button inherited the desktop `.row { align-items: stretch }` rule, which stretched it edge-to-edge across `.ask`'s 85%-wide mobile column now that it was the row's only child. Not subtle.
- **fix, pass 2:** mobile's `.row` now sets `align-items: center` instead of `stretch`, so the lone button sizes to its own label and centers, matching the rest of the hero's restraint.
- **verified:** `npm test` (191/191) and `npx astro check` (0 errors) both pass; live-checked in a real Chromium viewport at 390×844 — button no longer overlaps the headline, sizes to content, and a click lands on `/#beta` without an inline submit attempt.

## B-149 — website Lighthouse: contrast failure on room numbers + blocking Google Fonts request costing ~750ms of LCP

status: **fixed** (2026-09-10) · severity: medium (real accessibility + real-user performance regression on the public marketing site) · area: `website/src/components/Rooms.astro`, `website/src/layouts/Base.astro`

- **found:** 2026-09-10, live — owner ran a real Lighthouse audit against production (`https://apelles.studio/`) via Chrome DevTools and reported bad results with a screenshot (`scratch/lighthouse-production-performance-85.png`: Performance 85, Accessibility 97, Best Practices 100, SEO 100): *"can you run lighthouse i got like bad resilts and fix it."*
- **bug 1 — contrast:** `Rooms.astro`'s `.num` class (the "01"/"02"/"03" markers in the "Three rooms, one window" section) used `--pigment-ochre` (`#b4823a`) as a text color on the page's marble background (`#f4efe6`) — 2.95:1 contrast, below WCAG AA's 4.5:1 for normal text. This is exactly the misuse `tokens.css`'s own header comment warns against ("3.0:1 on marble, so it is never used for body text" — ochre is reserved for rules/marks/large display type). Fixed by switching to `--pigment-terracotta` (5.3:1 on marble), the token already documented as the working text color for this kind of use on a light section.
- **bug 2 — performance:** the Google Fonts stylesheet (`fonts.googleapis.com/css2?...`) was loaded as a synchronous `<link rel="stylesheet">` in `Base.astro`'s `<head>`, which is render-blocking regardless of the URL's own `&display=swap` param (that param only controls font-swap behavior once the CSSOM is built — it does not make the browser skip waiting for the stylesheet itself before first paint). A real Chrome DevTools performance trace against production measured LCP at 968ms, with 878ms (90.6%) of that in "render delay" directly correlated with the font CSS's own ~570ms round trip. Fixed with the standard non-blocking pattern: `<link rel="preload" as="style">` + a `media="print"` stylesheet link that swaps to `media="all"` `onload`, with a `<noscript>` fallback. Re-measured on the same production URL after deploy: LCP 968ms → 225ms, render delay 878ms → 113ms.
- **verified:** `npm run check` (0 errors), `npm test` (191/191), Lighthouse re-run against `https://apelles.studio/` after deploy — Accessibility 97 → 100, all four categories now 100/100; performance trace shows the LCP improvement above (Lighthouse's own Performance category score wasn't re-measured through the same tool used for the "85" — that number came from the owner's own Chrome DevTools Lighthouse panel, not this session's `lighthouse_audit` tool, which excludes the Performance category; the underlying LCP/render-delay numbers were measured directly via `performance_start_trace` before and after, on the same production URL, which is the real evidence for this fix).

## B-155 — `add_subject_mask` then `set_mask_adjust` on the same `maskId` returns "mask not found", and a stray full-frame mask briefly appeared instead

status: **two real causes found and fixed** (2026-09-10, D-306 + the `resyncClips` stash fix below); **left open** pending a live re-test of the original repro · severity: medium (breaks the masked-adjustment workflow — a mask can't be reliably created then edited in the same sequence) · area: `app/src/store/useSessionStore.ts` (`resyncClips`), `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/state.rs` (shot identity)

- **found:** 2026-09-10, live — owner asked for a masked "dawn window" treatment on C030 (push a bright blown window toward warm/dim instead of flat white). `add_subject_mask(bbox=[820,0,1100,680], mode="additive")` succeeded and returned a real `maskId` (`8da3c662-...`) with the bbox correctly reflected in the returned `adjustments.masks[0]`. The very next call, `set_mask_adjust(mask_id="8da3c662-...", exposure=-1.2, highlights=-60, temperature=45, tint=5)`, failed with `"mask not found: 8da3c662-2472-4c35-afb3-8d639fae7d16"` — same id, same session, no intervening calls that should have invalidated it.
- **compounding oddity:** that same failing response's `adjustments.masks` block was NOT empty — it showed a *different* mask (`a15f8e35-...`, a full-frame `additive` "Subject" submask spanning the entire 1920×1080 frame, none of the requested exposure/highlights/temperature/tint applied) that was never explicitly created by any call in this session. The active shot had also silently changed from C030 back to C024 (frame 1002) between these two calls, with no `set_active_shot` call in between.
- **resolved itself:** a follow-up `list_masks()` call showed `masks: []` (empty) on whatever shot was then active, and the shot's non-mask grade adjustments (contrast 24, exposure -0.3, highlights -28, colorGrading balance -8, etc. — the base "dark and moody" recipe) were intact, so no lasting damage was done. But the mask never got created/edited as intended, and the user got no warning that the active shot had moved out from under them mid-sequence.
- **traced, 2026-09-10 — the drift has a name: `useSessionStore.resyncClips`.** It is the only code path that replaces the editor's whole `adjustments` object with another shot's grade *without an explicit user or agent action*, which is precisely the reported "the active shot had silently changed with no `set_active_shot` call in between". It is a background poll that runs whenever the Colorist tab gains focus (D-071), it ends in `applyLoaded(newActive, null, grade)`, and it fires that branch on `activeChanged = prevActive?.id !== newActive?.id`. Both symptoms fall out of one swap: `set_mask_adjust` resolves its `mask_id` against `editor().adjustments.masks`, so a swap between the two calls makes the just-created mask genuinely absent ("mask not found") **and** puts the other shot's masks there instead — which is what `a15f8e35` was: the full-frame Subject mask created on C024 earlier in that same session (see B-153), not a mask that appeared from nowhere.
- **cause 1, fixed — the two ids being compared were unreliable (D-306).** `resyncClips` (and `_hydrateOpenDto`, and `reattachIds`) derived each shot's `id` from a `source path → clip id` map rebuilt on every poll. This project has two clips of one source file (that is B-150), and a map cannot hold two values for one key — so the doubled shot's id was whichever clip happened to be last, `activeChanged` could flip on a re-derivation rather than on a real change, and `grades[shot.id]` could hand back the *other* clip's grade and masks. D-306 removes the inference entirely: the decode session carries a real per-clip `ShotId` and reports it as `ShotDto.clipId`, which `reattachIds` reads straight through.
- **cause 2, fixed — the outgoing shot's in-flight work was discarded, not stashed.** Independently of the ids: `switchToShot` has always called `stashActiveGrade()` + `persistShotGrade()` before swapping, so an explicit shot change banks whatever the editor holds. `resyncClips` never did — it swapped `adjustments` wholesale. So a mask created seconds earlier, living only in `useEditorStore` until something stashes it, was simply dropped: no error, no toast, and nothing on disk. That is exactly the report's "the mask never got created/edited as intended" and why the follow-up `list_masks()` came back `masks: []` with the shot's non-mask grade intact. `resyncClips` now banks the outgoing shot's grade (and flushes it to its grade file) *before* the swap, mirroring `switchToShot`.
- **why this is still marked open rather than fixed:** both causes are real, both are fixed, and together they account for every symptom in the report — but the original repro was never reproduced deliberately in a running app (create a mask, immediately adjust it by the returned id), so this is a fix reasoned from the code, not one watched to work. Re-run that exact sequence against the owner's `2026-09-09-edit` project before closing it. If it still reproduces, the remaining suspect is mask *lookup* having its own bug on top, which is what this entry originally proposed and neither of the two causes above would cover.

## B-156 — RETRACTED, was never a real bug (analysis error, corrected same session)

**This entry was wrong and is kept only as a correction record — do not act on the text that follows this line, it describes a mistake, not a defect.** Originally claimed "the Edit timeline holds a full duplicate copy of the entire cut, rotated 180° from the other copy." That was a misreading of `project.json`: track 1 (6 clips, `rotation: 0`) is the **linked Audio 1 track**, not a second video track — audio clips carry a meaningless default `rotation` field that was wrongly read as evidence of a duplicated video track. There is no duplicate timeline. Caught live by the owner: *"i can see only 6 clips here and 7the one and audio how come you are sying its 12 clips ?"*, after which a correct `get_timeline` call (rather than the raw-file parsing that caused the error — see the process note below) confirmed track 0 = video/6 clips, track 1 = audio/6 clips (linked, mirrors track 0), track 2 = video/1 clip. The real, much smaller finding from that same correct data is folded into B-150's note below.
- **process lesson:** the error came from reaching for `python3` + raw `project.json` parsing instead of the real `get_timeline` MCP tool, then guessing at field semantics (`rotation` on a clip *record* isn't meaningful for an audio clip, but the field is still present and defaults/copies a value). `get_timeline` returns the correct `kind: "video"|"audio"` per track and the full clip fields directly — reaching for it instead of a hand-rolled file read would have avoided this. Per this file's own "fix the tool, don't route around it" rule: the tool wasn't broken here, it just wasn't used.

## B-157 — RETRACTED, was never a real bug (second wrong diagnosis in the same session, corrected by a live screenshot)

**This entry was wrong and is kept only as a correction record — do not act on the text that follows this line.** Originally claimed "Colorist's grading pipeline never applies the Edit timeline clip's rotation transform — every clip that needs rotation correction renders/grades upside-down in Colorist," reasoned from `list_shots`' schema having no `rotation` field. That reasoning doesn't hold: the owner then shared a screenshot of the live Colorist tab showing `A001_09091123_C024.MOV` (a `rotation: 180` clip) rendering correctly upright, with the exact grade values applied this session (Contrast 24, Highlights -28, Blacks -6) visible in the Adjustments panel. Colorist's real render clearly does apply rotation correctly, at least for this clip — a blanket "Colorist never applies rotation" claim is false.
- **what's still genuinely unresolved:** the owner's original report — *"why all the videos again got 180 degree tranformed it was fine just like 5 min befire"* and *"but a 10-20 minute ago we talked right whatever we do in timeline that need to be in the colorist and it was like that and then automatically reset"* — describes a real, live-observed flip that this entry failed to explain twice. The grade `adjustments` object does carry its own `rotation`/`orientationSteps` fields (confirmed present in every `set_primary`/`set_color_grade` response this session, currently `0`/`0` on the shots graded), separate from the Edit-timeline clip's `rotation`. Whether those ever held a different value and got reset, or whether the inline preview image this session's tool calls return can itself be stale/wrong for some shots (in the spirit of B-151's confirmed stale-screenshot bug on the Colorist tab, which was scoped only to `debug_screenshot` but was never checked against the mutating-tool inline image), is still an open question — not chased further live given two wrong theories already in a row. Whoever picks this up next should start from live app observation (like the owner's own screenshot above), not from tool-response inference.

## B-158 — switching the active Colorist shot (`chroma_session_set_active`/`_remove`) decodes the wrong frame and skips the clip's crop/scale/rotate/position entirely

status: **fixed** (2026-09-10) · severity: medium (a real pixel-correctness bug on shot switch, not just a display issue — but narrower than B-147/D-294's original scope, which this is a leftover gap in) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/session.rs` (`decode_and_install`), `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/colorist_view.rs` (new `frame_mapping`)

- **found:** 2026-09-10, during the B-154 fix (transport-bar readout), while tracing every place a Colorist shot's frame/duration is computed. Not from a live repro at the time — flagged from source reading.
- **confirmed live:** 2026-09-10, later the same day — the owner switched to shot `A001_09091129_C026.MOV` (a `rotation: 180` Edit-timeline clip) on the Colorist tab and it rendered upside-down, screenshotted with *"see no transformation"*. Exactly this bug: the shot-switch path never resolves the clip or applies its geometry.
- **the gap:** `chroma::commands::seek_and_install` (the transport's own scrub/playback path, `chroma_seek`/`chroma_play_frame`) is fully clip-aware since D-294/B-147: it maps a clip-local frame through `colorist_view::ClipView::source_frame` to the real source frame to decode, then runs `ClipView::apply_geometry` (crop/scale/rotate/position) on the result. `chroma::session::decode_and_install` — the pixel half of `chroma_session_set_active` and `chroma_session_remove`, i.e. what actually decodes a frame when the ShotStrip switches shots — did neither: it decoded `shot.frame` directly as if it were a **source** frame index, with no `source_frame` mapping and no `apply_geometry` call at all.
- **fix:** the clip-local → source-frame mapping (`clamped`, `decode_frame_index`) is now a single shared function, `colorist_view::frame_mapping(view, frame, source_frame_count)`, used by both `seek_and_install` and `decode_and_install` — so a third call site can't independently forget the clip branch the way this one did. `decode_and_install` now resolves `colorist_view::resolve_for(shot)`, maps through `frame_mapping`, decodes the source frame, and runs `ClipView::apply_geometry` before installing — mirroring `seek_and_install` exactly. 3 new unit tests in `colorist_view.rs` (`frame_mapping_with_a_resolved_clip_goes_through_its_trim_b158`, `_clamps_to_the_clips_own_length_not_the_sources`, `_with_no_resolved_clip_passes_the_frame_through`), all passing; `cargo fmt`/`clippy` clean on the touched code (pre-existing unrelated clippy debt elsewhere in the workspace, e.g. `apelles-ai`/`apelles-project`, left alone — out of scope for this fix). **Live-verified**: switching to shot index 2 (`A001_09091129_C026.MOV`) in the running app now renders right-side up.

## B-159 — the Agent Activity dock's "Hide" (X) button doesn't actually hide the dock

status: **fixed** (2026-09-18) · severity: low (cosmetic, whenever) · area: `app/src/components/chroma/AgentActivityDock.tsx`, `app/src/store/useAgentStore.ts`

- **found:** 2026-09-10, live — owner: *"agent activity close button does not work add it to backlog and clean it up when ever."*
- **cause, confirmed by reading the component:** the "X" button (line 230 at filing time — still line 230 when fixed, no drift) called `setFeedOpen(false)`, which only collapses the row list below the header — functionally identical to clicking the caret-toggle button right next to it (line 210 at filing time, still accurate — the filed text said `setFeedOpen((o) => !o)`, the real code reads `setFeedOpen(!feedOpen)`, same effect). The dock's header bar (title, row count, clear, hide) only stopped rendering at all when `rows.length === 0 && !showBanner` (line 200, exact) — with any activity present, the header stayed on screen no matter what the "Hide" button did, so it never visibly accomplished anything a user would recognize as "closing."
- **expected:** the X button should actually dismiss the dock (or at minimum do something visibly different from the collapse caret right next to it) — not silently duplicate it.
- **the wrong fix, ruled out:** a dock that stays hidden forever once dismissed would hide genuinely new agent activity from the user — worse than the original bug for anyone actually driving the app with an agent running.
- **fix:** new store state on `useAgentStore` — `dockDismissed: boolean` + `dismissedAtRowKey: string | null` (the newest activity row's key, spanning both the Colorist feed and the Edit/Motion entries the dock reads off `@apelles/history`'s `undoStack`, at the moment "Hide" was clicked) — and a `dismissDock(topRowKey)` action. The X button now calls `dismissDock(rows[0]?.key ?? null)`; the component derives `isDismissed = dockDismissed && rows[0]?.key === dismissedAtRowKey` and hides the whole activity-list card (not just the row list) while true. Because that comparison is against the *current* newest row, the dock re-shows itself the instant a genuinely new activity item (from either source) becomes newest — no separate "clear dismissal" call needed, and no forever-dismissed dock. The `request_human` banner (a separate card in the same fixed container) is untouched by any of this — it has its own `pending.cleared` guard.
- **verified:** new DOM-level test, `app/src/components/chroma/AgentActivityDock.dom.test.tsx` (jsdom + `@testing-library/react`, the same per-file `// @vitest-environment jsdom` pragma pattern `@apelles/player`'s `Player.rate.dom.test.tsx` already uses on an otherwise `environment: 'node'` workspace) — covers: hidden with no activity/no request; visible with activity; clicking Hide actually hides it; a new activity item after a dismiss re-shows it (with both rows still present); a plain re-render with no new activity stays hidden; the `request_human` banner stays visible through a dismiss. `npm test --workspace app` full suite green, `tsc --noEmit` (app) zero new errors.

## B-160 — a timeline clip drag is not smooth: the whole pane re-renders on every pointer-move tick

status: **fixed** (D-304, 2026-09-10) · severity: high (per CLAUDE.md's own priority order, performance first — a drag that stutters is a real defect, and this is the app's most-used gesture) · area: `packages/editor/src/TimelinePane.tsx`, `packages/editor/src/TimelineDragPreview.tsx` (new)

- **found:** 2026-09-10, live — owner, in the same breath as B-145: *"also i feel drag and drop in the timeline is still not smooth and animations are shakky :/"*. Investigated as its own bug rather than assumed to be a symptom of B-145, and it was one: unrelated cause, unrelated fix, and it was still there after B-145's fix landed.
- **expected:** a clip drag holds a steady frame rate. Everything else on this surface does — the same measurement shows a flat 16.7ms idle.
- **measured before assuming anything** (real Chromium, the real component via `app/harness.html` + CDP, 4 tracks × 6 clips against a stubbed backend — i.e. far *smaller* than a real edit, so a real project is worse): during a plain clip drag, frame intervals ran p50 16.7ms / **p90 24.3ms / max 47.8ms** against an idle p50 16.7 / p90 17.3 / max 18.6, with **88 renders of `TimelinePane` across 41 pointer-moves**.
- **what it is NOT, each ruled out by direct counting rather than by theory:** layout thrashing (2 `getBoundingClientRect` calls per move), DOM churn (1-2 mutations per move), long tasks (`PerformanceObserver` saw none), dnd-kit's `DragOverlay` config, and `framer-motion` — which is not a dependency of this repo at all (grep-confirmed; the pane's only animation is a Tailwind `animate-pulse` ring on rippled clips). B-145's own three-`applyOp` new-track sequence was also checked and is not involved: it runs once, on drop.
- **cause (D-304):** the live landing preview's state (`clipDragPreview` + `insertPreview`) lived on `TimelinePane` itself. D-201's audit had asked this exact question (roadmap 21.3) and answered *"no, it is change-gated"* — which is wrong in practice: at any ordinary zoom a few pixels of movement IS a different landing frame, so the gate almost never fires. Every tick therefore re-rendered the app's largest component — ruler, every track, every clip, every filmstrip and waveform — in order to move four small absolutely-positioned overlay boxes. Named conclusively by contrast: the Alt/slip path, which D-235 already suppresses that state for, held p90 at 18ms with **4** renders for the whole gesture.
- **same defect class as B-024**, reached from the other direction. B-024 was a prop identity changing on every tick, forcing the library to re-render every action; this is the parent re-rendering on every tick. That entry's own conclusion — "re-rendering N tracks' worth of actions on every tick is what actually froze the UI" — is the one to remember on this surface.
- **fix (D-304):** the state and the four overlays moved into `TimelineDragPreview.tsx`, which owns them and is written to through a `useImperativeHandle`. Nothing in the pane ever *read* the preview — it only ever set it — so a write-only handle costs no expressiveness. Geometry constants come in as props (the shape `TransitionBadges` already uses), so no import cycle and no second copy of the coordinate space.
- **verified, the same way it was measured:** **4 renders across 41 moves** (from 88) and frame-interval **p90 17.0ms** (from 24.3), i.e. indistinguishable from idle. `npm test --workspace @apelles/editor` 1737/1737 including `reactCompiler.test.ts` (the new component compiles with no React Compiler bailout), and the pane renders correctly in a real browser with the sync-lock ghosts, A/V-link ghosts and new-track ghost all still appearing and tracking.
- **the doc that was wrong is now right:** `TimelinePane`'s D-201 audit comment states what this bug found instead of what it originally claimed, rather than being left to mislead the next reader. Full map of the surface: `docs/notes/timeline-drag-interactions.md`.

## B-152 — a project's composition/export resolution can be silently derived from a reference-image clip instead of the real footage, distorting every export's aspect ratio

status: **fixed** (2026-09-10, **D-305**) · severity: high (silently distorts every export in an affected project — real camera footage gets resampled to an arbitrary image's aspect ratio) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/edit.rs` (`composition_size`, line 289)

- **found:** 2026-09-10, live — owner: *"also aspect ratio, is messed up as well not the real videos"*, on exports from the `2026-09-09-edit` project. Confirmed by direct inspection: the exported files were `2000×1130` (aspect 1.7699) while every real camera clip in the project is native `3840×2160` (aspect 1.7778, true 16:9) — a real, visible stretch, not a rounding artifact.
- **root cause:** `composition_size()` (`edit.rs:289`), with no project-level `width`/`height` recorded, fell back to *"the probed resolution of the timeline's first video clip"* — walking `timeline.tracks` in **index order** and taking the first non-empty-source clip on the first `TrackKind::Video` track, with no regard for whether that clip was real footage or a still. In the reported project, track 0's first clip is `color-match-reference-boston-street.png` (a `2000×1130` web reference photo imported for `match_to_reference` color work) — so every clip in the project, including the real `3840×2160` camera footage, was composited and exported at the reference photo's arbitrary aspect ratio.
- **fix (option (a) from the original writeup):** `composition_size()` now walks every video track's clips once and returns the first clip that is **real footage** (`!apelles_media::still::is_image_file(..)`) if the timeline has one anywhere, regardless of track order; only when the timeline is images-only (a genuine slideshow project) does it fall back to the first clip of any kind, unchanged from before. This is the same function the live preview and `chroma_timeline_clip_geometry` already share, so the preview, the overlay and the export all agree — a reference/comparison still dropped onto an earlier-indexed video track can no longer hijack the whole project's aspect ratio.
- **verified:** new unit tests in `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/edit.rs`'s `composition_size_tests` module — a track-0 `2000×1130` reference photo + a track-1 `3840×2160` real clip now resolves to `(3840, 2160)`; an images-only timeline still falls back to its still's own size; an explicit project `width`/`height` still wins over any clip. `cargo fmt` + `cargo clippy` clean, full existing test suite passes.

## B-162 — `editor_import_media` reports `hasAudio: true` for a source whose audio codec Apelles' playback pipeline cannot actually decode, and plays it silently muted

status: **fixed** (2026-09-12, **D-311**) · severity: medium (no audio during Edit-tab preview/scrub for any source using an unsupported audio codec; the metadata claiming audio exists is not itself wrong, but nothing anywhere tells the user playback can't use it) · area: `crates/apelles-media/src/audio.rs` (D-049's `symphonia`→`rubato`→`dasp_sample`→`cpal` pipeline), `crates/apelles-media/Cargo.toml`

- **found:** 2026-09-11/12, live — a video downloaded via `yt-dlp` (WebM container, AV1 video, **Opus** audio) imported cleanly (`editor_import_media` correctly reported `hasAudio: true, audioChannels: 2`, confirmed in `project.json`) and played video fine on the Edit timeline, but with no audio at all, no error anywhere in the app.
- **root cause, confirmed against the actual pinned dependency, not assumed:** `symphonia` (`crates/apelles-media/Cargo.toml`, pinned `0.6.1`) **has no Opus decoder at all, under any feature flag** — checked its published feature list directly. This is not a `Cargo.toml` misconfiguration: `mkv` (WebM container) and `vorbis` (a different lossy codec) are both already compiled in via symphonia's own default features, so a Vorbis-in-WebM file would already play — but Opus, which is YouTube's own modern default audio codec and therefore extremely common in anything `yt-dlp`-downloaded, has no decoder in this crate at any version up to the one pinned here. Video is unaffected because Apelles' video decode goes through ffmpeg-CLI (`apelles-media`'s `video` module, D-015), not symphonia — only the D-049 audio pipeline is affected.
- **the actual defect, precisely:** not "Opus is unsupported" alone (a real, known, acceptable-to-scope-later gap on its own) but that `hasAudio: true` gives the user and any MCP agent no signal that the audio which genuinely exists cannot be played — it fails silently, indistinguishable from a source that never had sound.
- **fix (option 1 — owner's call, D-311):** `symphonia-adapter-libopus` (a real libopus binding, not a transcode step — the original file's audio now decodes natively, nothing gets converted). `crates/apelles-media/src/audio.rs` builds its own `CodecRegistry` (`register_enabled_codecs` for everything symphonia already had, plus `register_audio_decoder::<OpusDecoder>()` for Opus) and both `make_audio_decoder` call sites now use it instead of the static `symphonia::default::get_codecs()`. See D-311 for the dependency comparison (`moosicbox_opus` rejected — under development, MPL-2.0, itself wraps `audiopus`).
- **a real environment gap found along the way, not a code bug:** `opusic-sys`'s build script needs `cmake` to compile the bundled libopus, and it wasn't installed on this machine. Installed via `brew install cmake` — a one-time toolchain requirement for anyone building this repo fresh from now on, not something to work around in the build script.
- **verified:** `cargo check -p apelles-media` and `cargo check -p apelles` both clean; `cargo fmt`/`cargo clippy -p apelles-media --lib` zero warnings; `cargo test -p apelles-media --lib`: 180/180 passing, no regressions. Live-verified against the running app: the original (untranscoded) `GENER8ION - STORM starring Yung Lean.webm` — the exact file that surfaced this bug — now plays with audio on the Edit timeline.
- **workaround used live, not a fix:** for the one clip this session actually needed, extracted the exact trimmed range with a direct `ffmpeg -c:v libx264 -c:a aac` re-encode of just that segment and re-imported the result — this un-blocks one specific clip, it does not close this bug for the next Opus source anyone imports.

## B-161 — website: a 192×192 PNG was the tab favicon, so every page load pulled 44 kB to draw a 16 px icon

status: **fixed** (found + fixed 2026-09-10, re-applied to `main` 2026-09-11) · severity: low-medium (real, universal page-weight waste on the public marketing site; no Core Web Vital moved) · area: `website/src/layouts/Base.astro`, `website/src/components/Hero.astro`, `website/public/`, `website/tests/palette.test.ts`

- **provenance, worth recording plainly:** this fix was originally done, verified, and committed on 2026-09-10 in an isolated worktree (dispatched for a Lighthouse/trace pass) — the same worktree whose careless `wrangler pages deploy --branch=main` (run while 3 commits behind real `main`) is the live incident behind `CLAUDE.md`'s "a dispatched agent never deploys to production itself" rule. That deploy was reverted immediately, which also reverted this favicon fix off production, and the worktree itself was never merged back into `main` afterward — it sat unmerged for a day until this session's disk-space cleanup pass found it, confirmed the underlying bug was still live on `main`, and re-applied the same code change fresh. Originally filed as "B-150" in that worktree's own copy of this file; that number was independently reused on `main` in the meantime for the unrelated per-clip shot-identity bug, so this is filed under a new number rather than reusing the collided one.
- **found:** 2026-09-10, a follow-up Lighthouse/trace pass over production after B-149 (the render-blocking font fix). Nothing in Lighthouse's four scoring categories flagged it (100/100/100/100 throughout); it showed up in the network list of a real `performance_start_trace` against `https://apelles.studio/`, where `/icon-192.png` was fetched on every navigation at 44,249 B — 17% of the home page's own-origin weight, and the single largest asset on four of the six pages.
- **root cause:** `Base.astro` declared five icon relations, the last a `<link rel="icon" href="/icon-192.png" sizes="192x192">`. A browser paints the tab with exactly ONE `rel="icon"` and selects it by declared size, so declaring a large one is not a harmless extra option — it is the one downloaded. Chrome picked the 192px PNG over the 32/48px ones to draw a 16px tab icon. `icon-192.png` and `icon-512.png` (273,855 B) were web-app-manifest sizes on a site with no manifest and no install story; the 512 was shipped and referenced by nothing at all.
- **fix:** dropped the oversized `rel="icon"` line and deleted both PNGs rather than rehoming them in a manifest the site does not otherwise want (Android's own add-to-home-screen falls back to `apple-touch-icon`, a different relation never fetched as a tab icon, so nothing real was lost). Chrome now fetches `/favicon.ico` (7,686 B) instead: 44,249 B → 7,686 B per page load, on every page. Also, same file: two multi-line `<!-- -->` comment blocks (B-149's font rationale, the hero image's own note) moved into Astro frontmatter, which the build does not emit as HTML — a page trimming bytes off a reader's connection should not ship its own changelog to them. `Hero.astro`'s comment was also stale: it claimed the hero JPG doubled as the `og:image`, which stopped being true once D-288 moved that to `/og/card.jpg`.
- **investigated and deliberately left alone** (numbers recorded in `Hero.astro`'s own header so a future pass doesn't redo the experiment): the hero WebP (208,898 B, already at the knee of its quality/size curve and not the LCP element — the h1 text is); the 278,908 B Newsreader variable font (non-render-blocking, not LCP, an owner design call on the `opsz` axis, not a bug); Cloudflare's own analytics beacon (kept deliberately per D-293).
- **verified (re-run 2026-09-11 against the re-applied change):** `npm run build` succeeds; built `dist/index.html` carries no `rel="icon"` over 48px and ships neither `icon-192.png` nor `icon-512.png`. The two new regression tests from the original fix (`tests/palette.test.ts`: no oversized `rel="icon"`, no unreferenced icon PNG shipped) pass. The original 2026-09-10 pass additionally measured this live against production (Lighthouse 100/100/100/100 before and after, LCP unchanged within run-to-run variance since the favicon was never the LCP element) — not re-measured live this time since the change is byte-identical to what was already verified live once; the numbers are deterministic, not re-derived.

## B-163 — `editor_add_clip` (and `editor_edit_in`) never gave a dropped clip its D-129 linked-audio half, unlike the real GUI drag

status: **fixed** (both `editor_add_clip` and `editor_edit_in`, 2026-09-12) · severity: medium (every clip placed via MCP landed with its audio still embedded and un-splittable instead of a real, independently addressable linked audio clip on its own track — the default behaviour of every reference NLE and this app's own GUI) · area: `packages/editor/src/useEditorControl.ts`

- **found:** 2026-09-11/12, live — owner: *"also just preserve... also just use ffmped..."* → *"now fix the apelles also when we drop a clip by default audio and video seerates into there own track instead of all sitting in one track thats the real behavious how come its not happening?"*, after a clip placed via `editor_add_clip` landed as a single clip with embedded audio, no separate audio track, `linkGroup: null`.
- **root cause, confirmed by reading the real code, not assumed:** the GUI's own drag-and-drop path (`TimelinePane.tsx`) builds a video+audio clip PAIR via `linkedClipsFromDraggedMedia` (`timeline.ts`, D-129) — real Sources-panel drops give the user a linked A1 the same way Premiere and Resolve do. `editor_add_clip`'s handler in `useEditorControl.ts` calls the exact same underlying `add_clip` op, which already fully supports an optional `linkedAudio` argument (`ensureAudioTrackWithRoom` creates/reuses the audio track) — but the handler hard-coded `link_group: null` and never constructed or passed `linkedAudio` at all. `editor_edit_in`'s own comment even documented this as deliberate ("an agent that wants the sound as its own clip places it explicitly and links it") — which is exactly the asymmetry `CLAUDE.md`'s own "every feature is built for a human AND an AI" rule exists to catch: the MCP tool and the GUI action are nominally "the same feature" but took genuinely different code paths.
- **fix (`editor_add_clip`, then `editor_edit_in` the same way):** mirrors `linkedClipsFromDraggedMedia`'s own gate (`media.video.hasAudio && !still`) to decide whether to link, builds a `linkedAudio: NewClipFields` with the SAME `source_start`/`duration` the caller requested (not necessarily the whole file — `editor_add_clip` supports an arbitrary trim, unlike the GUI drag path which always places the full source), and passes it through to the existing `add_clip`/`edit_in` op. Also reports the linked audio clip's own `track`/`clipId` back in each tool's response, so an agent doesn't need a separate `get_timeline` call just to discover where `ensureAudioTrackWithRoom` put it. `editor_edit_in`'s own comment (which had documented the asymmetry as deliberate) is corrected accordingly.
- **verified live:** removed and re-added the same clip against the running app — `editor_add_clip`'s response now carries `linkedAudio: {clipId, track}`; `get_timeline` confirms two tracks, `kind: "video"` and `kind: "audio"`, both clips sharing one `linkGroup`. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npm test` in `@apelles/editor`: 1754/1755 passing both times this was checked, the one failure (`TimelinePane.tsx` React Compiler bailout) confirmed pre-existing and unrelated — `git diff` shows that file untouched by either change. `editor_edit_in`'s own fix was verified by type-check + the same test suite (not re-run live against the app separately — same code shape as the already-live-verified `editor_add_clip` path, sharing the same underlying op).

## B-164 — one slow op permanently bricks the whole Colorist MCP surface for the session: a dispatch timeout drops the bridge claim, and a still-mounted registry never re-announces

status: **fixed** (2026-09-12) · severity: **high** (every Colorist MCP tool — `get_state`, `list_masks`, `add_component`, `set_color_grade`, the whole grading surface — becomes unreachable for the rest of the session after any single op exceeds its budget, with a message that actively misdescribes the cause) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/control.rs`

- **found:** 2026-09-12, live, while trying to live-verify D-310's new `add_component` schema against the running app.
- **repro:** with the app up and Colorist ops working, call any op that exceeds its frontend budget — `add_subject_mask` on a 4K video is the natural one (SAM 2 routinely runs past the default 20s). Then call *any* Colorist op again.
- **expected:** the slow op reports a timeout; subsequent ops keep working, since the frontend is healthy and still mounted.
