- **actual:** every subsequent Colorist op returns 503 `op '<name>' has no frontend handler subscribed yet — the Apelles window is still starting up (waited 30s)`. Observed continuously for ~40 minutes against a window that had been up over an hour, with the Colorist UI rendering perfectly (Adjustments panel, live histogram, sliders — confirmed by `debug_screenshot`). `debug_*` and `editor_*` ops kept working throughout, so only the Colorist registry was affected. Switching tabs away and back does **not** recover it.
- **cause (confirmed by reading the code, not inferred from the symptom):** `control.rs:465-474` — on *any* `recv_timeout` expiry, `dispatch` calls `registry.forget_serving(op)`, dropping the claim that served the op. Its own comment says "The next call to this prefix waits for a fresh handshake instead of repeating this" — but **nothing ever produces that fresh handshake**. A registry announces on `chroma://bridge-ready` exactly once, when its `listen()` promise resolves at mount (D-309). `useChromaControl` is mounted for the life of the webview and does not remount on a tab switch, so after its claim is forgotten the only thing that restores it is a full webview reload. D-309's design note assumed the forget path would be followed by a reload ("a mid-session webview reload self-heals to the cold-start path"); a plain slow op is the case where the claim is dropped with no reload to follow.
- **why the 503 text makes it worse:** the message blames startup ("the window is still starting up"), so the obvious reaction is to wait and retry — which can never work. The true state is "a healthy registry whose claim was discarded."
- **very likely the real cause of B-160** (`add_subject_mask` reporting a tool error on a call that had actually succeeded server-side): identical signature — SAM 2 overruns the budget, the op really does complete in the frontend, and the claim is dropped on the way out. Confirmed live here that the matte *did* land (the Agent-activity feed showed `added subject mask (additive)` with a working Undo) while the tool call reported failure and every later Colorist op 503'd.
- **fix (option (a) from the original writeup):** `dispatch`'s timeout branch (`control.rs`) no longer calls `registry.forget_serving(op)`. A timeout means slow, not gone — the mid-session-reload case `forget_serving` was actually written for doesn't need it: the NEW registry's own `announce()` already replaces a stale claim by prefix on every mount, reload included (see `a_re_announcement_replaces_rather_than_duplicates`), so nothing was relying on the forget path to self-heal.
- **correction, 2026-09-12:** the fix above originally kept `forget_serving` itself as a primitive, proposing "a `WindowEvent` teardown hook would be the correct caller." Checked before letting that stand: this app creates exactly one window (`app/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, one `WebviewWindowBuilder` call, no multi-window path) — so by the time that window is destroyed the process is exiting anyway, and there is no later `dispatch` call left to benefit from a cleared claim. The proposed caller doesn't actually exist for this app's real architecture, so `forget_serving` and its dedicated test (`a_timed_out_registry_is_forgotten_so_the_next_call_re_handshakes`) were removed outright rather than left as speculative dead code (`cargo check` had already flagged it unused) — CLAUDE.md's own "no dead code left just in case" rule, applied to a mistake in this very fix rather than someone else's.
- **verified (both passes):** `cargo fmt`/`cargo clippy -p apelles --lib` clean (zero warnings in `control.rs`, confirmed by name both times), `cargo test -p apelles --lib chroma::control`: 11/11 then 10/10 after the removal (one fewer test, none newly failing).
- **verified:** `cargo fmt`/`cargo clippy -p apelles --lib` clean (zero new warnings — confirmed none of the pre-existing 14 are in `control.rs`), `cargo test -p apelles --lib chroma::control`: all 11 tests pass unchanged, including `a_timed_out_registry_is_forgotten_so_the_next_call_re_handshakes` (tests `forget_serving` directly, not `dispatch`'s call to it, so it still passes with the call site removed). Not re-verified live against a real SAM 2 overrun this pass — the fix is a straight removal of the one line that caused the symptom, root-caused and reasoned through above, not a new mechanism needing its own live proof the way B-160/B-164's original discovery did.

## B-165 — three MCP curve docstrings document a `"ease"` preset that the parser rejects

status: **fixed** (2026-09-12) · severity: low (an agent that follows the docstring gets a hard error; the four real presets all work) · area: `mcp/server.py`

- **found:** 2026-09-12, reading `parseCurve` while modelling D-310's `CurveSpec`.
- **cause:** `set_clip_fade` and `editor_set_keyframe_ease` both say the preset names are `"linear" | "ease-in" | "ease-out" | "ease-in-out"` *(also "ease", CSS's own)*. `EASE_PRESETS` (`timeline.ts`) contains exactly four entries and `"ease"` is not among them, so `parseCurve` refuses it with `unknown curve "ease"` — correctly, since it never silently substitutes.
- **fix:** dropped the `(also "ease", CSS's own)` clause from both docstrings — replaced with an explicit "exactly these four, no others" statement naming this bug, rather than adding a real `"ease"` preset. D-310's `EasePresetName` literal already deliberately encodes only the four that work, so the published schema was already right; this fixes the prose to match it.
- **verified:** `mcp/.venv/bin/python -c "import server"` succeeds, same tool count as before.

## B-166 — the Motion ease docstrings say `y` is unbounded; the handler clamps it to -0.75..1.75

status: **fixed** (2026-09-12) · severity: low (an overshoot beyond the clamp is silently reduced, with a `warning` the caller has to notice) · area: `mcp/server.py`

- **found:** 2026-09-12, while modelling `EaseCurve` for D-310.
- **cause:** `motion_set_camera_2d`, `motion_set_layer_transform_keys` and `motion_set_keyframe_ease` all say "`y` outside `0..1` is legal and means real overshoot" and offer `[0.3, 0, 0.3, 1.4]` as an example, implying `y` is unbounded. `clampEaseCurve` (`easeCurve.ts`) clamps `y1`/`y2` to `EASE_Y_MIN`/`EASE_Y_MAX` = **-0.75..1.75**. The documented example survives; a bigger bounce does not. Note the handler is *stricter* than the manifest's own zod schema, which constrains only `x1`/`x2`.
- **fix:** all three docstrings now state the real `-0.75..1.75` clamp and that it's silently applied with a warning, immediately after the "`y` is legal outside `0..1`" claim that was true but incomplete.
- **verified:** `mcp/.venv/bin/python -c "import server"` succeeds, same tool count as before.

## B-167 — Relight's depth/normal bakes ignore the image's real rotation/flip, so a rotated or flipped clip shades against a misaligned depth map

status: **fixed** (2026-09-12) · severity: medium (silently wrong shading, not a crash — only triggers once a user rotates/flips the clip) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/mask_generation.rs`

- **found:** 2026-09-12, investigating the owner's "relight is buggy as hell, not industry grade." An initial hypothesis (the `rim` light's default `distance` value doesn't produce real backlighting) was built into a Rust GPU-render regression test, run against the real shader, and **empirically disproved** — reverted rather than shipped; see the session for the disproof. This is the actual defect found on the follow-up pass.
- **repro:** rotate or flip a clip in the Transform panel, then use any positional Relight light (key/fill/rim) with Bake Depth, Track Depth, or Bake Normals.
- **cause:** every AI-mask bake that needs to re-align with the *current* display transform (`generate_ai_depth_bitmap`, `generate_ai_sky_bitmap`, subject masks) reads `rotation`/`flipHorizontal`/`flipVertical`/`orientationSteps` off the mask's own parameters and threads them into `TransformParams` before warping — because the bake itself always runs on the ORIGINAL, untransformed source frame. Relight's three bake resolvers (`generate_relight_depth_bitmap`, `generate_relight_depth_bitmap_static`, `resolve_relight_normal_bitmap`) instead hardcoded `rotation: 0.0, flip_horizontal: false, flip_vertical: false, orientation_steps: 0`, on the stated reasoning "relight has no per-layer rotation/flip of its own, unlike a mask sub-mask" — but that field was never a per-mask concept, it's just each mask's own copy of the same whole-image transform. Relight was the only bake dropping it. Once a user rotates/flips the clip, the depth (and any baked normal) bitmap stops lining up with the displayed frame — wrong-side lighting, background depth mapped onto the foreground, or a rim/key light that appears to do nothing sensible.
- **fix:** added `relight_transform_fields()` (reads the four fields straight off `js_adjustments`, same convention as `adjustment_utils.rs`/`cache_utils.rs`) and threaded them through all three functions' `TransformParams` instead of the hardcoded zeros. The baked-normal path additionally negates the X channel on `flip_horizontal` and the Y channel on `flip_vertical` (mirroring the scene negates those normal components, not just their position) — `orientation_steps` (a 90°/270° rotation) still warps normal-map *positions* correctly now, but does not yet rotate the X/Y *vector values* themselves (would need a sign-aware channel swap); left as a documented follow-up rather than guessed at and silently wrong.
- **verified:** new test `static_bake_honours_the_real_flip_and_rotation_state` (`mask_generation.rs`) proves a horizontal flip actually changes which side of the depth bake is bright; full `cargo test -p apelles --lib` (302 tests) and `cargo clippy -p apelles --lib` clean, no new warnings.

## B-168 — `editor_import_subtitles` raised `NameError` on every call: eleven style arguments in its body were never added to its signature

status: **fixed** (2026-09-12) · severity: high (the tool was 100% dead — every call, with any arguments, failed) · area: `mcp/server.py`

- **found:** 2026-09-12, by the D-312 parity harness, on its very first capture run and before a single line of the Rust port existed. 2 of 237 recorded cases came back `isError` — both of them this tool, including the minimal case that passes nothing but the required `path`.
- **repro:** `editor_import_subtitles(path="/anything.srt")`. Nothing else needed.
- **actual:** `NameError: name 'animation' is not defined`. Through MCP this surfaced as the bare `Error executing tool editor_import_subtitles`, with the real reason discarded — which is why four days of it being completely broken went unnoticed.
- **cause:** D-241/D-242 (`090536a`, 2026-09-08) added the animated-caption style keys to this tool's *body* — it forwards `animation`, `highlightOpacity`, `highlightPadX`, `highlightPadY`, `enterSecs`, `enterRise`, `wordGap`, and the four per-word colours — but never added the matching parameters to its `def`. Python does not catch that at import time; the names simply resolve to nothing at call time. `editor_set_caption_style` got the same eleven parameters in the same commit and has them declared correctly, so this is a straight omission in one of the two, not a design question.
- **why nothing caught it:** the tool surface had no test that actually *calls* every tool. Import succeeds, the tool lists, its schema publishes, and the count checks in `mcp/README.md` and `website/src/data/mcp.ts` all count decorators, not working tools. The D-312 harness calls all 161, which is exactly how this surfaced.
- **fix:** added the eleven missing parameters to the signature, matching `editor_set_caption_style`'s own names and types exactly (`animation`, `active_color`, `spoken_color`, `upcoming_color`, `highlight_color`, `highlight_opacity`, `highlight_pad_x`, `highlight_pad_y`, `enter_secs`, `enter_rise`, `word_gap`), plus a docstring paragraph pointing at that tool for what each means and noting the `"default"` clear-token the body already implements. No behaviour was invented: the body was already correct and complete, and now the arguments it reads exist.
- **verified:** the tool now returns a real envelope for both a minimal and a fully-populated call (`animation="karaoke"`, `active_color="default"` → `activeColor: null`, `word_gap=0.1` → `wordGap: 0.1`); the re-captured corpus has **0** `isError` cases where it had 2, and the capture is byte-identical across two consecutive runs.

## B-169 — D-313's MCP sidecar crash-looped from the moment it shipped: nothing in the app's build ever built the binary the app spawns, so it spawned a pre-D-313 one that ignored `--http`

status: **fixed** (2026-09-12) · severity: blocker (D-313's headline feature — "the app runs an MCP server, a client only needs a URL" — was 100% non-functional on any machine whose `target/` predated D-313) · area: `app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, `app/package.json`, `crates/apelles-ai/src/sidecar.rs`, `crates/apelles-mcp/tests/http_transport.rs`

- **found:** 2026-09-12, within hours of D-313 merging, by the coordinating session watching the real app's log. `[sidecar/mcp] exited (exit status: 1) after ~0.5s ... recent stderr: ... Error: ConnectionClosed("initialize request")`, repeating on every backoff retry, forever.
- **repro:** with a `target/<profile>/apelles-mcp` built before D-313 (or with any other `apelles-mcp` binary that predates `cli.rs`), start the app. The supervisor spawns it, it exits 1 in well under a second, and the loop never converges.
- **actual:** `Error: ConnectionClosed("initialize request")`, exit 1, ~0.5s, on every attempt.
- **cause — not rmcp, and not `serve.rs`.** Two independent facts pin it:
  1. `Error: {Debug}` is what Rust's `Termination` impl prints for a `main() -> Result<_, E: Debug>`. D-313's `main.rs` returns `ExitCode` and prints `apelles-mcp: {Display}`; only the **D-312** `main.rs` (`e3218d1~1`) formats an error that way. That version also **ignores argv entirely** and unconditionally does `ApellesMcp::new(transport).serve(stdio()).await?` — so `--http --port N` was silently discarded, it served *stdio*, and `expect_next_message(&mut transport, "initialize request")` (rmcp-3.3.0 `service/server.rs:442`) hit instant EOF because a supervised child has no interactive stdin. Reproduced exactly with the current binary by forcing that path: `apelles-mcp </dev/null` → `apelles-mcp: connection closed: initialize request`, exit 1, sub-second.
  2. The reported output contains no `serving MCP over HTTP at …` line, which D-313's `serve::http` prints unconditionally before binding. The crashing process never entered HTTP mode at all.
- **why the binary was stale:** `apelles-mcp` is deliberately **not** a dependency of the `apelles` crate (D-313 declined that edge on purpose), and `tauri.conf.json`'s `beforeDevCommand`/`beforeBuildCommand` were `npm run dev`/`npm run build` — vite only. So *nothing in `npm run tauri:dev` or `npm run tauri:build` ever built `apelles-mcp`*, while `Launch::WorkspaceBin` resolves and spawns `target/<profile>/apelles-mcp` — whatever happened to be lying there from an earlier session. D-313 shipped a supervisor for a binary its own build never produced.
- **why the D-101 staleness guard did not catch it:** it structurally cannot, for a compiled sidecar. `expected_content_hash` for a `WorkspaceBin` hashes `resolve_bin(...)` — *the very file the child executes* — and the child's `/health` reports the hash of its own `current_exe()`. Same file on both sides, so they agree no matter how old the build is. The guard answers "is the running process the binary on disk?", never "is the binary on disk current with its source". The owned-child path compounded it: `supervise` sets `s.stale = false` with a comment reasoning that "a Rust-owned spawn is by construction running the exact `server.py` on disk" — true for `PythonUvicorn` (the interpreter reads the source at spawn time), false for a build artifact.
- **why the tests did not catch it:** `http_transport.rs` spawned its server as `tokio::spawn(async move { let _ = axum::serve(..).await; })` and **never looked at that task's result**, and every test dialled the server immediately and finished inside a few hundred milliseconds. A server that dies half a second after binding left all of them green. Confirmed empirically here: with a deliberate 500ms early exit injected into the serving task, the two original tests still passed and only the new idle test failed.
- **the D-313 report's "the sidecar starts, is healthy, and I called a real tool through it" claim was real but not general.** It was made after a by-hand `cargo build -p apelles-mcp`, which is exactly the step that masks this bug — it makes the binary current for that one session and leaves the build wiring broken for every other. Nothing in that verification exercised a fresh checkout, a machine whose `target/` predated D-313, or the sidecar sitting idle; the crash-loop failure mode was never tested, and the feature was reported working while being unable to start on its own.
- **fix (four parts, one concern — "the app must run the binary this build produced, and must notice when it does not"):**
  1. **The cause.** `tauri.conf.json`'s hooks now run `npm run tauri:before-dev` / `tauri:before-build`, two new scripts in `app/package.json` that are `cargo build -p apelles-mcp [--release] && npm run dev|build`. Tauri's own before-hooks are the framework's mechanism for "build this other thing first", so this uses the canonical pattern rather than adding the `apelles → apelles-mcp` Cargo edge D-313 declined (a plain `[dependencies]` entry would build the *library* and not the binary target anyway, so it would not have fixed it).
  2. **The regression guard**, `the_build_hooks_build_the_binary_this_spec_spawns` in `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/sidecar.rs`: follows both hooks from `tauri.conf.json` into `app/package.json` and asserts the resolved script builds the package `MCP`'s `Launch::WorkspaceBin` names. That chain is a string in a JSON file two directories from the spec that depends on it — nothing would fail to compile if someone simplified a hook back to `npm run dev`, which is precisely how this shipped.
  3. **The honesty fixes** in `crates/apelles-ai/src/sidecar.rs`: `expected_content_hash` and the `s.stale = false` reset now state what they do and do not cover per launch kind, and name the build hook as the thing that keeps the owned-child claim true. The fast-fail escalation no longer tells the user to "check the lines above for the **Python** error" — wrong instruction for a Rust sidecar, whose fast-failure is overwhelmingly a stale/missing binary — and instead prints `spec.code_desc()` plus the existing `spec.run_hint()`, i.e. the literal `cargo build -p apelles-mcp` that fixes it. Had it said that, this bug would have been self-diagnosing from the log.
  4. **The test blind spot**, `crates/apelles-mcp/tests/http_transport.rs`: the serving task is now held in a `Server` struct and every test ends by asserting it has not finished (surfacing `axum::serve`'s real error, or a panic, instead of discarding it), and a new `the_server_stays_up_when_no_client_ever_connects` binds the router, leaves it strictly alone for 3s with no client ever connecting, then checks both that the accept loop has not returned and that a *freshly opened* connection still gets a 200 from `/health`.
- **verified:** `cargo test -p apelles-mcp --test http_transport` 3 passed (the idle test taking the full 3s); `cargo test -p apelles --lib chroma::sidecar` 4 passed including the new guard and D-313's own end-to-end `the_supervisor_really_starts_the_server_and_the_exit_hook_really_stops_it`. Both new guards were **negative-controlled**: reverting `beforeDevCommand` to `npm run dev` fails the build-hook guard with the message naming the fix, and injecting a 500ms early exit into the serving task fails the idle test with `axum::serve failed: …`. The fix itself was exercised directly — deleting `target/debug/apelles-mcp` and running `npm run tauri:before-dev` puts it back. End to end: the app was run from a worktree on isolated ports (`CHROMA_CONTROL_PORT=19888`, `CHROMA_MCP_PORT=19890`) and its `[sidecar/mcp]` log lines, a real HTTP MCP tool call, and a sustained idle period were checked against the running process — see the CHANGELOG entry for what was observed. `cargo fmt` clean on both touched crates; `cargo clippy -p apelles-mcp -p apelles-ai --all-targets` adds no new warnings (the 3 in `apelles-ai` are pre-existing, all in `mask.rs`).
- **left open, deliberately:** (a) a `WorkspaceBin`'s *external* staleness check is subtly racy — `serve::self_content_sha256` caches its `current_exe()` read in a `OnceLock` at first health poll, so an external process that was started *and first polled* before a rebuild reports the old hash (correct), but one first polled after the rebuild re-reads the new bytes and reports fresh (wrong). Real, much narrower than this bug, and not touched here. (b) A **packaged** (`tauri build`) bundle still does not contain `apelles-mcp` — `beforeBuildCommand` now puts it in `target/release/`, which `resolve_bin`'s workspace sweep finds in a dev-shaped layout, but a real bundle needs it declared as a Tauri `externalBin`. That is the pre-existing `TODO(Phase 4)` in `resolve_dir`/`docs/notes/sidecar-lifecycle.md`, not something this fix claims to have solved — **the MCP sidecar is verified for dev runs only.**

## B-170 — deleting a project you just closed refuses with "cannot delete the currently open project", from a screen that plainly has no project open

status: **fixed** (2026-09-12) · severity: medium (a normal workflow — open a project, decide against it, go back, delete it — silently fails) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/project.rs`, `app/src/store/useSessionStore.ts`

- **found:** 2026-09-12, owner live: "delete project does not work[s]".
- **repro:** open any project, click "‹ Projects" to go back to the launcher, then try to delete that same project's card. Refused.
- **actual:** `chroma_project_delete` returns `Err("cannot delete the currently open project")` even though the launcher — which is only ever shown with no project open — is the only screen this button exists on.
- **cause:** `state::set_project`'s own doc comment already said the Rust side's notion of "the loaded project" should be "cleared only on an explicit close" — but no command ever existed for the frontend to make that call. `useSessionStore.ts`'s `closeProject()` (the "‹ Projects" button) reset its own Zustand state and left `state::PROJECT` stale indefinitely, with a comment calling this "harmless — the next open/new overwrites it, and every frontend save path guards on projectPath". True for the save guard it was reasoning about; not true for `chroma_project_delete`, which reads ONLY the Rust-side value and has no second guard. `chroma_project_delete`'s own doc comment assumed "the launcher itself is only ever shown with no project open" — correct about the frontend's OWN state, silently false about the backend's.
- **fix:** added `chroma_project_close` (`#[tauri::command] pub fn chroma_project_close() { state::set_project(None); }`), and `closeProject()` now calls it (best-effort, matching the existing save-flush's "must never block getting back to the launcher" reasoning — a failed IPC call here still clears the frontend state and returns).
- **verified:** new Rust test `closing_a_project_lets_its_own_delete_button_work` (`chroma/project.rs`) — asserts the SAME project is refused while still marked current, then deletes cleanly after `chroma_project_close`. New frontend tests in `useSessionStore.test.ts` — `closeProject()` actually calls `invoke('chroma_project_close')`, and still clears local state even if that call rejects. `cargo test -p apelles chroma::project` and `npx vitest run src/store/useSessionStore.test.ts` both green (13 and 12 tests respectively).

## B-171 — a new project auto-placed every picked clip onto the timeline, back-to-back, in file-picker order — an order nobody chose

status: **fixed** (2026-09-12) · severity: low (not incorrect, just an unwanted default — every clip still had to be manually re-ordered) · area: `crates/apelles-project/src/manifest.rs`, `mcp/server.py`, `crates/apelles-mcp/src/tools/colorist.rs`

- **found:** 2026-09-12, owner: "by default dont put everything on timeline when we open".
- **cause:** `new_project_in` (D-070) put every seed path on the fresh timeline as a `Clip`, in the order the OS file picker happened to return them, before the human had looked at any of them — the only way to reach a different order was to delete and manually rebuild the sequence.
- **fix:** seed paths still land in the media pool exactly as before (visible in the Sources panel immediately) but are no longer auto-placed. A timeline is still created whenever there is seed media, so there is somewhere to drag into right away — it just starts empty. Placement is now always a deliberate action (a drag from Sources, or `editor_add_clip`), never an automatic side effect of picking media. The `new_project`/`new_project_in` MCP tool docstrings (`mcp/server.py`, `crates/apelles-mcp/src/tools/colorist.rs`, kept byte-identical per D-312's parity requirement) now say so explicitly, so an agent calling this tool doesn't assume the media is already placed.
- **also fixed in the same pass (`ProjectLauncher.tsx`):** the New Project dialog's Create button is now disabled until both a name and at least one clip are chosen (previously always enabled, regardless of either).
- **verified:** `cargo test -p apelles-project` — 61 tests, including the updated `new_project_creates_dir_and_manifest` (now asserts the timeline starts empty and both seed paths land in the pool) and five other tests updated to place a clip explicitly where they need one (mirroring what a real drag from Sources does) rather than relying on the old auto-placement. `crates/apelles-mcp`'s golden corpus was re-captured (`parity/capture.py` against the updated `mcp/server.py`) and `cargo test -p apelles-mcp` re-verified against it, since the docstring change is a real, captured part of the tool's published contract.

## B-172 — `understand_video` can never download its own model: `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` is set unconditionally on the generate subprocess, so the "first-run model download" its own module doc promises is impossible

status: **fixed (2026-09-18, D-354)** — see "fix" below · severity was: blocker for the capability on any machine where `mlx-community/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-4bit` is not already in the HF cache · area: `ai-media/video_understand.py`, `ai-env/setup.sh`

- **found:** 2026-09-12, by D-314's end-to-end verification run — the first time anything had actually called `/understand_video` on this machine with real media, rather than exercising the code path or the MCP tool definition.
- **repro:** on a machine whose `~/.cache/huggingface/hub` has no `models--mlx-community--Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-4bit`, `POST /understand_video {path: <any real video>}`. The job runs through ffmpeg scene detection and frame extraction normally, then fails at the model call.
- **actual:** the job ends `state: "error"` after ~210 s with
  `RuntimeError: mlx_vlm.generate failed: s/mlx-community/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-4bit/revision/main: offline mode is enabled. To disable it, please unset the HF_HUB_OFFLINE environment variable.`
- **expected:** the model downloads once (~2.9 GB) and the job completes, which is what `video_understand.py`'s own module doc says happens — *"no network calls beyond a first-run model download (`HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` is set on the model subprocess, so a cached model never reaches the network at all)"* — and what `ai-media/README.md` and `ai-media/requirements.txt` both promise (*"Models are pulled from the HF cache on first use"*).
- **cause:** `_ENV_OFFLINE = {**os.environ, "HF_HUB_OFFLINE": "1"}` (`video_understand.py:108`) is passed as `env=` to the `mlx_vlm.generate` subprocess on **every** call (`:204`), with no condition on whether the model is already present. The intent in the doc is clearly "offline *once cached*" — the parenthetical says exactly that — but the code has no first-run branch, so the download it describes can never occur through this path. The transcript sibling is unaffected: `mlx_whisper` is called in-process by `transcribe.py`, not through this env, which is why `whisper-large-v3-mlx` *is* in the cache and transcription works.
- **why this went unnoticed:** the capability's model was presumably cached on whatever machine D-184/D-189 were developed on, so the offline env var was only ever exercised in its happy "already cached" state. Nothing in the repo pre-fetches the model, and the failure only appears on a machine that has never had it — the same shape as B-169 (a feature verified once under conditions that masked the bug, and unable to bootstrap itself anywhere else).
- **not a D-314 regression.** Verified: the error is raised by `huggingface_hub`'s offline guard before any model code runs, it reproduces identically to what the pre-D-314 venvs would do (the env var is read from `os.environ`, nothing venv-dependent), and once the model was fetched by hand into the shared HF cache the same shared-venv sidecar drove `mlx_vlm.generate` fine. The shared environment is not implicated.
- **why not fixed at the time:** D-314's scope was the Python environment, and the honest fix touches this repo's **local-first network policy** (`CLAUDE.md`: "Zero network calls in the grade path… any cloud call is an explicit opt-in fallback, never a default"). A 2.9 GB download silently triggered by an agent calling `editor_analyze_video` is a real product decision, not a typo — it wanted its own `D-NNN` (**D-354**), not a quiet patch inside a dependency change.
- **fix (D-354, option 2 of the three drafted above):** `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` stays hardcoded — that was correct, not the bug. `ai-env/setup.sh --fetch-models` is the new explicit, one-time step (network on for that command only) that populates the HF cache via `huggingface_hub.snapshot_download`, reading the model id from `video_understand.MODEL` so the two can't drift apart. `video_understand.describe_frames` now recognizes huggingface_hub's own offline-guard stderr (`_offline_download_error`) and raises a `UserFacingError` naming that exact command, instead of the opaque `mlx_vlm.generate failed: ...` dump above — `server._run_job`'s existing B-119 `UserFacingError` handling (see B-119) surfaces it to the caller verbatim. Options 1 (implicit fetch) and 3 (`GET /health` reporting) were considered and not chosen/not done — see D-354 for why option 1 specifically was rejected; option 3 remains open ground for later, not required by this fix.
- **verified:** `ai-media/test_video_understand_offline_model.py` (new) replays the exact stderr text captured in this bug's "actual" line above through `_offline_download_error` and through `describe_frames` end-to-end (with a stubbed `subprocess.run`, importable-free of MLX/ffmpeg — same discipline as `test_transcribe_offline_model_load.py`), asserting: the real offline-guard text resolves to a `UserFacingError` naming `ai-env/setup.sh --fetch-models`; an unrelated subprocess failure is correctly left unclassified (still an ordinary `RuntimeError`); and `describe_frames` itself raises the named error at the real call site while still passing `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` to the subprocess (D-354's hard-offline guarantee is unchanged by this fix). The `--fetch-models` snippet's import wiring (`sys.path` to `ai-media/`, `from video_understand import MODEL`) was also exercised directly against a stub `huggingface_hub.snapshot_download` to confirm it resolves and calls the right model id — a real download was not run as part of verification (no network access in this environment; `snapshot_download`'s own correctness is not this repo's code to verify).
- **historical workaround** (superseded by `--fetch-models` above): `ai-env/.venv/bin/python -c "from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download; snapshot_download('mlx-community/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-4bit')"`.

## B-177 — `npm run tauri:dev` never reached a running app: `build.rs` rewrote a watched resource on every build, so the dev watcher restarted the build forever

status: fixed (2026-09-13, D-315) · severity: high (the repo's documented dev command
could not start the app in a checkout whose staged resources were stale or absent) ·
area: `app/src-tauri/build.rs`

- **found:** 2026-09-13, D-315's MCP pass, trying to exercise the new tools against a
  real app in a fresh worktree.
- **repro:** delete `app/src-tauri/resources/ai-env/` (or start from a fresh checkout)
  and run `npm run tauri:dev`.
- **expected:** the app builds once and launches.
- **actual:** `Info File src-tauri/resources/ai-env/requirements.lock.txt changed.
  Rebuilding application...` — over and over, right at the end of every build.
- **cause:** `stage_ai_env_resources` used `fs::copy` **unconditionally**, and
  `fs::copy` bumps the destination's mtime even when the bytes are identical. `tauri
  dev` watches `src-tauri/` for changes, so the very act of staging the resource
  invalidated the build that had just staged it. The file is listed in the root
  `.gitignore`, which is what everyone assumes protects it — but that only helps a
  watcher that reads *that* ignore file, and this one plainly did not.
- **fix:** read the source, compare it against the destination, and write only when they
  differ. This is the same "already valid, skip it" shape the ONNX Runtime and `uv`
  downloads in the same file already use, and for the same reason — a build script has no
  business churning mtimes on files it did not change.
- **why it did not show up when D-315 landed:** the staged files were already present and
  current from a previous run in the checkout it was developed in, so the copy was a
  no-op in practice. It bites a fresh worktree, a fresh clone, and anyone who edits
  `ai-env/requirements.lock.txt` — the same "verified once under conditions that never
  exercised it" shape as B-169 and B-173.

## B-176 — the website's own anti-fabrication guard could never pass: it looked for the bridge's 504 wording in `mcp/server.py`, which does not author it

status: fixed (2026-09-13, D-315) · severity: low (a docs page quoting an error string the
app stopped raising, and a red test that had stopped being read) · area:
`website/tests/mcp-data.test.ts`, `website/src/data/mcp.ts`,
`website/src/pages/docs/_mcp.astro`

- **found:** 2026-09-13, D-315, on the first `npx vitest run tests/mcp-data.test.ts` after
  adding the AI-environment group — 79 passed, 1 failed, and the failure was nothing to
  do with this change.
- **cause:** `ERROR_FRAGMENTS` holds the two error strings the docs page quotes, and the
  guard asserts each really appears in the server. But it only ever read
  `mcp/server.py`. The "cannot reach the app" one is authored there; the bridge's
  503/504 bodies are authored in **Rust**, by `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/control.rs`. So
  the 504 fragment could not match whatever it said, and when B-153 reworded that
  message (`"… did not respond (its window may be closed or busy)"` →
  `"… got no reply from the frontend within Ns …"`), the guard whose entire job is to
  catch that drift reported it as its own failure instead.
- **fix:** the guard now reads both files that author these strings; the fragment and the
  docs-page copy are updated to what the control server actually says today — including
  the part B-153 added that the page was missing, that a 504 is **inconclusive**, not a
  failure, because the op can still complete after the bridge gives up.
- **not caught earlier because** nothing runs `website/`'s tests in this repo's normal
  loop (it is deliberately outside the npm workspace, D-255/D-264) and its `node_modules`
  is not even installed in a fresh checkout.

## B-175 — `add_subject_mask` / `track_subject` reported `ok: true` for an AI call that failed: the error was swallowed into a GUI toast

status: fixed (2026-09-13, D-315) · severity: high (an agent was told a matte existed that
did not; every subsequent decision was made on a false premise) · area:
`app/src/hooks/useAiMasking.ts`, `app/src/hooks/useChromaControl.ts`

- **found:** 2026-09-13, D-315, while making the AI-backed MCP tools return a
  distinguishable "the environment is still building" answer. The two most prominent of
  them turned out to be incapable of returning *any* failure.
- **repro:** stop the `ai/` sidecar (or call it before D-315's environment build has
  finished) and call `add_subject_mask` over MCP on a video clip.
- **expected:** `{ok: false, error: …}` naming the reason.
- **actual:** `{ok: true, result: {maskId, subMaskId, bbox, mode}}`. A mask container and
  sub-mask really were created; the matte behind them was not, and nothing said so.
- **cause:** `handleGenerateAiMask` and `handleTrackSubject` ended their `catch` with
  `toast.error(...)` and returned `undefined`. A toast is the GUI's answer and reaches
  nobody else. The op handlers `await`ed them and then returned their own success object
  unconditionally, so `useChromaControl`'s `respond({ ok: !result?.error, … })` saw no
  error to report. `handleTrackDepth`, written later, already returned `{ error }` — the
  right shape existed in the same file and these two predated it.
- **fix:** both now return `{ error }` after toasting (and a success object otherwise),
  and both op handlers propagate it. The GUI toast is unchanged, so nothing about the
  human path moves.
- **why nothing caught it:** the MCP parity harness replays what the layer *sends* against
  a stub app, which is the right boundary for D-312 and cannot see an app-side handler
  that lies. Nothing else calls these ops with a deliberately broken sidecar.

## B-180 — `ai_env_retry` promised a retry that could never happen: `retry_now()` returned `true` in the one phase whose supervisor thread has already exited

status: fixed (2026-09-13, D-315) · severity: medium (a "Retry now" button and an MCP tool
both reported an attempt had started, forever, on a machine where none ever would) · area:
`crates/apelles-ai/src/ai_env.rs`

- **found:** 2026-09-13, D-315, building the `ai_env_retry` MCP tool on top of the
  same function the GUI button uses.
- **repro:** run with `CHROMA_AI_ENV_NO_BOOTSTRAP=1` (or any build with no bundled `uv`,
  or no `requirements.lock.txt`) so the phase is `unavailable`, then call `ai_env_retry` /
  press Retry now.
- **expected:** `false` — nothing to retry.
- **actual:** `true`. The `retry_requested` flag was set and `wake.notify_all()` called
  with nobody listening; the phase never moved.
- **cause:** `retry_now()` declined for `Ready` and `Phase::is_working()` and accepted
  everything else. But `supervise` **returns** when it reaches `Unavailable` — all three
  routes into that phase (`CHROMA_AI_ENV_NO_BOOTSTRAP`, no `ai-env` directory, no bundled
  `uv`) are early returns — so there is no thread left to wake. D-315's own note already
  said `unavailable` is not retried on a timer "because nothing about waiting would change
  it, and a UI promising an automatic retry there would be lying"; the manual retry told
  the same lie.
- **fix:** `retry_now()` returns `false` for `Phase::Unavailable`, with the reason in its
  doc comment and a case in `retry_now_declines_only_while_an_attempt_is_in_flight`.
- **note on the `ready` half:** a concurrent D-315 commit changed `retry_now` the other
  way for `Ready` — it now *accepts* there, because ready is a cached answer and a venv
  deleted by hand afterwards would otherwise be reported healthy forever. The two calls
  point opposite ways for opposite reasons and both are right: `ready` is a cached answer
  worth invalidating, `unavailable` is a standing fact about the machine with nothing
  listening for the request. Both reasons are written into `retry_now`'s doc comment so
  the next reader does not "simplify" one into the other.

## B-173 — `npm run tauri:build` (the documented release-build command, `CLAUDE.md`'s own "Running the app" section) fails immediately: `error: unrecognized subcommand 'tauri'`

status: **fixed** (2026-09-12) · severity: medium (the one release-build entry point this repo's own docs point to didn't work at all) · area: `package.json`

- **found:** 2026-09-12, while measuring a real release-build size for the D-315 (AI-env bootstrap) sizing discussion — the first time this session actually ran `npm run tauri:build` rather than only `tauri:dev`.
- **repro:** `npm run tauri:build` from the repo root.
- **actual:** `npm run tauri --workspace app -- tauri build` runs `app`'s own `"tauri": "tauri"` script with the extra args `tauri build` appended, producing the literal shell command `tauri tauri build` — the Tauri CLI sees `tauri` as its subcommand and rejects it: `error: unrecognized subcommand 'tauri'`.
- **cause:** the root `tauri:build` script pre-pended a redundant literal `tauri` before the real subcommand, left over from a version of the script apparently written against a different form of the passthrough. `tauri:dev` never hit this because it goes through `npm run start --workspace app` → `app`'s `"start": "tauri dev"` script, which is a complete, correctly-formed command on its own, not a passthrough.
- **fix:** `"tauri:build": "npm run tauri --workspace app -- build"` (dropped the redundant leading `tauri`) — matches the root `"tauri"` script's own documented passthrough shape (`npm run tauri --workspace app -- <tauri-cli-args>`).
- **verified:** `npm run tauri:build` now runs `tauri build` for real (confirmed it reaches `beforeBuildCommand`/`cargo build --release`/the frontend build, past the point the old command never reached at all).

## B-174 — "Captions from Transcript" hangs forever: a cached model still tries to phone home, and that call died mid-flight

status: **fixed** (2026-09-13) · severity: high (a shipped, documented feature — D-238 — became unusable with no error, no timeout, no way out but killing the sidecar) · area: `ai-media/transcribe.py`

- **found:** 2026-09-13, owner live: "30s transcribe takes like forever :) bro :/". Reproduced and root-caused live, not from a report alone.
- **repro:** click "Captions from Transcript" on any clip, on a machine where the transcribe model is already fully cached locally. The button sits on "Transcribing…" indefinitely.
- **actual:** `ps`/`top` showed the `ai-media` sidecar process at a flat **0% CPU across a live 4-second delta** (not merely "slow due to a big model" — genuinely doing no work), while `chroma_transcribe_status` kept reporting `jobs_running: 1`. `lsof -p <pid> -i` found the smoking gun: an outbound HTTPS connection in **CLOSE_WAIT** — the remote peer had already closed its end, but the process's own code never noticed and stayed blocked waiting on it, forever (no timeout anywhere in the path).
- **cause:** `mlx_whisper.load_models.load_model` calls `huggingface_hub.snapshot_download(repo_id=path_or_hf_repo)` unconditionally, with no `local_files_only`. Even when every file is already cached, `snapshot_download` still reaches out to the Hub to confirm the cached revision is current — directly contradicting `transcribe.py`'s own module doc, which promises "no network calls beyond a first-run model download." Today, that revision-check connection died mid-flight and the client-side code had nothing to notice or time out on.
- **fix:** added `_local_snapshot_or_repo()` — resolves the repo to its cached snapshot directory first, via `snapshot_download(repo_id=repo, local_files_only=True)` (raises immediately, no network, when nothing is cached — falls back to the bare repo id unchanged in that case, preserving the real first-run download path). `load_model` only calls `snapshot_download` itself when the string it's handed does **not** already exist as a real path — so handing it an already-resolved local directory skips the network call entirely, with no global env var (`HF_HUB_OFFLINE`) to mutate and therefore no thread-safety concern across concurrent jobs for different models.
- **verified:** killed and restarted the hung sidecar, confirmed `/health` came back clean (`jobs_running: 0`); a real end-to-end `transcribe()` call against a short audio-bearing fixture then completed in ~15s with zero hang (that time is the one-time model-weights load into MLX for a cold process, not a repeat of the bug). New test `ai-media/test_transcribe_offline_model_load.py`: an uncached/fake repo id degrades to the bare string with no exception (first-run path untouched), and a genuinely cached model resolves to a real local directory containing `config.json` (the fast path actually engages). Existing `test_transcribe_errors.py` (B-119) still passes unchanged.
- **not yet done:** this is the same class of bug as B-172 (`video_understand.py`, a different symptom of the same "a supposedly offline path still touches the network" family) — `ai/server.py`'s other model loads (SAM2, ViTMatte, MoGe-2, Video Depth Anything) were not audited for the identical pattern in this pass; worth a follow-up sweep.

status: **fixed** (2026-09-13) · severity: medium (the app crate's own test suite did not pass, so the next real regression in it had nothing to fail against) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/project.rs` (tests only)

- **found:** 2026-09-13, while independently verifying the D-315 branches — `cargo test -p apelles` was red on `main` itself, unrelated to D-315.

- **failure:** `index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0` — each test called `new_project_in(...)` with one or two seed paths and then indexed `tl.tracks[0].clips[0]`.

B-171 updated the six affected tests in `crates/apelles-project` and verified with `cargo test -p apelles-project`, but four tests in the *app* crate relied on the same auto-placement and were neither updated nor run at the time (`cargo test -p apelles` wasn't in that entry's "verified" line).
- **fix:** each of the four now places its clip(s) explicitly via `append_media_clip`, mirroring what B-171 did for the other six and what a real drag from Sources does.
- **verified:** `cargo test -p apelles --lib chroma::project::tests` → 13 passed, 0 failed. Full `cargo test -p apelles --lib` → 307 passed, 0 failed. `cargo fmt`/`cargo clippy` clean on the edited lines (one pre-existing, unrelated clippy note elsewhere in the file).

## B-179 — the AI-env health check deleted the 1.6 GB environment it was checking, because "I could not ask" was treated as "the answer was no"

status: **fixed** (same commit) · severity: high (destroys a correct, fully-installed
1.6 GB environment and forces a multi-minute rebuild) · area:
`crates/apelles-ai/src/ai_env.rs`

- **found:** 2026-09-13, D-315's own end-to-end run, live — not by a test.
- **what happened.** The run killed leftover processes by matching a path pattern. That
  pattern also matched `verify.py` running *through the venv's own interpreter*, so the
  health check was killed mid-flight. `health()` returned an error, `attempt()` treated
  that error like any other, re-installed, asked again, got killed again — and then took
  the second stage of the self-heal: **wiped a complete, working, fully-verified 1.6 GB
  venv and rebuilt it from scratch.** From the log:

  ```
  02:00:08 [INFO] [ai-env] Installed 91 packages in 8.81s
  02:00:24 [WARN] [ai-env] the environment still does not verify after re-installing
           (verify.py reported the environment unusable: ) — wiping ... and rebuilding
  ```

  Note the empty reason after the colon: the verifier was killed before it could write
  anything, so the log could not even say why. That emptiness *was* the evidence, and it
  was being thrown away.
- **cause.** `health()` collapsed two genuinely different outcomes into one `Err(String)`:
  *"`verify.py` ran and returned a verdict — `torch` will not import"* and *"`verify.py`
  never returned a verdict."* Only the first is evidence about the environment. The second
  is evidence about the check. The remedy for the first is destructive, so conflating them
  means a flaky, killed, or unrunnable checker can destroy a perfectly good environment.
- **fix.** `health()` now returns `Unhealthy::Broken` (a real verdict: the JSON `checks`
  array names what failed) or `Unhealthy::Inconclusive` (killed by a signal, or exited
  without the JSON it always writes when it actually runs). **Only `Broken` can trigger the
  wipe.** `Inconclusive` fails the attempt so the ordinary backoff re-asks the question,
  destroying nothing. Pinned by
  `a_health_check_that_never_answered_is_inconclusive_not_broken`, which drives a real
  Python that SIGKILLs itself, one that exits non-zero silently, and one that returns a
  genuine verdict — the last of those being the control, without which the wipe path could
  be dead code and the test would still pass.
- **why no test caught it.** Every existing test exercised a verifier that *answered*. The
  whole failure mode is a verifier that does not, and nothing in the suite had ever
  produced one — the scenario only appeared when a real process got killed at a real
  moment. The general lesson is the one worth keeping: a check whose failure path is
  destructive needs a test for *not being able to run the check*, not just for the check
  returning false.

## B-181 — `cargo build` on a fresh checkout could fail outright: the `uv`/ONNX Runtime download's implicit HTTP timeout was shorter than a real, working download can take

status: **fixed** (2026-09-13) · severity: high (blocks a first build entirely, with no override, on any network that isn't fast — not a corner case) · area: `app/src-tauri/build.rs`

- **found:** 2026-09-13, the first time `cargo build`/`cargo test --workspace` ran in a fresh `target/` after D-315 merged — the `main` checkout had never built `stage_uv`'s download path before (every prior build of this session happened in a worktree that already had the binary cached).
- **repro:** `cargo build --workspace` on a checkout with no `app/src-tauri/binaries/uv-aarch64-apple-darwin` staged yet.
- **actual:** all 3 of `fetch_uv`'s built-in retries failed identically: `error sending request for url (...)`. A direct `curl -sI` to the same URL looked fine (a normal 302 to a signed Azure blob URL), which pointed at first toward "server-side flake" — but `curl -sL` (actually following the redirect and downloading the real file) succeeded in **11.4 real seconds**, and a minimal standalone `reqwest::blocking::get` reproduction against the exact same URL, same dependency versions, failed with `TimedOut` every time. Nothing in `build.rs` ever called `.timeout(...)` on any HTTP client — `reqwest::blocking::get`'s implicit default client has some built-in timeout, undocumented at the call site, shorter than the ~11s this specific download reliably takes.
- **cause:** `download_and_verify` (used for the ONNX Runtime library) and `fetch_uv` (D-315's `uv` binary) both used the bare `reqwest::blocking::get(url)` shorthand — no explicit timeout anywhere. `fetch_uv`'s own 3-attempt retry loop (added because "this genuinely flakes") retried the exact same too-short timeout three times, which cannot succeed any more than the first attempt did; the loop's own comment mis-attributed the flakiness to "a transient DNS/TLS blip" rather than the real, fixed cause.
- **why this went unnoticed until now:** every worktree that had already built once (all four dispatched-agent worktrees this session) had the binary cached and skipped the download entirely (`stage_uv`'s own "already staged and valid" short-circuit) — this is the same "verified once under conditions that never exercised it" shape as B-169/B-173/B-177.
- **fix:** a shared `http_client()` builds one `reqwest::blocking::Client` with an explicit 120s timeout (generous for a binary this size on any network that completes at all), used by both `download_and_verify` and `fetch_uv`'s retry loop instead of the bare `get()` shorthand.
- **verified:** `cargo build --workspace` on a fresh `target/`, no binary staged: real `uv` archive download completes, sha256-verifies, and the extracted binary is confirmed `Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64` at `app/src-tauri/binaries/uv-aarch64-apple-darwin`. `cargo fmt`/`cargo clippy` clean on `build.rs`. Full `cargo test --workspace` afterward: every crate green (apelles 311, apelles-ai 55, apelles-mcp's suites, etc.).

## B-182 — the shared "Sources" panel toggle silently ate every click in Colorist, and only Colorist

status: **fixed** (2026-09-13) · severity: high (a shared, shell-level control — present and visually correct — did nothing at all on one of three tabs, with no error) · area: `packages/shell/src/Shell.tsx`

- **found:** 2026-09-13, owner live: the shared floating Sources toggle (top-left of the content area) opened/closed correctly in Motion and via a direct `debug_set_sources_panel` state write in every tab, but a real click on it in Colorist did nothing — not "wrong state", literally nothing observable.
- **repro:** open a project, switch to Colorist, click the Sources chip (top-left of the preview).
- **actual:** a temporary `console.log` placed directly inside the button's `onClick` never fired on a real click in Colorist (confirmed via the app's own frontend log) — the event never reached React at all. The same button, same code, fired correctly on Motion, and the underlying state (`useShellStore.sourcesPanelOpen`) and the `SourcesPanel` component both rendered correctly in Colorist when set programmatically — ruling out a state or rendering bug.
- **cause:** the chip was `absolute … z-10`. Colorist's own `EditorToolbar` wrapper (`app/src/components/panel/Editor.tsx:2113`, `relative z-10`) sits at the *identical* z-index, and Colorist's whole content subtree renders AFTER this chip in `Shell.tsx`'s own DOM order — so at a tied z-index, later-in-DOM wins the stacking order, and Colorist's toolbar silently absorbed the pointer event before it ever reached the chip beneath it. Motion has nothing at this position/z-index (its own `z-10`/`z-20` usages are deep inside `KeyframeTimeline.tsx`, nowhere near the top-left corner), which is exactly why only Colorist showed this.
- **how this was isolated:** DOM inspection alone couldn't show it (`pointer-events: auto`, correct rect, correct z-index — all looked fine in isolation); a `debug_set_sources_panel` state write proved the panel and its state both work; only a live `console.log` inside the real `onClick`, compared against a real user click producing zero output, proved the event was being intercepted before React ever saw it. Raising the chip's z-index to an extreme test value (`z-[9999]`) confirmed it was a stacking conflict before landing the real, minimal fix.
- **fix:** raised the chip to `z-20` — safely above Colorist's `z-10` toolbar, with a comment naming the exact competing element so a future z-index bump on either side doesn't silently reopen this.
- **verified:** live, repeatedly, in the real running app — a real click now opens and closes the panel correctly in Colorist (confirmed via the same `console.log` instrumentation before it was removed, and by the owner directly). `npx vitest run packages/shell` (20 tests) and `npm run typecheck` (zero new errors against the existing baseline) both clean after the fix.
- **not caught by any existing test:** `jsdom` (this repo's frontend test environment) computes no real layout or paint order, so a z-index stacking-tie bug like this is invisible to any DOM test — it can only be caught by a real browser/webview render, which is why this was found live rather than by the test suite.

## B-184 — `TimelinePane.tsx` fails its own D-201 React Compiler coverage test on `main`: a ref is read directly during render

status: **fixed** (2026-09-18, **D-355**) · severity: medium (the whole ~3400-line component silently loses all React-Compiler auto-memoization — D-201's own stated failure mode — not a user-visible bug today, but exactly the drift D-201's test exists to catch before it becomes one; also this is the Edit tab's highest-update-frequency surface, the one D-201 and D-325 both exist to keep cheap, and CLAUDE.md's priority order puts performance first) · area: `packages/editor/src/TimelinePane.tsx` (~L3746), guard: `packages/editor/src/reactCompiler.test.ts`

- **duplicate merged in:** this entry absorbs **B-210** (filed independently 2026-09-16 by the D-338 pass against the same statement, ~61 lines further down after D-325/D-334 inserted code above it — same compiler bailout reason, same single ref read, same fix). Do not re-file separately.
- **found:** 2026-09-13, flagged by the D-316 (on-canvas caption transform) dispatch as pre-existing on `main`, unrelated to its own work — independently reproduced: `npx vitest run packages/editor/src/reactCompiler.test.ts` fails identically on a clean `main` checkout with no other changes.
- **repro:** `npx vitest run packages/editor/src/reactCompiler.test.ts` → `TimelinePane.tsx compiles with no React Compiler bailout` fails: `expected [ 'Cannot access refs during render' ] to deeply equal []`.
- **exact location** (the test's own logger only reports the reason string, not a location — found by re-running the same Babel transform standalone with the full `CompileError` event printed): `TimelinePane.tsx:3746` (was `:3685` when first filed; D-325/D-334 inserted ~61 unrelated lines above it since), `const clipDragPress = trimPressRef.current;`, read directly in the component's render body (not inside an event handler, effect, or memo callback) and used to compute `isSlipOrSlideDrag`, which feeds `dragOverlayLabel`'s JSX output.
- **why it's there, and why the obvious fix is not safe to make casually:** the surrounding comment (`TimelinePane.tsx:3672-3684`) explains this is deliberate — a slip/slide's mode must be "resolved once, from the press that started the drag," not reactively from live state, so a modifier key changing mid-drag can't retarget a gesture already in flight. `trimPressRef` itself is populated by a raw `pointerdown` `addEventListener` (not a React handler) specifically so that listener "never re-binds" (see its own doc at `:1483`/`:1503`) — it is deliberately NOT `useState`. The render-time read at `:3685` only works correctly *because* that pointerdown listener always fires and synchronously stamps the ref before whatever sets `activeDrag` triggers the re-render that reads it — a real, working timing dependency on dnd-kit's own drag-start ordering, documented across B-137/B-144/D-098/D-250/D-261 in the same file.
- **why not fixed here:** promoting `trimPressRef` to `useState` (the standard fix for "a ref value needs to affect render output") risks disturbing that exact timing relationship without careful, dedicated verification against the real drag gesture this whole cluster of prior bug fixes was written to protect — not a change to make inside an unrelated dispatch's verification pass. Needs its own focused pass: preserve the "resolved once, at press time" semantics (likely by setting a companion `useState` in the same `onPointerDown` listener, read at `:3685` instead of the ref, verified against `TimelinePane.marquee.dom.test.tsx`-style real DOM interaction) without touching the timing contract the surrounding comments document.
- **impact today (before the fix):** none observable — the component still worked, it just rendered via React's normal (non-compiled) path instead of the Compiler's auto-memoized one, silently, exactly as D-201's own module doc describes as the failure mode this test exists to catch.
- **fixed (D-355), and NOT by the shape suggested above.** The press is now snapshotted into a `clipDragPress` state inside `onDndDragStart` — beside the `setClipGrab` that has done exactly this since B-137 — and the render reads that state instead of the ref. The pointerdown listener is **not touched at all**, so its never-re-binds contract is preserved by construction rather than by re-verification.
- **why the suggested "companion `useState` in the pointerdown listener" was rejected:** it would re-render this entire ~3,400-line pane on *every* press anywhere in the edit area, including a plain click that never becomes a drag — the exact cost B-137's ref-then-promote pattern exists to avoid, i.e. trading a performance regression for a performance fix. Snapshotting at drag start costs zero extra renders (it batches into the `setActiveDrag` render that was already happening) and is *more* provably correct on the timing question this entry worried about: `onDndDragStart` fires only once dnd-kit's 4px activation constraint is satisfied, which is strictly after the capture-phase pointerdown listener has stamped the ref. That is not a new assumption — it is the same ordering `clipGrab` has depended on since B-137, already covered by that bug's own DOM tests. Full reasoning in **D-355**.
- **the timing fear in this entry turned out to be about the wrong hazard.** There was never a race between the listener and the render; the hazard was only ever *when* you read. Reading at drag start pins the press for the whole gesture, which is strictly closer to the "resolved once, at press time" doctrine than the old live re-read on every render was.
- **verified, with a negative control** (the coverage question this entry raised): `reactCompiler.test.ts` 99/99, `TimelinePane.tsx` bailout-free (was the one failure). Real-`PointerEvent` DOM coverage for this exact path already existed and is `TimelinePane.slipSlidePreview.dom.test.tsx` (B-144's own 6 cases), not `marquee` as guessed above — it plus `dragGhost`/`trim`/`trimTools`/`clipDrag` is 48 real drag-gesture tests, all passing. Proved non-vacuous by deliberately breaking the snapshot: 4 of those 6 cases fail immediately (both Alt-armed *and* both tool-picked slip/slide entrances) while the two "the move ghost must still show" controls stay green. Full editor suite **2043/2043** across 112 files, including `TimelinePane.playheadCost.dom.test.tsx`'s commit-count guard (D-325) — the extra state adds no commits. `tsc` on `@apelles/editor`: 3 errors before, the identical 3 after (all pre-existing, all in test files, none in `TimelinePane.tsx`).

## B-183 — a selected caption drew NOTHING on the canvas: no box, no handles, no indication it was selected

status: **fixed** (2026-09-13, D-316) · severity: high (a whole interaction surface silently absent for one clip kind) · area: `packages/editor/src/TransformOverlay.tsx`, `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/edit.rs` (`clip_geometry`)

- **found:** 2026-09-13, live — owner: *"fix that caption is not selectable movable / resizable at all :) and it should propogate to whole caption right :)"*. Confirmed with a real screenshot before any code was read: the caption text renders correctly in the preview, the clip is visibly selected in the timeline AND shows a full, working Inspector (Position X/Y, Font Size, Colour, Align, Pad X/Y, Animation), and the canvas shows nothing whatsoever.
- **root cause:** `TransformOverlay` gets a clip's box size from `chroma_timeline_clip_geometry`. That command answers for a media clip (source resolution), for a title (D-262's measured ink box) and for an adjustment clip (the whole frame) — but a caption clip has an **empty `source_path`**, so it fell through to `if c.source_path.is_empty() { return Err("clip has no source") }`. `useClipGeometry` maps any failure to `null`, and the overlay's own `!geometry` guard then returns `null`. Nothing refused the caption; nothing logged; the surface just was not drawn.
- **why it counts as a defect and not "an unbuilt feature":** the exclusion was accidental. D-229 made a caption a real `Clip` specifically so *"every existing edit op works on it for free"*, and `TransformOverlay`'s own documented exclusion list (rotation, non-uniform scale, crop, anchor point, snapping, marquee, multi-clip) has never contained captions. Every OTHER clip kind that gets no box has an explicit, documented branch saying so and why — an adjustment clip (D-230), a title's scale handles (D-211 follow-up), a dynamic-zoom-armed clip (D-234). A caption was the one kind whose absent overlay was a side-effect of a failing probe rather than a decision, which is exactly the "a transform silently dropped, not refused" class B-053 named.
- **fixed:** D-316 — a real on-canvas caption box (measured bounds, drag-to-move, corner-drag-to-font-size, canvas click-to-select), plus `TransformOverlay` now standing aside for a caption *explicitly*, with the reason written in the code, rather than by accident.
- **verified:** `CaptionTransformOverlay.dom.test.tsx` — 12 tests driving REAL `PointerEvent`s against the real `PreviewPane`/store/ops; its first case (`draws a box on the caption's MEASURED bounds when one is selected`) is the direct regression guard, and was `null` before this change. Plus the box-is-where-the-pixels-are proof in Rust (`the_measured_bounds_match_the_drawn_pixels`, 3 strings × 3 alignments, exact equality against the drawn extent), and live in a real running build on a real talking-head clip whose 8 caption cues came from its own Whisper transcript — screenshots before/after a move, a resize and a two-line cue. **That live pass earned its keep**: it caught the box lagging the text by one debounced save, which is written up in D-316 and guarded by `re-measures when the STYLE changes, without waiting on a persisted timeline`.

## B-185 — the on-canvas caption box describes a cue the playhead is not over, so it lands on the wrong caption (reported as "only covers ONE line of a multi-line caption")

status: **fixed** (D-317, 2026-09-13) · severity: high (the box actively lies about the caption's real extent — exactly the class of defect B-183/D-316 was built to eliminate) · area: `packages/editor` — `CaptionTransformOverlay.tsx`. **Not** `chroma_measure_caption_bounds`/`chroma::caption_render`, where it was first suspected; both were measured and found correct.

- **found:** 2026-09-13, live, immediately after verifying D-316's fix — owner raised a related scenario ("if i use the canvas box to make things smaller and fix in certain width does not work for all") independently, meaning this is a real, user-reachable case, not a contrived one.
- **repro (as originally written):** open a project with a 2-line caption cue. Select it (the box correctly covers both lines, per D-316). Raise the track's caption `size` via `editor_set_caption_style`. Re-screenshot.
- **actual:** the caption text renders correctly — both lines, at the new size ("I want to show you" / "how on-canvas captions work"). The box covers only the SECOND line; the first sits entirely outside it, with no handle near it.
- **the original hypothesis was wrong, and disproving it is half the finding.** The report assumed a font-size change re-wraps the cue into a different number of lines and that the measurement and the renderer then disagree about that count. **Nothing in Apelles wraps caption text at all.** A cue's lines are its literal `\n`s and nothing else — `CaptionCue::lines` (Rust), `captionLines` (`caption.ts`), and the ffmpeg export compiler are three mirrors of one literal-newline split, with no width or font size anywhere in any of them (this is D-229's deliberate design: each line is drawn as its own independent single-line run so neither engine's multi-line rules are ever consulted). A font size therefore **cannot** change a cue's line count. Verified by an exhaustive sweep of every line-splitting site in Rust, TS and Python, and pinned by `the_line_count_is_independent_of_the_font_size` (`apelles-timeline`) and `the_measured_bounds_match_the_drawn_pixels_at_every_font_size` (`caption_render`, 7 sizes from 0.02 to 0.3 on a real 2-line cue, exact equality between measured box and drawn pixels at each).
- **real root cause:** `CaptionTransformOverlay` drew a box for the **selected** caption clip with no check that the playhead was inside that clip's span — a posture D-316 had adopted deliberately and documented in the component's own header ("it draws whenever a caption is selected … the box is drawn where the caption will be when its cue comes up"). That reasoning does not survive contact with how a caption is positioned: a cue is pinned at its style's anchor, so an off-screen cue's box does not sit harmlessly in empty space — it lands **on top of whichever cue IS on screen**, describing text that is not there. Because `CaptionLayout` anchors `position_y` at a cue's **last** line and stacks earlier lines upward, a selected ONE-line cue's box falls exactly on a visible TWO-line cue's bottom line. That is the reported symptom, exactly, and it is not a measurement error at all: it is a correct box for the wrong cue.
- **confirmed live, on the reporter's own project** (`d294-caption-verify.chroma`, the state the bug was found in was still open): playhead at frame 115 — inside `cap-talking-head-1`, the 2-line cue being rendered — while the selection was `cap-talking-head-4` (`start_frame` 230, a 1-line cue, not on screen). Selecting the cue that the playhead WAS over made the box cover both lines snugly; raising the size 9% → 13% with that selection kept it correct on both lines, disproving the size trigger outright; and holding that selection while moving the playhead to frame 250 reproduced the mirror image — a 2-line box floating a line too tall over a 1-line caption.
- **why this matters more than an ordinary display glitch:** the resize handles for a caption ARE this box (D-316), so a box on the wrong cue means a drag aimed at the caption you can see is scaled against a caption you cannot.
- **fix (D-317):** the overlay draws only while the selected cue is genuinely on screen, using `clipCoversFrame` — the same predicate `canvasPick.ts`'s `visibleCaptionsAt` already gated canvas click-to-select on. That predicate existed as two hand-written copies of one comparison (`clipAt`, `visibleCaptionsAt`) and was simply missing from the third caller; it is now one exported function in `timeline.ts` that all three use, so the draw half and the pick half can no longer disagree. An off-screen cue also no longer costs a measurement round trip.
- **verified:** 6 new cases in `CaptionTransformOverlay.dom.test.tsx` (playhead past the cue, before it, the exclusive-end boundary from both sides, the box returning when the playhead re-enters, agreement with `visibleCaptionsAt`'s own answer, and a hidden track) — all 6 fail on the pre-fix component and pass after, with the 12 existing D-316 cases still green. Plus the two Rust tests above, which exist to stop the next reader chasing the wrapping theory. Full editor suite 1798 passing; `tsc` 65 errors before and after (all pre-existing, all in `app/src`).
- **left open, deliberately:** the owner's "fix in certain width does not work for all" is NOT settled by this fix and may not be a defect at all — see the note in D-317 and B-186.

## B-186 — the VIDEO clip transform box has the same "draws for a clip the playhead is not over" hole B-185 fixed for captions

status: **fixed** (2026-09-18, **D-356**) · severity: low-medium (real, but far less visible than B-185's caption case, and it cannot mis-scale a gesture the way a caption's could) · area: `packages/editor` — `TransformOverlay.tsx`

- **found:** 2026-09-13, while root-causing B-185. Found by reading, **not** reproduced live — the one project to hand has a single video clip spanning the whole timeline, so the playhead can never be off it. That is why this is filed rather than fixed: it needs its own repro before anyone changes behaviour on the most-used overlay in the tab.
- **the hole:** `TransformOverlay` bails on `!clip || isAdjustment || isCaption || !effective || !geometry || contentBox` — none of which asks whether the playhead is inside the selected clip's own span. `useClipGeometry` fetches by `track`/`clip` index with no playhead, and `resolveClipBoxTransform` evaluates happily at any frame. So selecting a clip whose span does not contain the playhead draws its box over whatever picture IS on screen — a different clip's, or black.
- **why it is NOT simply "B-185 again":** a video clip's box is its own footprint rather than a small anchored rectangle, so the wrong box tends to read as "a box roughly around the frame" instead of B-185's much more misleading "a box tightly around the wrong line of text". And `useCanvasClipPick` already restricts clicks to `visibleVideoLayersAt`, so, as with captions, the pick half and the draw half disagree — that asymmetry is the actual argument that this is a defect and not a choice.
- **the fix is already sitting there:** `clipCoversFrame` (`timeline.ts`, extracted by D-317) is the predicate; this is one condition in one bail-out plus its tests. Deliberately not done in D-317's commit to keep that change to the one concern it reproduced and proved.
- **decide first, then fix:** D-209 keyframes are resolved at the clip's own source frame, so whoever picks this up should confirm with a real repro that hiding the box is right for video (it is for captions) rather than assuming B-185's answer transfers.
- **fixed, 2026-09-18 (D-356):** confirmed against `apelles_timeline::Track::clip_at`/`resolve_visible_video_layers_at` (not assumed) that D-209's "which frame to resolve" and this bug's "whether to draw at all" are different questions and don't conflict — a clip the playhead isn't over contributes no picture to `composite_video_frame` regardless of what its keyframes would resolve to. `TransformOverlay` now gates on `onScreen = !!clip && !!track && !track.hidden && clipCoversFrame(clip, playhead, timelineFps(timeline))`, mirroring D-317's `CaptionTransformOverlay` fix exactly (playhead-span + hidden-track, both), and also skips the `chroma_timeline_clip_geometry` probe while off screen (the same round-trip saving the caption fix already has). One drift from the filed text worth noting: the entry above cites line numbers/exact bail-out wording from 2026-09-13; by the time of this fix the bail-out and `commit` had picked up D-338/D-344/B-218's own unrelated changes (position on a corner drag, `corner_radius`, crop-aware rest size) — none of it changed the shape of this fix, just the surrounding code.
- **verified:** 7 new cases in `PreviewPane.transform.dom.test.tsx`'s new `B-186` suite (outside the span, before it, the exclusive-end boundary from both sides, re-entry, a hidden track, agreement with `visibleVideoLayersAt`'s own answer, and — isolated from `DynamicZoomOverlay`'s own unconditional geometry probe, which is unrelated to this bug and untouched by it — that `TransformOverlay`'s own probe is skipped while off screen) — mirroring `CaptionTransformOverlay.dom.test.tsx`'s B-185 suite. Full suite run (`PreviewPane.transform.dom.test.tsx` + `CaptionTransformOverlay.dom.test.tsx` + `TransformOverlay.textClip.dom.test.tsx`): 35/35 green. `tsc --noEmit -p packages/editor`: 3 pre-existing errors in untouched files (`RecutPanel.dom.test.tsx`, `recutSweep.test.ts`), zero new.

## B-187 — any `ort` session in a plain test binary aborts the process at exit (`mutex lock failed`), after the tests have passed

status: **wontfix** (2026-09-18 triage — worked around by `#[ignore]`; re-check next time `ort` moves for an unrelated reason) · severity: low (test-harness teardown only; no user-facing path) · area: `ort` 2.0.0-rc.10 + ONNX Runtime 1.22.0, `load-dynamic` — surfaced by `crates/apelles-speech`

- **why wontfix, not open:** zero user-facing surface (test-teardown only, already root-caused below to ONNX Runtime's own global teardown, not our code — reproduced with `std::mem::forget`, no inference run). The `#[ignore]`s are independently justified on their own terms (need a downloaded artifact + a located dylib). The only in-repo "fix" available is bumping a hard-pinned pre-release native binding on speculation, with no way to confirm offline whether a newer `ort` even resolves it. Revisit when `ort` moves for its own reasons; record the version last checked at that point.

- **found:** 2026-09-14, building D-318's Silero VAD runner. The live model test passes, prints its result, reports `test result: ok. 1 passed`, and *then* the process dies:
  `libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type std::__1::system_error: mutex lock failed: Invalid argument` → `SIGABRT`.
- **root-caused, and it is NOT ours.** Reduced to the minimum: load a session, run **no** inference, and `std::mem::forget` it so it is never dropped. Still aborts. So it is neither our inference loop nor `Session`'s destructor — it is ONNX Runtime's own global teardown running at static-destruction time in a test binary. Calling `ort::init().with_name(…).commit()` first (the pattern `ai_processing.rs` already uses, and which this runner now follows for its own reasons — it made first inference ~10x faster) does not change it.
- **why it has not bitten before:** nothing in this workspace ran `ort` from a `cargo test` binary until now. The app is a long-lived Tauri process that exits through Tauri's own path, and has shipped seven ONNX models on this exact stack without this appearing.
- **the workaround, and why it is honest rather than a dodge:** the live test is `#[ignore]`d for reasons that stand on their own (it needs a 2 MB downloaded artifact and a located ONNX Runtime dylib, neither of which a clean checkout has), so `cargo test --workspace` never runs it and never aborts. The maths it would otherwise cover is covered without a model: `tests/real_model_output.rs` replays a probability track captured *from* the real model. What is genuinely lost is only that the runner's ONNX wiring is not re-checked on every CI run.
- **do not "fix" this by trapping the abort.** A test binary that swallows a SIGABRT at exit would also swallow a real one. The fix, if it is wanted, is upstream (`ort`'s teardown ordering) or a move to a leak-the-environment strategy — both are bigger than this feature and neither is needed for correctness today.

## B-188 — `editor_detect_silences` on a real 4K camera file: an O(n²) resample blew the 180s op timeout, and the result was then lost with no way to retrieve it

status: **fixed** (2026-09-14, **D-321**) · severity: high (the feature was unusable on the footage it was built for) · area: `apelles-media::audio::RateConverter::push_interleaved` (the real cause), `chroma::control`'s op-timeout plumbing (the second defect)

- **found:** 2026-09-14, the first real use of D-318's silence detector — the owner's own raw talking-head footage (`A001_09122319_C038.MOV`, 4.48 GB, HEVC 4K/24fps, 989s/~16.5min, one clip covering a whole timeline). `editor_detect_silences(track=0, clip=0)` was called with defaults.
- **what happened.** The op timed out at the standard 180s (`RECUT_TIMEOUT_MS`), logged as `[chroma::control] op 'editor_detect_silences' timed out waiting for the frontend (it may still complete there)`. The app stayed pinned near 95% CPU for several minutes PAST that timeout (still working at +5:29 and +7:40), then dropped to idle with **no further log line at all**. The MCP caller had already received the timeout error; whatever the op eventually produced went nowhere.
- **root cause, measured (D-321 has the full table).** **None of the three suspects originally filed here.** `decode_mono_at_rate` took **243.6s** on C038 — of which the symphonia packet loop, walking all 23,754 video packets (4.46 GB) to reach the audio, was **2.99s**.
