The other ~240s was the **resample**: `RateConverter::push_interleaved` is a *streaming* helper (written for playback, which pushes one packet at a time) whose per-chunk `acc[c].drain(0..chunk_frames)` memmoves the entire unconsumed tail. D-318's `decode_mono_at_rate` pushes a whole clip in ONE call, making that line quadratic in clip length — 47.5M frames ⇒ ~10¹² sample moves. Confirmed by its scaling: 100s→1.4s, 200s→4.9s, 400s→24.3s, 800s→174.8s.
- **the three originally-suspected causes, all ruled out by measurement.** (1) `next_packet()` walking past video packets: real, but 2.46s, not minutes. (2) debug-build overhead: this workspace's `[profile.dev]` is already `opt-level = 2`, so the unoptimized build hypothesised here does not exist — every number above IS the dev profile. (3) per-window ONNX/`Tensor::from_array` overhead: 5.0s for 30,922 windows, matching D-319's own benchmark. None was changed.
- **fixed:** a cursor + a single reclaim per call, replacing the per-chunk drain (and borrowed slices instead of a per-chunk `to_vec`). `decode_mono_at_rate` on C038: **243.6s → 4.9s**; on C040 (686s): **169.5s → 3.0s**. Output is unchanged — the VAD scores bit-identically either way (14393/30922 speech windows on C038, 9586/21448 on C040). End to end (decode + VAD) that is **9.8s / 7.9s** in `dev` and **7.0s / 3.8s** in `release`, i.e. fixed for both the shipped app and the `tauri:dev` loop.
- **the second, distinct defect — also fixed.** A slow op's result was unrecoverable: `chroma::control`'s timeout path had no way to retrieve a late result, and D-318's tools deliberately did not follow `editor_get_transcript`/`_status`'s async-poll design because its benchmark said VAD was fast enough not to need one. Speed alone does not fix this (no measurement guarantees the *next* file finishes in time), so D-321 gave both detectors the same store-backed start-then-poll shape the transcript tools already use, plus `editor_detect_silences_status` / `editor_detect_retakes_status`. A finished-but-unpolled detection is now held, not discarded. `RECUT_TIMEOUT_MS` is deleted from both MCP servers as a result.

## B-189 — `ai-media` sidecar (mlx-whisper) leaks GPU/Metal memory per transcription job, unbounded, contradicting its own documented process-isolation design

status: **fixed** (2026-09-14, D-322) · severity: high (unbounded growth, contributed to 21GB/22.5GB system swap in one session) · area: `ai-media/server.py` (port 8766), mlx-whisper transcription path

- **found:** 2026-09-14, running two real transcriptions back-to-back (C038 ~16.5min, C040 ~11.4min audio) for D-318's retake detection, then noticed via Activity Monitor that "Python" was showing 5.87GB, then 11.18GB minutes later after the second transcription — the SAME process (PID confirmed identical both times) growing, not two different processes.
- **`ps`'s RSS metric is blind to this and reported the process as fine (~35-39MB) the entire time** — the leaked memory is 100% in the `IOAccelerator (graphics)` category (Metal/GPU-resident), confirmed via macOS's own `footprint` tool (the same accounting Activity Monitor uses):
  ```
  Python [6163]: Footprint: 11 GB
    11 GB  IOAccelerator (graphics)   — 6,847 regions
  ```
  Anyone diagnosing this with `ps`/`top` alone will conclude — wrongly — that the process is fine. `footprint <pid>` (or Activity Monitor's Memory tab, not CPU/RSS) is the only way to see it.
- **directly contradicts the module's own documented design.** `ai-media/server.py`'s header comment states plainly: *"No model weights are ever resident in this process... every model call is a subprocess (`transcribe.py` as a whole)... so the OS reclaims its multi-GB working set on exit. That is deliberate: `ai/server.py` had to grow a TTL idle-unloader (D-084) because its lazily-loaded singletons never released weights, and this design makes that failure mode structurally impossible here rather than re-solving it."* The doc's premise — that subprocess isolation makes GPU memory reclaim structurally guaranteed — is false in practice: the LONG-LIVED PARENT uvicorn process itself is accumulating the GPU memory, not the short-lived subprocess. Either MLX's Metal allocator/IOAccelerator connection is being set up or shared at the parent level (so a child's GPU allocations get attributed back to it), or the "subprocess" isolation for GPU/Metal resources specifically doesn't behave the same as it does for ordinary heap memory. Not yet root-caused to the exact mechanism — needs an investigation into how `transcribe.py` is actually invoked (real subprocess with `subprocess.run`/`Popen`, vs. some form of in-process call) and whether MLX's Metal command queue/device handle is created once at parent startup and reused by "subprocess" calls that aren't truly separate OS processes for GPU purposes.
- **root cause (D-322): there was no subprocess.** The header comment describes a
  boundary the transcribe path never crossed. `ai-media/server.py:62` did
  `import transcribe as transcribe_mod`, and `:216` called
  `transcribe_mod.transcribe(...)` — an ordinary in-process function call, so
  `mlx_whisper` loaded its weights and allocated its Metal buffers inside the
  long-lived uvicorn process, where nothing ever exits to reclaim them. Nothing
  exotic about MLX's Metal context or about "subprocess isolation not applying
  to GPU resources" (both hypothesised above) turned out to be involved:
  `video_understand.py` really does spawn `sys.executable -m mlx_vlm.generate`
  and really does release everything; transcription simply never did the same
  thing. Reproduced from clean before touching anything — a fresh process at
  **10 MB** grew to **4,387 MB** (3,866 MB of it `IOAccelerator (graphics)`)
  after ONE 9-second in-process transcription, and stayed there.
- **fixed:** `transcribe.transcribe_subprocess()` runs `transcribe.py` as
  `__main__` through `sys.executable` — the sibling pattern already proven in
  this same file for the VLM — and `POST /transcribe` calls that. The HTTP
  contract, the transcript shape and the `_GPU` serialisation are unchanged;
  the subprocess result was compared against the in-process result for the same
  input and is **identical**. Verified with `footprint` on a real sidecar over
  real HTTP: the uvicorn parent sat at **47 MB with no `IOAccelerator` line at
  all** before, between and after two real transcriptions. `UserFacingError`
  crosses the new boundary as exit code 3 + a marked stderr line, so B-119's
  sentence still reaches the Edit tab verbatim (checked end to end against the
  running sidecar). `ai-media/test_transcribe_subprocess.py` covers the argv,
  the result round-trip, both error paths, the timeout, a real spawned child,
  and — the actual regression — that `POST /transcribe` reaches
  `transcribe_subprocess` and never `transcribe`.
- **for anyone diagnosing something similar:** `ps`/`top` cannot see this class
  of leak at all. Use `footprint <pid>`.
- **(pre-fix note) mitigation while it was open.** Restarting the sidecar process (kills and reclaims all of it; the app's `sidecar` supervisor module treats an already-running instance as external/unmanaged and will spawn a fresh one on next need, so this is safe and non-destructive to app state). Real fix needs the root-cause investigation above before choosing between: (a) verifying/fixing true OS-process isolation for the subprocess call so its Metal context genuinely dies with it, (b) explicitly releasing MLX's Metal memory pool after each job if the parent does hold it directly, or (c) as a fallback matching `ai/server.py`'s own precedent, giving this sidecar a TTL idle-unloader too (D-084) — despite the header comment's claim that this "makes that failure mode structurally impossible," it demonstrably has not.


## B-190 — audio goes permanently silent at the first cut of a ripple-deleted timeline, and only a stop/start brings it back

status: **fixed** (D-323, 2026-09-14) · severity: high (the recut workflow D-318/D-321 exists for is unusable with sound) · area: `apelles-media::audio::run_session`

- **found:** 2026-09-14, playing back two raw 4K HEVC talking-head clips after `editor_ripple_delete_ranges` removed ~95–155 silence/retake spans from each, leaving 60–96 tiny clips butted together with no gaps. Reported as *"it kinda stop getting voice, then I stop and start and it starts working"*.
- **the stop/start detail is the diagnosis.** A ring-buffer underrun self-heals within a chunk; this did not. The session was ending outright and idling silent with the device still open, and only `begin_request` tearing it down and building a new one restored sound.
- **root cause:** `run_session`'s mix loop broke out of `'mix` the first time `decoded.iter().all(is_done)`, and the timeline re-resolve that would have found the next clip runs on a *different clock* — every `RESOLVE_INTERVAL_SECS` (0.1 s ≈ 4.7 loop iterations at 1024 frames / 48 kHz), where exhaustion is noticed immediately. So ~4 iterations in 5, "everything is done" was decided against a resolve up to 100 ms of timeline stale, taken before the clip starting at that very frame existed. B-111 had put the resolve ahead of the check for exactly this reason but left the two on different schedules. Invisible on one long clip (nothing exhausts mid-playback); the steady state on a butted timeline, where each clip ends exactly as the next begins.
- **ruled out by measurement:** a synchronous open stalling the mix thread. `open_source` on the real 4.48 GB MOV costs **0.4–4.7 ms** and the first `take()` after it **96–148 ms** — against a ring buffer holding up to 2 s. Real work, but it cannot cause an audible dropout, let alone a permanent one. No audio prefetch was built; nothing measured asked for one.
- **fixed in D-323:** exhaustion forces a re-resolve at the current position before it is allowed to end the session. The same pass retires exhausted sources, which that fix would otherwise have made reachable — see D-323 and B-192.
- **regression test:** `audio_keeps_playing_across_ripple_cut_boundaries` (`app/src-tauri/src/chroma/audio.rs`) — a 24-clip butted timeline played through the real command surface, asserting `chroma_audio_level`'s peak stays non-zero past several boundaries. Before: `0.091, 0.091, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 …` from 2.4 s on. After: `0.089–0.094` throughout.

## B-192 — an audio session that runs dry inside a genuine timeline gap still ends for good

status: **fixed** (**D-357**, 2026-09-19) · severity: low (no reported occurrence; a ripple delete leaves no gaps by construction) · area: `apelles-media::audio::run_session`

- **found:** 2026-09-14, while fixing B-190 — stated rather than discovered, the same way B-111's own "known gap" note was.
- D-323 makes exhaustion force a re-resolve *at the current position* before ending the session, which is exactly right when the next clip starts at the very frame the last one ended (the reported case). It does not help when the next clip starts *later*: the forced resolve finds nothing at that frame, `run_session` has no way to know a clip is coming, and the session ends — so a timeline with a real silent gap between two audio clips plays the first and never the second.
- **why not fixed there:** the honest fix is for the loop to keep mixing silence and re-resolving until the timeline says there is nothing further, but `run_session` deliberately knows nothing about a timeline's length (`ResolveAt` was a frame → sources closure and nothing more), and the current terminal condition is also what triggers D-280's time-stretch tail flush. Getting that right is its own change with its own test, not a rider on B-190's.
- **narrower than it was.** Pre-D-323 this fired at every butted cut as well; now it is only the genuine-gap case.
- **confirmed before fixing, by reproduction rather than by reading.** The gap-timeline harness written for the fix (`GapTimeline`/`drive_mix`, `crates/apelles-media/src/audio.rs`) reproduces the symptom exactly when the resolver is given the pre-fix signal — clip A 0–1 s, a real one-second silence, clip B 2–3 s: the session ends at ~1.0 s and clip B's window measures digital `0.0` for its whole length. That reproduction is kept as `without_the_timelines_extent_a_gap_ends_the_session_which_is_the_bug`.
- **fixed in D-357:** `ResolveAt` returns `ResolvedAudio { sources, timeline_end_frame }` instead of a bare `Vec` (`crates/apelles-media/src/audio.rs:1872`/`:1905`), and the terminal condition is the pure `session_is_over(all_done, current_frame, timeline_end_frame)` (`audio.rs:3242`) — everything exhausted **and** the playhead at or past the timeline's end. Inside a gap the loop keeps going and mixes silence; `mix_chunk` over an emptied `OpenSources` is a full chunk of zeros, which is what keeps the clock advancing so the scheduled re-resolve reaches the clip after the gap. The number comes from `chroma::edit::timeline_fps_and_end_frame` (`app/src-tauri/src/chroma/edit.rs:647`), which is `Timeline::duration()` out of the same manifest read that already produced the fps, so the resolver costs no extra I/O.
- **D-280's tail flush was the real hazard, and was traced rather than assumed.** That flush runs after the `'mix` loop and its only "no more input is coming" signal is that the loop exited — so a terminal condition that could stay false forever would silently stop it firing and drop the last ~12 ms of *every* session, with nothing to notice. `session_is_over` is therefore written to be guaranteed-terminating: `timeline_end_frame` is fixed for a fixed timeline and `current_frame` only advances. Both directions of the exhaustion/frame-clock race are harmless under that — late costs nothing, early costs at most a chunk or two of extra mixed silence, which the stretch stage consumes as ordinary input and which therefore pushes the real audio *out* of it rather than stranding it. Verified, not reasoned: `a_speed_ramped_tail_at_the_real_end_still_reaches_d280s_flush` drives a clip with a real 2× D-242 ramp running to the genuine timeline end, through a real 2× D-280 `TimeStretch`, and asserts the session ends, the ramped clip is audible to 2.95 s, the stage emitted ~input/rate frames, and `flush()` still returns a non-empty tail.
- **`run_session`'s loop body moved into `advance_mix`** (`audio.rs:3849`) so that decision is testable at all — `run_session` opens a real `cpal` device on its own thread and cannot be. The split lands on D-280's own timeline/real-time seam: ring buffer, backpressure, the stretch stage and the generation checks all stayed in the caller. One behaviour change fell out of it, noted in D-357: the forced re-resolve no longer runs a second time in an iteration where the scheduled one already ran at the same frame (identical answer, and inside a gap `all_done` is true ≈47×/s).
- **regression tests:** `cargo test -p apelles-media` 203/203, `cargo test -p apelles --lib chroma::audio` 39/39 (D-323's own `audio_keeps_playing_across_ripple_cut_boundaries` still green). Six new tests plus the harness — see D-357 for the list.

## B-191 — every cut of a ripple-deleted timeline costs a full ffmpeg keyframe seek in the playback hot path (~300 ms, ~7 dropped frames)

status: **fixed** (D-324, 2026-09-14) · severity: high (playback of the recut output is unwatchable) · area: `apelles-media::decode_pipe`, `chroma::edit::timeline_frame_image`

- **found:** 2026-09-14, same session and same two files as B-190. Reported as *"FPS just lags like hell"* during playback and scrubbing of the recut timeline.
- **root cause:** `decode_pipe` (D-030) restarts its `ffmpeg` whenever the target frame goes backwards or more than `MAX_FORWARD_SKIP` (48) forward. A ripple-delete's boundaries are by construction large, arbitrary jumps in source-frame space — the next clip points at the same file thousands of frames from where the last one stopped — so **every** boundary is a forced respawn. With 95–155 of them inside one continuous playthrough, a path D-030's own doc called "no worse than today" under its stated assumption of rare scrubs became the steady state.
- **measured** (`A001_09122319_C038.MOV`, 4.48 GB HEVC 4K/24, decoding at the preview's 1280 px scale): sequential read **6.7 ms/frame**; a respawn **248–337 ms**, of which `Command::spawn` is only **0.8–1.0 ms**. The cost is ffmpeg's keyframe seek, not process creation and not decode throughput — which is why raising the skip threshold and why proxy media (D-030 option B, D-128) both fail to address it.
- **fixed in D-324:** the pipe for the upcoming clip is spawned and seeked ~0.5 s before the playhead reaches the cut, on the strength of the edit list the app already has, and adopted at the boundary. End to end through the real preview path at 24 fps pacing: **307.0 ms → 31.1 ms** at a cut (mid-clip 11.1 → 8.7 ms), i.e. inside one frame's 41.7 ms budget, so a cut no longer drops a frame.
- **regression tests:** see D-324 — the standby-adoption and no-leak suite in `decode_pipe.rs`, `playback_primes_the_upcoming_cut_and_a_scrub_does_not` and the env-gated `ripple_cut_playback_throughput` in `edit.rs`.
## B-193 — `chroma_project_save` silently wipes a project to empty if `load_manifest` fails for ANY reason, not just "doesn't exist yet" — real data destroyed live tonight

status: **fixed** (2026-09-15, **D-326**) · severity: **critical** (silent, irreversible destruction of a real edited project — no backup, no versioning, no warning) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/project.rs` (`chroma_project_save`, line ~517), `crates/apelles-project/src/manifest.rs` (`load_manifest`)

- **found:** 2026-09-15, live — the owner's `2026-09-12-c040` project (a real 96→61-clip silence/retake edit, ~330s of cut footage) was silently replaced with a brand-new, completely empty manifest (`shots: []`, one video track with `clips: []`) sometime during a session that involved: an app crash from severe system-wide memory pressure (`app exiting — killing sidecar pid 77010` in the app log), a restart, and an `open_project` MCP call that itself timed out (`op 'open_project' got no reply from the frontend within 20s`). The owner's reaction: *"what the fuck where is my clip ? gone which we edits?"*
- **root cause, confirmed by reading the code, not guessed:**
  ```rust
  // app/src-tauri/src/chroma/project.rs:517, inside chroma_project_save
  let mut manifest = load_manifest(&dir).unwrap_or_else(|_| {
      ProjectManifest::fresh(&dir.file_stem()...)
  });
  ```
  `load_manifest` (`crates/apelles-project/src/manifest.rs:1748`) returns a plain `Result<ProjectManifest, String>` with **no distinction whatsoever** between "project.json genuinely does not exist yet" (`std::fs::read_to_string` failing with `NotFound` — the ONLY case where falling back to a fresh manifest is correct) and every other failure mode: a transient I/O error, a race with a concurrent writer, a momentarily-truncated read during system memory pressure, a JSON parse failure, an unsupported/corrupt schema. `chroma_project_save` — called on **every debounced autosave tick**, per its own doc comment — treats all of these identically: "couldn't read it, so it must be new," and then calls `save_manifest`, **overwriting the real file with an empty one**, no error surfaced, no confirmation asked, nothing.
- **why this specific incident:** the timestamps on the destroyed `project.json` (`created: 2026-09-15T08:35:06Z`, i.e. 14:05:06 IST) line up almost exactly with an `open_project` call made during real environmental instability (the app had just crashed and restarted minutes earlier under severe memory pressure — swap nearly full, free RAM near zero). The exact transient failure `load_manifest` hit at that moment is not pinned down (a real read racing a concurrent write from the just-restarted app is the leading guess), but it does not need to be: **the bug is that ANY transient failure here is catastrophic**, regardless of what specifically caused this one.
- **recovered, this time, by luck rather than by design:** the coordinating agent had independently saved the exact silence/retake frame ranges used to build this project's cut to a local scratch file earlier in the session, and was able to re-import the source media and replay `editor_ripple_delete_ranges` with the identical saved ranges — verified byte-identical clip count/duration to the original. **This will not be true the next time this bug fires.** A project this destroys has no other recovery path: this app has no autosave versioning, no `.bak` rotation, and (confirmed live) no Time Machine configured on this machine at all.
- **fix (D-326, 2026-09-15)** — all four points below were carried out; point 3 turned out to be already done.
  1. **`load_manifest` now returns a typed `LoadManifestError`**, not a `String` (`crates/apelles-project/src/manifest.rs`). `NotFound` (the `read_to_string` failed with `io::ErrorKind::NotFound`) is a distinct variant from `Io` / `Parse` / `Schema` / `Shape`, and `is_not_found()` is the one predicate a caller may branch on. `Display` is byte-identical to the old strings — `packages/editor/src/timelineStore.test.ts` and the Edit tab's B-034 "No project open" handling key off `parse project.json: …` — and a `From<LoadManifestError> for String` keeps all ~90 `?` call sites compiling unchanged, so only the callers that genuinely must branch had to change.
  2. **`chroma_project_save` substitutes a fresh manifest only on `is_not_found()`** (`app/src-tauri/src/chroma/project.rs`). Every other failure returns `Err("refusing to save over <dir>: its project.json exists but could not be read (…). Your work on disk has NOT been modified…")` and writes nothing. A failed save the user can see beats a successful one that destroys their work.
  3. **`save_manifest` was already atomic** — temp-file-then-`rename`, landed by B-034/D-112 back on 2026-09-04; the bug report's point 3 was written without checking and is wrong on that. What was genuinely missing is the `fsync` that completes the pattern (without it `rename` can publish a file whose data blocks were never committed, so a power loss leaves `project.json` present but zero-length — worse than the old content). Added; the directory `fsync` deliberately not, see D-326 for the measured numbers and why.
  4. **Decided yes: a rolling `project.json.bak`** (D-326). Written before the new content is renamed into place, via `hard_link` (O(1), no data copy; `fs::copy` fallback), never via `rename(project.json → .bak)` — that would leave a window with no `project.json` at all, and a reader landing in it would see exactly the `NotFound` this bug turns into "must be a new project."
- **regression tests** (each confirmed to fail on the pre-fix code before being kept):
  - `chroma::project::tests::chroma_project_save_refuses_to_overwrite_an_unreadable_project_json` — writes a real truncated `project.json`, calls the real `chroma_project_save`, asserts both that it returns `Err` **and** that the on-disk bytes are unchanged. On the pre-fix code it returns `Ok(ProjectSaveDto{…})`, i.e. the silent wipe.
  - `chroma::project::tests::chroma_project_save_still_creates_a_fresh_manifest_when_there_is_none` — the one case that must keep working.
  - `manifest::tests::only_a_genuinely_absent_project_json_is_not_found` — all five failure modes (absent / truncated / zero-length / unsupported schema / wrong shape) classified.
  - `manifest::tests::load_manifest_error_messages_are_unchanged`, `save_manifest_keeps_the_previous_good_manifest_in_a_bak`, `save_manifest_writes_exactly_the_bytes_it_promises`.
- **the same class of bug exists elsewhere, now filed separately** — the D-326 audit swept every persisted-document read in the repo. The Apelles-native document layer is otherwise clean (`grade.json`, the motion scene manifest, both tab stores, and all ~20 other `load_manifest` call sites all propagate properly); `project.rs:517` was the single outlier. Five real instances were found in RapidRAW-inherited code and are filed as **B-194**, **B-195** and **B-196** below. They are deliberately NOT fixed in D-326's commit — different subsystems, different types, and mixing them in would have made a critical data-loss fix unreviewable.


## B-194 — a corrupt or briefly-unreadable `settings.json` is silently replaced with defaults on app boot, no user action required

status: **fixed** (2026-09-18) · severity: **high** (silent loss of the user's real app settings, on launch, with nothing to notice) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/app_settings.rs` (`load_settings`), `app/src/hooks/useAppInitialization.ts`, `app/src/store/useSettingsStore.ts`

- **found:** 2026-09-15, by the D-326 audit sweeping for B-193's exact shape (read a persisted document, swallow the error into a default, then write the default back over the real file). Found by code reading, not reported live — but it is the same mechanism and the same silent-overwrite outcome.
- **cause, Rust half:** `app_settings.rs:648` did `serde_json::from_str(&content).unwrap_or_default()`. The I/O half was safe (`?` on `read_to_string`), but a *parse* failure silently became `AppSettings::default()`. `settings_modified` was then guaranteed true — `is_first_migration` (L676) is `copy_paste_settings.known_adjustments.is_empty()`, which is true for a default — so the write at L702–704 (`let _ = fs::write(&path, json_string)`) put the defaults straight back over the user's real settings. The `let _` also hid the write's own failure.
- **cause, frontend half (independent, same file):** `useAppInitialization.ts:196–202` caught a failed `load_settings` and called `setAppSettings({ lastRootPath: null, theme: DEFAULT_THEME_ID, thumbnailSize: … })` — a three-field default object. The effect at L219–231 then fired automatically (`isInitialMount.current` is cleared in the `.finally()` that runs right after the catch) and persisted it via `useSettingsStore.ts:55` `invoke(SaveSettings, …)` ~500 ms later, unprompted.
- **fix, Rust half:** copied D-326's `LoadManifestError` shape verbatim onto a new `app_settings::LoadSettingsError` (`NotFound`/`Io`/`Parse`, `is_not_found()`, `From<LoadSettingsError> for String` so every existing `?` call site keeps compiling). `load_settings` now calls a new pure `read_settings_file(path: &Path)` — a direct `read_to_string` + `serde_json::from_str`, no `path.exists()` pre-check (same TOCTOU reasoning as `load_manifest`) — and only substitutes `AppSettings::default()` on `is_not_found()`; every other error (a real I/O failure or a corrupt/unparseable file) now propagates out of the `#[tauri::command]` instead of defaulting, so the migration-driven write-back can never fire over an unreadable file. `thiserror` (already a workspace dependency via `apelles-project`/`apelles-types`, pinned "2") is now also a direct dependency of `apelles` (`app/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`) for this — no new crate enters the build.
- **fix, frontend half:** `useAppInitialization.ts`'s `LoadSettings` catch no longer calls `setAppSettings` with a fabricated default object — `appSettings` stays `null` (its initial state), which is what every auto-persist effect in that file already gates on (`if (isInitialMount.current || !appSettings) return;`), so nothing gets written back. The failure is now a real, inspectable state instead: `useSettingsStore` gained `settingsLoadError: string | null` + `setSettingsLoadError` (mirrors `packages/editor/src/timelineStore.ts`'s `status`/`error` pattern, the established shape for "a load failed, and that's a first-class fact" in this codebase), and the catch also `toast.error(...)`s so the user sees it immediately, matching the existing `toast.error` idiom used throughout `app/src/hooks/*` for exactly this kind of invoke failure.
- **verified:** `cargo test -p apelles --lib app_settings` — 4 new tests: a missing file classifies `NotFound`; a truncated/invalid-JSON file classifies `Parse` (not `NotFound`) and is confirmed byte-for-byte untouched on disk after the failed read; a valid file still loads normally; an `io::Error` that isn't `NotFound` (read through a path whose parent is a file, not a directory) classifies `Io`. `cargo fmt`/`cargo clippy` clean on both changed files. Frontend: new `app/src/store/useSettingsStore.test.ts` (3 tests) plus the full `app` vitest suite (21 tests) green; `tsc --noEmit` clean (one now-unused `Theme` type import removed from `useAppInitialization.ts` as part of the same change).
- **not done here, deliberately:** no new full-screen "settings failed to load" UI (unlike `EditorTab.tsx`'s `status === 'error'` screen) — settings failing to load doesn't block the rest of the app from being usable (every consumer already reads `appSettings` through `?.` with sensible fallbacks), so a toast + inspectable store field was judged proportionate. B-195 (`load_sidecar`) and B-196 (`presets.json`) are the same anti-pattern in two other files and are being fixed separately; this pass did not touch `exif_processing.rs`, `file_management.rs`, `tagging.rs`, or `usePresets.ts`.

## B-195 — `load_sidecar` swallows both I/O and parse failures, and twelve read-modify-write call sites then write the defaulted sidecar back

status: **fixed** (2026-09-19) · severity: **high** (silent loss of a photo's tags, rating, colour label, EXIF and adjustments — on an ordinary save) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/exif_processing.rs` (`load_sidecar`), `app/src-tauri/src/file_management.rs`, `app/src-tauri/src/tagging.rs`, `app/src-tauri/src/export_processing.rs`, `app/src-tauri/src/image_loader.rs`

- **found:** 2026-09-15, by the D-326 audit. Code reading, not a live report.
- **cause:** `load_sidecar` returned `ImageMetadata` rather than a `Result`, and swallowed *both* failure modes — `let Ok(content) = fs::read_to_string(…) else { return ImageMetadata::default() }` (L181–183) and `serde_json::from_str::<ImageMetadata>(&content).unwrap_or_default()` (L185). Every caller is a read-modify-write: load the sidecar, change one field, write the whole struct back. So a transient read failure or a corrupt `.rrdata` erased everything the caller did not happen to be setting.
- **filed count corrected: twelve write-back sites, not eleven.** This entry's own title said eleven while the bullet below it enumerated twelve; re-counted against the code as it stood on 2026-09-19 and the enumeration was the right number. The real inventory at fix time was **15 `load_sidecar(…)` call expressions** — `file_management.rs` ×9 (L97, L419, L442, L1585, L1696, L1791, L1899, L1981, L2017), `tagging.rs` ×1 (L26), `export_processing.rs` ×3 (L1011, L1014, L1573), `image_loader.rs` ×1 (L902), and `exif_processing.rs` ×1 (L1508, inside `load_primary_metadata`) — resolving to **12 distinct read-modify-write sites** and **5 read-only consumers**. The two extra `file_management.rs` calls over the filed list are L419 and L442, which are the *same* site: `update_exif_fields` loaded the very same sidecar twice in one pass and defaulted both times. `load_primary_metadata`'s one call fans out to 3 of the 12 (`read_exif_data` L1584/1586, `persist_exif_if_missing` L1608/1611, `write_rrexif_sidecar` L1633/1635) plus 1 read-only use in `read_rrexif_sidecar`. The filed entry counted no read-only consumers at all; those are `export_processing.rs` ×3, `image_loader.rs` ×1, and that `read_rrexif_sidecar` use.
- **fix, the one function:** new `exif_processing::LoadSidecarError` (`NotFound`/`Io`/`Parse`, `is_not_found()`, `From<LoadSidecarError> for String`), copied from B-194's `LoadSettingsError`, itself copied from D-326's `LoadManifestError`. `load_sidecar` now returns `Result<ImageMetadata, LoadSidecarError>` and reads directly instead of `exists()`-then-reading, dropping the stat it used to race against. The policy every caller needs lives in exactly one place beside it — `load_sidecar_or_fresh`: *a missing sidecar may be defaulted and written; a sidecar that exists but failed to load may not.* The self-write at L197–198 (the bloated-EXIF auto-heal) is unchanged and was never an independent hazard: it can only run on a sidecar that parsed.
- **fix, the twelve write-back sites, by what each can honestly do about a failure.** Six propagate to the caller because their signature already returns `Result`: `save_metadata_and_update_thumbnail` (the main "save the user's edit" path), `load_metadata`, `tagging.rs`'s `modify_tags_for_path` (both its callers already log per path), `apply_auto_adjustments_to_paths` (its per-path body is already a `Result` closure whose `map_err` logs), `write_rrexif_sidecar`, and the `update_exif_fields`/`set_color_label_for_paths` pair — those last two run a `par_iter` over many paths, so they now skip *only* the paths whose sidecar is unreadable, finish the rest of the batch, and return one aggregated error naming what was skipped. Three more are batch `par_iter` bodies that continue into thumbnail work and cannot abort cleanly, so they `log::error!` and skip that one path: `apply_adjustments_to_paths` (paste), `reset_adjustments_for_paths`, and `read_exif_data`/`persist_exif_if_missing` (which now also distinguish "no sidecar → write the EXIF to the `.rrcache` as before" from "a sidecar is there and broken → write nothing"). The last, `resolve_image_metadata`, is a grid-listing read whose XMP sync writes back: a real failure now degrades that one entry to unrated/untagged and writes nothing.
- **the 5 read-only consumers are no longer silently defaulted either.** All now go through `load_sidecar_or_fresh` and propagate: a corrupt sidecar at `export_processing.rs` L1011/L1014 used to mean *silently export the ungraded image*, at L1573 an estimate of the wrong image, and at `image_loader.rs` L902 *open the photo as if it had never been edited* — which then set up the user's next save to write that blank state back. `read_rrexif_sidecar` is the one deliberate exception: it is a pure EXIF cache lookup, so it logs the real failure and falls through to re-deriving the EXIF from the image bytes rather than failing.
- **the related `.rrcache` defect is fixed in the same pass, as this entry asked.** `load_rrcache_for_folder` defaulted an unreadable or corrupt `.rrcache` to an empty map that `save_exif_to_rrcache` then marked dirty and `flush_all_dirty_caches` wrote over the real file, dropping every *other* image's cached EXIF in that folder. The read is now classified by the same `LoadSidecarError` (new `read_rrcache_file`); absent still means an empty map, and anything else adds the folder to a new `ExifCacheState::poisoned` set that both the save and the flush refuse to write for. Degradation only — re-derivable from the image bytes — which is why "no cache for this folder this session" is the right answer rather than a hard failure.
- **verified:** `cargo test -p apelles --lib` green, 10 new tests. Mirroring B-194's shapes: a missing sidecar classifies `NotFound`; a truncated one classifies `Parse`, not `NotFound`, and is confirmed byte-for-byte untouched afterwards; a non-`NotFound` `io::Error` classifies `Io`; a valid sidecar still loads; `load_sidecar_or_fresh` defaults for absent and refuses for corrupt, and reading an absent sidecar does not create one. Plus real call-site regressions rather than only the classifier: `write_rrexif_sidecar` refuses an unreadable target sidecar and leaves its bytes intact (and still writes normally when the target has none yet), and `file_management`'s `resolve_image_metadata` leaves a corrupt `.rrdata` byte-for-byte intact when a valid `.xmp` beside it would previously have been merged into a default and written straight over it (with the "no sidecar yet + an XMP" case pinned alongside it, since that one *must* still create the sidecar). The `.rrcache` classifier has its own test. `cargo fmt` + `cargo clippy` clean on all five changed files.

## B-196 — a failed `presets.json` read empties the preset list in memory, and the next preset edit writes the empty list back

status: **fixed** (2026-09-18) · severity: **medium** (total loss of the user's preset library, but needs one user action rather than firing on boot) · area: `app/src/hooks/usePresets.ts`

- **found:** 2026-09-15, by the D-326 audit. Code reading, not a live report.
- **cause:** the `catch` in `loadPresets` did `setPresets([])` on any load failure. The Rust `load_presets` (`file_management.rs:2044–2050`) correctly propagates both I/O and parse errors — reconfirmed while fixing this, still true — so a corrupt or briefly-unreadable `presets.json` reached this catch and emptied the in-memory library. `savePresetsToBackend`'s debounced body then wrote that empty list plus whatever the user just did. The filed count of call sites ("twelve") had drifted from the real code by the time this was fixed: there are **eleven** (`addPreset`, `addFolder`, `deleteItem`, `renameItem`, `configurePreset`, `overwritePreset`, `duplicatePreset`, `movePreset`, `reorderItems` ×2 branches, `sortAllPresetsAlphabetically`).
- **not automatic**, unlike B-194: it needs the user to add, rename or reorder a preset while the list is wrongly empty. When that happens it is total loss.
- **fix:** `usePresets.ts` now carries an explicit `PresetsLoadStatus` (`'idle' | 'loading' | 'ready' | 'error'`), mirroring `packages/editor/src/timelineStore.ts`'s `TimelineLoadStatus` (B-034/D-112) — the sibling pattern this was modelled on: the status says only what the *read* is doing, and is never inferred from the data it left behind. `loadPresets`'s catch no longer clears `presets` at all — it keeps whatever was already in memory (the last known-good load, or the pre-first-load `[]`) and sets `loadStatus: 'error'` plus a real `loadError` message. All three import paths (`importPresetsFromFile`/`importLegacyPresetsFromFile`/`importPresetsFromFiles`) mark `loadStatus: 'ready'` on success too, since the Rust side re-reads+merges+saves and hands back the true on-disk list — a confirmed-good state, including recovery from a prior `'error'`. `savePresetsToBackend`'s debounced body (not each call site — `lodash.debounce` can fire well after the call that scheduled it) now checks a `loadStatusRef` and refuses to call `invoke(Invokes.SavePresets, ...)` unless `loadStatus === 'ready'`, logging why instead. Both `loadStatus`/`loadError` are exposed from the hook's return value for a future consumer (e.g. `PresetsPanel.tsx`, which today can't tell a failed read apart from a genuinely empty library either — left as-is, out of this bug's scope).
- **verification:** `app/src/hooks/usePresets.dom.test.ts` (new, jsdom via per-file `@vitest-environment` pragma — the `app` workspace's vitest defaults to `environment: 'node'`) drives the real hook with a mocked `invoke`: (1) a failed initial load followed by `addPreset` never calls `invoke('save_presets', ...)` even after the 500ms debounce elapses; (2) a successful load followed by `addPreset` DOES persist, proving the gate doesn't block legitimate saves; (3) a successful load, then a failed refresh, keeps the previously-loaded presets in memory (not cleared to `[]`) and still refuses to persist. All three pass. `tsc --noEmit` on `app/`: same 65 pre-existing errors as the baseline, none in `usePresets.ts` or its consumers — zero new errors.

## B-214 — `emphasis`'s `ring` preset draws a fully opaque ring for the whole scene BEFORE its own `at`

status: **fixed** (2026-09-17) · severity: medium (wrong pixels in shipped output — a stray graphic parked on screen pointing at nothing, in a scene that had already been reviewed and approved; no crash, no data loss) · area: `packages/motion-engine/src/primitives/Emphasis.tsx`, the `preset: "ring"` branch

- **found:** 2026-09-17, building `c040-recap`. Two rings scheduled at `at: 8.6` and `at: 10.2` were visible at `t = 3.4`, sitting on top of an unrelated layer.
- **cause:** the branch computed `opacity` as `outAt(frame, start + dur*0.4, start + dur)` and nothing else. `outAt` is `interpolate(..., {extrapolateLeft: "clamp"})`, so for every frame BEFORE its range it returns `1`, not `0`. Radius came from `inAt(...)`, which correctly clamps to `0` on the left — so the net effect was a ring at 60% of its final size, at **full opacity**, from frame 0 of the scene until its `at`. (After `start + dur` the maths does reach `0`, so the trailing half was invisible and only the leading half ever showed.)
- **why it survived review:** the two other presets behave correctly and hid the asymmetry — `pulse`/`glow` gate on an `active` boolean the file already computes, and `scribble` gates on `lifetime()`, which clamps both ends. `ring` was the only one reading a raw `outAt`. It was also *less visible* before 2026-09-17: every `ring` in this project carried an explicit blue `#5b8def`, which reads as near-background on the dark ground. The `apelles-studio` theme pass removed those explicit colours so the rings inherit the ochre accent — at which point the stray ones were impossible to miss. **The defect is older than that pass; the pass only exposed it.**
- **confirmed in shipped output, not just theory:** `c040-whatisattention.mp4` at `t = 1.0` shows two ochre rings floating in empty space. Their `at` values are `4.4` and `7.2`, and the words they circle do not appear until `1.5`.
- **fix:** `if (!active) return null;` at the top of the `ring` branch — `active` (`local >= 0 && local <= dur`) is already computed above for `pulse`/`glow` and is exactly the intended window, so every in-window frame is byte-unchanged and only the out-of-window draw is removed.
- **blast radius:** every existing `ring` in every manifest loses a stray graphic it was never meant to show. That is a look change, and a deliberate one — there is no manifest that wants a ring before its own start time.

## B-213 — `motion_set_layer_size` on a `matrix` writes `cell = w / cols`, while `motion_list_primitives` describes `w` AS the cell

status: **fixed**, 2026-09-18 · severity: low (wrong size, immediately visible, trivially worked around) · area: `packages/motion/src/propCatalog.ts`'s `sizeFields('matrix')` (~L423), cross-checked against `packages/motion/src/manifestEdit.ts`'s `setLayerSize`/`layerWorldSize` `'scalar'` branches (~L512–521, ~L585–593)

- **found:** 2026-09-17, building the `c040` motion-graphics set. `motion_set_layer_size(w=62, h=62)` on a 7-column `matrix` stored `cell: 8` (≈ 62/7), so the grid rendered at roughly a ninth of the intended size and read as a small smudge rather than a diagram.
- **why it is a contract bug, not just a surprise:** `motion_list_primitives` reports `matrix`'s size as `{key: "cell", kind: "scalar"}` — i.e. "the resizable field IS `cell`". An agent reading that reference (which is exactly what it is for) computes a cell size and passes it as `w`. The op instead treats `w` as the grid's TOTAL width and divides. Both readings are defensible; only one is written down, and it is not the one implemented.
- **workaround used:** set `cell` directly with `motion_set_layer_field`, which is unambiguous.
- **verified before fixing, not assumed:** a THIRD surface, `motion_list_layers` (`layerWorldSize`'s own `'scalar'` branch, `manifestEdit.ts` ~L512–521), already reports a `matrix` layer's `size` as the same TOTAL footprint the op reads/writes (`w = cols*(cell+gap)-gap`, `h = rows*(cell+gap)-gap` — `Matrix.tsx`'s own formula) — so the op and `motion_list_layers` were already the majority-agreeing pair, and `motion_list_primitives`' catalog description was the outlier, as suspected going in.
- **the "different conventions" claim, checked, not assumed:** `text`/`deviceframe` genuinely use two MORE conventions, confirmed by reading both branches directly, not touched by this fix:
  - `text` (`kind: 'w-only', key: 'maxWidth'`) — `setLayerSize`'s w-only branch (`manifestEdit.ts` ~L609) writes `raw.maxWidth = W` **verbatim**, no derivation at all.
  - `deviceframe` (`kind: 'scale', key: 'scale'`) — a genuine third convention: the op (~L602–604) computes a **ratio** to the device model's fixed intrinsic body size (`(W/body.width + H/body.height) / 2`), not a footprint-to-count division and not a direct passthrough.
  - Neither was in scope to change (this fix is `matrix`-only, and B-225 was working `Graph.tsx`/`graph` in parallel) — recorded here so the next person doesn't have to re-verify it.
- **fix:** kept the op's arithmetic (`matrix`'s `w`/`h` = TOTAL footprint) since it already agreed with `motion_list_layers` — changing that would have flipped the majority-correct surface to match the minority-wrong one. Instead, `sizeFields`'s `SizeKind` type gained an optional `note?: string` (`propCatalog.ts`), populated only for `matrix`, stating in plain language that `w`/`h` are the grid's TOTAL footprint, matching `motion_list_layers`, NOT the per-cell size — surfaced verbatim through `motion_list_primitives`'s `size` field, so the ambiguity that produced this bug's original misread no longer has to be inferred from `{kind: "scalar", key: "cell"}` alone.
- **verification:** `packages/motion/src/motionOps.test.ts`'s new `B-213` test builds a `matrix` layer via `motion_add_layer`, resizes it via `motion_set_layer_size`, and asserts `motion_list_layers`' reported `size`, `manifestEdit.ts`'s own `layerWorldSize`, and `motion_list_primitives`' catalog `size` (including the new `note`) all agree on the same (578, 382) TOTAL-footprint reading — not the 88px `cell`. Full `@apelles/motion` suite (761 tests) and `tsc --noEmit -p packages/motion/tsconfig.json` both clean.

## B-212 — `emphasis`'s `pulse` and `glow` presets render NOTHING from a manifest: both are children-only wrappers, and a manifest layer has no children

status: **fixed** (2026-09-18) · severity: medium (two of four documented presets are silently inert from the one authoring surface that matters; no error, no warning, just an invisible layer) · area: `packages/motion-engine/src/primitives/Emphasis.tsx` (the `pulse` and `glow` branches, then ~L51–72, now ~L59–118)

- **found:** 2026-09-17, building the `c040` motion-graphics set — a `glow` layer authored to be a moving spotlight rendered as nothing at all.
- **cause:** `pulse` returns `<div style={{transform: scale(...)}}>{children}</div>` and `glow` returns `<div style={{filter: drop-shadow(...)}}>{children}</div>`. Both decorate `children` and draw nothing themselves. `ring` and `scribble`, by contrast, draw their own SVG from `box` and work fine. A manifest layer is constructed by `registry.ts`'s adapter from JSON props only — there is no way to give a primitive `children` from a manifest — so `pulse` and `glow` are reachable only from hand-written React (the `compositions/` demos), never from the scene manifest.
- **why it is not caught:** `motion_list_primitives` advertises all four presets for `emphasis` with no note, and `motion_set_layer_field` accepts `preset: "glow"` without a warning because it IS a legal enum value. The layer then renders an empty `div`.
- **workaround used (superseded by the fix below):** `ring` (an expanding ping — note it draws a CIRCLE of radius `max(w,h)*0.55`, ignoring the box's aspect) and `scribble` (a hand-drawn ellipse `w*1.18 × h*1.5` around the box) carried every emphasis beat in the `c040` set.
- **fix:** took the first of the two options this entry originally listed — `pulse`/`glow` now derive a `box`-driven self-drawn shape, the same pattern `ring`/`scribble` already used, rather than dropping them from the preset enum (which would have meant touching both MCP surfaces' schemas and `crates/apelles-mcp/tests/golden/corpus.json` for a rendering-only bug). Concretely: the `if (!box) return null` / `cx`,`cy` centre computation that only `ring`/`scribble` used to reach now runs for all four presets before the branch on `preset`, and `pulse`/`glow` each draw a `roughEllipse` around `box`, marked `data-motion-box` like their siblings — `pulse` sizes it by the original scale-bob factor `s` instead of scaling a (nonexistent) child, `glow` keeps the exact original breathing formula (`12 + g * 22`px blur) as a `drop-shadow` filter on the drawn ellipse instead of on an empty wrapper. Both are now gated on `active` (`local >= 0 && local <= dur`, matching B-214's `ring` fix) rather than persisting a static `s = 1` state outside their window. The `children` prop is removed from `Emphasis`'s type entirely — nothing in the codebase passed it (`compositions/PrimitivesDemo.tsx` only ever exercised `scribble`), so there was no real caller to preserve backward compatibility for.
- **verified:** new `packages/motion-engine/src/primitives/Emphasis.dom.test.tsx` renders a manifest `emphasis` layer through the REAL path — `registry.ts`'s own `emphasis` adapter feeding the real `Emphasis` component with no `children`, exactly what `Video.tsx` does (`<C {...props} />`, self-closing) — and asserts `pulse`/`glow` produce a real `<svg><path data-motion-box d="...">` with non-empty `d`, not the pre-fix empty `<div>`; plus a gating check (nothing drawn outside `[start, start+dur]`) and a sanity check that `ring`/`scribble` still draw (proving the harness itself, not just the fix). `packages/motion-engine` had no test runner at all before this — added `vitest` + `@testing-library/react` + `jsdom` as devDependencies (already-adopted repo-wide tools, same versions `@apelles/player` pins) and a `test` script, matching the monorepo's existing `*.dom.test.tsx` convention. 4/4 new tests pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean on `packages/motion-engine`; full `packages/motion` suite still 760/760 (no other package renders this primitive).

## B-221 — `editor_remove_clip` silently removes the OTHER half of an A/V link group too, and its docstring says nothing about it — so "remove both halves" deletes a neighbouring clip instead

status: **fixed** (2026-09-19) · severity: **high** (silent data loss on a normal-looking sequence of two documented calls; only caught because the caller re-read the timeline immediately afterwards) · area: the Edit tab's remove op / `editor_remove_clip`'s own contract — the propagation itself is arguably correct behaviour for a link group, the defect is that nothing says so

- **found:** 2026-09-17, `2026-09-12-c040-mgfx-recut`, replacing one Motion-overlay clip that existed as a linked video/audio pair (track 1 clip 7 + track 3 clip 7, same `linkGroup`).
- **repro, exactly as hit:**
  1. `editor_remove_clip(track=1, clip=7)` → `{ok: true}`. This removed **both** the track-1 clip and its linked track-3 twin. Nothing in the response says a second clip was removed; nothing in the docstring says it can happen. (The docstring's whole text is "Remove one clip from the timeline, leaving a gap in its place.")
  2. `editor_remove_clip(track=3, clip=7)` → `{ok: true}`. Track 3's index 7 was by now the NEXT clip (`c040-payoff.mp4`), so this removed **that** — and, by the same undocumented propagation, its track-1 twin as well.
  - Net: two calls intended to remove one linked pair removed **two** linked pairs. `c040-payoff` was gone from both tracks with no error, no warning and no `removed:` list in either response.
- **why a caller writes that sequence:** every other Edit-tab op in this workflow is per-track and explicitly non-propagating — `editor_swap_clip_media`'s own docstring goes out of its way to say "the swap does NOT propagate to a linked clip." Having swap explicitly not propagate while remove silently does is the trap: the two tools sit next to each other, address clips identically, and disagree about link groups without saying so.
- **recovered:** `editor_add_clip(track=1, media_id=…, start_frame=5257, duration=435, at_index=8)`, which re-created the linked audio half automatically — verified against the pre-removal `start_frame`/`duration` and re-checked for overlaps across all four tracks.
- **fix, two parts:** (1) say it in the docstring — `editor_remove_clip` removes the clip AND every clip sharing its `linkGroup`, the same way the GUI's own delete does; (2) return what was actually removed (`removed: [{track, clip, id}]`) rather than a bare `{ok: true}`, so a caller can see the second deletion in the response instead of discovering it in a later read. A `propagate_links: false` opt-out would be the more complete fix but is not required to close the silent-loss part.
- **fixed, 2026-09-19.** Both MCP docstrings (`mcp/server.py` and `crates/apelles-mcp/src/tools/edit.rs`'s `editor_remove_clip`) now say plainly that removing a linked clip also removes its A/V partner, naming `editor_swap_clip_media`'s own docstring as the contrasting (does-NOT-propagate) case so the two are read together rather than assumed to agree. The `editor_remove_clip` handler in `packages/editor/src/useEditorControl.ts` now works out its intended targets the same way the reducer's own `remove` case groups them (`linkGroupMembers` on the clip's `link_group`, exported from `timeline.ts`), then diffs the timeline before/after the op and reports only the ids actually gone as `removed: [{track, clip, id}]` — so a locked-track refusal (D-129: the whole group is refused if any member's track is locked) reports an empty `removed` rather than a false positive, and an unlinked clip reports itself alone. The `removed` shape is additive (`ok`/`track` unchanged), so this is not a breaking response-shape change for an existing caller. `propagate_links: false` remains not built — still the more complete fix, still not required to close the silent-loss part this entry was filed for.
- **verification:** new `packages/editor/src/editorRemoveClip.dom.test.tsx`, at the real `chroma://request` op-dispatch layer (this repo's established pattern per `recutSweep.dom.test.tsx`'s own header) — three cases: removing one half of a linked pair reports both clips in `removed` and both are actually gone from the live timeline (checked across every track, since removing the audio track's only clip prunes that now-empty track per D-054/D-058); removing an unlinked clip reports itself alone; a locked-track refusal reports an empty `removed` while the clip stays put. `npx vitest run packages/editor/src/editorRemoveClip.dom.test.tsx` 3/3 passed; full `npx vitest run packages/editor packages/player` green (no regressions). `crates/apelles-mcp`'s parity corpus re-captured (`mcp/.venv/bin/python crates/apelles-mcp/parity/capture.py`) for the changed description text — `cargo test -p apelles-mcp --test parity` 5/5 passed, confirming the Rust docstring now matches Python's byte-for-byte. `tsc -p packages/editor` introduces zero new errors (the same 3 pre-existing `RecutPanel.dom.test.tsx`/`recutSweep.test.ts` fixture-typing errors B-227/D-349 already disclosed). `cargo fmt --check -p apelles-mcp` and `cargo clippy -p apelles-mcp --all-targets` clean.

## B-220 — `editor_trim_clip` with a NEGATIVE `delta` on `edge: "end"` collapsed a clip to 1 frame instead of extending it, and the next call to the same tool hard-errored and left the app with no project open

status: **half-fixed** (2026-09-18 — the arithmetic half is root-caused and fixed; the project-teardown half is still open and still unreproduced) · severity: **high** (the first half is silent, wrong-direction data loss; the second half drops the whole Edit session's project) · area: `packages/editor/src/timeline.ts` (`clampedTrimEndDuration`) and its Rust mirror `crates/apelles-timeline/src/lib.rs` (`clamped_trim_end_duration`) — the same op as B-215, a different and more destructive failure

- **found:** 2026-09-17, `2026-09-12-c040-mgfx-recut`, extending an overlay clip after its source render grew from 360 to 558 frames.
- **repro part 1 — wrong direction, silently:** `editor_trim_clip(track=1, clip=7, edge="end", delta=-198)` on `c040-recap.mp4` (`start_frame` 4601, `duration` 360, `source_len` 558, `source_fps` 30 on a 24 fps timeline). Per the tool's own docstring, "positive shortens the clip, negative extends it back into previously-trimmed source material (up to the source's own bounds)" — 558 frames of source were available, so the expected result was `duration` 558. Response: `{"ok": true, "result": {"ok": true, "track": 1}}`. Actual `duration` afterwards, read back from both `get_timeline` and the saved `project.json`: **1**. Not 360 (no-op), not 162 (`360 - 198`), not 558 (the ask) — **1**. The same call on track 3 produced the identical result, so it is deterministic, not a race.
- **repro part 2 — the next call takes the project down:** `editor_trim_clip(track=1, clip=7, edge="end", delta=-10)` against the now-1-frame clip returned a bare `Error executing tool editor_trim_clip` with no message. Immediately afterwards `editor_get_state` reported `projectOpen: false`, `hasTimeline: false`, `openProject: null`, `status: "idle"` — the Edit tab had dropped the project entirely. No data was lost (everything up to that point was already on disk; `open_project` restored it cleanly), but an op erroring should not close the user's project.
- **the B-215 connection, and what is new:** B-215 documents `editor_trim_clip(edge: "end")` silently NO-OPPING on clips that are the last on their track with a `source_fps` different from the timeline's. This clip shares the mixed-rate property (30 vs 24) but is **not** last on its track, the delta is **negative**, and the result is not a no-op — it is a collapse to a single frame. Both entries point at the same arithmetic (`timelineFramesToSource` on a clip whose native rate is not the project's, B-077's old ground), but they are different symptoms and this one destroys content rather than ignoring the request.
- **worked around, and the workaround is the useful part:** `editor_remove_clip` + `editor_add_clip(start_frame=…, source_start=0, duration=558, at_index=…)` places the clip at exactly the wanted length in one call and was verified by frame arithmetic. ~~Until this and B-215 are root-caused, **re-place a clip rather than trim it whenever the target length is known**~~ — **superseded 2026-09-18**: both are root-caused and the trim path no longer rewrites a duration nobody asked it to touch, so trimming is trustworthy again. Re-placing remains the right move for a clip that is ALREADY out of bounds (`duration` past its own `source_len`), which a trim now deliberately refuses to extend rather than truncate. Read B-221 first either way, because the remove half of that workaround has its own trap.
- **ROOT CAUSE of the arithmetic half, found 2026-09-18 by reading, and it is not the mixed-fps arithmetic either entry suspected.** `clampedTrimEndDuration` computed `clampInt(c.duration + deltaSource, 1, maxDur)` — it clamped the **absolute new duration** against `maxDur`, rather than bounding the DELTA. `maxDur` is a statement about where a trim may take the clip; it is not a fact about where the clip already is. So for any clip whose stored `duration` ALREADY exceeded `maxDur` — an inconsistent state no trim created — every trim, of any size and either direction, rewrote `duration` straight down to `maxDur` and silently discarded the entire pre-existing overhang. A 20-frame trim could destroy 100 frames; the reported 360 → 1 is the extreme form of exactly this, reached whenever `maxDur` itself evaluates to 1 (`maxDurPosition` is `max(nextStart - c.start_frame, 1)`, so a sibling clip at the same `start_frame` pins it at 1, and `maxDurSource` is `max(source_len - source_start, 1)`, so an unprobed/zero `source_len` does the same). Both are reachable on this exact project — B-226 documents the same Motion-overlay clips carrying durations derived from a 30 fps render against a 24.005 fps timeline, and B-219 documents their `source_path`s pointing at another project's renders, so a stale or wrong `source_len` on one of them is not hypothetical. **D-352 named this as B-220's real remaining defect and it is now fixed.**
- **the fix, and why this shape rather than a rejection or a truncation:** the upper bound is now `max(maxDur, c.duration)` in both engines. An op must never make an existing violation WORSE, and must never silently "repair" one by throwing away frames the caller did not ask to lose. So: a **shortening** trim still shortens by exactly the delta asked for (and may bring the clip back into bounds, which is progress, and still stops at the 1-frame floor like any other trim); a **lengthening** trim on an already-over-long clip clamps to the clip's current duration, changes nothing, and is refused by `checkTrim` with a reason that states the clip's duration, the room it actually has, which bound is the binding one, how many frames the old code would have discarded, and that re-placing the clip at the wanted length is the reliable fix. Blanket-rejecting every trim of an over-long clip was considered and rejected: shortening one is exactly what a user wants and is harmless. Truncating it to `maxDur` "to fix it" was rejected outright — that is the bug. The new expression is **identical to the old one for every in-bounds clip** (`max(maxDur, duration) === maxDur` whenever `duration <= maxDur`), so no well-formed timeline changes behaviour at all; a test pins that.
- **both engines moved together.** `crates/apelles-timeline/src/lib.rs`'s `clamped_trim_end_duration` carried the identical expression and got the identical fix, so the TS reducer and its Rust mirror still agree field for field. The Rust `trim_end`'s own `Result` already surfaces its other rejections as real errors (`TrackLocked`, `NoSuchClip`, `EmptyClip`, `LinkDesync`), and it has no MCP or app call path of its own — it is the reference model — so B-215's `checkTrim` has no Rust counterpart and did not need one.
- **the second half — the hard error that left the app with no project open — is NOT fixed and was NOT reproduced.** Reading cannot explain it: `applyOp` on a 1-frame clip takes the `newDur === c.duration` path and returns the timeline unchanged, with nothing that throws. It needs a live repro, and a live repro needs a deliberately-collapsed 1-frame clip; the only app instance running during this pass was open on the owner's real `2026-09-12-c040-mgfx-recut.chroma`, so deliberately corrupting a clip in it to chase the crash was not on. **Left open as its own follow-up** — the plausible suspects (the preview compositor or the autosave choking on a degenerate clip and taking the store down, rather than `applyOp` itself) are all in the app, not in the two functions fixed here. Note that the arithmetic fix removes the main way a clip got into that 1-frame state in the first place, so this may now be hard to reach at all — which is a reason to keep the entry open, not to close it.
- **verification:** 5 new cases in `timeline.test.ts`'s own B-220 block (an over-long clip shortens by exactly the delta rather than collapsing to the bound; a lengthening trim on one is refused with a reason naming the overhang; the sibling-at-the-same-`start_frame` shape that makes `maxDur` 1 no longer collapses a 360-frame clip; shortening can return a clip to bounds and still stops at 1; an in-bounds clip clamps exactly as before, both against the media and against a neighbour) plus 4 matching `cargo test` cases in `apelles-timeline`. `cargo test -p apelles-timeline` **263 passed / 0 failed**; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean. `npx vitest run packages/editor packages/player` **2092 passed / 0 failed (116/116 files)** on the rebased base — fully green, since main's B-184/D-355 fix landed in the meantime and retired the one bailout failure this pass had been carrying. `tsc -p packages/editor` introduces zero new errors (the same 3 pre-existing `RecutPanel.dom.test.tsx`/`recutSweep.test.ts` fixture-typing errors B-227/D-349 already disclosed).

## B-219 — a filesystem-COPIED project keeps absolute `source_path`s pointing into the ORIGINAL project, so `motion_render`'s "a re-render refreshes the placed Edit clips" silently does nothing — and `motion_get_edit_links` confirms it will work

status: **fixed** (2026-09-19, **D-359**) — both things that CAN be fixed without an in-app copy operation; see the last bullet for what is deliberately still out of scope · severity: **high** (the documented Motion→Edit refresh contract is silently void for any copied project, and the tool built to answer "what will this re-render refresh?" answers wrongly) · area: project copy / media-pool `source_path` resolution, plus `motion_get_edit_links`' scene→clip matching

- **found:** 2026-09-17, `2026-09-12-c040-mgfx-recut` — a project made by copying `2026-09-12-c040-mgfx.chroma` on the filesystem (the standard "work on a copy, leave the original alone" move this whole recut has been done under).
- **what happens:** the copy's `project.json` carries the media pool verbatim, so each of the 9 Motion-overlay pool items still has `source_path: /…/2026-09-12-c040-mgfx.chroma/motion/renders/<scene>.mp4` — the **original** project's renders directory. `motion_render` in the copy correctly writes to the copy's OWN `motion/renders/`, and correctly auto-imports each output as a **new** pool item. But every clip already on the timeline still references the old item, so nothing on the timeline changes. D-260's contract ("re-rendering a scene REFRESHES the Edit clips already placed from it… you do NOT re-import, and you do NOT call `editor_swap_clip_media`") is simply not true here, and nothing says so.
- **measured on the live project:** after a full 9-scene `motion_render`, all nine files under the copy's own `motion/renders/` had fresh mtimes and the re-authored `c040-recap.mp4` was 3,002,732 bytes / 558 frames — while `editor_list_media` showed **19** items: the original 10 plus 9 freshly-imported duplicates, one per scene, differing only in `source_path`. The Edit timeline still played the original project's 360-frame recap.
- **`motion_get_edit_links` actively confirms the wrong answer.** It reported, for every scene, `rendered: true`, `clipCount: 2`, and the two placed clips — with `sourcePath` printed as the **original** project's path. It matches a scene to pool items by `motionSceneId`, not by which file the render will actually write, so the one tool whose job is "see what a `motion_render` will refresh before you run one" says "these two clips" for clips the render cannot reach. Reading its output as a green light is exactly the mistake available here.
- **worked around for this project, disclosed not fixed:** all 18 overlay clips (tracks 1 and 3, 9 scenes) were repointed with `editor_swap_clip_media` to the copy's own pool items, and the one clip whose source had changed length was re-placed at its new length. The project is now self-contained; `motion_render` → Edit refresh works in it from here.
- **fix, in order of how much it closes:** (1) make a project copy rewrite `source_path`s that live INSIDE the source project directory to the new project's own directory — the assets are part of the project, a copy should own its copies; (2) failing that, have `motion_render` detect that a scene's existing pool item resolves outside the open project and repoint or warn instead of quietly adding a duplicate; (3) at minimum, make `motion_get_edit_links` compare the pool item's `sourcePath` against the path the render will WRITE, and report `rendered`/`clipCount` against that — an honest `clipCount: 0` here would have made this visible in one call.
- **fixed (D-359) — (2) and (3). (1) is NOT this entry's to take**, because there is no in-app copy operation to hook: copying a project is the user's own OS-level file action (Finder, `cp -R`), confirmed by search. Building one is a real feature, not a bug fix, and is deliberately left.
  - **(2) — `refresh_media` now takes the open project's root** (`crates/apelles-project/src/manifest.rs`) and reconciles what a copy inherited before its exact-string path match runs. An item is recognised as an inherited copy of the file being written when all three hold: it carries the scene's Motion stamp, its path is NOT inside the open project, and it sits at the SAME project-relative location (`motion/renders/<scene>.mp4`) under a different root. That triple is what tells "a different project's copy that happens to share a path prefix" from a render deliberately sent elsewhere (fails the third) or an unrelated file (fails the first). Such an item is **repointed** at the new path, keeping its id — so the Edit clips already placed from it stay linked and genuinely do pick up the copy's own render, which is D-260's contract restored rather than merely reported. When the copy was already re-rendered before this fix (the state this bug was found in), the inherited item instead loses its scene stamp: the pool item stays, because clips may still be reading it, it just stops claiming to be that scene's render. `Path::starts_with`/`ends_with` compare whole components, so `/…/c040.chroma` does not "contain" `/…/c040.chroma-recut` — the exact pair of names this was found on.
  - **(3) — `motion_get_edit_links` answers against the file a render will WRITE.** `computeEditLinks` takes the project root, prefers an in-project item over an inherited one (the live shape here put the STALE one first, so "the first wins" picked precisely the wrong file), and stamps each link with `refreshedByRender`. A scene whose only link is unreachable now reads `rendered: false`, `clipCount: 0`, `refreshedByRender: false`, with the whole inherited link reported as `staleLink` (its `mediaId`/`sourcePath`/`clipCount`/`clips` and a `reason` naming the fix) and a top-level `warning` on the response. The honest `clipCount: 0` this entry asked for, without throwing away what was actually found. `refreshedByRender` is three-valued — `null` means no project root reached the tab, which is not a "no".
  - **the containment check is deliberately necessary-not-sufficient**, and says so in code: deriving the exact render path in TypeScript would mean a second copy of `motion.rs`'s `default_output_path` and would be wrong for every caller-named output. "A render of a scene in this project writes inside this project" is enough to separate the two cases, and is exactly the condition this bug is made of.
  - **the GUI half, same value:** a scene row whose clips are unreachable shows a red `N stale` badge instead of the green `N in Edit` one, whose tooltip says a re-render will not refresh them and what to do.
  - **regression tests:** four in `crates/apelles-project/src/manifest.rs` (the repoint keeps the item id; a NEGATIVE CONTROL passing no project root reproduces the old duplicate shape exactly, proving the test measures the new rule; the already-duplicated copy has the stamp cleared and no item removed; and the three things that must not be adopted) plus seven in `packages/motion/src/editLinks.test.ts` (the headline, the pool-order tie-break, the sibling-name boundary, the three-valued `null`) and five in `motionOps.test.ts` for the tool's own reporting.

## B-218 — the live preview applies scale BEFORE crop, contradicting `editor_get_capabilities`' own documented crop-then-scale order

status: **fixed** (2026-09-18, **D-346**) · severity: high (the documented `full_width_half_height_recipe` cannot produce its own promised result, and preview/export disagree the same way B-201 did) · area: `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/edit.rs` (`composite_layer_onto`, `ClipTransform::effective_size`, `blend_layer_sampled`) vs `crates/apelles-mcp/src/tools/edit/capabilities.json`'s `position_and_crop_units`/`full_width_half_height_recipe` entries

- **found:** 2026-09-17, while working out a crop-based side-panel composite for `2026-09-12-c040-mgfx`.
- **measured, not inferred:** `crop_left 0.35, crop_right 0.35, scale 0.30, position (0,0)` was expected (per the capabilities doc's own stated order — crop applied before scale) to yield a `0.30 × <full-crop-adjusted-height>` box. The live preview instead measured **0.091 × 0.302** of canvas, offset 0.104 from the left edge — exactly `0.30 × 0.30`, i.e. the crop is being applied to the ALREADY-scaled box, with `position` still anchored to the pre-crop (uncropped) origin.
- **why this matters beyond one recipe:** `capabilities.json`'s own `full_width_half_height_recipe` is built entirely on "crop is applied before scale" being true. It is not, in the preview. Anyone who follows that documented recipe gets a box in the wrong place at the wrong size.
- **~~not yet known:~~ answered — the export followed the docs and the preview did not**, so this WAS the second B-201-shaped divergence this entry suspected. `buildClipFilterChain` emits `crop=` then `scale=` then `overlay=`, in that order, and has since B-074; only `composite_layer_onto` was out of step.
- **~~workaround found (not a fix):~~ do not use it.** The `scale: 1.0` + crop + compensating `position_x` recipe this entry recorded was measured in the PREVIEW only. Under the export's (correct, and now the preview's) order, `scale: 1.0` resizes the cropped column back up to the full canvas width — so anything authored against that workaround exports completely differently from what was checked. Kept here as a correction record; the ordering it worked around no longer exists.
- **cause:** `composite_layer_onto` treated a crop as an ALPHA MASK over the full layer (D-132's deliberate "a crop does not move the remaining picture" reading, matching Premiere's Crop effect and Resolve's Crop mode) and then resized that whole masked layer into the placement box. The box therefore had the UNCROPPED footprint's size and the kept picture occupied only the crop's own fraction of it. Self-consistent, and the opposite of both the documentation and the exporter.
- **fixed (D-346):** the preview moved to the exporter's order — it resizes the crop's SUB-IMAGE into the box — for the same reason D-338 moved `position_*` to meet it, plus the one first-party vendor rule that exists on the question (Final Cut Pro's "Crop clips": *"The cropped image automatically expands to fill the screen"*). `effective_size` now derives an un-overridden height from the CROPPED aspect ratio, which is what `h='-2'` means on the export side, and that reduces to the old formula exactly at zero crop. `corner_radius` was rounding the uncropped box and is correct for free.
- **regression test — the cross-engine PAIR this entry asked for**, one non-trivial crop+scale combination through both engines against one independently written-down rectangle: `composite_layer_onto_agrees_with_the_exporter_on_the_crop_parity_rectangle` (`chroma::edit`) and `'B-218 — crop-then-scale parity with the live-preview compositor'` (`packages/editor/src/timelineExport.ffmpeg.test.ts`, real ffmpeg). Confirmed non-vacuous: the pre-fix compositor fails every corner assertion in the Rust half.
- **also found and fixed in the same line of code:** B-223 below.

## B-217 — Vite/HMR can silently duplicate a Zustand store instance, wedging the Edit tab into showing one project's timeline under a DIFFERENT project's identity

status: **fixed** (2026-09-18, **D-358** — both halves: the stores are HMR-resilient singletons AND every MCP op now refuses to run while they disagree; see the last three bullets) · severity: **medium** (re-rated 2026-09-18 triage, was high — production loads a static `../dist` bundle with no HMR graph at all, so this is dev/agent-workflow-only, never a production path; still silent — no error, no crash; an MCP write during the wedge risks landing against the wrong project identity, and the only visible symptom is the Motion tab saying "no project open" while the Edit tab is plainly showing a real timeline) · area: `app/src/Root.tsx`'s `useSessionStore.projectPath` → `useEditorTimelineStore`/`useMotionProjectStore` bridge, under Vite dev-mode HMR

- **found:** 2026-09-17, after many hours of continuous `npm run tauri:dev` with heavy HMR churn (dozens of live-app-driving agent passes in one session).
- **symptom:** `open_project("2026-09-12-c040-mgfx")` returned success and the Rust backend genuinely held that project, but `motion_get_state` reported `loadState: "no-project"` and `editor_get_state` reported `openProject: "untitled:Untitled"` — while the Edit tab's own preview was visibly rendering c040's real timeline and clips.
- **root cause:** `Root.tsx` bridges the session store's `projectPath` into the Edit/Motion stores, but after enough HMR reloads, `Root` held a DIFFERENT in-memory instance of `useSessionStore` than `useChromaControl` (the actual op handler) was reading — two live copies of what should be one shared store, per D-020's "one shared state" rule. Proof: `save_project` returned `saved: true` (only possible with a real, non-`Untitled` `projectPath`), while `Root`'s own bridge was still pinned to `untitled:Untitled` — the two halves of the app were provably looking at different store instances simultaneously.
- **worked around:** a full page reload (forcing Vite to restart) cleared the duplication; a fresh `open_project` afterward loaded correctly (`loadState: "ready"`).
- **~~not fixed:~~ as filed (2026-09-17):** the stores had no guard against HMR re-instantiation producing two live copies of what must be a singleton — they do now, see the fix bullets below. Whether this affected any EARLIER live-app-driving pass that night is not established either way — every such pass verified its own results by reading real persisted project-file/`get_timeline` state directly rather than trusting in-memory assumptions, which is the mitigating practice, not a guarantee this class of bug can't recur.
- **~~fix:~~ done, 2026-09-18, D-358 — and it is both halves, not either.** The entry proposed "either … or"; both landed, because they close different things (see the last bullet for what remains unverified).
  - **The stores are HMR-resilient singletons.** New bottom-layer package **`@apelles/store`**: `createSharedStore(key, initializer)` keys the instance into `import.meta.hot.data` — Vite's own documented mechanism for handing state from a module instance to its replacement — so a re-evaluated store module returns the instance that already exists instead of building a second one. `useSessionStore` (`app.session`), `useEditorTimelineStore` (`edit.timeline`), `useMotionProjectStore` (`motion.project`) and `useMediaPoolStore` (`bridge.mediaPool`) all go through it. `import.meta.hot` is `undefined` in a production build and under vitest, so it is a plain `create()` in both. An edit to a store's *actions* still takes effect without a reload: the re-run initializer's function-valued properties (plus any genuinely new key) are merged onto the surviving instance.
  - **An op-time consistency check, which is the more valuable half.** `useSessionStore` registers as the project-identity **authority**; the three stores `Root.tsx` bridges that identity into register what they actually hold (Motion against the project *path*, the other two against the project *key* — the same asymmetry `selectProjectKey` already documents). All three MCP op registries — `useChromaControl.ts`, `@apelles/editor`'s `useEditorControl.ts`, `@apelles/motion`'s `useMotionControl.ts` — `await assertProjectIdentity(op)` before executing anything. On a divergence the op fails with a message naming both identities and both stores, `console.error` carries it to the Rust log via `frontendLogBridge`, and a non-dismissing toast says so in the GUI. **Reads are guarded as well as writes, deliberately** — the first symptom here was `editor_get_state` answering confidently about the wrong project, not the write that would have followed it. The check tolerates the composition root's one-tick React-effect bridge lag (a bounded 1 s settle window) so a legitimate lag is not reported as a wedge; a real duplicate-instance wedge never settles.
