  - **Tests: 16, in `packages/store/src/`.** `projectIdentity.test.ts` induces this entry's exact measured wedge (session on a real project, Edit store still on `untitled:Untitled`) and pins that the op is refused, that both identities are in the message, that the loud sinks both fire, that an Untitled session is *not* a divergence, and that the one-tick bridge lag resolves instead of failing. `sharedStore.test.ts` pins that a second evaluation returns the same instance with its state intact and the new actions adopted.
  - **What is NOT verified by an automated test, stated plainly:** real Vite HMR behaviour. `sharedStore.test.ts` drives the factory with an explicit registry, which *is* the mechanism `import.meta.hot.data` provides, but no test exercises a running dev server deciding to re-evaluate a module, and this bug needed hours of live churn to appear once — it has no repro. Nor was a live dev-server session run to reproduce-then-confirm. That unverifiable gap is exactly why the second half exists and why it was not treated as optional: if HMR resilience ever fails, the wedge is now loud on the first op instead of silent for a session.
- **a factual correction to this entry's own 2026-09-18 re-rating note:** it claimed `import.meta.hot` "appears nowhere in `app/src` or `packages/`". It did appear once, in `app/src/utils/frontendLogBridge.ts` (a `hot.on('vite:error')` listener forwarding Vite errors to the Rust log). That use calls no `accept()` and creates no HMR boundary, so the re-rating's *conclusion* — dev-only, no production HMR graph — is unaffected; the stated fact was wrong and is corrected here rather than left to be re-derived.

## B-216 — `editor_detect_retakes`/`editor_detect_silences` have no "sweep the whole timeline" mode, so a cleanup pass silently misses whole clips

status: **the entry as titled is fixed** (2026-09-17, **D-343** — both halves, the MCP surface AND the GUI panel); **its two discovered sub-failures are half closed**: the transcription one is fixed 2026-09-18 by **D-349** (the dropped speech is now detected, re-read and spliced back in), the **clip-straddling one is still open** and is the bigger of the two — see the last two bullets · severity: medium (no wrong data, no crash — but a real, demonstrated cause of missed content: several genuine retakes and one 5-10s silence survived to the final cut) · area: workflow/tool surface — `crates/apelles-speech/src/retake.rs`'s algorithm itself is not at fault; the gap is that every caller (`app/src-tauri/src/chroma/speech.rs`'s Tauri command, `crates/apelles-mcp/src/tools/edit.rs`'s MCP tool, `packages/editor/src/RecutPanel.tsx`'s GUI panel) requires one explicit `track`/`clip` index per call, with no batch-all convenience anywhere in the stack

- **CONSOLIDATED STATUS, 2026-09-19 — read this bullet first, the rest of the entry is the investigation trail that produced it.** Answering "how reliable is retake/silence/transcription cleanup right now, end to end": four adjacent bugs found along the way are fixed and confirmed — **B-224** (transcription non-reproducibility, D-349), **B-198** (retake detection missing a 3x-repeated line, D-327), **B-188** (silence detection O(n²) timeout on 4K, D-321), **B-189** (mlx-whisper GPU/Metal memory leak, D-322) — plus this entry's own title (D-343) and its transcription sub-failure (D-349, the "dark region" detector, ~80% precision on real footage). **What is left, ranked by how much of "bad cuts" it explains:** (1) **clip-straddling blindness** — both detectors only see inside one clip's own trimmed range, so a retake split across a cut point is invisible to per-clip grouping no matter how accurate the transcript is; this is architecture, not tuning, and is why several genuine retakes still survive a swept cleanup pass (see the two "REAL USE" bullets below for the exact confirmed cases). (2) **phantom duplicates** — the whole-file transcript occasionally invents a repeated word/phrase that isn't in the audio; the dark-region detector only catches missing speech, not invented speech. (3) **the "honest false positive"** — a genuine build-up utterance can score as a retake; documented in `retake.rs`'s own comments but has no regression test. None of these three are model-quality problems (Whisper is already `large-v3`; the 0.82 similarity threshold was empirically calibrated against real restarts) — they are gaps in what the surrounding tool sees, not in what the model hears.

- **found:** 2026-09-17, reviewing `2026-09-12-c040` against 10 owner-placed markers. Several were genuine retakes that survived the cut (e.g. two full takes of "the encoder reads your whole message once and..." both kept), plus one 5-10s dead-air silence.
- **verified it is NOT a detection-algorithm bug**: the "encoder reads your whole message" pair was run through the real `similarity()`/`containment()` code (`retake.rs:276`) with the project's exact wording — it scores **0.8413, above the default 0.82 threshold**. This pair WOULD be flagged as a retake if `editor_detect_retakes` were ever called against the clip containing it. Likewise `editor_detect_silences`' default `min_silence_ms: 600` would trivially catch a 5-10s gap. Neither tool has a scoring or threshold problem here.
- **the real cause**: this timeline has ~75 clips (retakes/silences already cut once). `editor_detect_retakes`/`editor_detect_silences` both require a caller to name one `track`/`clip` at a time — `RecutPanel.tsx` (line 328) literally instructs "Select **one** clip on the timeline." A cleanup pass naturally covers the specific clip(s) a report points at and stops there; nothing forces or even reminds the caller (human or agent) to re-sweep every remaining clip after later edits reshape the timeline. The new markers cluster in exactly the stretch (QKV/encoder-decoder/lost-in-middle/recap) that the original D-327 pass's own reported repro never touched.
- **a related, separate, already-documented weakness** (not the cause here, but worth not conflating): `retake.rs`'s own doc comment (lines 256-275) acknowledges `containment`'s sliding-window score can also go the OTHER way — a false POSITIVE when a later utterance genuinely just extends an earlier one (a build-up, not a retake) rather than replacing it, "the honest false positive." Confirmed via this investigation that this exact shape has **no regression test** pinning either the false-positive risk or a fix for it — a real, separate gap, filed here for visibility but distinct from B-216's own root cause.
- **fix: done, D-343 — `clip` became OPTIONAL on the four existing tools rather than growing `*_all` twins.** Omit it and `editor_detect_silences` / `editor_detect_retakes` (and both `_status` polls) sweep every analysable clip on the track. Deliberately not a new tool name: an agent that already knows the tool gets the sweep by leaving an argument out, where a second name would have to be *discovered* first — the same discoverability failure this entry is made of, one level up.
- **why a client-side loop would not have been a fix, root-caused in that pass:** `app/src-tauri/src/chroma/control.rs`'s `serve()` is a single-threaded, one-request-at-a-time HTTP loop (`for mut req in server.incoming_requests()`, no per-request spawn). 75 calls queue there and are served in strict sequence however concurrently a caller issues them, while the per-clip work is cheap (a per-FILE cached transcript plus string similarity; a short VAD pass). The round trips were the cost, so the sweep is a native loop inside ONE dispatch.
- **measured, by counting rather than by stopwatch** (`recutSweep.dom.test.tsx`, per `docs/notes/performance-instrumentation.md` §4): 20 clips sweep in **exactly one** dispatch; the same 20 named one at a time cost **20**. Wall-clock alongside, at load average 1.80: **88 ms vs 1066 ms** — in jsdom, where the HTTP and queue costs are zero, so that ratio is a floor on the real gap.
- **the GUI half landed in the same pass:** `RecutPanel.tsx`'s "select one clip" instruction is gone. It now carries a "This clip / Whole track" scope toggle on one control, and with nothing selected on a single-video-track timeline it offers the sweep rather than refusing. Both interfaces decide what is analysable through the same `sweepTargets`.
- **still open and adjacent, not fixed here:** the false-POSITIVE regression gap noted two bullets up remains unpinned, and **B-197** (`ripple_delete_ranges` silently dropping ranges from a large batch) was untouched at the time — since **fixed** by D-361 (2026-09-19), so a big swept cut now reports which ranges it could not apply and why, instead of needing its frame arithmetic re-derived by hand.
- **FIRST REAL USE, 2026-09-17 (`2026-09-12-c040-mgfx-recut`), and it found a SECOND, DIFFERENT blind spot the sweep does not close.** The sweep itself worked exactly as specified: 75 clips, one dispatch each, `totals.analysable: 75`, and it caught the 5-10 s dead air the owner's marker 9 flagged. But against the same 10 markers it reported only **one** retake group, on a 7-frame clip — while **eight** of the ten markers were real, confirmed content defects. The reason is stated in the tools' own docs and is not a defect in D-343's work, but it defeats the workflow this entry was filed to fix: **each clip is still analysed only within its OWN trimmed range.** On a talking-head timeline already cut into 75 short clips, a retake almost always straddles a clip boundary — the flubbed tail sits at the end of clip N and the good take starts at clip N+1 — so there is no single clip in which both takes appear, and per-clip grouping cannot see the pair however many clips are swept. The very pair this entry was opened over ("the encoder reads your whole message…", scored 0.8413) is one of these: in the real timeline the flubbed take is the whole of clip 42 and the good take begins at clip 43.
  - **worse, this interacts with a transcription failure that hides the same material twice.** Whisper's whole-file pass silently swallowed four multi-second regions of this source (365.7-370.1, 518.2-521.6, 615.7-618.0, 638.9-645.4 s), emitting one word stretched across each gap rather than any text. Three of those four contained an entire flubbed take. So a caller reading the transcript ALSO cannot see them. Re-transcribing each suspect window in isolation (a 2-9 s `ffmpeg` extract through the same `ai-media/transcribe.py`) recovered every one of them cleanly and immediately.
  - **the cheap detector for this, worth building:** flag any clip whose own source range contains a stretch of ≥1.2 s with no transcript word in it but with real VAD energy. That is a two-signal cross-check over data both detectors already have, it found all four dark regions here with no false positives, and it is exactly the "there is speech here nobody has read" case that both the retake grouper and a human reading the transcript are blind to.
  - **suggested real fix for the straddling case:** group retakes over the track's own CONCATENATED surviving material (or over a window of adjacent clips) rather than per clip, so a pair split across a cut point is still a pair. Not attempted in the recut pass; the eight markers were worked by hand from raw source seconds instead.
- **SECOND REAL USE, 2026-09-17 (same project, the owner's 4 follow-up markers), and it adds three concrete things to the two above rather than repeating them.**
  - **a FIFTH dark region, and it is the worst one yet: `268.3-271.2 s`.** The whole-file pass emitted no usable text across it; an isolated 2.4 s `ffmpeg` extract through the same `ai-media/transcribe.py` returned `"Constantly. Constantly."` immediately and unambiguously. Per-50 ms RMS over the same window shows two clean speech bursts (269.2-270.0 and 270.4-270.9, peak ≈ 2400-3200 against a 20-25 room floor) — i.e. the audio is not marginal, quiet or clipped; Whisper simply did not read it. **Both bursts were live on the timeline** as clips 22 and 23 (two orphan pickup takes of the word "constantly", each starting a third of the way into the word), which is exactly what the owner's marker said and what nothing automated had found. This is now five confirmed dark regions in one 684 s source: 268.3-271.2, 365.7-370.1, 518.2-521.6, 615.7-618.0, 638.9-645.4.
  - **the whole-file pass does not merely OMIT across a dark region — it also mis-places the words either side of it, so the transcript reads plausibly and is wrong.** It reported `Self` at 271.22-271.90 where the RMS floor is flat silence until 271.85; the real utterance begins at 271.858, which is (correctly) where the surviving clip's in-point already sat. Any caller that maps clips to the whole-file transcript therefore gets confident, readable, incorrect text for every clip in and adjacent to a dark region — the failure has no visible signature at all. (The proposed "≥1.2 s of clip source with no transcript word but real VAD energy" detector in the bullet above would have flagged this region too.)
  - **a NEW failure mode in the same pass, the mirror of the first: the whole-file transcript also emits PHANTOM duplicates.** It reported `" it."` twice at 557.20-557.58 and 557.58-557.72. An isolated re-transcription of 555.5-559.5 returns a single `"…instead of against it."`, and the RMS shows one word plus its 0.15 s decay tail, not two. So a retake sweep or an agent reading the whole-file transcript can be sent chasing a duplicate that does not exist, in the same file where two real ones are invisible. Both directions of error argue the same thing: **for any cut decision, re-transcribe the disputed window in isolation and cross-check against the amplitude envelope — never cut (or decline to cut) on the whole-file transcript alone.**
  - **clip-boundary blindness reconfirmed on a second, independent pair.** The duplicated "constantly" the owner marked near the recap is precisely a straddling pair: the complete word ends clip 63 (source 614.06-615.25) and a partial second one opens clip 64 (source starts 625.990, a third of the way into the word). No single clip contains both, so per-clip grouping cannot see it regardless of threshold — the same shape as the "encoder reads your whole message" pair this entry was opened over.
- **THE TRANSCRIPTION SUB-FINDING IS NOW ROOT-CAUSED AND THE PROPOSED DETECTOR IS VALIDATED, 2026-09-18** — research only, no product code changed. Full trail with every measurement: **`docs/notes/whisper-dark-region-research.md`**. The six things that change what the follow-up fix should build:
  - **The mechanism is none of the things it looks like.** Per-window decode telemetry (`seek` / `no_speech_prob` / `avg_logprob` / `temperature`, which `mlx_whisper` records and `ai-media/transcribe.py` strips) shows every dark region sits inside a window that decoded **at temperature 0.0** with `no_speech_prob` 0.043-0.171 against a 0.6 threshold and `avg_logprob` -0.249 to -0.460 against a -1.0 threshold. The no-speech skip path fired **zero times in the whole file**. Not VAD chunking (there is none), not the temperature ladder, not hallucination suppression (`hallucination_silence_threshold` is `None`), not `condition_on_previous_text`. **The model reads the audio and declines to transcribe an utterance inside a window it is otherwise transcribing confidently**, and the DTW alignment then stretches the surviving words across the hole — which is where "one word stretched across each gap" comes from. The stretched word is the symptom, not the cause.
  - **The loss is biased towards retakes specifically, not spread randomly.** The isolated re-transcription of c040's 365.7-370.1 is `"The encoder reads your whole message once and published a build"` — i.e. **the flubbed take of the very pair this entry was opened over**; the whole-file pass kept the good take 10 s later and dropped this one. c038 repeats the shape. So the transcript is most likely to be missing precisely what the retake grouper is hunting for, which compounds the clip-straddling blindness above rather than being independent of it.
  - **It is NOT deterministic, which is why 268.3-271.2 could not be reproduced.** Three identical runs of the identical file gave 925 / 923 / 913 words and three different transcripts — `mlx_whisper` samples on an unseeded MLX RNG at any temperature > 0. Filed as **B-224**. The severe regions (365.7, 518.2, 614.8) reproduce in every pass; only the marginal ones flicker. **`638.9-645.4` should be struck from this entry's list of five** — the VAD reads it as genuine silence (peak RMS 452 against a 1062 floor for real speech in this file) and an isolated pass returns one word; it was over-counted.
  - **It happens on other footage.** `A001_09122319_C038.MOV` (989 s, never previously analysed) shows 9 candidates, **7 confirmed real** — e.g. 5.48 s at 217.26 recovering `"trick being used to bring and tricks being used to bring that cost back down"` behind a single stretched ` down.`. Across both files: ~10 confirmed multi-second drops in 1676 s, one per ~3 minutes of raw source.
  - **The detector works, and needs no new dependency** — `crates/apelles-speech` already ships the Silero v6.2.1 runner (`vad.rs`) and the span builder (`silence.rs::speech_spans`) it needs. But **this entry's own wording, "a stretch of ≥1.2 s with no transcript word in it", misses more than half the real cases**, because the stretched word gives the gap coverage: 4 vs 2 candidates on c040, 9 vs 4 on c038. A word longer than **2.0 s** (whisper's own anomaly bound, `mlx_whisper/transcribe.py:329`) must contribute no coverage. **1.2 s itself is confirmed right** — candidate counts are identical from 1.0 s to 1.5 s on both files.
  - **Measured over 111 labelled windows** (every uncovered stretch ≥1.2 s in both files, each cut out, re-transcribed in isolation and RMS-profiled): this entry's formulation scores 72.7 % precision; adding an RMS-peak gate calibrated per file takes it to **100 %**; also summing VAD speech across an uncovered stretch rather than requiring one contiguous span gives **90 % precision at the best recall of the four variants**. Recall against a Silero-independent energy criterion is **100 %** for every variant — no region containing ≥1.2 s of speech-level energy was missed; every apparent "miss" holds under 0.5 s of speech. **Recommended: uncovered stretch (words >2.0 s excluded) → sum overlapping VAD speech → flag at ≥1.2 s → per-file RMS gate → report the VAD∩stretch intersections as the located regions.**
  - **A NEW variant of this same pair surfaced again, 2026-09-18, this time as an A/V-SYNC gap rather than a missed cut — worth recording since it is a different failure shape from anything above.** The owner re-found the "encoder writes the reply while constantly glancing back" straddling pair (same one as the "reconfirmed on a second, independent pair" bullet above) by ear, marked it, and manually cut the correct 29-frame span (timeline 4977-5006, source ≈207.4-208.6s) out of the CAMERA track himself — that half was already fine. What was NOT fine: the project's real narration audio comes from a separately-generated Adobe-Podcast-enhanced track (`track 4`, rendered once from an earlier snapshot of this same cut), and that render still had BOTH deliveries in full — the video-side manual fix was never propagated to it, so the flawed "glancing" repeat kept playing under what was now a silent-black gap on screen. Confirmed the fix was needed with a whisper cross-check consistent with this entry's own findings above: an isolated re-transcription of the audio still showed `glancing` spanning an anomalous 1.5s (0.76→3.02s of a 4s slice) — the same "one word stretched across a hole" signature this entry root-caused, not two distinct words, exactly as predicted. Fixed by splitting `track 4`'s clip at the identical two frame numbers and removing the middle piece (left as a gap, not rippled, to match the video side and keep everything after it in sync) — **no new detector code, just closing the same hole on the second of two tracks that carry the same performance.** Filed here rather than as a new bug because the underlying defect (whisper's dropped-speech blind spot making this class of duplicate invisible to a transcript-based sweep) is this entry's own; the actionable NEW lesson is process, not code: **a track rendered from an earlier snapshot of an edit (an enhanced-audio bounce, a burned-in caption file, anything pre-rendered rather than composited live) needs the same manual retake fix re-applied to it — nothing currently tracks or reminds a caller that such a derivative exists and has drifted.** Worth a line in `docs/04-roadmap.md` if a second derived-audio project hits the same thing; not generalized here from a single instance.

- **THE TRANSCRIPTION SUB-FINDING IS NOW BUILT AND SHIPPING, 2026-09-18 — D-349.** The detector this entry proposed exists, the recovery this entry did NOT propose exists with it, and **B-224 is fixed** so both are reproducible. What landed:
  - **`crates/apelles-speech`'s new `dark` module** implements the research's recommendation exactly: uncovered stretch (words >2.0 s excluded from coverage) → sum the overlapping VAD speech → flag at ≥1.2 s → gate on a per-file-calibrated RMS floor → report the VAD∩stretch intersections. 18 unit tests, including one built specifically to fail against **this entry's own original wording** (a word stretched across the hole must not hide it) and one pinning that the floor is relative to the recording, not absolute.
  - **Validated independently on the same two real sources**, through `tests/dark_live.rs` (the real Silero model, the real whole-file transcripts): **c040 — 4 regions, 1 gated out; c038 — 6 flagged stretches, 1 gated out.** All 10 stretches were then re-read in isolation through the real product entry point: **8 of 10 returned the speaker's own dropped content**, including every case the research had confirmed by hand. The other 2 returned short off-topic room asides — real audible speech, not retakes. ~80 % precision counted strictly.
  - **The recovery, which is the part this entry did not ask for and is the actual fix.** `ai-media/transcribe.py` gained `--start-secs`/`--duration-secs` (timestamps shifted back to absolute source seconds), plumbed through the sidecar, `apelles_ai`, the Tauri command and the store. `editor_detect_retakes` now scans each clip's range, re-transcribes every located window **in isolation**, and **splices the recovered words into the transcript it groups** — so the grouper finally sees the flubbed takes this entry was opened over instead of a hole where they were. Default ON (`recoverDarkRegions: false` opts out). The same `clipTranscriptView` runs behind the Recut panel, which says so when a grouping read recovered lines, and the Index panel marks a recovered transcript row **recovered**.
  - **One thing the research did not find, caught in validation:** language auto-detection is unreliable on a short window — 2 of the 10 isolated passes first came back in an entirely different script. The recovery pass now **pins the language to the whole-file pass's own detection**, and both read correctly with it.
  - **`editor_detect_dark_regions` / `_status`** exist on both MCP surfaces for the standalone question ("how much of this file did whisper not read?"), parity-tested.
  - **Struck as this entry's 2026-09-18 update already directed:** `638.9-645.4` is not a dark region and is not reported by the shipped detector either.
- **WHAT REMAINS OPEN IN THIS ENTRY, after D-349 — do not read the above as closing it.**
  - **The clip-straddling blindness is untouched and is still the bigger half.** A retake whose flubbed tail ends clip N and whose good take opens clip N+1 has no single clip containing both, so per-clip grouping cannot see it however good the transcript is. D-349 fixes what the grouper READS, not what it reads it OVER. The suggested fix — group over the track's concatenated surviving material, or over a window of adjacent clips — is still unattempted.
  - **The phantom-duplicate failure** (the whole-file pass emitting `" it."` twice where there is one word) is untouched. The dark detector finds missing speech, not invented speech.
  - **The standing advice stands unchanged:** never cut, or decline to cut, on the whole-file transcript alone. D-349 makes that transcript better, not trustworthy.
  - **The false-POSITIVE regression gap** noted far above (a later utterance that merely EXTENDS an earlier one, `retake.rs`'s "honest false positive") is still unpinned by any test.


## B-215 — `editor_trim_clip` on `edge: "end"` silently no-ops on some clips: returns `{ok: true}`, changes nothing

status: **fixed** (2026-09-18) · severity: medium (no data loss, no crash — the op just does nothing, with no error or warning to say so) · area: `packages/editor/src/timeline.ts` (`applyOp`'s `trim_start`/`trim_end` cases), `packages/editor/src/useEditorControl.ts` (`editor_trim_clip`)

- **found:** 2026-09-17, trying to close a 105-frame gap-vs-overlap sync issue between `c040-thefix` (a Motion-overlay clip, track 0, ends at timeline frame 4980) and `c040-recap` (narration for it starts ~4875, 105 frames earlier).
- **repro:** `editor_trim_clip(track=0, clip=6, edge="end", delta=105)` against `2026-09-12-c040-mgfx`'s real timeline. Response: `{"ok": true, "result": {"ok": true, "track": 0}}` — no error, no `note`, nothing suggesting a clamp or refusal. Re-read the clip via both `get_timeline` and the project's own `project.json` immediately after: `duration` and `startFrame+duration` (4980) are **byte-identical to before the call**. Repeated the identical call a second time (in case of an off-by-one needing two applications) — still no change.
- **verified it is not an indexing mistake:** `get_timeline`'s own `track.clips[6]` and a direct read of `project.json`'s `timelines[].tracks[0].clips[6]` agree on exactly which clip index 6 is (`c040-thefix.mp4`) — the tool and the file are not disagreeing about which clip this addressed.
- **not yet isolated to `edge: "end"` specifically, this clip specifically, or `editor_trim_clip` generally** — only one clip/edge/delta combination was tried before working around it (see below); this entry is the repro as found, not a root-caused diagnosis.
- **worked around, not fixed:** rather than trim `c040-thefix`, moved `c040-recap`'s clip to `start_frame: 4875` to close the visible gap — which then OVERLAPPED `c040-thefix` (ends 4980) by 105 frames on the same track, since the trim that was supposed to make room silently didn't happen. Caught immediately (checked `project.json` after the move) and reverted `c040-recap` back to `start_frame: 4985`, its original non-overlapping position. **The net result: the sync issue (recap's graphic lands ~4.4s / 105 frames after its own narration starts) is UNFIXED and left as a known, disclosed gap** — not silently left broken, but also not resolved tonight.
- **fix:** read `app/src-tauri`'s real trim handler for this clip/edge combination and find why it accepts the call, reports success, and changes nothing — a silent no-op is worse than a refusal, since nothing in the response distinguishes "trimmed" from "asked to trim and didn't."
- **REPRODUCED 2026-09-17, second independent case, and it narrows the bug usefully.** On `2026-09-12-c040-mgfx-recut`, `editor_trim_clip(track=1, clip=8, edge="end", delta=13)` against `c040-payoff.mp4` (an unlocked overlay clip, `start_frame` 5367, `duration` 435 @30 fps on a 24 fps timeline) returned `{"ok": true, "result": {"ok": true, "track": 1}}` and left `duration` at 435 — a different clip, a different track, a different source file, a different delta, same silent no-op. **What both cases share is the shape, and it is a real lead:** both are the LAST clip on their track, both are a shortening `edge: "end"` trim, and both clips have a `source_fps` (30) that differs from the timeline's own rate (24). The mixed-rate detail is the one worth checking first given B-077's history in exactly this arithmetic (`timelineFramesToSource` on a clip whose native rate is not the project's). Note the counter-example from the same session: `editor_trim_clip(track=0, clip=64, edge="start", delta=-184, ripple=True)` on a 24.005 fps camera clip applied correctly and was verified — so this is not `editor_trim_clip` being broken generally, and `edge: "start"` is known-good on at least one real case.
- **worked around again, disclosed again:** the 13-frame overhang was removed by MOVING the overlay 13 frames earlier (`editor_move_clip` to 5354) so it ends flush with the camera track, rather than by trimming it. The clip is still its full authored length; nothing was shortened.
- **ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED 2026-09-18, and the mixed-fps lead above was a red herring.** D-352 had already retired the sign-convention theory (both engines consistently implement "a positive delta moves that edge later in time"; only the MCP docstrings were wrong, fixed separately). This pass retired the mixed-rate theory too: `timelineFramesToSource` is doing its job correctly in both reported cases. What is actually happening is much simpler, and is the same defect B-227 found for `editor_remove_gap` — **`applyOp`'s `trim_start`/`trim_end` cases reject by `return tl`, and `useEditorControl.ts`'s `editor_trim_clip` handler dispatched that op and then returned `{ok: true, track}` unconditionally**, so a caller could not distinguish "trimmed" from "refused." Both reported clips are the LAST on their track with the tail already at the media's end, so `clampedTrimEndDuration` returns exactly the current `duration` and the reducer's own `if (newDur === c.duration) return tl` fires. That refusal is CORRECT (there is no source material left to extend into); reporting it as success is the bug, and always was.
- **fix, the `checkRemoveGap` pattern of B-227 applied to the second of the three functions that entry names:** a new pure, exported `checkTrim(tl, track, clip, edge, delta, ripple, fps)` in `timeline.ts` holds every precondition the two reducer cases used to enforce inline — the clamp making no difference, the 1-frame floor, D-129's lockstep-or-reject link rule, and (for the D-235 rippled form) the empty shared range, the zero clamped delta and B-033's straddling sync-locked track. `applyOp`'s two cases and the MCP handler both call it, so they cannot drift. A rejection now comes back as a real `error` naming the actual CONSTRAINT rather than the refusal: which bound clamped it (the media's own remaining length with its `source_start`/`source_len` printed, the following clip's `start_frame` with D-054's no-overlap rule cited, the previous clip's end, the 1-frame floor), which linked member disagreed and in which group, or that the delta rounds to zero of this clip's own source frames. The reference-equality backstop after dispatch (`timeline === tl`) is kept exactly as B-227 left it, so any future silent-reject path this pre-check does not yet mirror still surfaces as an honest error. `editor_trim_clip` also now reports the resulting `startFrame`/`duration` instead of a bare `{ok: true, track}` — the clamp routinely applies less than the delta asked for, and being unable to see that was the other half of what made this bug invisible.
- **not a behaviour change to what a trim DOES.** Every clamp, bound and lockstep rule is unchanged; only their visibility to a caller changed. The one exception is B-220's clamp, fixed in the same commit — see that entry.
- **still true, and worth keeping:** `edge: "start"` was never broken, and the counter-example above still applies. The remaining GUI half — surfacing `checkTrim`'s reason in the UI when an edge drag is refused, rather than the drag simply not moving — is NOT done here, matching B-227's own scope (it wired the reducer and the MCP handler, not a toast).
- **verification:** 8 new `checkTrim` cases in `timeline.test.ts` (B-215's own reported shape rejected with the media bound named; the neighbour bound named instead when that is what blocks it; agreement with `applyOp` on the success case including the clamped duration it reports; a locked track, an out-of-range track, an out-of-range clip and a zero delta each named; the D-054 head clamp named; the D-129 link partner named by group and index; the B-033 ripple straddle named) — see this entry's sibling B-220 for the rest of the run.

## B-211 — a transient dangling graph-node reference permanently wedges the Motion tab's still-preview; it survives a tab switch AND a project reload, while the Remotion render path stays healthy

status: **half-fixed** (2026-09-17 — half 1 is now ACTUALLY done, after a second pass found the real root cause the first one missed; half 2, making an already-wedged preview recoverable, is still open) · severity: **high** (the Motion tab's only visual feedback loop dies for the rest of the app session, with no error text anywhere — an agent or a human editing a manifest is left authoring blind) · area: the Motion tab's still-preview fetch path (frame-by-frame rendered stills, per `debug_frame_timing`'s `scrub`/`fetch` counters); manifest data itself is fine

- **found:** 2026-09-17, building the `c040` motion-graphics set.
- **how to reproduce:** on a `graph` layer, shrink `nodes` (drop an id) BEFORE narrowing the `edges`/`pulses`/`highlight` arrays that still reference it. For one render pass the manifest is internally inconsistent, and `Graph.tsx` dereferences `layout[id]` for a node that no longer exists (`at()`, ~L123 — `p.x` of `undefined`).
- **what wedges:** from that moment every frame of EVERY scene comes back as a broken image — the preview canvas is black with a broken-image glyph, at any playhead, including scenes never touched. `debug_dom_tree` finds no error text and `motion_get_state` reports `parseError: null`, so nothing names the failure.
- **proved it is not the data:** the offending arrays were restored to the exact values that had rendered correctly minutes earlier, and the preview stayed dead. `motion_save_manifest` + a full `open_project` reload (which does re-load the manifest — `Save` greyed out afterwards) did not clear it either. A `debug_set_active_tab` round trip did not clear it.
- **proved it is only the preview:** `motion_render` rendered all 8 scenes of that same manifest successfully throughout, the Sources panel's per-scene thumbnails (drawn from those renders) were correct, and the EDIT tab's own compositing preview rendered the same clips correctly. Only the Motion tab's still-preview is stuck.
- **worked around, not fixed** (flagged per CLAUDE.md rather than presented as done): the rest of that session reviewed scenes by `motion_render` + `ffmpeg -ss … -frames:v 1` on the rendered MP4s. That is a strictly better artefact than a preview still — it is the real output — but it costs a full multi-scene render per look instead of a sub-second scrub, which is not a workable authoring loop.
- **RECURRED 2026-09-17, same session, and that found the REAL root cause.** Rebuilding `c040-selfattn`'s `graph` layer wedged the preview again, in exactly the documented way, *with half 1 already in place*. The reason half 1 did not help: the crash is not (only) the render-side `layout[id]` dereference it guarded. **d3-force itself throws first.** `forceLink.initialize` calls `find()` on every link endpoint and does `throw new Error("node not found: " + nodeId)` (`d3-force/src/link.js` L8-10) for any id the node list does not carry — and `Graph.tsx` builds that simulation inside its layout `useMemo`, which runs *before* any of the `at()` null-guards can do anything. So the first fix hardened the second-order symptom while the first-order throw was still live on the identical reproduction.
  - **why it was not caught:** half 1 shipped with no automated test (its own note says so — "this package has no test runner of its own"), and was verified by hand against a render, which is precisely the path that never wedges. Nothing exercised the layout memo.
  - **fixed properly this time:** the links handed to `forceLink` are filtered to those whose BOTH endpoints exist, via an exported pure `resolvableEdges(nodes, edges)` — dropping the link rather than inventing a placeholder node, since the edge is skipped at draw time anyway and a synthetic node would perturb the force layout of the real ones. Covered by 5 cases in `@apelles/motion`'s `graphEdge.test.ts`, including the exact live reproduction (nodes replaced wholesale, edges stale for one pass), so this cannot regress silently again.
- **fix, two halves:** (1) **done** — `Graph.tsx`'s `at()` now returns `null` instead of dereferencing a missing `layout[id]`, and every caller (`edges`, `pulses`) skips that one item rather than throwing; `nodes` was never actually at risk (it only ever asks `at()` for an id it just took from `nodes` itself) but got a defensive fallback too since `at()`'s return type is now nullable. A dangling reference now renders every OTHER edge/pulse/node correctly and simply omits the broken one, instead of crashing the whole frame. Not yet covered by an automated test — this package has no test runner of its own (D-340's own note), and the fix was verified by hand against a real render with a deliberately dangling edge rather than added to `@apelles/motion`'s suite, which doesn't reach into `motion-engine`'s React components. (2) **still open** — making an ALREADY-wedged preview recoverable (retry on next manifest change, surface a real error instead of a bare broken-image glyph) is a separate area, the app's still-preview fetch/cache path, not touched here.
